events.name: Collective Care Lab: What is revolutionary in our lives?
events.description:
Designed and led by Aurélie Harp — Wemanity Coaching

​If you’re tired of moving forward alone, or feeling lonely, or want to do something new and with others, this is for you.

​Collective Care Lab is a monthly, facilitated 90-minute group gathering at Fabrik. It exists to practice something simple and rare: being human together.

​Each gathering is shaped around one magic question to move us, challenge us, and open something new between us.

​This month Magic question: "What is revolutionary in our lives?" - Not revolutionary as in headlines and history books, revolutionary as in ours.

​No pretending.
No fixing ourselves in isolation.

​This is a space for real interaction.
For disagreement and friction.
For getting closer and building joy together.

​We work with conversation, presence, and play to generate the warm relational energy that makes us human.

​Come curious.
Leave less alone.

​What to expect

​• A warm interactive 90-minute group experience
• A mix of conversation, reflection, and creative play
• No therapy. No self-help coaching. No pressure to share
• Just a willingness to participate and create together
• Free judgement zone, come as you are

​I’ll welcome you in with a simple opening activity or question—music, something to drink, time to arrive—then we’ll introduce ourselves as a collective.

​About me

​I’m Aurélie, a Fabrik Dumbo founder, a relational and group development coach and theater performer interested in what happens when we stop treating life like a drama and start approaching it with a bit more theater, creativity, and courage. Wemanity Coaching is my practice, a place for everyone ready to grow together joyfully.

So what gives you a lasting edge? We think it's the oldest technology we have: real human connection.

🌍 Tanya Montméan, VC, brings the newest signals from SF Tech Week: what's shaping AI and capital right now.

Then we put it into practice. Sasha guides the room through structured connection, so you leave with a few relationships that go deeper than small talk.

This is for founders with a product in the market, plus the operators, angels, and VCs who back them.

events.name: Permission To Talk Money
events.description:
Permission to Talk Money: A live event and podcast recording

​Money is one of the last real taboos. We'll talk about our relationships, our therapy, our bodies, our fears — but ask a woman what she earns, what she owes, what she's saving, or what she's terrified of financially, and the room goes quiet.

​We've been taught that talking about money is impolite, immodest, or just not something "good girls" do. Permission to Talk Money is here to break that silence, once and for all.

​This is a night built for women who are tired of pretending they have it all figured out financially — and who are ready to say the things about money we're not supposed to say out loud.

​Whether you're anxious about your savings, ashamed of a purchase, confused about investing, avoiding your bank app altogether, or just exhausted from carrying financial stress alone, this room is for you.

​You've just never been given permission to talk about it honestly.

​Tonight, that changes.

For The Firsts is a meetup club for those building without a blueprint
​Expect an evening of interesting conversation in an inviting space as you meet and mingle with other "firsts" — those who are the first in their family to choose their professional path with intention instead of inertia.

​Enjoy refreshing drinks, delicious bites, and the chance to connect with other professionals, creatives, students, and founders. Each of our meetups looks something like this:

​6:00 - 6:30 PM: Arrival & Open Mixer

​6:30 - 6:40 PM: Introduction

​6:40 - 8:00 PM: Guided Networking Experience

​8:00 - 9:00 PM: Open Mixer

​If you are approved, please try to arrive on time, as our events regularly hit capacity and we have many folks on the waitlist.

​​Here’s what to expect:
​Cringe-Free Conversation: This isn't a networking event. It's a purpose-led meetup where who you are will always be more important than what you do. The dress code is always 'come exactly as you are, meet exactly who you need'.

​Guided Moments of Connection: This experience is at the core of For The Firsts. We’ll have a few rounds of guided connection meant to introduce you to others who share your story. Remember the first rule of For The Firsts: go deeper than your job title!

​Firsts, not Followers: Each meetup is curated to bring together the best possible group of professionals, creatives, and founders in NYC who are the architects of their own lives. Intention is in everything we do, and you'll find that in the people you meet. Remember, the best way to get to know someone is to get someone to know you.

​I want to encourage you to connect on who you are and your purpose for your work and life. Remember Rule #1: No job titles, go deeper. Tell us why, how and for whom you do what you do.

events.description:
The scariest thing about Halloween isn’t the ghouls, it’s the landfill. An estimated 35 million costumes get tossed in the US every year 💀

This Halloween, join Simply Sustainable for a cozy costume swap, while sipping hot chocolate + eating freshly baked goods 🏚️🍪

Clothing Swap
Bring 1-5 clean, gently used costumes, accessories, wigs or props you won’t wear again and trade them for something new to you! Think of it as a way to find a costume in a fun, sustainable and affordable way while giving your old ones a new home.

All sizes and styles are welcome! We'll have items sorted by category to make them easy to discover, a clothing rack & a full-length mirror.

Why swap?

Millions of costumes end up in landfills every year, and most are made from non-recyclable synthetic materials worn once. Swapping keeps them in circulation, saves you money, and makes finding your look a lot more fun.

🎉 Thanks and excited to see you there! ​🎉

About Simply Sustainable

Our mission is to make sustainable living accessible. We're building a place to make it easy to discover independent sustainable brands in personal care and cleaning!Check us out at SimplySustainable.eco!

events.name: Drop-In Men's Work Group
events.description:
A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

​Why does your best friend save obsessively while you can't walk past a sale, even though you make the same salary?

​Why do you know exactly what you "should" do with your money and still not do it?

​Why did you inherit your dad's spending anxiety instead of his frugality?

LinkedIn, Minus the Ick
Build visibility without losing yourself in the process. 

LinkedIn can be cringe: the forced positivity, the AI content, and the pressure to post like everyone else in your feed. This Mastermind is a discussion, not a lecture, on how to show up on the feed while building your own voice.

Juliette and Sondra have grown their audiences past 5K and pivoted industries, landed projects, and received job offers because of posting consistently on LinkedIn.

We'll dig into what makes content feel human, the systems we use to get started and keep going, and what we wish we knew at the beginning. Then we'll create small groups to share your goals and how to take the first step to showing up on LinkedIn. 

Leave with:

  • A tactical plan to engage more on LinkedIn

  • A clearer sense of how to create human content instead of AI-sounding content

  • An accountability buddy for your LinkedIn goals

Perfect for:

  • Solopreneurs, founders, and consultants building a personal brand

  • Anyone job hunting or career pivoting who wants LinkedIn to work for them

  • Ambitious professionals who are tired of feeling icky about self-promotion

About Sondra Yu

Sondra is a dynamic community builder and creator who has landed her last two roles by being visible on LinkedIn and in-person. Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.

events.name: For the Firsts
events.description:
For The Firsts is a meetup club for those building without a blueprint
​Expect an evening of interesting conversation in an inviting space as you meet and mingle with other "firsts" — those who are the first in their family to choose their professional path with intention instead of inertia.

​Enjoy refreshing drinks, delicious bites, and the chance to connect with other professionals, creatives, students, and founders. Each of our meetups looks something like this:

​6:00 - 6:30 PM: Arrival & Open Mixer

​6:30 - 6:40 PM: Introduction

​6:40 - 8:00 PM: Guided Networking Experience

​8:00 - 9:00 PM: Open Mixer

​If you are approved, please try to arrive on time, as our events regularly hit capacity and we have many folks on the waitlist.

​​Here’s what to expect:
​Cringe-Free Conversation: This isn't a networking event. It's a purpose-led meetup where who you are will always be more important than what you do. The dress code is always 'come exactly as you are, meet exactly who you need'.

​Guided Moments of Connection: This experience is at the core of For The Firsts. We’ll have a few rounds of guided connection meant to introduce you to others who share your story. Remember the first rule of For The Firsts: go deeper than your job title!

​Firsts, not Followers: Each meetup is curated to bring together the best possible group of professionals, creatives, and founders in NYC who are the architects of their own lives. Intention is in everything we do, and you'll find that in the people you meet. Remember, the best way to get to know someone is to get someone to know you.

​I want to encourage you to connect on who you are and your purpose for your work and life. Remember Rule #1: No job titles, go deeper. Tell us why, how and for whom you do what you do.

events.name: Founder Pitch Clinic
events.description: Join us in NYC for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you're preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, this session will give you practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering both sides of a great pitch: how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down30-minute interactive workshop with Dave Wolovsky (Coach & StartX mentor) Building a company, raising capital, & leading at a high level all require founders to manage stress under pressure. But performing at your best doesn't necessarily mean trying to calm yourself down. In this interactive session, Cognitive Performance Coach Dave Wolovsky will show you how to compose yourself when pitching & presenting. Through practical exercises, you'll learn techniques to pitch with greater presence, work with pressure rather than against it, & operate more effectively in high-stakes moments. About Dave WolovskyDave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders to maintain focus in high-pressure moments & establish better habits for managing their daily energy. Learn more at effortwise.com/founders. He also serves as a mentor in the StartX accelerator program. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors30-minute workshop with Anthony Rose What makes investors lean in? Anthony will break down the art of delivering a compelling founder pitch-from communicating your vision & opportunity to presenting your business in a way that resonates with potential investors. Expect practical insights from someone who has worked with thousands of startups navigating fundraising & investment. About Anthony RoseAnthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle their legal needs, used by more than 50,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, Anthony's career spanned 3D graphics, P2P music, internet video, & social TV, including leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can put to work in your very next pitch.

events.name: Agentic Loops Demo Day
events.description: Agents that keep working while you sleep Join AI Tinkerers NYC for a themed demo night on agentic loops: agents that plan, build, verify, & retry without a human in the loop. Not chat wrappers. Systems that run for hours & hand you a result in the morning. Keynote by Conveo engineer Vincent Vankrunkelsven, author of Nightwatch: how to get your agents to keep working while you sleep. Then a full lineup of community demos on the same theme. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of live demos, real PRs, real failures, & a room full of people building the same thing. Keynote: Nightwatch, reviewed liveConveo runs a skill called /nightwatch. An engineer plans a feature in the afternoon, a fleet of agents builds it overnight on a remote box, & one reviewed PR is waiting at breakfast. Every layer is a loop: each worker builds, verifies with a script it can run itself, pushes, & drives its PR until the review agents approve. The orchestrator wakes every 15 minutes, checks progress, & replaces anything that died. The whole thing loops again the next day, with the night's logs feeding the next version of the skill. For this event, Conveo will kick off a real Nightwatch run the afternoon of October 21, then do the morning review live on stage. You'll see what the fleet actually built overnight: the master PR, the generated test plan, the screenshots, & whatever broke. A recorded run is on standby in case the demo gods disagree. What you'll take away: The four capabilities you need to run your own overnight loop: a spawner, a durable message bus, validation agents, & a way to wake a running agentHow to write tickets with a closed verification loop so workers converge instead of driftingThe failure modes that each cost Vincent a night, & the fixesHow the agent mesh keeps messages from getting lost when a laptop closesSpeaker: Vincent Vankrunkelsven, Senior Engineer, Conveo. Joined by Dieter (CEO) & Maarten Claes (CTO). What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise.

events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild - Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: The Human Edge - Founders Cacao Salon
events.description: The Human Edge: A Founders Salon for the Age of AIBreakfast  Cacao  Capital  Curated Connection AI is making it easier than ever to build. But trust, conviction, introductions, & the relationships that actually move companies forward are still deeply human. The Human Edge brings together an intimate group of founders, investors, & operators for a morning in Tribeca designed around useful insight & meaningful connection. The morning is structured so the right conversations have time to actually go somewhere. What you'll walk away withA current read on fundraising & what investors are paying attention to, fresh from San Francisco Tech Week A practical perspective on leading teams & building companies as AI changes how we work Three or four people you'll genuinely want to reconnect with A focused, energizing start to your day The morning9:45 AM  Doors openBreakfast & arrival 10:00 AM  Welcome 10:15 AM  Cacao openingA short guided ritual with Sasha Sakhar to arrive, settle in, & set an intention for the morning. 10:45 AM  What investors are seeing nowTanya Montman shares observations from San Francisco Tech Week: where capital is moving, what investors are asking founders, & how AI is changing the fundraising landscape. 11:00 AM  The human side of building with AIGeoff Scott on building companies, teams, & products where AI amplifies people rather than replaces human leadership. 11:15 AM  Open conversation & Q&A 11:30 AM  Curated connection roundsGuided small-group conversations matched around stage, interests, & goals so the conversation gets past the usual networking script. 11:50 AM  Closing + open networking 12:00 PM  Close In the room Tanya Montman  VC & fundraising advisor. After a decade at J.P. Morgan across leveraged finance & M&A, Tanya founded StartLinkVentures to connect founders with capital & advises companies across New York, Boston, & Silicon Valley.  Geoff Scott  CTO, founder, & advisor. Board member at SIM New York Metro & creator of KindnessFlywheel.org, focused on human-centered leadership in the age of AI.  Sasha Sakhar  Founder of SUGARHAUS, an NYC experiential studio reimagining how people gather. For seven years, Sasha has facilitated cacao rituals, connection experiences, & curated gatherings for founders, teams, & creatives. Why cacao?Ceremonial cacao creates a simple transition from doing to being present. Its naturally occurring theobromine offers a gentler, steadier lift than coffee, while the ritual gives us something rare in founder culture: a moment to arrive before the titles, pitches, & ideas begin. You don't need to know anything about cacao. events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: Can Your Agents Actually Ship?
events.description: Can your agents actually ship?Compose your AI-native SDLCYour AI agents can't be trusted with data they can't find, can't understand, & aren't sure they're allowed to touch. And even when they get it right, the code they write still stalls in a delivery pipeline built for human speed. On Nov2 we will tackle both: first the data foundations agents need to trust, then the SDLC they need to ship through. Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust The evening opens with Grzegorz Krl on the data foundations AI agents need to find, understand & safely access your data. We've run this talk at Boston & San Francisco Tech Week, & both times it ran long because nobody wanted to stop asking questions. Full session details: https://luma.com/il0xoz9a Main session: Can your agents actually ship? AI can write code. Getting that code to production is another matter. Most engineering organizations hit the same wall: the bottleneck isn't the agent, it's everything downstream of it. Pipelines, CI, reviews, security gates, release processes: all of it was built for human speed, not AI. Visdom, built by VirtusLab, is the missing layer between AI coding & production. It lets you compose an AI-native SDLC, piece by piece: the context, validation, governance & orchestration agents need to ship safely & at scale. Come see what that looks like in practice. We'll cover: Why AI adoption stalls after the first wave of excitement What infrastructure an AI-native SDLC actually requires How Visdom connects agents to your SDLC, component by component Live demos of AI agents shipping production-ready code Q&A with the Visdom team Evaluating AI coding assistants or already rolling them out across teams? This session is about what happens after the code is written.  What you'll see liveA hands-on walkthrough of how Visdom removes friction across context, execution, & validation, turning your SDLC into a system AI agents can reliably operate on: Deep repository scanning that builds the semantic context AI agents actually need: not just open files, but the full dependency & intent graph across your codebase Blast radius scoring on an AI-generated PR before it touches CI, catching what code review misses when your team merges 3x more than last quarter Governed sandbox execution with full audit trails: the missing layer between the AI suggested it & it's running in production A live maturity assessment on a real delivery pipeline: where it stands today, & the smallest concrete step that unlocks the next level Who should join?CTOs, CDOs, VPs of Engineering & Data, Heads of Platform & AI, & senior engineers responsible for developer productivity, data platforms & AI adoption strategy. Especially if your AI tools shine in demos but stall in your CI/CD pipeline, or your agents can't tell which table is the right one. Why it's worth your time Get a practical diagnostic for making your data usable by AI agents See what an AI-native SDLC looks like in practice (live demo) Learn how to assess your AI maturity, step by step Learn how to start small, validate quickly, & evolve without big upfront risk Agenda6:00 PM - Doors open, drinks & networking6:30 PM - Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust (incl. Q&A)7:00 PM - Panel: real stories from AI adoption7:45 PM - Live demo: Visdom8:15 - 9:00 PM - Q&A & networking SpeakersPractitioners working hands-on with AI-driven delivery, data platforms, developer tooling, & real-world implementation: Grzegorz Krl, Tech Lead & Data Architect at VirtusLabGrzegorz believes that solid data systems start with a deep understanding of what the business actually needs. He works closely with organizations to put their business domains at the center of every data initiative, so that architectures, models & pipelines reflect how the business really operates. Artur Skowroski, Head of Application Development at VirtusLabArtur has spent more than ten years in the industry, on everything from greenfield builds to systems older than he is. He has worked as a Software Engineer, Tech Lead, Architect & Technical Product Manager, which gives him a broad view of the problems he tackles. He still likes to stay hands-on & has been writing a weekly roundup of the JVM ecosystem at jvm-weekly.com for over two years. Hosted by VirtusLabWe work with organizations ranging from global brands (including top-tier investment banks, Databricks, Airbnb, & DHL) to fast-growing startups, helping them build data platforms & AI systems that actually scale. At our core, we're engineers working with engineers, & we actively support the community through meetups, events, & shared learning. If you're working on AI in software delivery, this is where it starts to actually work.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Fandom, Cities & Psychology Of Collective Emotion
events.description: Fandom, Cities, & the Psychology of Collective Emotion Why do sports fans feel so deeply connected to teams, cities, & even complete strangers? This talk explores the science of fandom & the social psychology that transforms spectators into communities. Drawing on research in social identity, belonging, collective emotion, & fan behavior, this talk examines how rituals, rivalries, & shared experiences turn they into we. From a Knicks championship transforming the emotional temperature of New York City to the 2026 FIFA World Cup activating cities around the globe, the talk considers how sport mega-events create collective identity-and whether fandom functions as social infrastructure in an increasingly disconnected world. SpeakerGina Antoniello, Clinical Assistant Professor & Director, Women's Sport Collective, NYU SPS Preston Robert Tisch Institute for Global Sport; Faculty Athletics Representative, NYU

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Solution Smithing - How To Raise & Give A Million Dollars
events.description: Join Anew & pop-up foundation The Haven Fund on October 20th for a brainstorming discussion on an urgent need: how to deploy resources efficiently & quickly towards the most pressing issues of our time. The Haven Fund, part of Anew's Fall 2025 cohort of Entrepreneurs in Residence, was born out of a desire to tackle an urgent problem - the immigration crackdown in NYC - by directing capital quickly to those organizations on the ground with the deepest knowledge of the issue. Since Lisa Cowan started this endeavor at the beginning of this year, it has distributed almost $1 million in funds to organizations throughout New York City, no strings attached. In an era of rolling, overlapping crises, we want to ask the audience & panelists, is this model replicable? If so, what would it take to create a template that anyone can use to tackle issues in their community & in different places? Join us as we together explore why this model was a success & how might The Haven Fund scale this model to address additional urgent issues. Panelists include: Iara Peng, Founder & CEO, JustFund, Emily Shechtman, Founder & Director, South Brooklyn Sanctuary, & Jennifer Ching, Executive Director, North Star Fund Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts. The Haven Fund is a pop-up foundation that is raising $1 million in 1 year to support neighborhood-level immigration organizations in New York City. Lisa Cowan is the founder & Director of the Haven Fund. Formerly the Vice President of the Robert Sterling Clark Foundation, she is an organizer, weaver, writer & New Yorker.

events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: TransportationCamp 2026
events.description: Join us on Saturday, October 24, for TransportationCamp NYC 2026! TransportationCamp NYC will be held on Saturday, October 24 at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering in Downtown Brooklyn. Join us to discuss all things transportation & connect with professionals, students, & enthusiasts alike! TransportationCamp is an unconference - every session is planned, proposed, & led by attendees like you. It's the perfect opportunity to share your transportation passion with a diverse gathering of individuals from our multidisciplinary industry. TransportationCamp welcomes all attendees, whether you're a planner, software developer, engineer, student, transportation professional, community member, policymaker, or just excited about mobility! Register here to join us for a fun day of transportation learning & networking on October 24! Interested in sponsoring?We are seeking sponsorship from engineering firms, research centers, planning organizations, & more to make TCNYC26 extra special! To learn about sponsorship packages, contact TCampNYC@gmail.com. Put your organization's name in front of the people who are working on the latest & greatest at the intersection of transportation & technology. Student ScholarshipApplications are now open for our student scholarship! TransportationCamp NYC will award one $500 scholarship this year thanks to the support of VHB! All undergraduate students, as well as full-time master's degree students, are eligible to apply. The deadline for scholarship applications is Sunday, October 18, at 11:59pm ET! Presenting?Thinking about presenting at a session? Sessions may come in a variety of formats: informal discussions, birds-of-a-feather, lightning talks, presentations, & others. If you have an idea for a session, feel free to write it down in advance & bring it with you to the event. First time at a TransportationCamp?How To TransportationCamp: Review the TransportationCamp 101 guide that explains all aspects of the event.Participation Encouraged: Sessions are formed as the day goes on, so be sure to come with topics for discussion. events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches.
