events.name: Creativity Is Dead, Long Live Creativity - Gen AI & Meaning Of Art
events.description: The concept of creativity has a surprisingly short history. While ancient philosophers expounded on imagination & free will, theorizations of creativity as a distinct trait only date to the past hundred years. GenAI suggests that creativity is not unique to humans or even conscious organisms, but is reducible to mere calculation & programming. Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 5:30PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:00PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.  ------------------ABOUT COHORTCohort is a space & home for ideas, & the people who think about them, create new ones, & build things from them. Many of us are founders, builders, artists, researchers, & their supporters here in NYC. Our goal is to turn the city into a campus after college. We hold idea & discussion events, coworking events for support & accountability for those building & creating things, & pure social events to build genuine relationships & community. Subscribe, browse our calendar, & join us for our next events!  Photography Notice We may take photos & video at our events to share on social media & our website. We use it to spread the word & help more people find this community. By attending, you're giving us permission to use those photos & videos in anything related to Cohort's promotion & outreach. If you'd rather not be photographed, just let us know when you arrive & we'll make sure you're not included. More from Cohort Monday Oct 19 Wednesday Oct 14 Dating the Dead Oct 15 Halloween crawl Oct 31 Calendar

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: [Legal Engineers] What Do Clients Want - Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

Meet Founders, Investors, & Talent - Build or Scale Your Startup  Bring a business question to the room Meet founders, entrepreneurs, builders, operators & investors at Ascent Valley's NYC mixer. Talk through business decisions & meet people you could work with. Locals & visitors are equally welcome. Bring a question about finding customers, building your team or growing your business. When you find a reason to stay in touch, you can continue the conversation through Ascent Valley after the evening. What to Expect Product & growth: discuss finding customers, product decisions & growing a business. Talent & hiring: meet builders & operators, talk about team needs & explore working together. Fundraising: share what you've learned about preparing a pitch & raising capital. Company pitches: discover what other companies are building & ask their representatives questions. Want to Pitch? Present your company to the room & walk guests through your pitch deck, followed by a short Q&A. events.name: Future Of AI Infrastructure
events.description: Let's talk about what's coming in the world of AI infra. Anthony Erondu is a Principal Consultant focused on AI infrastructure, GPU compute & Physical AI. He partners with high growth companies across the space to build product & engineering teams, placing talent from VP level leaders through senior ICs across some of the most critical areas of the AI stack. Akaanksha Sinha is an award-winning trailblazer in AI, cybersecurity & governance architecture. Over a decade in the enterprise stack. She founded AKAVAM, a governance-through-architecture company for enterprise AI. Its platform, AEVO, combines infrastructure as code, policy as code & compliance as code into deterministic execution, turning organizational context into operating capability. Ex-IBM, Deloitte, CUNY Srinivas Venkatanarayanan is a Senior Systems Research Engineer in Nvidia, Working in Cosmos Search. He works in Autonomous Vehicle & Robotics domain. Joshua Ness is a Senior AI Advisor & Consultant based in New York City. He currently advises PE-backed global technology firms on AI implemention & organizational structure, including tech infrastructure modernization & regulatory compliance. Joshua holds a Fulbright Specialist appointment through which he works with the government of the Philippines on national AI readiness programs. He holds certifications from AWS, IBM, & IEEE in applied AI & cloud infrastructure.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: The Quantified Self: What AI Can Actually Tell You About Your Data
events.description: This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT. Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data. He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots. His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model. When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it. Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims. Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it. Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret. AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades. Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer. Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product. BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks 7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf 8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book Signing And don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.description: IT IS BACK! CALLING ALL FOUNDERS! Hosted by Plug & Play NYC & Pioneering Minds AI Apply to pitch here:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOGgbEqUmtEHmKrhqpzynRzYX4Lk4EUC8qrYvSt6YZhXrGvg Pitching is one of the most important skills a founder develops, yet it's rarely practiced in a setting where you can iterate in real time. In this interactive workshop, founders will present their pitch, receive direct feedback, & immediately refine it live. events.name: Wind-Win Startup Showdown
events.description: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables:  An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. This is a special year for us: the program set a record high: 118 applications & the strongest competition reviewers have seen to date. In 2026, we also drew in a more diverse cohort than ever before by broadening this year's technology scope  a 123% increase in application numbers compared to last year's, reflecting the parallel growth in industry demand for novel solutions needed in the market.Presented by the Offshore Wind Innovation Hub, this networking & pitch event brings together stakeholders across the climate landscapeinvestors, founders, academia, industry, & thought leadersfor an evening of connection, collaboration, & celebration.Come see it for yourself! Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage:  Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - Platform for smarter customs workflows for offshore wind components.TMA The Hazardous Goods Companion (Germany) - RFID & AIoT inventory visibility & predictive inventory management solution.Tree Composites (The Netherlands) - Composite joints for offshore support structure to realise material & manufacturing optimization.Vital Ocean (Oregon, US) - Intelligence platform combining ocean data, marine environment, & decision interface.Stay tuned in the next few weeks on our website & LinkedIn for updates on our selected cohort!Innovation in FocusOur 2026 cohort takes the stage to pitch ocean & maritimes most promising technologies. This year's lineup features innovations spanning ports, O&M, environmental monitoring & coexistence, workforce development, installation, construction, & commissioning, maritime applications, among others. The scope doesn't just stop there. The majority of this year's solutions are dual-use, carrying relevance across adjacent industries & global markets, a reflection of just how far the blue economy reaches.Marking the official launch of the 2026 Innovator program, this event offers a unique chance to connect directly with the founders behind these ready-to-scale solutions. Explore their real-world impact, uncover new business opportunities, & spark the kind of strategic partnerships that move ideas forward.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator ProgramA world-class program open to global offshore wind innovators. Building on three successful cohorts, this eight-month intensive program provides unparalleled support for innovators looking to develop novel technology & advance commercialization in New York & beyond.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub is an initiative led by Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering & the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium (NOWRDC) in collaboration with the New York State Research & Development Authority (NYSERDA) & New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC).The Innovator program is also supported by industry partners Equinor, rsted, & Vestas.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: Code & Coffee Hackathon
events.description: Everyone's a builder here: coders, PMs, designers, & the just-curious.Get ready to build something real for Newark! We're taking over Rutgers iHub for a full-day hackathon focused on solving problems that actually matter to the people who call this city home, from water safety to food access to just making city government easier to navigate.Theme:Description:This hackathon challenges participants to pick a real issue facing Newark & build something that actually helps: a tool, an assistant, a dashboard, whatever gets the job done. Teams can dig into problem areas like environmental & water justice, food access, cost of living, or civic transparency, or bring their own idea if they see a sharper angle. Expect AI to play a role in your build, but what we're really looking for is a solution that works. Judging will weigh usefulness & execution as heavily as technical approach.Technical Scope:Participants can use any technical stack they prefer (code-based, no-code, or a mix)Projects must be built from scratch during the hackathon, no prebuilt solutionsTeams are free to choose one of our suggested problem areas or pitch their own. We'll share a few starting points at kickoff, but the direction is yoursJudging Criteria:Relevance & Impact: Does this solve a real, specific problem for Newark residents, & could someone actually use it?Execution: How complete & functional is the prototype, given the short build window?Thoughtful AI Use: How & why did you use AI? A simple, well-executed approach counts; bonus points for teams who push further with multi-step reasoning or tool use where it genuinely fits the problem.Usability & Creativity: Would a non-technical resident actually get it? Does the approach show real originality?Pitch & Clarity: Can you clearly explain the problem, the solution, & who it's for in your demo?Agenda:10:00  10:30 AM | Check-in & NetworkingRegistration, coffee/light breakfast, casual networking10:30  11:00 AM | Welcome & Opening RemarksTheme & judging criteria overview11:00  11:30 AM | Team Formation & Idea PitchesParticipants pitch project ideas, team matchmaking session11:30 AM  4:00 PM | Hacking SessionTeams build prototypes, mentors available for tech & business guidance, lunch break at 1:00 PM4:00  5:00 PM | Project Demos & Pitches35 minute demos from each team, judged by partners & industry reps5:00  5:30 PM | Awards & Closing RemarksWinners announced, closing remarks5:30  6:00 PM | Networking & Wrap-UpInformal mingling with participants, judges, & partners

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: Ugly Talks: Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: [Legal Engineers] What Do Clients Want - Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.

events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

His experience also includes precision oncology, biotechnology, ConcertAI, & McKinsey.Gary Burnett | Healthcare + Transformation ExecutiveGary works at the intersection of healthcare innovation, organizational transformation, talent strategy, & community impact. Come ready to connect. Come ready to find your next opportunity.Disclaimer: By attending The Rise Circle, you consent to being photographed and/or recorded during the event.
