events.name: AI For Operators
events.description: AI for Forward-thinking OperatorsA 2-hour hands-on workshop for execs, VPs, operators, fractional leaders, & founders.You're further along in your career than you are in AI - & you're tired of nodding along while colleagues & vendors pitch magic & your team runs experiments you can't evaluate.This isn't a talk. It's a working session. Bring your laptop. In two hours you'll set up Claude Code, Muse, or Hark - connect them to the tools & services you actually live in, & produce something real. Something that'll solve an actual problem you tackle, or something that'll help your work.Past execs have left with having created things like:dynamic competitive research & action toolsomething that runs analysis on their products & sales & automatically finds room for offloading inventory, dynamic promos, & actionable customer segmentshelps them hold their vendors & teams accountable automatically using briefs, followups, real-time measurementcloses their monthly books accuratelyautomates sales research & outreach relevant to them, not boilerplateautomates HR paperwork relevant to them, not boilerplateSmall by design: 3-5 seats, hands-on help throughout. We build alongside you & troubleshoot in real time, so you walk out ready to run this inside your company, immediately.About the host: Deepak DevjaniSomewhere along the way I started training my own team on AI, just so we could ship faster. And the coaching thing kind of fell in my lap. Turns out I love it.Then execs started coming to me. They wanted the same thing for themselves. Then other founders. For the last couple years I've been training execs & their C-suite teams, & honestly the change is night & day. They have more time. They get way more done.One thing I learned fast: for this to actually work, it has to be as close to personal & private as possible  essentially 1:1. That's the whole reason this class is small. You can literally know nothing walking in & you'll be OK; that's by design. And what you leave with isn't just a tool you built  it's the confidence to walk into work & actually use this.So that's what Reliable Bits is now. We still go into companies & implement AI for real. But a big part of what we do is coach the people doing the actual work. Operators, execs, VPs.

events.name: Peptide Freedom vs Proof First
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & is building infrastructure for the peptide space, from education to real-world outcome data. He argues that the answer to uncertain evidence is more transparency & better data, not keeping adults from making their own choices Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Creative Showcase
events.description: A chance for creatives to show off what they've been working on or be inspired by others in a series of quickfire 20-slide presentations.This is an opportunity to share a creative project that you have been working on with the Index Community in the form of a Pecha Kucha-a rapid presentation style where each person presents 20 slides, for 20 seconds each. This fast pace encourages storytellers to be concise, creative, & to the point-perfect for keeping the audience's attention. Whether you are presenting or just attending, this is an open forum, a space to gather & share, a place to mingle with other NYC creatives. Come be inspired or present what you've been working on. Interested in sharing your work? Applications for this event are now closed, but we hope you'll come see our amazing presenters & submit your project for consideration next time! Clipart Studio by Sami Smith Clipart Studio is a website where visitors can take magazines from the Internet Archive & make collages from them by "cutting" them out & arranging the pieces, or uploading their own materials to work with. There's also a gallery where you can see the thousands of wonderful user-submitted collages made with the program. Palestine Skating Game A videogame in development that centers Arabic electronic music, graffiti, & Splatoon-style paint shooting. The game team employs coders in Gaza & the West Bank. Brooklyn Design Archive by Gerardo Torres Davila Acultural project advancing the understanding of important pieces from the fields of furniture & industrial design. Ball-Jointed Doll Making by Tatyana Deslandes Mustakos Tatyana delves into both the theoretical & technical sides of her doll making practice & how it's evolved over the years. Urban Fossil by Suyeon Kim Urban Fossil is an immersive exhibition that transforms street debris into a typographic system & visceral data visualization. It translates ephemeral waste into a functional alphabet across an interactive website, a printed zine, & a gallery installation. Katie Ehrlich is a Brooklyn-based graphic designer, photographer, & founder of StudioKat. Her clients have ranged from brands like Google, American Express, & TikTok to publications for Stanford, the Smithsonian, & Cultured Magazine. Her work has been recognized by Communication Arts, Black + White Photography, & the CASE Awards.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.description: Explore cool spots, meet makers, & dive into history at the Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House! The Brooklyn Navy Yard's Annual Open House Discover the Yard's 300-acre innovative campus during our Annual Open House, part of Open House New York Weekend. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, & technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access & immersive activations. This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. This includes active construction areas.If buildings & businesses are open, please be respectful while in their spaces & remain mindful that these are working studios & manufacturing centers.Participating businesses may choose to close their spaces at their discretion, including if they determine that visitors are being disruptive.The Brooklyn Navy Yard is an active manufacturing & industrial campus. Visitors are expected to walk on sidewalks where possible & to be mindful of road traffic.To ensure proper pedestrian movement, do not congregate in ways that block entrances, exits, roadways, or parking lots during your visit.Visitors are prohibited from causing damage to Brooklyn Navy Yard property or causing disruptions to other visitors, business owners or workers, & volunteers & staff working at the event. Photo Acknowledgement & Permissions By registering for the event, you understand that photography and/or video may be taken at the event for marketing or promotional purposes & you consent to being filmed or photographed for such use. Furthermore, you release the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, its officers, employees, & agents, from any liability in connection with such photography or videography & the use thereof, & waive any claims you may have for payment in connection with such materials & the use thereof.  Newsletter Acknowledgement & Permission By signing up for this event, you are agreeing to be added to the free Brooklyn Navy Yard public newsletter list. Newsletters are sent 1 - 2 times each month & list public programs, events, & exhibitions at the Yard. You may unsubscribe at any time.

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup  x NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome the 3rd Annual ATLAS Next Program, a special Startup Showcase organized in partnership with ATLAS & its local Landing Pad, the Transatlantic Innovation Hub. Get ready to connect with the next wave of Italian innovation! We're bringing together the NYC Tech Community & a new, selected group of Italian founders building ambitious projects for the future. This year's event highlights the active role of Transatlantic Innovation Hub, a thriving operational center located right here in New York, dedicated to scaling Italian & European startups. Why Attend? Mingle with innovators: network with founders, tech leaders, & ecosystem builders. Discover ground-breaking technologies: get early access to disruptive European & transatlantic solutions. Invest in tomorrow's leaders: evaluate high-potential projects & back the startups you like best. Enjoy Italian focaccia & piadina from PIADI, paired with Mionetto Prosecco. Salute!  Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it! Agenda 6:00 PM - Doors Open & Networking with Italian Aperitivo6:30 PM - Welcome & Startup Demos8:00 PM - Community Ask/Offer8:15 PM - After Party & Networking Demo Lineup AstraTab - A revenue management & premium-access platform for the world's most in-demand venues. Astradyne - High-power satellite platforms designed for orbital computing. Dear.io - An AI-powered personal reflection platform that applies dialogical science to support meaningful interactions & individual well-being. ForLead - A sales intelligence platform that helps companies identify the right prospects at the moment they are most ready to buy. IdolMatch - A platform connecting athletes & brands to create new opportunities for sponsorships, marketing, & monetization. Jyamma GAMES - Crafting fun, culturally-rich gaming experiences that bring Italian folklore literature to life. Math Biology - A non-invasive technology platform supporting prevention, performance, & lifelong well-being. Nadit - A matching platform that connects students with the right academic programs & universities with the right prospective students. Prometheus Plasma Systems - Advanced plasma technologies designed to help turn nuclear fusion into a commercially viable energy source. SKNR - AI-powered skin & scalp pre-screening from a single photo, connecting users with a dermatologist, clinic, or pharmacy the same day. TeamKeys - An AI-native basketball intelligence platform that transforms performance data into actionable insights for scouting, recruitment, & match analysis. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS & Transatlantic Innovation Hub ATLAS & its US Hub form a flagship ecosystem dedicated to internationalizing European startups. Headquartered in Rome & rooted in New York City, at 417 5th Ave, the organization delivers hands-on strategic support, market access, & tailored education to help founders establish & grow their presence in the US market.

events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: [Legal Engineers] What Do Clients Want - Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House
events.description: Explore cool spots, meet makers, & dive into history at the Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House! The Brooklyn Navy Yard's Annual Open House Discover the Yard's 300-acre innovative campus during our Annual Open House, part of Open House New York Weekend. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, & technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access & immersive activations. This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. This includes active construction areas.If buildings & businesses are open, please be respectful while in their spaces & remain mindful that these are working studios & manufacturing centers.Participating businesses may choose to close their spaces at their discretion, including if they determine that visitors are being disruptive.The Brooklyn Navy Yard is an active manufacturing & industrial campus. events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

His experience spans founding companies, leading engineering teams, & scaling global products. Nate HinmanNate Hinman is Senior Director at Plug & Play Tech Center. As the largest coworking space in FiDi, we combine premium private offices, shared workspaces, & an exclusive Lounge with top-tier amenities & exceptional service, creating the ultimate environment for your business to thrive. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

He partners with high growth companies across the space to build product & engineering teams, placing talent from VP level leaders through senior ICs across some of the most critical areas of the AI stack. Akaanksha Sinha is an award-winning trailblazer in AI, cybersecurity & governance architecture. Over a decade in the enterprise stack. She founded AKAVAM, a governance-through-architecture company for enterprise AI. Its platform, AEVO, combines infrastructure as code, policy as code & compliance as code into deterministic execution, turning organizational context into operating capability. Ex-IBM, Deloitte, CUNY Srinivas Venkatanarayanan is a Senior Systems Research Engineer in Nvidia, Working in Cosmos Search. He specializes in multimodal reasoning, search & Curation for Post-training Vision Language Action Models. He works in Autonomous Vehicle & Robotics domain. Joshua Ness is a Senior AI Advisor & Consultant based in New York City. He spent 6 years at Verizon 5G Labs where he advised on enterprise adoption of 5G & edge computing technologies for clients, including the NFL, Disney, & MasterCard. He currently advises PE-backed global technology firms on AI implemention & organizational structure, including tech infrastructure modernization & regulatory compliance. Joshua holds a Fulbright Specialist appointment through which he works with the government of the Philippines on national AI readiness programs. He holds certifications from AWS, IBM, & IEEE in applied AI & cloud infrastructure.

events.name: Nexus Meetup
events.description: A casual, pay-your-own-way networking event designed for professionals to connect, share ideas, & build lasting relationships across the broader business & technology ecosystem. Meet fellow professionals, expand your network, & enjoy a relaxed evening together. Food & beverages are available for individual purchase. Who Attends: Founders & startups PR & Agency teams Venture Capitalists Consultants Finance professionals Content & social media marketers Marketing technology professionals Attendance is limited to help keep conversations meaningful, so please apply for a spot. We look forward to meeting you! About Our Meet Ups: Our Meet Ups are relaxed, industry-agnostic gatherings built for professionals who want to unplug from the standard corporate routine & connect on a human level. Whether you are looking to exchange fresh perspectives, brainstorm new concepts, or simply meet peers navigating similar spaces, this environment is designed for open-ended conversation & organic relationship-building. What It Is: An open, welcoming community space to meet new connections. An opportunity to exchange industry perspectives & uncover unexpected collaborations. A low-pressure, welcoming atmosphere with no formal agenda or mandatory pitches. What It Isn't: RTM Nexus Meet Up is not a curated buyer/seller event & is not structured around guaranteed access to a specific target audience, vertical, company type, or decision-maker profile (ICP). Looking for something more targeted? If you need to connect with a specific niche-such as retail, fashion, beauty, CPG, or enterprise brand leaders-check out our "Retail Leaders Receptions" & "Nexus Mixers" instead. Those events are intentionally curated & sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series A+)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders. Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC) August was our pilot. Here's how it performed. Our intent 20 founders, 6 investors. The real turnout: 30 guests: 20 founders, 10 capital allocators $70M+ raised collectively by the founders present $3.5M average raised per founder $2.3B+ combined AUM across the investors $1M average check, $100K minimum $10M+ in live check capacity This is today objective: Every founder in the room is doing $1M+ in ARR or has raised a round of $1M or more. Raised your 1st round, onto your 2nd, or bootstrapped to $1M ARR? You're in the right place. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.
