events.name: Creativity Is Dead, Long Live Creativity - Gen AI & Meaning Of Art
events.description: The concept of creativity has a surprisingly short history. While ancient philosophers expounded on imagination & free will, theorizations of creativity as a distinct trait only date to the past hundred years. GenAI suggests that creativity is not unique to humans or even conscious organisms, but is reducible to mere calculation & programming. Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 5:30PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:00PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.  ------------------ABOUT COHORTCohort is a space & home for ideas, & the people who think about them, create new ones, & build things from them. Many of us are founders, builders, artists, researchers, & their supporters here in NYC. Our goal is to turn the city into a campus after college. We hold idea & discussion events, coworking events for support & accountability for those building & creating things, & pure social events to build genuine relationships & community. Subscribe, browse our calendar, & join us for our next events!  Photography Notice We may take photos & video at our events to share on social media & our website. We use it to spread the word & help more people find this community. By attending, you're giving us permission to use those photos & videos in anything related to Cohort's promotion & outreach. If you'd rather not be photographed, just let us know when you arrive & we'll make sure you're not included. More from Cohort Monday Oct 19 Wednesday Oct 14 Dating the Dead Oct 15 Halloween crawl Oct 31 Calendar

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: Robot Hackathon - Code That Moves
events.description: Build physical AI applications with real robot arms @ Viam! About the Event We're excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm & support from Viam experts throughout. No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI & some software experience. See what engineers built at the last hackathon here. Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis. What You'll Build Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam & a real robot arm. Each team will have access to: UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101) Linux compute machine RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm) Webcams A free Viam account We'll provide a variety of objects for your robot to manipulate. You are encouraged to bring anything required for the project you have in mind. Please bring your own laptop. In your application, please summarize what project you have in mind. Ideas from past events: training a VLA, playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, manipulating a robot arm using computer vision & hand gestures. Prizes We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. Each member of a winning team will take home SO-101 pre-assembled robot kits, including: a leader arm, a follower arm, & a camera + Viam credits. Gold: SO-101 arm + $5,000 in Viam credits Silver: SO-101 arm+ $2,500 in Viam credits Bronze: SO-101 arm + $1,000 in Viam credits Please bring your own laptop. We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even if you only go through the first lessons, it will help you get the hang of things quickly. Schedule Friday, October 169:00 AM: Check-in & breakfast9:30 AM: Kickoff: Welcome & crash course on building with Viam10:00 AM: Teams & hardware10:30 AM: Hacking begins1:00 PM: Lunch6:00 PM: Dinner9:00 PM: Hard close: Robots power down, doors close (no overnight hacking) Saturday, October 179:00 AM: Doors open, breakfast9:30 AM: Hacking resumes12:30 PM: Lunch3:30 PM: Demos & drinks5:00 PM: Awards6:00 PM: Event concludes What Skills You Need No robotics experience required, but you should be comfortable with: Coding: Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C++ Linux: Using SSH & running basic terminal commands JSON: Reading & editing configuration files Git: Basic workflows so your team can build together Bonus: knowing how to plug in a pre-trained vision model (like YOLO or OpenCV) to help the robot see & identify objects (not required) Before the Event We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even the first few lessons will help you get the hang of things quickly. How to Join Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis. We'll select a curated group of ambitious software developers & send official confirmations to accepted participants. Attendees must be approved in advance to participate. Presented By Viam - The robotics software platform we'll use to configure, control, & deploy models to your robot. Viam makes it easy to get a robot up & running quickly.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. events.name: Peptide Freedom vs Proof First
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & is building infrastructure for the peptide space, from education to real-world outcome data. He argues that the answer to uncertain evidence is more transparency & better data, not keeping adults from making their own choices Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & is building infrastructure for the peptide space, from education to real-world outcome data. He argues that the answer to uncertain evidence is more transparency & better data, not keeping adults from making their own choices Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.description: Event DescriptionSkip the resume pile. Get Hired Hack is a one-day, in-person hackathon at Columbia Startup Lab where NYC's fastest-growing startups bring real problems from their roadmaps, & you show them what working with you looks like. Founders who are hiring will be in the room, watching you build. events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

In this session, Anthony & Anna will work directly with founders in a live pitch lab, helping them sharpen their narrative & strengthen how they present their ideas. Come have a sales pitch, demo pitch, or even a VC pitch! Anthony RoseAnthony Rose is a pioneering technology entrepreneur best known as the co-creator & former CTO of the BBC iPlayer, one of the world's first large-scale streaming platforms that fundamentally changed how millions consume television. He has spent decades building technology at the intersection of consumer platforms, developer ecosystems, & emerging tech. His experience spans founding companies, leading engineering teams, & scaling global products. Nate HinmanNate Hinman is Senior Director at Plug & Play Tech Center. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. As the largest coworking space in FiDi, we combine premium private offices, shared workspaces, & an exclusive Lounge with top-tier amenities & exceptional service, creating the ultimate environment for your business to thrive. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance professionals, founders, students, operators, & domain experts are strongly encouraged to join.Coaching & mentorship will be available onsite.What We'll ExploreAI agents & workflow automationHuman + AI collaborationProduct design in the age of AICritical thinking & human judgmentLegal AIFintech & insurtechRapid prototypingStartup product strategyVenture-style pitchingSchedule09:00  09:30 Check-in humans in the front seat.We help our AI pioneers understand AI deeply & turn it into real-world value.Our mission is straightforward:Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to rapidly turn ideas into working prototypes.Foster Collaboration: Bring together students, engineers, operators, domain experts, & founders to solve meaningful problems.Create Lasting Impact: events.name: Tech Meetup: International Edition
events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup  x NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome the 3rd Annual ATLAS Next Program, a special Startup Showcase organized in partnership with ATLAS & its local Landing Pad, the Transatlantic Innovation Hub. Get ready to connect with the next wave of Italian innovation! We're bringing together the NYC Tech Community & a new, selected group of Italian founders building ambitious projects for the future. This year's event highlights the active role of Transatlantic Innovation Hub, a thriving operational center located right here in New York, dedicated to scaling Italian & European startups. Why Attend? Mingle with innovators: network with founders, tech leaders, & ecosystem builders. Discover ground-breaking technologies: get early access to disruptive European & transatlantic solutions. Invest in tomorrow's leaders: evaluate high-potential projects & back the startups you like best. Enjoy Italian focaccia & piadina from PIADI, paired with Mionetto Prosecco. Salute!  Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it! Agenda 6:00 PM - Doors Open & Networking with Italian Aperitivo6:30 PM - Welcome & Startup Demos8:00 PM - Community Ask/Offer8:15 PM - After Party & Networking Demo Lineup AstraTab - A revenue management & premium-access platform for the world's most in-demand venues. Astradyne - High-power satellite platforms designed for orbital computing. Dear.io - An AI-powered personal reflection platform that applies dialogical science to support meaningful interactions & individual well-being. ForLead - A sales intelligence platform that helps companies identify the right prospects at the moment they are most ready to buy. IdolMatch - A platform connecting athletes & brands to create new opportunities for sponsorships, marketing, & monetization. Jyamma GAMES - Crafting fun, culturally-rich gaming experiences that bring Italian folklore literature to life. Math Biology - A non-invasive technology platform supporting prevention, performance, & lifelong well-being. Nadit - A matching platform that connects students with the right academic programs & universities with the right prospective students. Prometheus Plasma Systems - Advanced plasma technologies designed to help turn nuclear fusion into a commercially viable energy source. SKNR - AI-powered skin & scalp pre-screening from a single photo, connecting users with a dermatologist, clinic, or pharmacy the same day. TeamKeys - An AI-native basketball intelligence platform that transforms performance data into actionable insights for scouting, recruitment, & match analysis. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS & Transatlantic Innovation Hub ATLAS & its US Hub form a flagship ecosystem dedicated to internationalizing European startups. Headquartered in Rome & rooted in New York City, at 417 5th Ave, the organization delivers hands-on strategic support, market access, & tailored education to help founders establish & grow their presence in the US market.

events.description: Join us in NYC for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you're preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, this session will give you practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering both sides of a great pitch: how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down30-minute interactive workshop with Dave Wolovsky (Coach & StartX mentor) Building a company, raising capital, & leading at a high level all require founders to manage stress under pressure. But performing at your best doesn't necessarily mean trying to calm yourself down. In this interactive session, Cognitive Performance Coach Dave Wolovsky will show you how to compose yourself when pitching & presenting. Through practical exercises, you'll learn techniques to pitch with greater presence, work with pressure rather than against it, & operate more effectively in high-stakes moments. About Dave WolovskyDave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders to maintain focus in high-pressure moments & establish better habits for managing their daily energy. Learn more at effortwise.com/founders. He also serves as a mentor in the StartX accelerator program. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors30-minute workshop with Anthony Rose What makes investors lean in? Anthony will break down the art of delivering a compelling founder pitch-from communicating your vision & opportunity to presenting your business in a way that resonates with potential investors. Expect practical insights from someone who has worked with thousands of startups navigating fundraising & investment. About Anthony RoseAnthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle their legal needs, used by more than 50,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, Anthony's career spanned 3D graphics, P2P music, internet video, & social TV, including leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can put to work in your very next pitch.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael of the Pivot Point podcast is shooting photography, video, & follow-up interviews with select attendees. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. Join here Want to sponsor a room? One sponsor per event so it never feels crowded. Email stephen@propel.earth Media ConsentPhotography & Video Acknowledgement. By registering for & attending this event, you acknowledge that Propel Earth (the "Organizer") may record the session (including video, audio, & chat transcripts). You grant the Organizer a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, & distribute any such recordings or photographs for promotional, educational, or commercial purposes. You waive any right to inspect or approve the finished product & understand that no compensation will be provided for your appearance in these materials. Attendance at the event shall be deemed as conclusive evidence of your agreement to these terms. Connect with Me Join the Newsletter Join Propel as a Founder Join Propel as a Service Provider Follow Propel Earth Find me here Join the Propel Founder WhatsApp Event Co-Hosting & Sponsorship Partner With Propel Earth

events.name: Visions Summit
events.description: Commerce is cultural expression. It's in the things we make, the stories we tell, & the ways we live. VISIONS brings business leaders into conversation with designers, cultural thinkers, & technologists to expand their worldview & communicate a clearer vision for what comes next. On stage Featured voices include former U.S. Secretary of Commerce Carlos Gutierrez, designer & writer Elizabeth Goodspeed, & leaders from Etsy, MoMA Retail, Herms, Coach, Westfield Rise US, Hello Sunshine, & more. The program explores human creativity & AI, retail as cultural storytelling, craft & innovation, consumer behavior, wellness, & the changing media landscape. Every pass includes The full summit program of keynotes & conversations. Full-day MoMA admission, with hosted museum tours during the 1-3 PM lunch break. Access to the FC Bookshop & a book signing with Carlos Gutierrez, author of Sheer Will: Learning to Lead When There Is No Path. The VISIONS afterparty. One year of FC+, including access to event recordings after the summit. The VIP experience Everything in the Full-Day Pass, plus hosted lunches, VIP store tours, a salon dinner, & a guaranteed signed copy of Sheer Will. Additional signed copies are first come, first served. Store-tour routes & timing, plus salon dinner invitations & reservation details, will follow registration closer to the event. Afterparty venue & timing will also be shared with attendees. Early bird through September 25 Through September 25: Full-Day $549  VIP $999. From September 26: Full-Day $749  VIP $1,199. FC+ annual subscriber prices from September 26 are Full-Day $549 & VIP $999. Existing FC+ annual subscribers receive $200 off in both pricing periods. Through September 25: Full-Day $349  VIP $799. Select the FC+ Annual ticket & register using your membership email. Every attendee using this rate must have an eligible annual membership. Future Commerce verifies membership before approving these tickets; Luma places a payment hold until approval. Companies can register multiple attendees in one Luma checkout. Every summit attendee receives one year of FC+; activation details will follow registration. Plan your day The show begins promptly at 10 AM. Arrive early to allow for check-in & use the 53rd Street entrance at 11 West 53rd Street, New York. The summit takes place in MoMA's Roy & Niuta Titus Theater. We break for lunch from 1-3 PM, with hosted museum tours during the break. Hosted lunches are included for VIP guests. Food is otherwise not included, & food is not permitted inside the museum except in the caf. All attendees have access to the afterparty. We will not livestream the event. Recordings will be available to FC+ members afterward. VISIONS ticket refunds & transfers Full refunds are available until 30 days before the event. Tickets are not transferable. Use Contact the Host on this page for refund requests, attendance, accessibility, or dietary questions. Partner with VISIONS Explore the partnership deck. Presented by Future Commerce. With support from Klaviyo. *By registering, you are granting permission for your name & contact information to be shared with sponsors.

events.name: AI Founders Supper Club
events.description: Hi fellow founders  Angela & Hamza here from the AI Furnace. The AI Founders Supper Club is a private founders dinner club hosted by The AI Furnace (the largest community of AI startups in the world). Once a month, we host 15-20 early stage AI founders for a night of delicious food, discussions & connections with curated high quality founders in NYC. This is a referral based network, so feel free to apply here but the other way to get in is by being referred in by an existing founder member. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Meet dope founders building out of NYC Real conversations & place to vibe with other founders, solving similar problems ABOUT OUR HOSTS & SPONSORS The AI Furnace is NYC's largest & most active AI community. It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. Fidelity Private Shares brings certainty to startup founders with their cap table platform to help automate equity management operations & financings in a single collaborative hub. Leverage the scenario modeling tool & secure data room to prepare for the next round of funding. From inception to IPO, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Connect with Charlie Stephens for more information. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform designed to save businesses time & money. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.
