events.description: Ten companies. Twelve minutes each. An investor room in New York. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. Demo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run, 26,666 people on the guest list & 35+ investors in the room. This is that format, built for the companies coming out of our cohort & the investors who back them. Every attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation. Founders leave with investor conversations, investors leave with deal flow they did not have to source. The night 6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waiting7:00 Ten companies, twelve minutes each, pitch & questions8:15 Room favourite, voted live8:30 Open floor with the investors in the room9:00 Close Tickets General admission, free. Open to founders, investors, operators & anyone building.Present Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room, professional video of your pitch, & your company in the post event send.Title Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per Demo Day. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.Free for Propel Private Network members. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public, our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase at Propel Demo Day in front of an investor room. Applications for the next cohort are open at this link. 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders 5  Providers already in the room. This is not theoretical. Moshe Cohen, CPA of Cohen & Co runs tax strategy, bookkeeping & fractional CFO work for Propel founders & takes bookings through us. Thirty minute paid session, 120 dollars  Book Moshe. Stephen Michael Consulting, a 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises entering the startup ecosystem, 150 dollars  Book a strategy call. If you provide a service & want a table at the next one, that is what the provider ticket is. On camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Work with Stephen directly. A 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises trying to get into the startup ecosystem. Book a strategy call, browse the marketplace50 Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: AI for operators
events.description: AI for Forward-thinking OperatorsA 2-hour hands-on workshop for execs, VPs, operators, fractional leaders, and founders.You're further along in your career than you are in AI - and you're tired of nodding along while colleagues and vendors pitch magic and your team runs experiments you can't evaluate.This isn't a talk. It's a working session. Bring your laptop. In two hours you'll set up Claude Code, Muse, or Hark - connect them to the tools and services you actually live in, and produce something real. Something that'll solve an actual problem you tackle, or something that'll help your work.Past execs have left with having created things like:dynamic competitive research and action toolsomething that runs analysis on their products and sales and automatically finds room for offloading inventory, dynamic promos, and actionable customer segmentshelps them hold their vendors and teams accountable automatically using briefs, followups, real-time measurementcloses their monthly books accuratelyautomates sales research and outreach relevant to them, not boilerplateautomates HR paperwork relevant to them, not boilerplateSmall by design: 3-5 seats, hands-on help throughout. We build alongside you and troubleshoot in real time, so you walk out ready to run this inside your company, immediately.About the host: Deepak DevjaniSomewhere along the way I started training my own team on AI, just so we could ship faster. And the coaching thing kind of fell in my lap. Turns out I love it.Then execs started coming to me. They wanted the same thing for themselves. Then other founders. For the last couple years I've been training execs and their C-suite teams, and honestly the change is night and day. They have more time. They get way more done.One thing I learned fast: for this to actually work, it has to be as close to personal and private as possible  essentially 1:1. That's the whole reason this class is small. You can literally know nothing walking in and you'll be OK; that's by design. And what you leave with isn't just a tool you built  it's the confidence to walk into work and actually use this.So that's what Reliable Bits is now. We still go into companies and implement AI for real. But a big part of what we do is coach the people doing the actual work. Operators, execs, VPs.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Create Once. Publish Everywhere.
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Create Once. Publish Everywhere.Learn how top creators turn one idea into newsletters, videos, podcasts, social posts, presentations, & more using AI-powered content systems. Creating the idea is only half the work. Then comes the newsletter. The social posts. The video. The presentation. The podcast. The clips. And somehow, every platform wants something different. What if you didn't have to start from scratch every single time? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how creators, entrepreneurs, educators, filmmakers, & small teams are using AI-powered content systems to turn one strong idea into an entire ecosystem of content. We'll look beyond simply asking AI to write me a post & dig into how you can build repeatable workflows that help you create, adapt, & distribute your ideas across formats-without losing your voice in the process. Together we'll explore:  How to turn one core idea into multiple pieces of content  AI workflows for newsletters, social posts, video, podcasts, presentations, & more  How to adapt an idea for different platforms instead of simply copying & pasting  Ways to build repeatable content systems that save time & creative energy  How to keep your voice, perspective, & cultural context consistent across AI-assisted content  Practical strategies for spending less time feeding the content machine & more time developing ideas worth sharing The goal isn't to create more content just for the sake of creating more content. It's to make your best ideas work harder for you. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to learn how AI can support a smarter, more sustainable creative process. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & social media professionals  Podcasters & video creators  Anyone with ideas they want to share more consistently Whether you're building a personal brand, growing a business, educating an audience, promoting your creative work, or simply tired of reinventing the wheel every time you post-this conversation is for you. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can start applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.name: Creativity Is Dead, Long Live Creativity - Gen AI & Meaning Of Art
events.description: The concept of creativity has a surprisingly short history. While ancient philosophers expounded on imagination & free will, theorizations of creativity as a distinct trait only date to the past hundred years. GenAI suggests that creativity is not unique to humans or even conscious organisms, but is reducible to mere calculation & programming. Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 5:30PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:00PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.  ------------------ABOUT COHORTCohort is a space & home for ideas, & the people who think about them, create new ones, & build things from them. Many of us are founders, builders, artists, researchers, & their supporters here in NYC. Our goal is to turn the city into a campus after college. We hold idea & discussion events, coworking events for support & accountability for those building & creating things, & pure social events to build genuine relationships & community. Subscribe, browse our calendar, & join us for our next events!  Photography Notice We may take photos & video at our events to share on social media & our website. We use it to spread the word & help more people find this community. By attending, you're giving us permission to use those photos & videos in anything related to Cohort's promotion & outreach. If you'd rather not be photographed, just let us know when you arrive & we'll make sure you're not included. More from Cohort Monday Oct 19 Wednesday Oct 14 Dating the Dead Oct 15 Halloween crawl Oct 31 Calendar

Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 5:30PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:00PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.  ------------------ABOUT COHORTCohort is a space & home for ideas, & the people who think about them, create new ones, & build things from them. Many of us are founders, builders, artists, researchers, & their supporters here in NYC. Our goal is to turn the city into a campus after college. We hold idea & discussion events, coworking events for support & accountability for those building & creating things, & pure social events to build genuine relationships & community. Subscribe, browse our calendar, & join us for our next events!  Photography Notice We may take photos & video at our events to share on social media & our website. We use it to spread the word & help more people find this community. By attending, you're giving us permission to use those photos & videos in anything related to Cohort's promotion & outreach. If you'd rather not be photographed, just let us know when you arrive & we'll make sure you're not included. More from Cohort Monday Oct 19 Wednesday Oct 14 Dating the Dead Oct 15 Halloween crawl Oct 31 Calendar

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: PM 2.0 - Product Mgmt In Age Of AI
events.description: Product Management in the Age of AIIf AI can write the PRD, summarize customer feedback, research competitors, & build prototypes  what is the Product Managers job now?Join Pioneering Minds AI for an interactive workshop on how product management is changing in the age of AI, & what makes a great PM today.Well bring together both experienced old-school PMs & a new generation of AI-native PMs to compare how the role has evolved, which skills still matter, & what students should focus on if they want to work in product.What Well DiscussWhat great PMs looked like before AIWhich traditional PM skills still matterWhich parts of the job AI is already changingHow PMs can use AI for research, prototyping, prioritization, & product discoveryWhether PMs need to become more technicalWhy judgment, taste, communication, & problem selection may matter more than everWhat companies may look for in the next generation of PMsWell also discuss a bigger question:When AI makes execution easier, does the PMs real value shift from managing the process to deciding what should be built in the first place?No previous PM or technical experience is required. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.name: Robot Hackathon - Code That Moves
events.description: Build physical AI applications with real robot arms @ Viam! About the Event We're excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm & support from Viam experts throughout. No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI & some software experience. See what engineers built at the last hackathon here. Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis. What You'll Build Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam & a real robot arm. Each team will have access to: UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101) Linux compute machine RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm) Webcams A free Viam account We'll provide a variety of objects for your robot to manipulate. You are encouraged to bring anything required for the project you have in mind. Please bring your own laptop. In your application, please summarize what project you have in mind. Ideas from past events: training a VLA, playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, manipulating a robot arm using computer vision & hand gestures. Prizes We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: AI/ML Lecture & Mixer
events.description: A monthly ML research colloquium by the New York Machine Learning Research Guild - this session in collaboration with our partner, CUNY Tech Prep. Speaker: Zayne Sprague  PhD Researcher, Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, NYU & GoogleTopic: From Chain of Thought to Agent Swarms: A Brief Story on Reasoning in LLMs Giving language models more time to think has produced substantial gains, but in targeted domains, & the benefits appear to remain uneven across tasks. This talk explores how models can use additional computation at inference time effectively, reviewing the progression from prompt based methods to multi-agent systems. We will begin with chain-of-thought prompting, asking a model to think before giving a final answer, presenting our work showing that chain-of-thought prompting has its strongest benefits concentrated in mathematics & symbolic reasoning. These domains also share a practical advantage: answers can often be checked automatically, providing feedback that can be used to train models through reinforcement learning. This leads us to SkillFactory, where we use a model's own successful & unsuccessful attempts to construct training examples that demonstrate checking answers & retrying. Combining supervised finetuning on these examples with reinforcement learning helps models develop these behaviors & generalize to harder problems. Finally, we will discuss recent work on agent swarms, exploring how reasoning can scale in parallel & what role verification can play in making that additional computation useful. This session is a close-quarters look at that work, with plenty of room to push back & dig in. # Who this is forNY-MLR colloquia are small by design. The room is capped, & we keep it that way so the discussion stays substantive & everyone in it can contribute. We'd love to see you if you're:- A practitioner working seriously on ML, in industry or in a lab- A researcher or graduate student in ML, NLP, or an adjacent field- A highly motivated student or self-directed learner of any age or background, with real depth of interest # Schedule5:00 - 5:30 PM - Doors open, arrivals, mingling5:30 - 6:30 PM - Speaker Lecture6:30 - 7:00 PM - Moderated Q&A7:00 - 8:00 PM - After hours, mingling, wind-down8:00 PM - Lights out Venue: Amazon JFK27 ("Hank")  12 W 39th St, New York, NY 10018

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

solutions. Strategic & Channel PartnersDistributors, retailers, service providers, & organizations exploring collaboration opportunities. Industry Leaders & OperatorsProfessionals who can offer KISED operates programs that help Korean startups develop their capabilities, explore new markets, & build connections with domestic & international business ecosystems. Through its international programs & overseas offices, including the KISED New York Office, KISED supports Korean startups in pursuing global expansion & connecting with opportunities in the U.S. market. OPERATED BYPEN Ventures PEN Ventures is a global accelerator & investment firm supporting startups through investment, acceleration, corporate collaboration, open innovation, & global market-entry programs. With an international network across major innovation hubs, PEN Ventures connects startups with investors, corporations, public institutions, & strategic partners to facilitate business expansion & cross-border collaboration. events.name: How To Raise Your First Priced Round
events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. Location will be the beautiful Gunderson Dettmer NYC offices above Flatiron. Generously sponsored by Jose Rivera & Tonna Obaze of Gunderson Dettmer, Kelly Caviglia of Mercury, & Paul Brezovsky III of Qapita. Session 1: Taught by Ramesh Karra & Paul Brezovsky III's team at Qapita will focus on Data Room. What goes in, what doesn't, what investors are looking for, & how not get get tripped up. Session 2: Taught by Jose Rivera of Gunderson Dettmer will focus on the term sheet negotiation. What terms matter & which don't. How to affect outcomes that are durable & beneficial for your business. Session 3: Taught by me will focused on how to find, pitch, & close priced round investors. Session 4: Will be a panel discussion & fireside chat with 3 partners at NYC VC firms. I've purposely chosen folks who represent software & hardware investors as well as funds that operate outside of healthcare. Mat Kaliski of Acronym Venture CapitalBrian Laung Aoaeh, CFA of REFASHIOND Ventures: The Industrial Transformation FundOwen Willis of Opal Ventures & Primary Venture Partners

events.name: Tech Table Talk: At The Intersection Of Tech, Media & AI
events.description: Tech Table Talk is an intimate dinner bringing together women shaping what's next across technology, media, commerce, & AI. Hosted by People Culture & Belonging & Black Affinity Group in partnership with Baddies in Tech, the evening is designed to create space for meaningful connection, candid conversation, & thoughtful exchange around how women are influencing the future of these rapidly evolving industries. What to ExpectArrival & ConnectionEase into the evening with drinks, light bites, & time to connect with fellow guests before dinner begins. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts. The conversation will invite guests to share what they're building, exploring, questioning, & imagining for the future of technology, media, commerce, & AI. Dessert & Fireside ConversationTo close the evening, Randi Gray, Head of IT at MERIT Beauty, will join Allie Joy Tsahey, CEO of Baddies in Tech, for an intimate fireside conversation exploring the intersection of technology, AI, media, & commerce. Together, they'll unpack how emerging technology is reshaping the way people discover, consume, create, shop, & engage with content & products, & what that evolution means for the women helping shape what comes next. What You'll Leave WithNew relationships & a stronger sense of community Fresh perspective on the future of AI, media, technology, & commerce Deeper insight into how women are influencing these industries A meaningful connection to the Baddies in Tech & People communities A new question, idea, or perspective to carry with you beyond the evening Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 30-35 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: PM 2.0 - Product Mgmt In Age Of AI
events.description: Product Management in the Age of AIIf AI can write the PRD, summarize customer feedback, research competitors, & build prototypes  what is the Product Managers job now?Join Pioneering Minds AI for an interactive workshop on how product management is changing in the age of AI, & what makes a great PM today.Well bring together both experienced old-school PMs & a new generation of AI-native PMs to compare how the role has evolved, which skills still matter, & what students should focus on if they want to work in product.What Well DiscussWhat great PMs looked like before AIWhich traditional PM skills still matterWhich parts of the job AI is already changingHow PMs can use AI for research, prototyping, prioritization, & product discoveryWhether PMs need to become more technicalWhy judgment, taste, communication, & problem selection may matter more than everWhat companies may look for in the next generation of PMsWell also discuss a bigger question:When AI makes execution easier, does the PMs real value shift from managing the process to deciding what should be built in the first place?No previous PM or technical experience is required. The session is designed primarily for students, aspiring PMs, & early-career professionals interested in product, startups, & AI.Hackathon PreviewThis workshop takes place the day before the Pioneering Minds AI Hackathon & will also serve as a warm-up for participants.Well share an early look at the hackathon tracks:Critical Thinking & LearningAI for Product Management WorkflowsLegal Tech WorkflowsFintech & Insurtech WorkflowsWell also provide guidance on choosing a strong problem, designing an AI-native workflow, & what judges will be looking for.If youre joining the hackathon, this is your chance to get a head start.About Pioneering Minds AIAt pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI-native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly while keeping humans in the front seat.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez
