events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: Jev Demo Day
events.description: Jev Demo Day: show us what you've been tinkering with. Before LinkedIn finds Jev, join us for a demo day focused on anything built with Typesafe AI's new shiny Jev model, the System One model that made classifier models cool again.Jev launched two weeks ago, so nobody has a finished product yet, & that is the point. Work-in-progress is not just allowed, it is encouraged. Half-working prototypes, weird experiments, dead ends, benchmarks, & here is what I learned talks are all welcome.Part demo day, part unconference. Five-minute demos, hot takes, half broken projects, burning opinions on the main stage. No demo? Grab a slot anyway & talk about what you tried with Jev, what surprised you, or where it broke. Sponsors & venue to be announced. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQ Some slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsBuilt something with Jev, or tried to? This is your moment to share it with people who will actually get it. The format is part demo day, part unconference. A demo or talk is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress or shares lessons learned, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!) Ideas for what to bring: A routing layer that decides code vs LLM vs humanTool-call gating for an agentJev as a judge or jurorA System One vs System Two bake-off against Claude or GPT on the same decisionLatency experimentsAnything through OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare, LangChain, or Langfuse FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo or talk. Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:15 Open floor / unconference9:00 Doors Close

events.name: Against The Inevitable - Finding Creative Agency In Age Of AI
events.description: We can do something about it, actually!Frontier AI companies are relying on the inevitability narrative to push every sector to adopt their techuse their products, or get left behind. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Code & Coffee Hackathon
events.description: Everyone's a builder here: coders, PMs, designers, & the just-curious.Get ready to build something real for Newark! We're taking over Rutgers iHub for a full-day hackathon focused on solving problems that actually matter to the people who call this city home, from water safety to food access to just making city government easier to navigate.Theme:Description:This hackathon challenges participants to pick a real issue facing Newark & build something that actually helps: a tool, an assistant, a dashboard, whatever gets the job done. Teams can dig into problem areas like environmental & water justice, food access, cost of living, or civic transparency, or bring their own idea if they see a sharper angle. Expect AI to play a role in your build, but what we're really looking for is a solution that works. Judging will weigh usefulness & execution as heavily as technical approach.Technical Scope:Participants can use any technical stack they prefer (code-based, no-code, or a mix)Projects must be built from scratch during the hackathon, no prebuilt solutionsTeams are free to choose one of our suggested problem areas or pitch their own. We'll share a few starting points at kickoff, but the direction is yoursJudging Criteria:Relevance & Impact: Does this solve a real, specific problem for Newark residents, & could someone actually use it?Execution: How complete & functional is the prototype, given the short build window?Thoughtful AI Use: How & why did you use AI? A simple, well-executed approach counts; bonus points for teams who push further with multi-step reasoning or tool use where it genuinely fits the problem.Usability & Creativity: Would a non-technical resident actually get it? Does the approach show real originality?Pitch & Clarity: Can you clearly explain the problem, the solution, & who it's for in your demo?Agenda:10:00  10:30 AM | Check-in & NetworkingRegistration, coffee/light breakfast, casual networking10:30  11:00 AM | Welcome & Opening RemarksTheme & judging criteria overview11:00  11:30 AM | Team Formation & Idea PitchesParticipants pitch project ideas, team matchmaking session11:30 AM  4:00 PM | Hacking SessionTeams build prototypes, mentors available for tech & business guidance, lunch break at 1:00 PM4:00  5:00 PM | Project Demos & Pitches35 minute demos from each team, judged by partners & industry reps5:00  5:30 PM | Awards & Closing RemarksWinners announced, closing remarks5:30  6:00 PM | Networking & Wrap-UpInformal mingling with participants, judges, & partners

events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. Happy hour runs from 2 to 4 on Saturday, October 10th, out on the water with the harbor & the skyline as the backdrop.nWhat to Expect:nA cross-section of people working on cities & public systems: public servants, technologists, founders, funders, consultants, & nonprofit operatorsnGenuine conversations across different corners of civic & urban tech: different roles, different focus areas, all in one placenNo sales pitches, no panels, just good companynFun prizes via our always-popular raffle nOptional activities before the happy hour so you can make a full island day of itnMake a Full Day of It:nThe main extra is a volunteer session with the Billion Oyster Project. They're restoring NY Harbor with oyster reefs, a natural fit for a group that spends its weekdays working on cities & public systems.nYou can also join Jer Thorp for Bird Data Portraits from 1 to 2. Jer is a data artist & bird enthusiast, & he'll help you make a data portrait of your favorite local bird using data from eBird. All materials will be provided, & you'll wrap up right as the happy hour begins.nPick Your Ticket:nHappy Hour Only: The main event, 2 to 4 on the water. Ferry over whenever works for you.nHappy Hour + Volunteer: The volunteer session, then straight into the happy hour. Starts with a 9:15am ferry & wraps at 2:30. Spots are limited, & we'll follow up with details.nHappy Hour + Workshop: Bird Data Portraits with Jer Thorp from 1 to 2, then straight into the happy hour. events.name: Coding Agents w/ Elastic Memory + Evolution To Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: Scene By Scene - Brand Relevance, Video AI & Next Era Of CTV
events.description: As billions of advertising dollars shift to Connected TV, the industry is entering a new era. The challenge is no longer simply reaching the right audience - it's ensuring every advertising dollar reaches viewers at exactly the right moment. New advances in AI - including scene-level understanding that can interpret video content with unprecedented context - are transforming how premium video inventory is valued, bought, & sold. Join an invitation-only gathering of the voices defining the future of brands & CTV. From the leaders responsible for the world's largest advertising budgets to the innovators building the next generation of AI & video technology, this evening will feature an intimate fireside conversation, followed by networking among the industry's top decision-makers.   About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI & accelerated computing. Its platforms power work across data centers, graphics, robotics, & autonomous systems, & underpin much of the AI infrastructure the technology industry runs on today.   About PYLER PYLER is an AI-driven company specializing in video understanding & brand safety for digital advertising. Its core product, AiD, interprets video, audio, & metadata in real time to ensure ads appear in safe, relevant, trusted contexts. PYLER is a winner of the 2025 NVIDIA Inception Startup Grand Challenge.   About Supermomos Supermomos is a community platform connecting more than 35,000 founders, investors, & operators across New York, Boston, San Francisco, London, & Singapore. We host curated gatherings that bring together the people building & funding what comes next.  Speakers:Matt Groshong, Business Development Director, AdTech & MarTech, NVIDIA: Matt Groshong is a Business Development Director at NVIDIA, covering AdTech & MarTech. He has been in technology, advertising & media long enough to remember when "digital" was a separate budget line, & now spends most of his time helping the ecosystem work out what AI & accelerated computing actually do for them, rather than what the keynote said they would. Lately he is preoccupied with agentic systems, & what happens to marketing when the software starts making its own decisions. Before NVIDIA he was an Account CTO at Microsoft, aligned to WPP, & EMEA CTO at McCann Worldgroup. Earlier stops include the BBC, ServiceNow & the Newspaper Licensing Agency. He started his career at Microsoft, so the loop is closed. He lives in North London with his wife, three children, a cat, a dog, & more bikes than he will admit to anyone who isn't a cyclist. Jaeho Oh, Co-Founder & CEO, PYLER ($40M raised): Jaeho Oh is the founder & CEO of PYLER. Under his leadership, the company has scaled to 2 million videos analyzed a day, the equivalent of 60 years of content every 24 hours, for advertisers including Samsung & Kenvue. He sold his first company, a port decentralization protocol startup, at 18. He spoke on multi-modal video intelligence at NVIDIA GTC 2026 & has been named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House
events.description: Explore cool spots, meet makers, & dive into history at the Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House! The Brooklyn Navy Yard's Annual Open House Discover the Yard's 300-acre innovative campus during our Annual Open House, part of Open House New York Weekend. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, & technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access & immersive activations. This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Plug&Play x PMAI Hackathon - Rapid Response
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild: Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Product Leader Collective - The Software Factory Debate
events.description: The software factory is under construction. Come debate what it should look like.A lot of teams are trying to build a software factory: AI agents that can help plan, build, test, & ship software. The idea is compelling, but the reality is still messy. The tools are changing quickly, the playbook is far from settled, & the biggest bottlenecks may be showing up in places teams are not expecting. Join Ben Levine, CPO @ Candidly & product & engineering leaders for an open conversation about what's actually working & what still gets in the way. Then, get a close look at a few teams putting these ideas to work today. Who should be in the room  Product & engineering leaders figuring out where AI agents belong in the product development process, & what changes when they move from demos into daily work. Come ready to Pressure-test software factory claims with people doing the work. Think beyond coding agents: how should planning, specs, feedback, & handoffs change? Debate real tradeoffs instead of sitting through another polished product demo. Ben Levine is Chief Product Officer at Candidly, where he leads product, data science, & design. Previously, Ben worked as a Data Scientist at Twitter & a Research Fellow at Microsoft Research Labs. A Fulbright Scholar, he holds an MSc from the London School of Economics & completed PhD coursework in Quantitative Marketing at Columbia University. We're keeping the event intimate to facilitate meaningful conversation. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.

events.name: Real-Time Video Agents Hack
events.description: The VAST Builders Challenge is a three-city technical event series bringing together founders & engineers across New York, London, & San Francisco to build production-ready AI systems. Spend the day building agents to unlock the value of video. Because video is hard to search & analyze,  most of it stays in storage, unwatched & underused. Experiment with the latest AI infrastructure, collaborate with other ambitious builders, & turn your ideas into shippable prototypes - with access to expert guidance, compute, & the tools you need to ship. Hosted with VAST Data in collaboration with NVIDIA, SpaceXAI, CoreWeave & Weights & Biases. Note: Registration closes on Oct 6th. Prizes1st place: NVIDIA DGX Spark HuggingFace Microduck Cursor Credits Cash Gift Cards The Builders StackYou don't have to worry about starting from scratch, we've set it up for you: Video understanding: reason over a video clip with NVIDIA Cosmos. Semantic search: find moments across hours of footage using natural language. Object detection: real-time detection & tracking across frames with YOLO. General-purpose LLMs: models from Weights & Biases to power your application logic (e.g. video agents). The VAST AI OS orchestrates the video ingestion & data layer, models are served on CoreWeave GPUs, & builders ship with Cursor. Build your own video agent or something no one's thought of. events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: UGLY TALK: YOUR FIRST $100K DEAL
events.description: Your first six-figure deal can expose every weak spot in your sales process.You chased the wrong buyer. Priced from fear. Followed up too late. Let one internal champion carry the whole deal.Then the contract lands. You celebrate. The next question hurts more: can you do it again?This Ugly Talk gets into the hard calls behind closing a major customer. You will hear what founders got wrong. You will see what made the deal move. You will leave with a clearer path from one big win to $1M ARR. Why you should be in this room.Spot the sales mistakes that quietly kill large deals.Find the buyer with budget, urgency, and enough power to move.Learn what changes across pricing, pitching, negotiation, and follow-up.Build a sales motion that can survive beyond one lucky contract.Understand what needs to break before your company reaches $1M ARR. What's on the table.Choosing the right deal: Which customers deserve months of your runway.Reaching the real buyer: How to navigate stakeholders and build an internal champion.Closing six figures: The decisions that move a large deal across the line.Owning the mistakes: Where founders lose ground on pricing, pitching, negotiation, and follow-up.Getting past one win: How to turn an early contract into repeatable revenue. events.name: Columbia Starup Lab - Get Hired Hack
events.description: Event DescriptionSkip the resume pile. Get Hired Hack is a one-day, in-person hackathon at Columbia Startup Lab where NYC's fastest-growing startups bring real problems from their roadmaps, & you show them what working with you looks like. Founders who are hiring will be in the room, watching you build. Ship something great & your demo becomes your first commit. Problem StatementStartups don't hire resumes. They hire people who ship. But hiring still runs on LeetCode, keyword filters & 45-minute calls that tell a founder almost nothing about how you work. At Get Hired Hack, each hiring startup brings one real, scoped problem it would actually assign a new engineer. Pick a track, build against it, & demo it to the founder who wrote it. Founders get the best hiring signal there is: real work on their real problem. You get a shot at a role on proof of work, not pedigree. The Challenge Tracks Each track is a real problem from a hiring startup: TBD Expect problems across: AI agents & LLM-powered features Full-stack product work Infra, devtools & data pipelines Growth & internal tooling What to ExpectFounders who are hiring pitch their problem at kickoff [~6] hours of focused building on real startup problems Teams of 4 Demos to the founder whose problem you picked Lunch, coffee & a room full of people building NYC's next great companies PrizesEvery track winner gets a fast-tracked final-round interview with that startup's founder JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers with real shipping experience (full stack, backend, AI/ML, infra) Senior engineers curious about joining an early-stage startup Builders who'd rather show their work than talk about it Engineers who want to be a startup's first or fifth hire, not its five-hundredth You don't need to be actively job hunting. Come build, meet founders & see what's out there. SponsorsTBD HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Columbia Startup Lab: Columbia's home for alumni founders, a coworking space & community in SoHo.

events.name: Sampura Research Talk & Lunch
events.description: Sampura Research: Hill-climbing Alignment using Humans Sampura Research is a London-based nonprofit, founded by Google DeepMind alumni, building Human-AI Complementarity for AI alignment. As AI systems grow more capable, the judges we use to train, evaluate & monitor them increasingly fall short. Most of the field responds by replacing humans with LLM judges; we think humans & AIs have complementary strengths, & that human oversight is an uncorrelated layer of defence that AI-only judges can't provide. In this talk we'll share how we're building better judges: a leaderboard of 50+ alignment-relevant datasets, & methods that route, decompose & assist across humans & AIs to hill-climb it. Schedule (you can join for any part)12:30 - Talk (20 min)12:50 - Q&A (20 min)13:10 - Informal chat with the team (20 min) Backed by an $11M grant from Coefficient Giving, we're a small in-person team hiring founding technical staff, looking to solve alignment instead of pausing AI. Come along & say hello! Apply: Founding Member of Technical Staff applicationWebsite: https://sampura.org/ Lunch will be provided! Update: We're almost at capacity, & will admit folks based on their profile

events.name: Plug&Play x PMAI Hackathon - Rapid Response
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.
