events.name: Future Of AI Infrastructure
events.description: Let's talk about what's coming in the world of AI infra. Anthony Erondu is a Principal Consultant focused on AI infrastructure, GPU compute & Physical AI. He partners with high growth companies across the space to build product & engineering teams, placing talent from VP level leaders through senior ICs across some of the most critical areas of the AI stack. Akaanksha Sinha is an award-winning trailblazer in AI, cybersecurity & governance architecture. Over a decade in the enterprise stack. She founded AKAVAM, a governance-through-architecture company for enterprise AI. Its platform, AEVO, combines infrastructure as code, policy as code & compliance as code into deterministic execution, turning organizational context into operating capability. Ex-IBM, Deloitte, CUNY Srinivas Venkatanarayanan is a Senior Systems Research Engineer in Nvidia, Working in Cosmos Search. He specializes in multimodal reasoning, search & Curation for Post-training Vision Language Action Models. He works in Autonomous Vehicle & Robotics domain. Joshua Ness is a Senior AI Advisor & Consultant based in New York City. He spent 6 years at Verizon 5G Labs where he advised on enterprise adoption of 5G & edge computing technologies for clients, including the NFL, Disney, & MasterCard. He currently advises PE-backed global technology firms on AI implemention & organizational structure, including tech infrastructure modernization & regulatory compliance. Joshua holds a Fulbright Specialist appointment through which he works with the government of the Philippines on national AI readiness programs. He holds certifications from AWS, IBM, & IEEE in applied AI & cloud infrastructure.

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: Real-Time Video Agents Hack
events.description: The VAST Builders Challenge is a three-city technical event series bringing together founders & engineers across New York, London, & San Francisco to build production-ready AI systems. Spend the day building agents to unlock the value of video. Because video is hard to search & analyze,  most of it stays in storage, unwatched & underused. Experiment with the latest AI infrastructure, collaborate with other ambitious builders, & turn your ideas into shippable prototypes - with access to expert guidance, compute, & the tools you need to ship. Hosted with VAST Data in collaboration with NVIDIA, SpaceXAI, CoreWeave & Weights & Biases. Note: Registration closes on Oct 6th. Prizes1st place: NVIDIA DGX Spark HuggingFace Microduck Cursor Credits Cash Gift Cards The Builders StackYou don't have to worry about starting from scratch, we've set it up for you: Video understanding: reason over a video clip with NVIDIA Cosmos. Semantic search: find moments across hours of footage using natural language. Object detection: real-time detection & tracking across frames with YOLO. General-purpose LLMs: models from Weights & Biases to power your application logic (e.g. video agents). The VAST AI OS orchestrates the video ingestion & data layer, models are served on CoreWeave GPUs, & builders ship with Cursor. Build your own video agent or something no one's thought of. We'll share the videos to get you started on building video agents. JudgesDiego Garzon - Senior Solution Architect for AI/AV Simulation @ Nvidia Ravi Garg - Solutions Architect @ Nvidia Ram B. - Sr. Developer Advocate @ VAST Data Brian Verkley - Director, AI Data Platform @ VAST Data Prashanth Nalubandhu - Staff AI Solutions Architect @ CoreWeave Brandon Kates - Founding FDE @ CoreWeave Vera A - Senior Solutions Architect @ Weights & Biases Who should attendDevelopers, ML/AI engineers, agent builders, & data engineers, from startups to enterprise teams working with video or multimodal AI. While individuals are welcome, we encourage teams of up to four members & will prioritize team applications. You can form a team on the day of the event or arrive with one already assembled. Applications are required. Space is limited. events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.description: We're bringing together engineers, founders, builders, & investors for an evening of agentic commerce, live demos, & building with the Ophelia API. Ophelia gives consumer software the infrastructure to search, book, buy, & transact end-to-end directly inside the products, agents, & devices people already use. Let a wearable turn find me a workout into a booked class Create a new interface for commerce that doesn't look like a checkout page Or build something we haven't imagined yet THE HACK CHALLENGEUse the Ophelia API to build a product, feature, agent, or experience that turns intent into a real transaction. We're especially interested in what happens when commerce moves inside the products, agents, devices, & interfaces people already use. Available commerce categories include:  Restaurants & reservations Flights & travel Hotels Events & tickets Fitness & classesand thousands of other services with Ophelia V3 PLEASE COME WITH PRODUCT OR DEMO ALREADY BUILT. We strongly encourage you to build beyond a chatbot or general-purpose AI assistant. THE NIGHT6:00 PM: Check-in + drinks Meet other NYC builders, grab a drink, get set up, & meet the Ophelia team. 6:30 PM: Ophelia API kickoff We'll give you a quick walkthrough of the API, what you can build, & how to get started. 6:45 PM: DEMOS Teams will have a short window to demo what they built. Show us the actual customer experience not just a pitch. 8:00 PM: JUDGING + WINNER Both the audience & our team will select one winning builder or team based on the quality of the build, creativity of the experience, & how compellingly it demonstrates the future of agentic commerce. 8:30 PM: WINNER + AFTERPARTY Announce the winner, celebrate, & keep the conversations going.  THE PRIZEThe winning team gets the opportunity to: Pitch their startup or idea directly to Betaworks. Plus:  AI credits across Betaworks teams $100 in Ophelia credits + merch Meta smart glasses Whether you're building a startup, experimenting with an idea, or just want to see what you can make with the infrastructure, come build. Come if you:  Build AI agents Build consumer apps Work on systems through one integration, allowing software to parse availability, initiate checkout, process payments, & complete transactions directly within the products people already use. 3.8M+ users are already routed through Ophelia-powered products. Built for platforms. events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: UGLY TALK: FAILURE IS KEY TO SUCCESS
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie.The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping and start doing math at 3:00 AM.Founders are expected to eat it quietly and keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next.Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them. Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next.Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways.Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore.Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration.Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building. What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progressThe moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, and what changed afterwardFailure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomesTreating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, and how to decide fastRejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the noHabits for staying focused and resilient when everything feels uncertain Run of show6:00  6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks)6:30  6:40 PM: Welcome remarks6:40  6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean6:50  7:30 PM: Panel Discussion7:30  7:45 PM: Audience Q&A7:45  8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks and drinks Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, HungryrootBen McKean is the Founder and CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, and nutrition effortless and enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President and General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food and beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nations leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide and nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynchs technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University and currently lives in North Carolina with his wife and kids.Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, BizbeStephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, and logistics. He's the founder and CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage and lower middle market M&A firm based in New York and Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded and led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics and Webster Logistics.Dmitry Koltunov - Founder and CEO, ArborDmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, and storyteller. He is the founder and CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video and beyond. Previously, he co-founded and served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group.Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New Yorks oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies.Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter and theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science and Economics from the University of Pennsylvania and is a CFA charterholder.Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder and CEO, Sweetling HealthGwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder and CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk and hard-to-reach populations. Shes a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative and brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, and POPSUGAR before founding and scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA and founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap. Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup StationVictoria Yampolsky is the Founder and President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm and financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, and fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders and access to capital, and has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Womens Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank and Capgemini, and holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University and an MBA from Columbia Business School. Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders and operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include:Founders and co-founders (pre-seed to Series A)Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff)Product and Engineering leads building through ambiguityGrowth and GTM leads working through missed targets and pivotsFinance and strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making Who's backing this.The Startup StationThe Startup Station - is a CFO advisory and financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials and tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, weve helped 150+ founders raise over $50M and educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, and check size.Mind Your BusinessEvery attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKeans Mind Your Business.  Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, and what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcodethe way purpose, belonging, imagination, and courage shape how they work. Told with humor and warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, and acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isnt doing more workits knowing what work is worth doing.GREY JournalGREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News). About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough \

events.description: Jev Demo Day: show us what you've been tinkering with. Before LinkedIn finds Jev, join us for a demo day focused on anything built with Typesafe AI's new shiny Jev model, the System One model that made classifier models cool again.Jev launched two weeks ago, so nobody has a finished product yet, & that is the point. Work-in-progress is not just allowed, it is encouraged. Half-working prototypes, weird experiments, dead ends, benchmarks, & here is what I learned talks are all welcome.Part demo day, part unconference. Five-minute demos, hot takes, half broken projects, burning opinions on the main stage. No demo? Grab a slot anyway & talk about what you tried with Jev, what surprised you, or where it broke. Sponsors & venue to be announced. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQ Some slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsBuilt something with Jev, or tried to? This is your moment to share it with people who will actually get it. The format is part demo day, part unconference. A demo or talk is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress or shares lessons learned, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!) Ideas for what to bring: A routing layer that decides code vs LLM vs humanTool-call gating for an agentJev as a judge or jurorA System One vs System Two bake-off against Claude or GPT on the same decisionLatency experimentsAnything through OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare, LangChain, or Langfuse FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo or talk. Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:15 Open floor / unconference9:00 Doors Close

events.name: Scene By Scene - Brand Relevance, Video AI & Next Era Of CTV
events.description: As billions of advertising dollars shift to Connected TV, the industry is entering a new era. The challenge is no longer simply reaching the right audience - it's ensuring every advertising dollar reaches viewers at exactly the right moment. New advances in AI - including scene-level understanding that can interpret video content with unprecedented context - are transforming how premium video inventory is valued, bought, & sold. Join an invitation-only gathering of the voices defining the future of brands & CTV. From the leaders responsible for the world's largest advertising budgets to the innovators building the next generation of AI & video technology, this evening will feature an intimate fireside conversation, followed by networking among the industry's top decision-makers.   About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI & accelerated computing. Its platforms power work across data centers, graphics, robotics, & autonomous systems, & underpin much of the AI infrastructure the technology industry runs on today.   About PYLER PYLER is an AI-driven company specializing in video understanding & brand safety for digital advertising. Its core product, AiD, interprets video, audio, & metadata in real time to ensure ads appear in safe, relevant, trusted contexts. PYLER is a winner of the 2025 NVIDIA Inception Startup Grand Challenge.   About Supermomos Supermomos is a community platform connecting more than 35,000 founders, investors, & operators across New York, Boston, San Francisco, London, & Singapore. We host curated gatherings that bring together the people building & funding what comes next.  Speakers:Matt Groshong, Business Development Director, AdTech & MarTech, NVIDIA: Matt Groshong is a Business Development Director at NVIDIA, covering AdTech & MarTech. He has been in technology, advertising & media long enough to remember when "digital" was a separate budget line, & now spends most of his time helping the ecosystem work out what AI & accelerated computing actually do for them, rather than what the keynote said they would. Lately he is preoccupied with agentic systems, & what happens to marketing when the software starts making its own decisions. Before NVIDIA he was an Account CTO at Microsoft, aligned to WPP, & EMEA CTO at McCann Worldgroup. Earlier stops include the BBC, ServiceNow & the Newspaper Licensing Agency. He started his career at Microsoft, so the loop is closed. He lives in North London with his wife, three children, a cat, a dog, & more bikes than he will admit to anyone who isn't a cyclist. Jaeho Oh, Co-Founder & CEO, PYLER ($40M raised): Jaeho Oh is the founder & CEO of PYLER. Under his leadership, the company has scaled to 2 million videos analyzed a day, the equivalent of 60 years of content every 24 hours, for advertisers including Samsung & Kenvue. He sold his first company, a port decentralization protocol startup, at 18. He spoke on multi-modal video intelligence at NVIDIA GTC 2026 & has been named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders.Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC)This is the 3rd edition of our luncheon.This time, we're hosting it in an $8.5M townhouse, because we believe in high-class experiences, & incredible people. (Pictures Below)Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st:Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August.Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August.Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August.The investors at the table:We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more.1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10.2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12.$2B+ combined AUM across both events.$1M average check, $100K minimum.$10M+ in live check capacity.Who this room is forTo get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder.Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too.Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves.The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network.The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining)Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale.Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision.Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K$300K checks.Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor  advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup.Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs.Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1All 6 senior investors confirmed.Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed:Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community.If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room.What to expect for this:A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our teamConversations with fellow high-performing startup leadersAn experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problemsEvent to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loftOur intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it.Our Venue: Some PhotosOur Greek Inspired Menu:About the mealA three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre.The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.Why we do thisOur intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. events.name: Product Leader Collective - The Software Factory Debate
events.description: The software factory is under construction. Come debate what it should look like.A lot of teams are trying to build a software factory: AI agents that can help plan, build, test, & ship software. The idea is compelling, but the reality is still messy. The tools are changing quickly, the playbook is far from settled, & the biggest bottlenecks may be showing up in places teams are not expecting. Join Ben Levine, CPO @ Candidly & product & engineering leaders for an open conversation about what's actually working & what still gets in the way. Then, get a close look at a few teams putting these ideas to work today. Who should be in the room  Product & engineering leaders figuring out where AI agents belong in the product development process, & what changes when they move from demos into daily work. Come ready to Pressure-test software factory claims with people doing the work. Think beyond coding agents: how should planning, specs, feedback, & handoffs change? Debate real tradeoffs instead of sitting through another polished product demo. Ben Levine is Chief Product Officer at Candidly, where he leads product, data science, & design. He spearheaded the development of Candidly's patented next-best-dollar optimization technology & the launch of Cait, its AI financial planner, helping millions of Americans make smarter decisions about debt, savings, & long-term wealth building. Previously, Ben worked as a Data Scientist at Twitter & a Research Fellow at Microsoft Research Labs. A Fulbright Scholar, he holds an MSc from the London School of Economics & completed PhD coursework in Quantitative Marketing at Columbia University. We're keeping the event intimate to facilitate meaningful conversation. RSVP to save your spot.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The Road To Serfdom
events.description: An UNMUTED Book Club: Islamic Exceptionalism READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Friedrich Hayek's The Road to Serfdom, the 1944 book that argued central planning doesn't just fail on its own terms but sets a country sliding toward tyranny, no matter how decent the intentions behind it. Hayek wrote it as a warning to his adopted Britain, watching wartime economic controls & the postwar appetite for planning & fearing they'd curdle into something far worse. The core claim is uncomfortable: that the road to authoritarianism is often paved by well-meaning reformers who want the state to steer the economy toward fairness, & that once you hand government that kind of control, individual freedom rarely survives the trip. It's a foundational text of modern libertarian & conservative thought, & it's the book people keep reaching for when they want to argue that good intentions & coercion aren't opposites. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about planning versus markets, where Hayek looks prophetic, where he looks paranoid, & what an argument written against 1940s socialism has to say to a very different 2026. And we'll do a fun hypothetical case study. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.description: The VAST Builders Challenge is a three-city technical event series bringing together founders & engineers across New York, London, & San Francisco to build production-ready AI systems. Spend the day building agents to unlock the value of video. Because video is hard to search & analyze,  most of it stays in storage, unwatched & underused. Experiment with the latest AI infrastructure, collaborate with other ambitious builders, & turn your ideas into shippable prototypes - with access to expert guidance, compute, & the tools you need to ship. Hosted with VAST Data in collaboration with NVIDIA, SpaceXAI, CoreWeave & Weights & Biases. Note: Registration closes on Oct 6th. Prizes1st place: NVIDIA DGX Spark HuggingFace Microduck Cursor Credits Cash Gift Cards The Builders StackYou don't have to worry about starting from scratch, we've set it up for you: Video understanding: reason over a video clip with NVIDIA Cosmos. Semantic search: find moments across hours of footage using natural language. Object detection: real-time detection & tracking across frames with YOLO. General-purpose LLMs: models from Weights & Biases to power your application logic (e.g. video agents). The VAST AI OS orchestrates the video ingestion & data layer, models are served on CoreWeave GPUs, & builders ship with Cursor. Build your own video agent or something no one's thought of. We'll share the videos to get you started on building video agents. JudgesDiego Garzon - Senior Solution Architect for AI/AV Simulation @ Nvidia Ravi Garg - Solutions Architect @ Nvidia Ram B. - Sr. Developer Advocate @ VAST Data Brian Verkley - Director, AI Data Platform @ VAST Data Prashanth Nalubandhu - Staff AI Solutions Architect @ CoreWeave Brandon Kates - Founding FDE @ CoreWeave Vera A - Senior Solutions Architect @ Weights & Biases Who should attendDevelopers, ML/AI engineers, agent builders, & data engineers, from startups to enterprise teams working with video or multimodal AI. While individuals are welcome, we encourage teams of up to four members & will prioritize team applications. You can form a team on the day of the event or arrive with one already assembled. Applications are required. Space is limited. events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. events.name: Scene By Scene - Brand Relevance, Video AI & Next Era Of CTV
events.description: As billions of advertising dollars shift to Connected TV, the industry is entering a new era. The challenge is no longer simply reaching the right audience - it's ensuring every advertising dollar reaches viewers at exactly the right moment. New advances in AI - including scene-level understanding that can interpret video content with unprecedented context - are transforming how premium video inventory is valued, bought, & sold. Join an invitation-only gathering of the voices defining the future of brands & CTV. From the leaders responsible for the world's largest advertising budgets to the innovators building the next generation of AI & video technology, this evening will feature an intimate fireside conversation, followed by networking among the industry's top decision-makers.   About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI & accelerated computing. Its platforms power work across data centers, graphics, robotics, & autonomous systems, & underpin much of the AI infrastructure the technology industry runs on today.   About PYLER PYLER is an AI-driven company specializing in video understanding & brand safety for digital advertising. Its core product, AiD, interprets video, audio, & metadata in real time to ensure ads appear in safe, relevant, trusted contexts. PYLER is a winner of the 2025 NVIDIA Inception Startup Grand Challenge.   About Supermomos Supermomos is a community platform connecting more than 35,000 founders, investors, & operators across New York, Boston, San Francisco, London, & Singapore. We host curated gatherings that bring together the people building & funding what comes next.  Speakers:Matt Groshong, Business Development Director, AdTech & MarTech, NVIDIA: Matt Groshong is a Business Development Director at NVIDIA, covering AdTech & MarTech. He has been in technology, advertising & media long enough to remember when "digital" was a separate budget line, & now spends most of his time helping the ecosystem work out what AI & accelerated computing actually do for them, rather than what the keynote said they would. Lately he is preoccupied with agentic systems, & what happens to marketing when the software starts making its own decisions. Before NVIDIA he was an Account CTO at Microsoft, aligned to WPP, & EMEA CTO at McCann Worldgroup. Earlier stops include the BBC, ServiceNow & the Newspaper Licensing Agency. He started his career at Microsoft, so the loop is closed. He lives in North London with his wife, three children, a cat, a dog, & more bikes than he will admit to anyone who isn't a cyclist. Jaeho Oh, Co-Founder & CEO, PYLER ($40M raised): Jaeho Oh is the founder & CEO of PYLER. Under his leadership, the company has scaled to 2 million videos analyzed a day, the equivalent of 60 years of content every 24 hours, for advertisers including Samsung & Kenvue. He sold his first company, a port decentralization protocol startup, at 18. He spoke on multi-modal video intelligence at NVIDIA GTC 2026 & has been named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Sovereign AI At Application Layer - Enterprise, Finance & Data
events.description: An AI Alliance Meetup, co-hosted with Neo4j & IBM | October 7, 2026 | IBM One Madison Avenue, New York Every enterprise now has the same problem in a different form. The data that would make a model useful is the data you are not allowed to move. It sits inside one firm, under one regulator, in a schema few have mapped. The interesting work in AI has quietly shifted from training bigger models alone to developing systems to utilize the data enterprises have. This afternoon is about how that is actually built. Potential topic areas: Context. Structuring the data inside a firm so a model may reason. Federation. Connecting institutions to train & evaluate to move an industry forward. Privacy. The architecture that makes cross-institution work permissible. Regulation. Why banks are now being asked to do this. What institutions may or may not allow connecting with closed models. Aligned with these topics sits Project Tapestry, the AI Alliance's consortium driven open-weights model effort. We will open with where it stands: Milestone 0 complete, Milestone 1 underway, & the ecosystem as it develops. This is a technical afternoon for engineers, architects, & data leads. Join with hard questions & connect with others facing similar challenges.  Agenda 2:00 PM: Doors open & refreshments 2:30 - 2:40: Welcome & Housekeeping2:40 - 2:55: Tapestry Updates Tentative Speaking Agenda (confirmed by 10/1)Part 1: The stack 2:40 - 3:20: Context is the product: memory & context graphs on financial data  Neo4j3:20 - 3:45: Federated learning in regulated industries3:45 - 4:00: Privacy-preserving architecture between institutions 4:00 - 4:15: Break Part 2: Why enterprises & banks care right now 4:15 - 4:35: The regulated stack: what open source is being asked to solve4:35 - 4:50: Partner Lightning talk: Practitioner view, from inside a financial institution4:50 - 4:55: Close & where to go next5:00 - 6:00 PM: Food & networking Speakers for the remaining sessions are being confirmed & will be added as they are announced. The auditorium is on the 10th floor. events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Money In Politics
events.description: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THOUGHT GALLERY (thoughtgallery.org) DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 Money in Politics, baby! Everyone agrees money runs American politics. The disagreement is whether that's a feature or a disease. In 2010, Citizens United v. FEC held that the government can't ban corporations, unions, or nonprofits from spending money on political speech. The First Amendment, the Court said, doesn't get weaker because the speaker is an organization rather than a person. Fifteen years later, it remains one of the most loved & most loathed decisions in modern constitutional law. For its defenders, the case is a straightforward win for free speech. Political speech is the most protected speech there is, & spending money to spread a message is part of how speech actually reaches people. Let the government decide who's allowed to spend on politics, the argument goes, & you've handed incumbents a tool to silence their critics. The answer to speech you dislike is more speech, not a federal permission slip. For its critics, the case broke American democracy. It opened the floodgates to super PACs & unlimited outside money, & turned elections into auctions where a few hundred families & corporations drown out everyone else. When a sliver of the wealthiest Americans funds the campaigns, candidates listen to them, not to you. That isn't free speech, the argument goes. It's legalized corruption wearing the First Amendment as a costume. One question every voter feels in a democracy that increasingly answers to its donors. Ilya Shapiro is a senior fellow & director of constitutional studies at the Manhattan Institute & has filed more than 500 Supreme Court amicus briefs over his career. The author of Lawless: The Miseducation of America's Elites & Supreme Disorder, he's one of the country's most prominent free-speech-first voices on constitutional law. If you want the case that Citizens United got the First Amendment exactly right, he's your guy. Lawrence Lessig is the Roy L. Furman Professor of Law & Leadership at Harvard Law School & the founder of Equal Citizens. A former Scalia & Posner clerk who turned from copyright law to the fight against money in politics, he wrote Republic, Lost: How Money Corrupts Congress & ran a 2016 presidential campaign built entirely around the issue. He has testified before the Senate against Citizens United & the rise of super PACs, & is currently litigating to push the Court to revisit it. If you want the case that Citizens United corrupted American democracy, he's the person to ask. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Humor. Tension. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.
