events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. Happy hour runs from 2 to 4 on Saturday, October 10th, out on the water with the harbor & the skyline as the backdrop.nWhat to Expect:nA cross-section of people working on cities & public systems: public servants, technologists, founders, funders, consultants, & nonprofit operatorsnGenuine conversations across different corners of civic & urban tech: different roles, different focus areas, all in one placenNo sales pitches, no panels, just good companynFun prizes via our always-popular raffle nOptional activities before the happy hour so you can make a full island day of itnMake a Full Day of It:nThe main extra is a volunteer session with the Billion Oyster Project. They're restoring NY Harbor with oyster reefs, a natural fit for a group that spends its weekdays working on cities & public systems.nYou can also join Jer Thorp for Bird Data Portraits from 1 to 2. Jer is a data artist & bird enthusiast, & he'll help you make a data portrait of your favorite local bird using data from eBird. All materials will be provided, & you'll wrap up right as the happy hour begins.nPick Your Ticket:nHappy Hour Only: The main event, 2 to 4 on the water. Ferry over whenever works for you.nHappy Hour + Volunteer: The volunteer session, then straight into the happy hour. Starts with a 9:15am ferry & wraps at 2:30. Spots are limited, & we'll follow up with details.nHappy Hour + Workshop: Bird Data Portraits with Jer Thorp from 1 to 2, then straight into the happy hour. Materials provided, spots are limited.nWho Should Come:nIf you work in civic & urban tech, or anywhere adjacent, you belong here. Whether you've been to every happy hour or never made it to one, a Saturday afternoon on the island is a pretty great place to start. Expect good company & the kind of conversations that only happen when we get out from behind our screens.nGetting There:nGovernors Island is a short ferry ride from Lower Manhattan or Brooklyn. Suggested ferry times & a map to the exact spot on the island will be shared upon RSVP approval.nnFine print: By attending this event, you agree to abide by our code of conduct.

No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. events.name: The Quantified Self - Gary Wolf On What AI Can Actually Tell You About Your Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten - #AIWeekNY
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Coding Agents with Elastic Memory + The Evolution To Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week - Let's Talk about Jev)
events.description: We decode tech and market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, and decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors and operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, and taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, and testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL and connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in and Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, and a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, and it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news and wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Sobremesa  A Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

Space is limited. Maximum team size is four. All attendees must submit an application & be approved to attend. If selected as a finalist we require one person from your team to record a demo on-site September 26th which will then be displayed at .local NYC. To be eligible to win, finalists must also be available on September 30th to attend MongoDB.local NYC & present their project.

events.name: The Veiled Truth Unga 81 | An Evening Of Women, Culture & Global Impact
events.description: A Philanthropic Fashion & Cultural Experience During UNGA 81Saturday, September 26, 2026 | 5:00 PM29 Nassau Avenue | Brooklyn, New York Fashion  Philanthropy  Diplomacy  Women's Health  Culture  Global Leadership During United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week, an extraordinary community of global leaders, philanthropists, fashion & beauty executives, entrepreneurs, creators, healthcare voices, cultural figures, & changemakers will come together in New York City for The Veiled Truth. This is not simply a fashion show. It is not simply a fundraiser. It is a room designed to create conversations, relationships & impact. In collaboration with Eloquence Production, Mahogany Hospitality Group, & 1nfluenc3 Media, across an immersive three-story experience in Brooklyn, guests will move through an evening where fashion becomes storytelling, culture becomes connection, philanthropy becomes action, & influence becomes an opportunity to create meaningful change. At the center of the evening is one powerful idea: The conversations we bring into the light have the power to change what comes next. THE EXPERIENCEThe evening begins at 5:00 PM with cocktails, curated brand experiences, beauty & wellness activations, media, photography & intentional networking. At 6:00 PM, the main experience begins. Guests will experience: Curated Designer Runway PresentationsGlobal Leadership & Goodwill MessagesWomen's Health Stories & ConversationsLive Cultural PerformancesBeauty Atelier & Creator ExperiencesWomen. Health. Impact. Opportunity. Leadership PanelLive Philanthropic AuctionMedia & Professional PhotographyCocktails & Curated Brand ExperiencesIntentional Networking with a Global Community The featured panel begins at 7:30 PM. FEATURED KEYNOTEHer Excellency, Ambassador Professor Olufolake AbdulRazaq First Lady of Kwara State  Chairperson Nigeria Governors Spouses' Forum A distinguished diplomat, humanitarian, & advocate for women & community development, Her Excellency has dedicated her career to public service, gender advancement, & expanding opportunity for women & underserved communities. At The Veiled Truth, she will deliver a keynote centered on women, leadership, health, service, opportunity, & collective impact. The evening asks: How do we create a world in which women can lead, thrive, & build opportunity without sacrificing their health or wellbeing? SPECIAL GUEST SPEAKER Netflix's Owning ManhattanLuxury Real Estate Leader  Entrepreneur  Media Personality Jordan joins the evening to explore the power of visibility, relationships, storytelling, personal brand & influence-and how showing up authentically in the right rooms can create extraordinary opportunities. WOMEN. HEALTH. IMPACT. OPPORTUNITY.The Veiled Truth creates space for conversations that too often remain behind closed doors. Women's health. Mental & hormonal wellbeing. Access to essential healthcare & medications. Economic opportunity. Entrepreneurship. Leadership. Identity. Sustainability. Fashion. events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

Deals in the room - one matched meeting at a time.

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: Papers We Love
events.description: Papers We Love, Espresso AI, & Antithesis are pleased to present the September edition of PwL. Papers We Love is a community of programmers who love reading & discussing computer science papers. What was the last paper within the realm of computing you read & loved? What did it inspire you to build or tinker with? Come share the ideas in an awesome academic or research paper with fellow engineers, programmers, & paper-readers. Lead a session & show off code you wrote that implements these ideas, or just give us the lowdown on the paper. Otherwise, just come, listen, learn, & discuss. Speaker: Samuel Laferriere More about Sam: I'm a Staff Software Engineer at Seismic, where I work on the execution layer of an EVM-compatible privacy L1 - a reth fork running BFT consensus inside TDX enclaves. Before that I spent three years at EigenLabs, where I led the integrations team for EigenDA, a high-throughput BFT blobstore, building & maintaining its rollup integrations (Optimism, zkSync, & others). For the details, have a look at my resume. I work mostly in Rust & Go on distributed systems: BFT consensus + blobstore, EVM, & confidential compute. Before blockchain, I did academic research in robotics, developing Koopman-based control algorithms for self-driving cars & quadrotors. I completed my Master's degree at the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA), where I developed Bayesian optimization algorithms for neurostimulation, & before that earned my bachelor's in mathematics & computer science at McGill University. Paper: https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~evans/cs551/saltzer/ Title: What Saltzer & Schroeder knew in 1975 about the agents we're building in 2026 Supporting Papers: Hardy, The Confused Deputy (1988)  Miller, Yee & Shapiro, Capability Myths Demolished (2003) Outline: Every discussion of sandboxing AI agents starts with the wrong noun. Container or microVM? gVisor or WASI? Those choices answer where computation happens. They say nothing about what authority that computation can exercise - & an agent inside a perfectly isolated VM can still exfiltrate your source through an allowed API, spend your cloud credentials, or push to main. Saltzer & Schroeder framed the real problem fifty years ago, with three of their eight design principles directly relevant to agent sandboxing problem: 1. Complete mediation turns out to be the whole reason an LLM proxy counts as security rather than decoration: the sandbox is enforcement only if the workload cannot route around it. 2. Least privilege is where agents genuinely break the classical model, because an agent's useful authority changes with its plan - authority becomes a runtime protocol, not a static profile. 3. Saltzer & Schroeder warned that a protection mechanism people find annoying will be circumvented by the people it protects. Fifty years later, the most popular sandbox configuration in the industry is --dangerously-skip-permissions. To close, a detour through Hardy's two-page note from 1988. Prompt injection is not a new vulnerability class - it's the confused deputy with a natural-language calling convention, & an LLM is the perfect confused deputy: maximally helpful, broadly authorized, & structurally unable to tell a request from data. The fix Hardy proposed is the fix Google's CaMeL rediscovered in 2025. 6:30pm - Doors 7:00pm - Speaker begins PwL curate a repository of papers & places to find them. Contributions welcome via PR. Join the PWL Discord & hop into the #nyc channel: Join Discord Server Papers We Love has a Code of Conduct. Be good to each other & to the PWL community.

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

events.name: Agentic Security - BSides NYC Week
events.description: Agentic Security NYC is a practitioner-only gathering for security engineers & leaders actually running AI agents in production not a conference, not a panel, & not a place to pitch a product. We ran the first one in August. This one lands during BSidesNYC week. The format: a small room, real conversation, no slides. Space is limited.

events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. events.name: NYFW Debrief - Fashion Mixer
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. And by the time it's over, everyone needs a minute to actually talk about what happened. That's what this is. Once the tents come down & the last show wraps, we're getting the industry back in one room, no seating charts, no dress codes to stress over, no rushing between venues. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. Whether you were front row every day or watching it all unfold from your feed, come compare notes with people who get it. What to expect: Open conversation on the season's best (and most bewildering) moments Drinks & light bites (cash bar) Genuinely good networking (the kind that happens when everyone's a little more relaxed than they were all week) A room full of people worth exchanging numbers with Who it's for:Anyone in or around the fashion industry, designers, stylists, editors, marketers, PR, buyers, creatives, & the people who make fashion week actually happen behind the scenes. Dress code: however you want. You've earned a break from the outfit planning. Mark your calendar now Fashion Forward is a NYC-based community connecting fashion founders, designers, photographers, stylists, & creative leaders through curated experiences that favor depth, quality, & real connection over crowded rooms. By RSVP'ing, you agree to receive occasional marketing communications that can be shared with third parties & acknowledge that photography & video may be captured during the event for promotional purposes.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week - Personal AI agents  Muse, Instinct, & fight for your inbox)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week - The Reality of Data Centers in Space)
events.description: We decode tech and market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, and decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors and operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, and taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, and testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL and connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in and Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, and a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" and a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, and maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate and energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital and infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news and wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Alex Chung Presented by Surface AI "As the cost of code goes to zero, distribution is your only moat." While marketing, distribution, & go-to-market are established fields with many tried & true methods, each startup's playbook will be as unique as its company. To help companies understand, define, & grow their distribution, Ari Spool of Surface AI brings together a selection of startup marketing leaders for a breakfast panel to strategize. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago & an MBA from Chicago Booth. This conversation gets into the core challenge of her work: how to take a product that customers don't fully understand, build credibility around it, find the right audience, & convert interest into lasting growth. The principles apply well beyond telehealth. Outside of work, Alex is training for her third marathon, in Tokyo. Surface AI is an autonomous landing-page optimization engine. events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.name: Distribution Is Your Moat
events.description: Distribution is Your Moat: A series on Distribution & Marketing for Startups August 6 9:30 am: Innovation Is Your Moat ft. Alex Chung Presented by Surface AI "As the cost of code goes to zero, distribution is your only moat." While marketing, distribution, & go-to-market are established fields with many tried & true methods, each startup's playbook will be as unique as its company. To help companies understand, define, & grow their distribution, Ari Spool of Surface AI brings together a selection of startup marketing leaders for a breakfast panel to strategize. Refreshments by Donut Pub. Alex Chung is Head of Growth at System, a telehealth company built around clinician-prescribed peptide therapies. Alex has worked on both sides of the growth equation. Before System, she led growth at a consumer AI startup. Before that, she invested as a venture capitalist. That mix shapes how she evaluates markets, builds trust in unfamiliar categories, & turns early attention into real revenue. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago & an MBA from Chicago Booth. This conversation gets into the core challenge of her work: how to take a product that customers don't fully understand, build credibility around it, find the right audience, & convert interest into lasting growth. The principles apply well beyond telehealth. Outside of work, Alex is training for her third marathon, in Tokyo. Surface AI is an autonomous landing-page optimization engine. We connect to your existing site with one line of code - a quick setup through your CMS. From there Surface automatically generates & tests new headlines, CTAs, layouts, & images in brand voice, shifting traffic toward what's winning & continuously optimizing over time. All attendees will receive a free 14-day trial of Surface!

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/
