events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. events.name: Coding Agents with Elastic Memory + The Evolution To Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: The Quantified Self - Gary Wolf On What AI Can Actually Tell You About Your Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: The Veiled Truth Unga 81 | An Evening Of Women, Culture & Global Impact
events.description: A Philanthropic Fashion & Cultural Experience During UNGA 81Saturday, September 26, 2026 | 5:00 PM29 Nassau Avenue | Brooklyn, New York Fashion  Philanthropy  Diplomacy  Women's Health  Culture  Global Leadership During United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week, an extraordinary community of global leaders, philanthropists, fashion & beauty executives, entrepreneurs, creators, healthcare voices, cultural figures, & changemakers will come together in New York City for The Veiled Truth. This is not simply a fashion show. It is not simply a fundraiser. It is a room designed to create conversations, relationships & impact. In collaboration with Eloquence Production, Mahogany Hospitality Group, & 1nfluenc3 Media, across an immersive three-story experience in Brooklyn, guests will move through an evening where fashion becomes storytelling, culture becomes connection, philanthropy becomes action, & influence becomes an opportunity to create meaningful change. At the center of the evening is one powerful idea: The conversations we bring into the light have the power to change what comes next. THE EXPERIENCEThe evening begins at 5:00 PM with cocktails, curated brand experiences, beauty & wellness activations, media, photography & intentional networking. At 6:00 PM, the main experience begins. Guests will experience: Curated Designer Runway PresentationsGlobal Leadership & Goodwill MessagesWomen's Health Stories & ConversationsLive Cultural PerformancesBeauty Atelier & Creator ExperiencesWomen. Health. Impact. Opportunity. Leadership PanelLive Philanthropic AuctionMedia & Professional PhotographyCocktails & Curated Brand ExperiencesIntentional Networking with a Global Community The featured panel begins at 7:30 PM. FEATURED KEYNOTEHer Excellency, Ambassador Professor Olufolake AbdulRazaq First Lady of Kwara State  Chairperson Nigeria Governors Spouses' Forum A distinguished diplomat, humanitarian, & advocate for women & community development, Her Excellency has dedicated her career to public service, gender advancement, & expanding opportunity for women & underserved communities. At The Veiled Truth, she will deliver a keynote centered on women, leadership, health, service, opportunity, & collective impact. The evening asks: How do we create a world in which women can lead, thrive, & build opportunity without sacrificing their health or wellbeing? SPECIAL GUEST SPEAKER Netflix's Owning ManhattanLuxury Real Estate Leader  Entrepreneur  Media Personality Jordan joins the evening to explore the power of visibility, relationships, storytelling, personal brand & influence-and how showing up authentically in the right rooms can create extraordinary opportunities. WOMEN. HEALTH. IMPACT. OPPORTUNITY.The Veiled Truth creates space for conversations that too often remain behind closed doors. Women's health. Mental & hormonal wellbeing. Access to essential healthcare & medications. Economic opportunity. Entrepreneurship. Leadership. Identity. Sustainability. Fashion. Culture. Because women should not have to choose between their health & their ambition, their wellbeing & their careers, or their families & their ability to lead. The evening connects these conversations to three broader global development priorities: SDG 5 - Gender EqualitySDG 8 - Decent Work & Economic GrowthSDG 12 - Responsible Consumption & Production Women. Economic Opportunity. Sustainability. PHILANTHROPY WITH PURPOSEProceeds from tickets & the auction will support participating designers, event production, & charitable partners, including organizations focused on women's health & empowerment. The evening will include a live philanthropic auction supporting designated initiatives advancing women's access, dignity, wellbeing, empowerment & opportunity, including: Waterlight Save InitiativeFlow With Pride Impact HubHerGhana This is philanthropy designed not simply to raise awareness-but to inspire compassion, participation & action. THE ROOMThe Veiled Truth is intentionally bringing together a community rarely found in one room: First Ladies & Global Leaders  Philanthropists & Family Offices  Fashion & Beauty Executives  Designers & Creative Leaders  Healthcare & Wellness Voices  Entrepreneurs & Corporate Leaders  Creators & Media  Cultural Figures  African Diaspora Leaders  International Guests Visiting New York During UNGA High-Level Week The goal isn't simply attendance. It's connection. Come prepared to meet someone you didn't know you needed to meet. Start a conversation. Share an idea. Build a relationship. And leave with something that continues long after the evening ends. DRESS CODEDRESS TO IMPRESS  THEME: HEAVENLY Come ready to be photographed. EVENT DETAILSSaturday, September 26, 202629 Nassau Avenue | Brooklyn, New York 5:00 PM - Doors Open / Welcome Experience6:00 PM - Main Program7:30 PM - Featured Leadership Conversation Attendance is curated. Registration does not guarantee admission & may be subject to approval. Space is limited. Awareness  Compassion  Action  Impact Because every woman deserves to be seen, heard & healed. HOST Richie HoseinFounder & CEO, FreeHealth.ai  1nfluenc3 MediaEntrepreneur  Investor  Community Builder Richie Hosein brings together leaders across healthcare, business, media, technology & culture through experiences designed to turn meaningful connections into lasting impact. events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. Happy hour runs from 2 to 4 on Saturday, October 10th, out on the water with the harbor & the skyline as the backdrop.nWhat to Expect:nA cross-section of people working on cities & public systems: public servants, technologists, founders, funders, consultants, & nonprofit operatorsnGenuine conversations across different corners of civic & urban tech: different roles, different focus areas, all in one placenNo sales pitches, no panels, just good companynFun prizes via our always-popular raffle nOptional activities before the happy hour so you can make a full island day of itnMake a Full Day of It:nThe main extra is a volunteer session with the Billion Oyster Project. They're restoring NY Harbor with oyster reefs, a natural fit for a group that spends its weekdays working on cities & public systems.nYou can also join Jer Thorp for Bird Data Portraits from 1 to 2. Jer is a data artist & bird enthusiast, & he'll help you make a data portrait of your favorite local bird using data from eBird. All materials will be provided, & you'll wrap up right as the happy hour begins.nPick Your Ticket:nHappy Hour Only: The main event, 2 to 4 on the water. Ferry over whenever works for you.nHappy Hour + Volunteer: The volunteer session, then straight into the happy hour. Starts with a 9:15am ferry & wraps at 2:30. Spots are limited, & we'll follow up with details.nHappy Hour + Workshop: Bird Data Portraits with Jer Thorp from 1 to 2, then straight into the happy hour. Materials provided, spots are limited.nWho Should Come:nIf you work in civic & urban tech, or anywhere adjacent, you belong here. events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: NYFW Debrief: Fashion Networking Event
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. And by the time it's over, everyone needs a minute to actually talk about what happened. That's what this is. Once the tents come down & the last show wraps, we're getting the industry back in one room, no seating charts, no dress codes to stress over, no rushing between venues. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. Whether you were front row every day or watching it all unfold from your feed, come compare notes with people who get it. What to expect: Open conversation on the season's best (and most bewildering) moments Drinks & light bites (cash bar) Genuinely good networking (the kind that happens when everyone's a little more relaxed than they were all week) A room full of people worth exchanging numbers with Who it's for:Anyone in or around the fashion industry, designers, stylists, editors, marketers, PR, buyers, creatives, & the people who make fashion week actually happen behind the scenes. Dress code: however you want. You've earned a break from the outfit planning. Mark your calendar now Fashion Forward is a NYC-based community connecting fashion founders, designers, photographers, stylists, & creative leaders through curated experiences that favor depth, quality, & real connection over crowded rooms. By RSVP'ing, you agree to receive occasional marketing communications that can be shared with third parties & acknowledge that photography & video may be captured during the event for promotional purposes.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Unique AI Presents - New AI Teammates
events.description: Meet Your AI Teammates: Remy, Casey, & IvyThree AI teammates, one perpetual memory.Any firm can deploy a generic AI assistant. But these tools weren't built to remember your clients or understand your relationships. Your firm already has the intelligence. What's missing is memory. What your firm knows about a client sits in inboxes, CRM notes, & people's heads. It gets rebuilt from scratch every time, & it walks out the door when someone leaves. Remy, Casey, & Ivy fix that - each one built for a different function, each backed by perpetual memory. Remy handles financial advisory, working the client lifecycle end to end - onboarding, meeting preparation, account review - backed by a continuously updated client memory. For compliance, Casey runs perpetual KYC & Source of Wealth work, flagging risk before it reaches a client. Her second brain holds the full relationship & case history. Ivy sits with investor relations, turning a living investor memory into faster, more consistent RFP & DDQ responses.   Join Dana Ritter, Chief Product Officer & the Unique AI Executive Leadership Team for a live look at the Teammates & what agentic AI can do for wealth & asset management.    Agenda 6:00 to 7:00 pm: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres 7:00 to 7:45 pm: 7:00 to 7:20 pm: Launch & live demo 7:20 to 7:45 pm: Client testimonial 7:45 pm onward: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres   What you'll see live We'll showcase how Remy helps advisors onboard clients, prep for meetings, & run account reviews - all while building a client memory that syncs back to your CRM. We'll also preview how Casey supports compliance teams & how Ivy helps investor relations teams manage RFP & DDQ workflows. Discover what agentic AI can do across all functions at your firm & connect with peers across wealth & asset management tackling the same questions.  Who should attend COOs, CTOs, & Heads of AI exploring agentic solutions to improve operational efficiency & scale technology investments within wealth & asset management platforms Financial Advisors, Wealth Advisors, & Relationship Managers who want to improve client prep, reduce administrative drag, & scale personalized service Heads of Compliance, KYC, & Financial Crime looking to modernize review & oversight workflows Heads of Investor Relations handling investor updates, DDQs, & RFPs at volume Learn more about Unique AI at unique.ai.

events.name: Building Better Trading Strategies w/ AI
events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Global Forum On Circular Economy & Urban Resilience
events.description: Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban ResilienceDate: Friday, September 25, 2026Venue: Club 135 by IndustriousAddress: 135 W 50th Street, New York, NY 10020Format: Invitation OnlyExpected Attendance: Approximately 200 participantsLanguage: EnglishHost: Office of the City of Yokohama Representative to the AmericasSponsors: ITO ENPartners: Greennex Global, ShibuLA Ventures, CleanLeap & Deep Tech Forum About the ForumThe global economy is undergoing a profound transformation driven by geopolitical uncertainty, the restructuring of global supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, & growing demand for energy & critical resources. Against this backdrop, the circular economy is emerging not only as an environmental agenda, but also as a strategic approach to strengthening economic competitiveness, resource security, industrial resilience, & sustainable growth. Held during Climate Week NYC 2026, the Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban Resilience will bring together city & regional government representatives, international organizations, corporations, investors, financial institutions, startups, & climate innovation leaders from Asia, North America, Europe, & beyond. Through business showcases, reverse pitches, keynote remarks, & cross-sector discussions, the Forum will connect urban challenges with innovation, investment, & international partnerships. It will also explore how cities can serve as platforms for collaboration among businesses, startups, investors, & global institutions. The Forum will serve as an important step toward Yokohama's major international initiatives in 2027, including GREENEXPO 2027, Asia-Pacific Circular Cities Forum (APCC-Forum), the Asia-Pacific Urban Forum, & broader international dialogue on circular & resilient urban development. View the Speaker ListMorning Programme: Business & Innovation ForumConnecting Innovation Ecosystems Across Asia, North America, & Europe 9:00-9:30 Registration & Networking Coffee9:30-9:40 Welcome Remarks9:40-10:30 Startup ShowcaseSelected startups will present innovative technologies & business models in the fields of the circular economy, climate technology, & urban sustainability. The session is designed to create opportunities for pilot projects, joint development, investment, strategic partnerships, & expansion into Japanese & broader Asian markets. Presenting Startups: TBD 10:30-11:20 Reverse PitchJapanese companies will present their business challenges, innovation priorities, & areas of interest to an audience of international startups. The session aims to identify potential partners & initiate discussions on joint development, pilot projects, & future business collaboration. Participating Companies: Nick Vega, Director on the Investments & Strategy team, Sumitomo Corporation Takeyori Nabeta, Business Development Manage at Chiyoda International Corporation / Venture Associate at DNX Ventures Junya Saka, Manager, Strategic Investment & Partnerships, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation Hirotaka Mori, Principal Researcher, Business Development & CVC, ENEOS Americas Additional companies: TBD 11:20-12:00 Innovation Leaders DialogueAI, the Circular Economy, & the Next Industrial Transformation Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries through major investment in semiconductors, data centers, digital infrastructure, & advanced industrial systems. At the same time, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition to a more sustainable & circular economy by improving efficiency across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI & the circular economy The potential of AI to improve resource efficiency & industrial decarbonization Partnerships needed to commercialize & scale next-generation technologies The roles of corporations, investors, & startups in the next industrial transformation Speakers: Durgesh Patel, Vice President, AI Center of Excellence, Hitachi Ray Hugel, CFA, Executive Director & Co-Head of Catalytic Capital & Private Credit, Closed Loop Partners Kazuhiko Nishioka, Co-Founder & CEO, Sun Metalon Kevin Ninomiya, CEO & Co-Founder, ShibuLA Ventures (Moderator) 12:00-1:30 Networking LunchAn opportunity for investors, startups, corporations, city leaders, & international organizations to connect across sectors, explore collaboration opportunities, & develop partnerships that can continue beyond the Forum. The networking lunch will also be open to participants attending the afternoon programme. Afternoon Programme: Policy & Leadership ForumAccelerating Circular Economy & Urban Resilience 1:30-1:40 Opening Remarks1:40-2:00 Keynote AddressThe Next Chapter of the Circular Economy: Competitiveness, Resilience, & Global Collaboration The circular economy is increasingly becoming a strategic framework for strengthening economic competitiveness, industrial resilience, resource security, & sustainable growth. The keynote will examine why accelerating the transition requires deeper collaboration among cities, businesses, investors, & international organizations, setting the stage for the Forum's discussions on innovation, partnerships, & global action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration Asia's rapid urbanization & growing policy ambition are making the region increasingly important to the global circular economy transition. Cities will play a central role in translating global goals into locally driven policies, partnerships, & practical action. This session will examine how Asian cities can work with global partners to accelerate circular solutions & create new opportunities for cooperation. Discussion themes include: Why Asia will be central to the next phase of the circular economy The role of cities in advancing circular solutions through policy, procurement, & partnerships Opportunities for collaboration between Asian cities & global partners Yokohama's role as a platform for international collaboration toward 2027 GREENEXPO 2027 & related international initiatives Speaker: Tomomi Yamashita, Director General for Global Initiatives, City of Yokohama Carlos Silva Filho, Member of United Nations Secretary-General's Advisory Board on Zero Waste 2:20-3:05 Session 2Investing in the Circular Economy: Innovation, Markets, & GrowthThe transition to a circular economy is creating new markets, attracting investment, & driving innovation across industries & cities worldwide. This session will explore how cities, businesses, investors, & innovation ecosystems can create market opportunities, attract capital & talent, & scale solutions capable of delivering both economic & environmental value. Discussion themes include: Emerging investment opportunities in the circular economy Building innovation ecosystems that attract capital & talent The role of cities in creating markets for circular solutions Public-private partnerships for scaling innovation Strengthening competitiveness through circular innovation Speakers: TBDModerator: TBD 3:05-3:50 Session 3Bridging Regions: Partnerships for Circular & Resilient Cities The circular transition cannot be delivered by cities, financial institutions, businesses, or international organizations acting independently. This session will explore how regional & global partnerships can connect urban priorities with technical expertise, investment, & implementation capacity. The discussion will focus on moving beyond the exchange of ideas toward concrete projects, financing mechanisms, & long-term collaboration. Discussion themes include: Connecting cities across Asia, North America, & other regions Mobilizing finance for circular & resilient urban projects Building pipelines of investable city projects Connecting cities with businesses, investors, & international institutions Scaling successful solutions across different markets Turning international dialogue into practical collaboration Continuing collaboration through international forums & Yokohama's initiatives in 2027 Speakers: Sandra Goldmark, Associate Dean for Engagement & Impact & Professor of Professional Practice, Columbia Climate School Local 2030 Coalition (Speaker TBA) Berat Senyerli, CEO of Bankable Zero Vijay Jagannathan, Senior Fellow at World Resources Institute (Moderator) 3:50-4:00 Closing RemarksWho Should AttendThe Forum is designed for: City & regional government representatives International organizations Corporations & business leaders Investors & financial institutions Startups & entrepreneurs Climate technology & circular economy experts Urban development & resilience professionals Innovation ecosystem leaders

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten - #AIWeekNY
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. RSVP to join us in NYC & stay in the loop. Come curious. Leave caffeinated-and a few steps closer to shipping.   Location: NYC, shared after RSVP Time: 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Cost: Free

events.name: Catalyzing Cities
events.description: Cities are increasingly expected to deliver climate resilience while navigating constrained budgets, aging infrastructure, & growing complexity. Yet many of the most impactful solutions already exist... the challenge is designing financing & partnership models that enable them to scale. This New York Climate Week, join Cool Climate Collective & Climate Vine, as we convene investors, city leaders, philanthropies & ecosystem partners for a discussion on how innovative financing structures & public-private collaboration can unlock catalytic outcomes for cities, particularly for New York. Drawing on emerging work in city outcomes & practical examples from around the world, we'll explore: New models for financing climate resilience beyond traditional procurement. How blended capital & partnership design can accelerate deployment. What is already working in practice & why. Lessons & systems insights informed by collaborators across the resilience ecosystem, including perspectives shared by our partners from UNDRR & Dark Matter Labs. The session is designed to be interactive, bringing together practitioners across sectors to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions, & identify opportunities for collaboration during Climate Week. Agenda 9:30 - 10:00 AM : Check-in & coffee networking 10:00 - 11:30 AM : Interactive discussion & programming 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM : Facilitated small-group discussions followed by open networking

events.name: AI & Sustainability Mgmt - Case Studies From The Field
events.description: This event is free entry with limited tickets available. The organizer will provide a calendar invite to guests up to capacity. If capacity is reached you will be notified. AI & Sustainability Management:Case Studies from the FieldAI is already playing a central role in many companies' sustainability strategy, management, & reporting efforts. Whether it is AI-based materiality, tools to assist in the calculation of greenhouse gas inventories, or AI-enabled sustainability reporting systems, this is an area of fast-moving innovation that has captured the imagination of sustainability practitioners. While we must take the environmental implications of AI usage seriously, we must also evaluate the potential that this technology represents - do the benefits outweigh the impacts? What We'll Explore: AI & Business Intelligence: How business intelligence data platforms are transforming data collection, analysis, & insight generation. AI-enabled sustainability - Is it worth the price?: What is the current state of the art knowledge in terms of the cost/benefit tradeoffs of AI in terms of environmental impacts? Building Qualitative & Quantitative Connections: How AI can help companies better understand the linkages between sustainability performance & financial performance. AI & Assurance: How AI-supported data processes & 3rd party verification connect. Is your organization ready for third party verification in the era of AI-based tools & processes? Speakers: Matt Gardner, Managing Partner at Sustainserv Julie Kae, VP of Sustainability at Qlik Technologies Julien Gervreau, Director at Sensiba LLP Who Should Attend:CSOs, CCOs, IROs, & sustainability professionals navigating the intersection of AI capabilities, reporting requirements, & stakeholder engagement in an increasingly complex sustainability landscape

events.name: Net Zero Value Chains - Advancing Credible Scope 3 Decarbonization
events.description: The corporate climate landscape is moving toward greater rigor, with growing expectations for companies to substantiate climate action through credible data, accounting, & reporting. The GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard (LSRS) introduces a more robust framework for accounting & reporting land-based emissions & CO removals. However, implementation remains challenging, with companies navigating supplier data gaps, limited traceability, allocation challenges, & evolving assurance expectations. At the same time, organizations are exploring how market-based approaches can help accelerate credible Scope 3 action beyond their direct operations. Join corporate sustainability leaders, standard setters, climate experts, & solution providers to explore two key developments shaping the future of value chain decarbonization: Panel 1: Implementing the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard Hear from experts & early adopters on the practical challenges of implementing the LSRS, including data quality, traceability, allocation, reporting, & assurance. Learn what organizations are doing today-and what may be needed to support scalable implementation in the years ahead. Speakers:Matt Ramlow, Senior Research Associate, GHG P Martha Stevenson, Senior Director, Strategy & Research, Forests, WWF Noora Singh, Senior Director, Global Sustainability, PepsiCoChristina O'Keefe, Head of Sustainability, North America, Kerry Panel 2: The emerging role of Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) Explore how carbon credits, environmental certificates, & other market-based approaches could support Scope 3 decarbonization. Hear the latest perspectives on developments across the GHG Protocol, AMI Standard, & SBTi's Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2, alongside practical insights from companies already piloting these approaches. Speakers:Alex Kazaglis, Chief Strategy Officer, SBTiDavid Spitzley, Director, Climate & Nature | Global Sustainability, StarbucksJacob Isaacson, Associate Director of Climate Strategy, 3DegreesCynthia Cummis, Senior Vice President Value Chain Strategies, ClimeCo The event will conclude with networking drinks, providing an opportunity to continue the conversation & connect with peers from across the corporate climate ecosystem. Who should attend? Corporate sustainability & climate leaders Scope 3 & procurement professionals Standards & accounting experts NGOs & policy stakeholders Sustainability consultants & solution providers Register now to secure your place.

events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: The Quantified Self - Gary Wolf On What AI Can Actually Tell You About Your Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.description: Distribution is Your Moat: A series on Distribution & Marketing for Startups August 6 9:30 am: Innovation Is Your Moat ft. Alex Chung Presented by Surface AI "As the cost of code goes to zero, distribution is your only moat." While marketing, distribution, & go-to-market are established fields with many tried & true methods, each startup's playbook will be as unique as its company. To help companies understand, define, & grow their distribution, Ari Spool of Surface AI brings together a selection of startup marketing leaders for a breakfast panel to strategize. Refreshments by Donut Pub. Alex Chung is Head of Growth at System, a telehealth company built around clinician-prescribed peptide therapies. Alex has worked on both sides of the growth equation. Before System, she led growth at a consumer AI startup. Before that, she invested as a venture capitalist. That mix shapes how she evaluates markets, builds trust in unfamiliar categories, & turns early attention into real revenue. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago & an MBA from Chicago Booth. This conversation gets into the core challenge of her work: how to take a product that customers don't fully understand, build credibility around it, find the right audience, & convert interest into lasting growth. The principles apply well beyond telehealth. Outside of work, Alex is training for her third marathon, in Tokyo. Surface AI is an autonomous landing-page optimization engine. events.name: Buildings & Materials Conference
events.description: WHERE BUILDING TECH & MATERIALS COME TOGETHERThe annual Buildings + Materials Conference explores innovation & emerging technology in the development, design, materials, & systems of buildings. The event examines the current state & trajectory of building planning & operational solutions, strategies, & processes, providing insights & guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, & challenges. Connect. Inform. Advance.The premier network for advancing innovation & catalyzing collaboration throughout the built environment ecosystem. It Began As a Digital Community Connecting, Sharing, & LearningIn the fall of 2013, BuiltWorlds analysts began harnessing the power of digital media, crowd sourcing, & open innovation, sharing what they were learning & who they were meeting via social media & drawing in ever more passionate, open, experts who shared even more insights & data. The resulting network effect produced a global community of thousands of people actively providing data & contacts, curated by our analyst team, who then shared with back with the community in the form of actionable insights & deeper understanding. From the Community, A Powerful Research Network EmergedBuiltWorlds emerged as a free community, fueled by subscribers & supported by a small groups of sponsors. However, as the community grew, more members of the community wanted to access more of BuiltWorlds' research & collaborate more actively with others in the community.  Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: The Energy Transition Deferred
events.description: The AI buildout has a bottleneck, & it isn't chips. It's power. Interconnection queues stretch for years, deals get signed under NDAs, & roughly 70% of Americans now oppose data centers in their own communities, with opposition crossing party lines. The energy transition everyone was promised keeps getting deferred by the race to feed the models. Yet new Princeton research points to an escape hatch. A 500-megawatt data center able to flex its grid demand for less than 1% of the year can reach full operation three to five years sooner than one that can't. Jesse Jenkins floated exactly that idea on Season One of Deep Tech LIVE, 18 months ago, when almost nobody was building that way. So is the real bottleneck electrons, or is it contracts & consent? Dr. Jesse Jenkins leads Princeton's ZERO Lab & the REPEAT Project, & was profiled by the Wall Street Journal as The Professor Helping Guide Billions in Climate Spending.' He has since added another hat, co-founding Firma Power, where he serves as CTO, working on the challenge of supplying clean firm power to hyperscale data centers. Jesse & moderator Duncan Turner (General Partner & Managing Director at SOSV HAX) will dig into what the analyst sees now that he is the one selling the power: Why flexibility, not new generation, may be the fastest path to powering AI Which new energy technologies are actually helping - from grid hardware & storage to geothermal & nuclear The exploding opposition to data centers crossing party lines sending midterm candidates scrambling (is it NIMBYism, or something else?) How clean firm power can be delivered to the right places at the right prices and, potentially, make hyperscalers & communities happy Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot! This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register & are approved.  Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, & technologists.

events.name: State Of Supply Chain Sustainability Report Launch
events.description: The 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report examines a paradox at the heart of corporate sustainability today: commitment is rising, even as the ability to deliver is becoming more difficult. The report explores how companies are responding to geopolitical disruption, governance gaps, fragmented sustainability data, rapid advances in Industrial & Agentic AI, & the broader challenge of embedding sustainability more deeply into supply chain decisions & operations. Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.
