events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.name: Backing Innovation - How States Investing In The Future
events.description: State venture funds are playing an increasingly important role in building regional innovation ecosystems. This panel brings together leaders from three of the Northeast's most active public VC programs - Connecticut Innovations, New York State's NY Ventures, & the New Jersey Economic Development Authority - for a candid discussion on how government capital is shaping the next generation of startups. Panelists will discuss how their funds source & evaluate deals, what differentiates public venture capital from traditional VC, & where they see the biggest opportunities for founders & investors across the region. Stick around afterwards for a happy hour with the founders & VCs. Meet the panelists: Danny Qiao is a Director on Connecticut Innovations' investment team, where he leads the team's consumer & international investment efforts. Prior to CI, he led consumer investing at Sweater Ventures, backing brands like IQBAR, Graza, Nomadica, OROS, & Havenly. He began his career at Accenture Strategy & later covered financial sponsors & financial institutions in investment banking at BNP Paribas. Danny holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management & a BS from Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations. Jennifer Tegan is the Managing Director of Empire State Development's New York Ventures, where she oversees over $320 million in investment programs aimed at fueling New York's startup ecosystem. Since joining in 2020, she has managed direct & indirect investment funds including the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund & the Emerging & Regional Manager Partner Fund (a fund of funds). An experienced investor & advocate, Jennifer previously spent 18 years as a partner at Cayuga Venture Fund. She has served on the board of the National Venture Capital Association & held leadership roles with Tompkins Financial Corporation & the Upstate Capital Association of New York. Jennifer holds an MBA from Cornell University, an MS from the University of Cincinnati, & a BA from Smith College. John Wisniewski is the Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives & Venture Products at New Jersey Economic Development Authority. His responsibilities include oversight of the state's investment into Strategic Innovation Centers, & venture investment programs. John started his career with ExxonMobil where he held various positions developing projects in the US & internationally.  He ran a private equity infrastructure fund based in the Middle East for Arcapita Bank, & then switched to venture capital working with Clean Energy Ventures Group. John has a BS in Chemical Engineering from Cooper Union, & an MBA from Rice University. Meet the hosts: Connecticut Innovations is Connecticut's venture capital arm, investing in early & growth-stage biotech, IT, & deep tech companies. NY Ventures is New York State's innovation venture capital fund, backing high-growth startups across the state. NJEDA's Venture Products team supports New Jersey's innovation ecosystem, including through the New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. Meet the sponsors: Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups & the accountants supporting them. With banking setup in minutes, cashback cards, & tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused, backed by support that goes to the end of the earth to help you win. Rho is a fintech company, not a bank. Checking & card services are provided by Webster Bank, N.A., member FDIC; savings account services are provided by American Deposit Management Co. & its partner banks. KPMG Private provides specialized advisory, audit, tax, & strategic consulting services tailored for emerging growth companies, startups, & private enterprises scaling up through various lifecycle stages. Whether you're launching a startup or accelerating your growth, the Emerging Growth team offers strategic insights & resources designed to support your business journey. #nyc #venturecapital #government

events.name: Turning Geospatial Data Into Action On Pollution & Climate
events.description: Join Leading Voices Shaping the Future of Climate & Conservation Technology SkyTruth is convening the field's top leaders & practitioners for a high-impact gathering focused on one overarching question: how can geospatial data accelerate our collective progress on the planet's most pressing environmental challenges? This isn't just a series of panels, but a working session designed to surface gaps, spark partnerships, & drive action. It is built around three of the most consequential data frontiers in environmental science today: Exposing Ocean Pollution at ScaleBe part of the conversation around SkyTruth's groundbreaking new report revealing the extent, concentration, & culpability of chronic oil pollution in our oceans - a major advancement for mapping human industrial activity at sea & an essential step towards holding polluters accountable. Uncovering the Hidden Costs of Oil & GasJoin leading organizations tackling one of climate's biggest blind spots: emissions caused by the offshore oil & gas industry. Help close the gap between detection & action on the sector's least-visible but most damaging climate impacts. Protecting Biodiversity from Industrial ThreatsContribute to cross-sector efforts spanning philanthropy, government, & the environmental movement to measure & mitigate the impact of mining operations on the world's most critical ecosystems. About the host: SkyTruth (skytruth.org) is a conservation technology nonprofit that leverages satellite imagery & environmental data to create tools & develop insights that drive accountability, accelerate climate action, & support biodiversity protection. Connect with us: LinkedIn: /skytruth Instagram, BlueSky: @skytruthFacebook: facebook.com/skytruthSign up for our newsletter: ttps://bit.ly/SkyTruth-newsletter

events.name: From Risk To Oppty - How Capital Can Enable Climate Resilience
events.description: Climate & nature-related risk is accelerating faster than markets can price it, & insurers are often the first to feel it. The same dynamic appears elsewhere: investors hesitate to finance conservation & adaptation projects, while financial inclusion in emerging economies stalls. These share the same underlying reason, that the risk has outpaced the tools we have to price & fund it. Swissnex, in collaboration with the Consulate General of Switzerland in New York, Swiss Business Hub USA, Greater Zurich Area, & Global Infrastructure Basel, convenes senior professionals from banking, insurance, asset management, development finance, policy, research, & community organizations for a single morning that follows this market failure end to end. Together we will explore where it originates, to how capital rebuilds what has been lost, what actually gets built afterward, & what else still stands in the way. Switzerland is well positioned to convene this conversation. It sits at the center of global re/insurance, while its banks & insurers are increasingly operating within a regulatory framework that integrates climate & nature-related risk governance, alongside a democratically mandated net-zero target for 2050. This puts Switzerland in a position where voluntary commitments are increasingly being tested against financial & regulatory realities. Bringing together representatives from government, finance, insurance, & development institutions, this program explores how climate & nature-related risks can be better measured, priced, & financed. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Coding Agents with Elastic Memory + The Evolution To Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. RSVP to join us in NYC & stay in the loop. Come curious. Leave caffeinated-and a few steps closer to shipping.   Location: NYC, shared after RSVP Time: 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Cost: Free

events.name: Circular Innovation & Resilient Futures - Insights From The Arctic
events.description: Bringing together leaders from business, Indigenous communities, policymaking, finance, & academia, this session explores how Arctic innovation, from Indigenous knowledge to cutting-edge circular economy solutions, can deliver practical & scalable responses to climate, economic, & geopolitical challenges. The Arctic is experiencing some of the world's fastest environmental, economic, & geopolitical change. In response, Indigenous communities, businesses, researchers, policymakers, & investors are developing innovative approaches that strengthen resilience while supporting sustainable economic growth. Long before the term circular economy existed, Arctic Indigenous Peoples developed knowledge systems grounded in stewardship, resource efficiency, & long-term thinking. Today, these principles are complemented by advances in circular business models, clean technologies, sustainable finance, & policy innovation. Finland has emerged as a global leader in circular economy solutions, while Indigenous leadership across Spmi & the wider Arctic continues to demonstrate how traditional knowledge & community-driven approaches can shape resilient futures.

events.description: 150 seats. One room. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). This year, we're raising the bar & want to double that number.  WHO'S BEEN IN THE ROOM: Invited Family Offices & Institutional Capital  KKR ($361B+ AUM, New York) - Global investment firm. Principal from KKR's Sustainability & Capital Formation team joining us.  Generation Investment Management ($44B+ AUM, San Francisco / London) - Al Gore's sustainable investment firm. Founding Partner Colin le Duc returning for the second consecutive year.  Rockefeller Foundation ($6B endowment, New York) - Director of Energy Technology & Innovation Shunondo Basu. Net-zero endowment commitment. Speaker at both 2025 summits, returning for 2026  Merit France / CMA CGM Saade Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  Energy Impact Partners ($4.5B AUM, New York) - Climate infrastructure VC backed by 80+ global utility & energy partners. Returning for 2026.  Schmidt Sciences (Multi-$B, Palo Alto) - Eric Schmidt's frontier science & technology initiative. Returning for 2026  Wittington Ventures ($500M venture platform / $21B Weston family, Canada) - The venture arm of one of North America's largest private family enterprises. Sending a new team member for the third consecutive event.  B Capital Group / EE Capital (Eduardo Saverin's $9B+ venture platform, Singapore) - One of Asia's most active frontier & climate tech investors, recently hired Temasek's Head of Sustainable Investing.  Merit France / CMA CGM Saad Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  TIME Ventures / Benioff Family ($300M+ committed to frontier tech & climate, San Francisco) - Salesforce founder Marc Benioff's personal fund backing fusion energy, reforestation, & ecopreneur ventures.  Ho Family Office / Banyan Group (100+ properties across 28 countries, Singapore) - Founder Ho Kwon Ping built a global hospitality empire from an abandoned tin mine. Now deploying family capital into resilience & adaptation across Asia.  PETRONAS Ventures ($800M+ CVC, Malaysia) - The energy giant's corporate venture arm, backing breakthrough energy startups from Kuala Lumpur to Silicon Valley.  Aglaia Family Office (Leading multi-family office, Singapore) - Independent MFO serving UHNW families from SEA.  BlackRock ($11.5T+ AUM, New York) - World's largest asset manager.  SK Discovery ($10B+ market cap, Seoul) - Korean industrial conglomerate's venture investment arm. Deploying across materials, energy, & chemicals innovation.  BASF Corporate Venture Capital ($87B revenue parent, Germany) - Venture arm of the world's largest chemical company.  Hennessy Capital Group ($1.8B+ deployed via SPAC, Houston) - Five completed climate & industrial technology SPACs.  SOSV HAX IndieBio ($1.5B AUM, San Francisco) - The #1 most active climate tech venture investor globally. GP returning for 2026 Invited Founders & Fund Managers  Nicholas Flanders - Co-Founder & CEO, Twelve (turning CO into jet fuel, backed by TPG Rise Climate)  Martijn Lopes Cardozo - Partner, Regeneration.VC (Leonardo DiCaprio-backed circular economy fund)  Brian Riordan - Co-Founder & COO, Avalanche Energy (compact fusion systems advancing next-generation clean energy)  Daria Saharova - General Partner, World Fund (350M European climate VC. Joining SF 2026)  Mira Inbar - Partner, ArcTern Ventures ($500M+ deployed into climate tech across 40+ companies. Joining SF 2026)  Jocelyn Matyas - Cisco Foundation (supporting climate innovation & early-stage impact ventures)  More speakers to be announced $110 BILLION in committed capital represented in this room. This is an 150-person event. Every seat is curated. No expo booths. No filler panels. Just the people writing checks & the founders building the future. OUR TRACK RECORD: WHO HAS BEEN IN THE ROOM: Since 2023, Family Offices & Investors summits & The Climate & Frontier Tech Coalition have convened 280+ verified family offices & LPs alumni across 8 cities - including New York, San Francisco, Paris, Singapore, & Abu Dhabi. Crown Property Bureau) PTT Group (Thailand) - ~$50B+ (PTT Public Company market cap + subsidiaries; state-owned energy) NEOM - ~$500B (official project budget; backed by PIF, Saudi Arabia's $925B sovereign wealth fund) TotalEnergies - ~$160B (market cap; $2B+ annual venture/low-carbon investment) Shell - ~$200B (market cap; Shell Ventures active in energy transition & deep tech) Frontier & Venture Capital Firms Who Have Attended: LowerCarbon Capital - ~$2B+ (AUM across 4 funds; Chris Sacca-led climate VC) SOSV - ~$1.5B (AUM; most active deep tech pre-seed investor globally) DCVC - ~$3B+ (total AUM across multiple deep tech funds + DCVC Climate Select ~$400M) Breakthrough Energy Ventures - ~$3.5B+ (committed capital across 3 flagship funds; backed by Gates, Bezos, Bloomberg) Combined estimated private market exposure represented at Atlas Coaliton's events: $2.5T+ USD  Sponsors & Partners: Get full access to our alumni directory of 280+ verified past family offices guests - including family offices, institutional LPs, & hardware / frontier tech founders - through our WeTheAtlas Family Office & Investors Matching System. Search by investor type, AUM range, sector focus, & geography. Request warm introductions to any previous guest directly through the platform. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. With $22B committed across 1,200 members (70% investors, 30% founders), the coalition hosted events in 8+ cities, share a monthly newsletter, conduct media interviews, & connect active frontier & climate investors through deal flow. Learn more: https://www.atlascoalition.com/ By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with the organizers of Climate Week NYC.

events.name: PMAI Fight Right - Co-Founders Guide To Disagreement
events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

It will also explore how cities can serve as platforms for collaboration among businesses, startups, investors, & global institutions. The Forum will serve as an important step toward Yokohama's major international initiatives in 2027, including GREENEXPO 2027, Asia-Pacific Circular Cities Forum (APCC-Forum), the Asia-Pacific Urban Forum, & broader international dialogue on circular & resilient urban development. View the Speaker ListMorning Programme: Business & Innovation ForumConnecting Innovation Ecosystems Across Asia, North America, & Europe 9:00-9:30 Registration & Networking Coffee9:30-9:40 Welcome Remarks9:40-10:30 Startup ShowcaseSelected startups will present innovative technologies & business models in the fields of the circular economy, climate technology, & urban sustainability. The session is designed to create opportunities for pilot projects, joint development, investment, strategic partnerships, & expansion into Japanese & broader Asian markets. Presenting Startups: TBD 10:30-11:20 Reverse PitchJapanese companies will present their business challenges, innovation priorities, & areas of interest to an audience of international startups. The session aims to identify potential partners & initiate discussions on joint development, pilot projects, & future business collaboration. Participating Companies: Nick Vega, Director on the Investments & Strategy team, Sumitomo Corporation Takeyori Nabeta, Business Development Manage at Chiyoda International Corporation / Venture Associate at DNX Ventures Junya Saka, Manager, Strategic Investment & Partnerships, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation Hirotaka Mori, Principal Researcher, Business Development & CVC, ENEOS Americas Additional companies: TBD 11:20-12:00 Innovation Leaders DialogueAI, the Circular Economy, & the Next Industrial Transformation Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries through major investment in semiconductors, data centers, digital infrastructure, & advanced industrial systems. At the same time, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition to a more sustainable & circular economy by improving efficiency across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI & the circular economy The potential of AI to improve resource efficiency & industrial decarbonization Partnerships needed to commercialize & scale next-generation technologies The roles of corporations, investors, & startups in the next industrial transformation Speakers: Durgesh Patel, Vice President, AI Center of Excellence, Hitachi Ray Hugel, CFA, Executive Director & Co-Head of Catalytic Capital & Private Credit, Closed Loop Partners Kazuhiko Nishioka, Co-Founder & CEO, Sun Metalon Kevin Ninomiya, CEO & Co-Founder, ShibuLA Ventures (Moderator) 12:00-1:30 Networking LunchAn opportunity for investors, startups, corporations, city leaders, & international organizations to connect across sectors, explore collaboration opportunities, & develop partnerships that can continue beyond the Forum. The networking lunch will also be open to participants attending the afternoon programme. Afternoon Programme: Policy & Leadership ForumAccelerating Circular Economy & Urban Resilience 1:30-1:40 Opening Remarks1:40-2:00 Keynote AddressThe Next Chapter of the Circular Economy: Competitiveness, Resilience, & Global Collaboration The circular economy is increasingly becoming a strategic framework for strengthening economic competitiveness, industrial resilience, resource security, & sustainable growth. The keynote will examine why accelerating the transition requires deeper collaboration among cities, businesses, investors, & international organizations, setting the stage for the Forum's discussions on innovation, partnerships, & global action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration Asia's rapid urbanization & growing policy ambition are making the region increasingly important to the global circular economy transition. Cities will play a central role in translating global goals into locally driven policies, partnerships, & practical action. This session will examine how Asian cities can work with global partners to accelerate circular solutions & create new opportunities for cooperation. Discussion themes include: Why Asia will be central to the next phase of the circular economy The role of cities in advancing circular solutions through policy, procurement, & partnerships Opportunities for collaboration between Asian cities & global partners Yokohama's role as a platform for international collaboration toward 2027 GREENEXPO 2027 & related international initiatives Speaker: Tomomi Yamashita, Director General for Global Initiatives, City of Yokohama Carlos Silva Filho, Member of United Nations Secretary-General's Advisory Board on Zero Waste 2:20-3:05 Session 2Investing in the Circular Economy: Innovation, Markets, & GrowthThe transition to a circular economy is creating new markets, attracting investment, & driving innovation across industries & cities worldwide. This session will explore how cities, businesses, investors, & innovation ecosystems can create market opportunities, attract capital & talent, & scale solutions capable of delivering both economic & environmental value. Discussion themes include: Emerging investment opportunities in the circular economy Building innovation ecosystems that attract capital & talent The role of cities in creating markets for circular solutions Public-private partnerships for scaling innovation Strengthening competitiveness through circular innovation Speakers: TBDModerator: TBD 3:05-3:50 Session 3Bridging Regions: Partnerships for Circular & Resilient Cities The circular transition cannot be delivered by cities, financial institutions, businesses, or international organizations acting independently. This session will explore how regional & global partnerships can connect urban priorities with technical expertise, investment, & implementation capacity. The discussion will focus on moving beyond the exchange of ideas toward concrete projects, financing mechanisms, & long-term collaboration. Discussion themes include: Connecting cities across Asia, North America, & other regions Mobilizing finance for circular & resilient urban projects Building pipelines of investable city projects Connecting cities with businesses, investors, & international institutions Scaling successful solutions across different markets Turning international dialogue into practical collaboration Continuing collaboration through international forums & Yokohama's initiatives in 2027 Speakers: Sandra Goldmark, Associate Dean for Engagement & Impact & Professor of Professional Practice, Columbia Climate School Local 2030 Coalition (Speaker TBA) Berat Senyerli, CEO of Bankable Zero Vijay Jagannathan, Senior Fellow at World Resources Institute (Moderator) 3:50-4:00 Closing RemarksWho Should AttendThe Forum is designed for: City & regional government representatives International organizations Corporations & business leaders Investors & financial institutions Startups & entrepreneurs Climate technology & circular economy experts Urban development & resilience professionals Innovation ecosystem leaders

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: Building Better Trading Strategies w/ AI
events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: The New Blueprint - Climate Resiliency By Design
events.description: Discover how NYC is shaping the future of climate-resilient infrastructure & buildings through new policy, guidance, & real-world lessons. The New Blueprint: Climate Resiliency by Design As policymakers, planners & designers, we have learned a great deal over the last decade about the science & real-world impacts of our changing climate, as well as how to innovate & guide capital projects in New York City to become more resilient. We are now at a pivotal moment where this knowledge is being used to measure effectiveness & inform climate resilience requirements for the city's infrastructure & buildings. Representatives from the Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice, NYC Housing Preservation & Development, & Port Authority of NY & NJ will highlight key areas of focus within evolving climate resiliency design guidelines. This panel will provide valuable insights on updates to climate resiliency design requirements for capital infrastructure & building projects throughout New York City, while also showcasing lessons learned from ongoing & completed pilot projects. This panel presentation starts promptly at 10AM, attendees are encouraged to arrive early to grab coffee & a great seat! events.name: Making The Case For Climate-Aligned Abundance & Urbanism
events.description: We welcome all guests to stay after the panel for a light reception. The fiscal & climate case for infill housing is increasingly hard to dispute - but data alone hasn't been enough to overcome the political & aesthetic resistance to density, even if it's for the better. This panel is about the messaging gap: how advocates, designers, & coalition-builders are translating cost curves & emissions data & examples of beautiful infill housing from around the world into narratives & images that make compact, mixed-use development the changes communities yearn for rather than something imposed on them. Panelists will share what's worked around the country - & what hasn't - in turning abundance into a story policymakers, developers, & the public actually want to be part of. Speakers: Rushad Nanavatty (Moderator),Managing Director, RMI  Brian Hanlon, CEO, Metropolitan Abundance Project + California YIMBY  Caroline Spears, Executive Director, Climate Cabinet Education  Heather Clark, CEO, Housing Multiplier Project  Justyn Huckleberry, Projects & Research Associate, WRI This session is hosted by World Resources Institute, Metropolitan Abundance Project, Gehl, Climate Cabinet, & the Parking Reform Network & is a part of the Urban Climate Solutions Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Future US Role In Global Conservation
events.description: What should the future U.S. role in global conservation look like, & whose experience & ideas should shape it? The biodiversity funding landscape changed dramatically in 2025 as the USG abruptly abandoned its international conservation commitments. The loss of approximately $500 million in annual U.S. international conservation funding, along with decades of government capacity & expertise, disrupted conservation efforts around the world. This moment demands more than restoring the former system. It creates an opportunity to examine it critically: what worked, what did not, whose perspectives carried weight, & what must change to build a more effective & durable approach. Hosted by Reimagining Global Conservation, this event will bring together international & locally rooted conservation practitioners, policy experts, funders, & other Climate Week participants. One Earth Partners will present findings from Beyond the Funding Gap, its global assessment of USAID's distinctive role in climate & environmental programming, the structural effects of its 2025 withdrawal, & priorities for future U.S. engagement. A diverse panel of practitioners will then offer locally-grounded perspectives on the future U.S. role, including concrete reforms, institutional changes, & practical proposals for a new global conservation playbook. The session will create space for participants to question familiar assumptions & contribute ideas grounded in their own experience. Biodiversity conservation is inseparable from resilience, livelihoods, stability, & security. Join us for a candid, nonpartisan conversation about how the United States can learn from the past & engage differently in the future.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of The Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data.
