events.name: Aligning Housing Abundance & Building Decarbonization
events.description: A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.

events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. For more information, please visit the Queens AI website.

events.name: NYFW Debrief: Fashion Networking Event
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? This Climate Week NYC event will take a clear-eyed look at the environmental case for autonomous vehicles & examine where the evidence supports the hype, & where it does not. A panel of top experts will discuss along with a Q&A session: Jeffrey Tumlin - former Exec. Director, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) David Zipper -- Contributing writer, Bloomberg City Lab; former Senior Fellow, MIT Mobility Initiative Rachel Weinberger -- Vice President, Transportation & Peter W. Herman Chair, Regional Planning Association Jeral Poskey - Founder, Swyft Cities; former project executive for transportation planning, Google Format: Panel Discussion followed by Q&A The discussion will explore the complicated relationship between automation, mobility, & sustainability. Rather than assuming new technology automatically leads to better outcomes, the discussion will focus on the many potential impacts: energy use, induced demand, land use, transit interactions, fleet models, & the difference between theoretical efficiency & actual environmental performance. Join us for a timely discussion on climate & the future of urban mobility.

events.name: Carbon Newbie Summit
events.description: The Carbon Newbie Summit is back for its 6th edition!  What can whales teach us about economics? How is AI transforming the way buildings use energy? And how are global investors & insurers preparing for a changing climate? Hear fresh perspectives from senior leaders at Mubadala Investment Company, London Stock Exchange Group, Trane Technologies, ServiceNow, American Family Insurance, BrainBox AI & more-alongside renowned scientists, entrepreneurs & changemakers from Columbia Climate School, the University of Toronto, Rutgers University & the Clean Air Task Force. We'll explore everything from AI & decarbonization to living nature, carbon credits, climate risk, microplastics, geothermal energy & sustainable finance-all through lively, accessible conversations designed for curious minds. Whether you're completely new to climate or already working in the field, you'll leave with fresh ideas, practical insights & plenty to talk about. No climate experience necessary-just bring your curiosity! Meet our incredible speakers on the Carbon Newbie Summit website. Light breakfast & full lunch will be served  CO-HOSTSCNaughtDebevoise & PlimptonTrane TechnologiesUniversity of Toronto - Lawson Climate InstituteClever Carbon The Carbon Newbie Summit is an initiative of Clever Carbon.  LIVESTREAMING AVAILABLE - register for the livestream ticket to receive details Who should attend?From climate experts to professionals new to sustainability & climate, our Summit welcomes anyone curious & passionate about climate. By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with our co-hosts/sponsors. About CNaught:Trusted by buyers like Asana, Medium, & Tiger Global, CNaught makes it easy to drive real climate impact through high-quality carbon credit portfolios. We deliver access to sophisticated buying strategies, previously available only to the largest buyers, enabling companies of any size to take meaningful climate action. Learn more: https://www.cnaught.com/ About Debevoise & Plimpton:Debevoise & Plimpton LLP is a premier law firm with market-leading practices, a global perspective & strong New York roots. Our clients look to us to bring a distinctively high degree of quality, intensity & creativity to resolve legal challenges effectively & cost efficiently. We have particularly deep experience in the broad range of issues that arise as environmental, social & governance (ESG) concerns & requirements become increasingly important. The firm brings together sophisticated, multidisciplinary & multinational teams to provide tailored & practical guidance across the evolving ESG & business integrity spectrum by counseling on trends & prudential issues, delivering concrete legal advice on evolving sustainability regulations & policies, & helping clients prepare for the legal, financial & reputational risks arising in this rapidly changing landscape. Learn more: https://www.debevoise.com/ About Trane Technologies:Trane Technologies is a global climate innovator. Through our strategic brands Trane & Thermo King, & our portfolio of environmentally responsible products & services, we bring efficient & sustainable climate solutions to buildings, homes & transportation.https://tranetechnologies.com About University of Toronto - Lawson Climate Institute:Through a multidisciplinary approach, the Lawson Climate Institute is ramping up U of T's capacity to advance the technologies & policies needed for Canada to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. As one of U of T's most wide-ranging, comprehensive initiatives, the institute is unique in its aim to ensure students in every discipline across three campuses have an opportunity to gain the tools needed to take concrete steps toward implementing practical climate solutions. The institute is named in honour of Brian Lawson & Joannah Lawson in recognition of their transformative $60-million donation to help establish the institute.https://lci.utoronto.ca About Clever Carbon:At Clever Carbon, we teach people about carbon footprint in a hip & fun way! From content creation to carbon footprint workshops, we work with leading brands around the world to help raise carbon literacy because what gets measured gets changed! events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? Reach out to Amy Newhall at an2933@columbia.edu.  _________________________________________________________________________________________ To obtain additional information about program offerings at Columbia University's School of Professional Studies, please contact an Admissions Counselor at inquire@sps.columbia.edu. If you require closed captioning, sign-language interpretation, or any other disability accommodations, please contact Disability Services, disability@columbia.edu, at least 10 days in advance. Services requested less than 10 days in advance cannot be guaranteed. Please visit Columbia University's Hub for Emergency Preparedness to stay up to date on the latest campus health & safety policies. This event is open to individuals irrespective of identity & sex.

events.name: Addressing Cost Of Climate Impact - Actions At Scale Of The City
events.description: How do cities bridge the gap between high-level climate vulnerability data & everyday financial execution? While municipalities globally are tracking climate risks, the challenge lies in transforming these insights into the routine machinery of city governance: capital planning, investment, & budgeting. Co-hosted by C40 Cities & Climate Solutions International to discuss their landmark report, Mainstreaming Climate Adaptation in City Financial Planning & Budgeting, this high-level panel brings together policy architects & municipal finance leaders. Moving beyond theory, the session will unpack how pioneering cities are using the report's foundational frameworks to institutionalize climate resilience across all levels of urban governance. What you'll experience: Inside the C40 Framework: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the report's core strategies for embedding climate adaptation guidelines into multi-year capital plans. Governance & Procurement Shifts: Learn how leading municipalities are breaking down departmental silos & modernizing procurement frameworks to automate resilient investment. Peer-to-Peer Networking: Connect with peer sustainability directors, municipal finance officers, & climate policy experts. Refreshments will be served. Featured Panelists & Moderator: Dr. Jan Whittington (CEO, Climate Solutions International; Professor of Urban Planning, UW) Claire Markgraf (Director, City Finance Programme, C40 Cities) - Moderator Marissa Aho (Principal/Practice Leader, Climate, Fehr & Peers, & Former Director of the Executive Climate Office for King County) Lia Cairone (Associate Director for the Environmental Sustainability & Resiliency Task Force, NYC Mayor's Office of Management & Budget) This event is hybrid in nature. Please reach out nikita.tatachar@climatesolutionsintl.com for any accessibility needs.

events.name: Swiss Climatetech Showcase
events.description: Meet the next generation of Swiss climatetech founders as the Climate Collider 2026 cohort comes to Climate Week NYC. Eight Swiss startups - spanning carbon removal, geothermal drilling, sustainable agriculture, clean hydrogen, industrial efficiency, circular construction materials, advanced membranes, biomaterials, & textile recycling - will pitch their solutions to investors, researchers, & industry leaders shaping the future of climate innovation. Climate Collider is a startup camp powered by Innosuisse & managed by Swissnex, designed to strengthen transatlantic collaboration & connect Swiss startups with Boston & New York, two of the world's leading climatetech hubs. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: Local Climate Imperative - Public-Private Partnerships In Action
events.description: Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion during Climate Week NYC 2026 As climate action increasingly takes shape at the local level, cities, businesses, & communities are finding new ways to work together to drive meaningful progress. Yet opportunities for public-sector climate leaders & corporate sustainability professionals to learn from one another remain surprisingly rare. Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion at BelCham Atelier, exploring the power of public-private partnerships to accelerate climate progress. Rather than a traditional panel, the program will feature a select group of speakers sharing practical examples of how collaboration across government, business, & community partners is driving meaningful change - from policy development & implementation to corporate strategy & investment. The remainder of the event will focus on networking & facilitated discussion, creating space for participants to share best practices, discuss common challenges, & identify new opportunities to work together. Join us for a morning of insightful conversation, meaningful connections, & practical ideas to help strengthen the partnerships driving climate action forward. About Agendi & Run on Climate Run on Climate & Agendi share a belief that accelerating climate progress requires stronger connections between the public & private sectors. While Run on Climate helps local governments advance ambitious climate policies & implementation, Agendi partners with companies to translate climate commitments into actionable business strategies. Bringing these communities together creates a unique opportunity to exchange perspectives, identify shared challenges, & explore new models for collaboration that can accelerate climate action at the local level.

events.name: Sobremesa  A Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

events.name: SOSV's Hax Deep Tech Showcase
events.description: Deep tech has always mattered, but right now, the tailwinds are stronger & more urgent than at any point in the last 40 years. Global demand & national security priorities are converging, making this area critical to the next decade of industrial & economic growth. As part of Climate Week NYC, meet 20+ deep tech companies driving that transformation - all graduates of HAX, SOSV's hard-tech program & the world's most active pre-seed investor for deep tech founders. You will meet Seed & Series A companies building critical solutions with commercial traction across energy systems, industrial automation, robotics, plasma, critical minerals, & advanced chemistry. SOSV's HAX provides hard-tech founders a 6-month collaborative residency, hands-on engineering support, & an initial investment package of up to $550,000. HAX has a flagship 35,000 square foot facility in Newark, with additional offices in Shenzhen, Pune & Tokyo, & expansion planned for a new facility focused on applications of plasma physics called HAX Plasma Forge in Princeton. This event is for investors only. events.name: Net Zero Value Chains - Advancing Credible Scope 3 Decarbonization
events.description: The corporate climate landscape is moving toward greater rigor, with growing expectations for companies to substantiate climate action through credible data, accounting, & reporting. The GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard (LSRS) introduces a more robust framework for accounting & reporting land-based emissions & CO removals. However, implementation remains challenging, with companies navigating supplier data gaps, limited traceability, allocation challenges, & evolving assurance expectations. At the same time, organizations are exploring how market-based approaches can help accelerate credible Scope 3 action beyond their direct operations. Join corporate sustainability leaders, standard setters, climate experts, & solution providers to explore two key developments shaping the future of value chain decarbonization: Panel 1: Implementing the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard Hear from experts & early adopters on the practical challenges of implementing the LSRS, including data quality, traceability, allocation, reporting, & assurance. Learn what organizations are doing today-and what may be needed to support scalable implementation in the years ahead. Speakers:Matt Ramlow, Senior Research Associate, GHG P Martha Stevenson, Senior Director, Strategy & Research, Forests, WWF Noora Singh, Senior Director, Global Sustainability, PepsiCoChristina O'Keefe, Head of Sustainability, North America, Kerry Panel 2: The emerging role of Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) Explore how carbon credits, environmental certificates, & other market-based approaches could support Scope 3 decarbonization. Hear the latest perspectives on developments across the GHG Protocol, AMI Standard, & SBTi's Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2, alongside practical insights from companies already piloting these approaches. Speakers:Alex Kazaglis, Chief Strategy Officer, SBTiDavid Spitzley, Director, Climate & Nature | Global Sustainability, StarbucksJacob Isaacson, Associate Director of Climate Strategy, 3DegreesCynthia Cummis, Senior Vice President Value Chain Strategies, ClimeCo The event will conclude with networking drinks, providing an opportunity to continue the conversation & connect with peers from across the corporate climate ecosystem. Who should attend? Corporate sustainability & climate leaders Scope 3 & procurement professionals Standards & accounting experts NGOs & policy stakeholders Sustainability consultants & solution providers Register now to secure your place.

events.description: WHERE BUILDING TECH & MATERIALS COME TOGETHERThe annual Buildings + Materials Conference explores innovation & emerging technology in the development, design, materials, & systems of buildings. The event examines the current state & trajectory of building planning & operational solutions, strategies, & processes, providing insights & guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, & challenges. Connect. Inform. Advance.The premier network for advancing innovation & catalyzing collaboration throughout the built environment ecosystem. It Began As a Digital Community Connecting, Sharing, & LearningIn the fall of 2013, BuiltWorlds analysts began harnessing the power of digital media, crowd sourcing, & open innovation, sharing what they were learning & who they were meeting via social media & drawing in ever more passionate, open, experts who shared even more insights & data. The resulting network effect produced a global community of thousands of people actively providing data & contacts, curated by our analyst team, who then shared with back with the community in the form of actionable insights & deeper understanding. From the Community, A Powerful Research Network EmergedBuiltWorlds emerged as a free community, fueled by subscribers & supported by a small groups of sponsors. However, as the community grew, more members of the community wanted to access more of BuiltWorlds' research & collaborate more actively with others in the community.  Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Local Climate Imperative - Public-Private Partnerships In Action
events.description: Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion during Climate Week NYC 2026 As climate action increasingly takes shape at the local level, cities, businesses, & communities are finding new ways to work together to drive meaningful progress. Yet opportunities for public-sector climate leaders & corporate sustainability professionals to learn from one another remain surprisingly rare. Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion at BelCham Atelier, exploring the power of public-private partnerships to accelerate climate progress. Rather than a traditional panel, the program will feature a select group of speakers sharing practical examples of how collaboration across government, business, & community partners is driving meaningful change - from policy development & implementation to corporate strategy & investment. The remainder of the event will focus on networking & facilitated discussion, creating space for participants to share best practices, discuss common challenges, & identify new opportunities to work together. Join us for a morning of insightful conversation, meaningful connections, & practical ideas to help strengthen the partnerships driving climate action forward. About Agendi & Run on Climate Run on Climate & Agendi share a belief that accelerating climate progress requires stronger connections between the public & private sectors. While Run on Climate helps local governments advance ambitious climate policies & implementation, Agendi partners with companies to translate climate commitments into actionable business strategies. Bringing these communities together creates a unique opportunity to exchange perspectives, identify shared challenges, & explore new models for collaboration that can accelerate climate action at the local level.

events.name: AI Needs More Power - Who Builds It, What Gets Built & Who Gets Paid
events.description: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. On-site resources are becoming critical & can potentially offer flexibility while reducing ratepayer impact. Moderated by Lisa Martine Jenkins of Latitude Media, energy leaders & investors from Aston Power, Commonwealth Station A, & Redwood Materials will debate where capital is moving, what actually needs to get built, & whether the AI boom will fundamentally reshape how, & from whom, large energy users get their power Moderator: Lisa Martine Jenkins | Editor | Latitude Media Panelists: Doug Chambers | Chief Development Officer | Aston Travis Metcalfe | Energy Strategist | Commonwealth Asset Management Group Kevin Berekemeyer | Co-Founder & CEO | Station A Claire McConnell | Vice President of Business Development | Redwood Materials Antenna Group is the public relations & strategic marketing agency of choice for climate, energy, mobility, real estate, & infrastructure leaders. If you're a startup, investor, or global corporation that's looking to tell your climate story, demonstrate your impact, or accelerate your growth, Antenna Group's team of industry insiders is ready to help. Learn more at antennagroup.com.

events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. For more information, please visit the Queens AI website.

events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: Future US Role In Global Conservation
events.description: What should the future U.S. role in global conservation look like, & whose experience & ideas should shape it? The biodiversity funding landscape changed dramatically in 2025 as the USG abruptly abandoned its international conservation commitments. The loss of approximately $500 million in annual U.S. international conservation funding, along with decades of government capacity & expertise, disrupted conservation efforts around the world. This moment demands more than restoring the former system. It creates an opportunity to examine it critically: what worked, what did not, whose perspectives carried weight, & what must change to build a more effective & durable approach. Hosted by Reimagining Global Conservation, this event will bring together international & locally rooted conservation practitioners, policy experts, funders, & other Climate Week participants. One Earth Partners will present findings from Beyond the Funding Gap, its global assessment of USAID's distinctive role in climate & environmental programming, the structural effects of its 2025 withdrawal, & priorities for future U.S. engagement. A diverse panel of practitioners will then offer locally-grounded perspectives on the future U.S. role, including concrete reforms, institutional changes, & practical proposals for a new global conservation playbook. The session will create space for participants to question familiar assumptions & contribute ideas grounded in their own experience. Biodiversity conservation is inseparable from resilience, livelihoods, stability, & security. Join us for a candid, nonpartisan conversation about how the United States can learn from the past & engage differently in the future.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: Coding Agents with Elastic Memory + The Evolution to Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group and Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6!Engin Diri from Pulumi and Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, and networking with the New York City tech community. Continue the experience at ElasticON NYCElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, and registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts and the community, gain hands-on experience, and discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, and security solutions.Register for ElasticON NYC here Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001 Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, and everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co.Agenda:6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi and eat some food6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless and why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic)7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking and event wrap-up Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, and redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, and that empties every time you close your laptop.Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself and reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, and anything past the first page of the index gets dropped.agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, and session history are searchable and shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, and show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file.And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, and every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice.Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless and why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic)Details coming soon!

We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. backed by Gates, Bezos, Bloomberg) Combined estimated private market exposure represented at Atlas Coaliton's events: $2.5T+ USD  Sponsors & Partners: Get full access to our alumni directory of 280+ verified past family offices guests - including family offices, institutional LPs, & hardware / frontier tech founders - through our WeTheAtlas Family Office & Investors Matching System. Search by investor type, AUM range, sector focus, & geography. Request warm introductions to any previous guest directly through the platform. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. With $22B committed across 1,200 members (70% investors, 30% founders), the coalition hosted events in 8+ cities, share a monthly newsletter, conduct media interviews, & connect active frontier & climate investors through deal flow. Learn more: https://www.atlascoalition.com/ By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with the organizers of Climate Week NYC.

events.name: Global Forum On Circular Economy & Urban Resilience
events.description: Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban ResilienceDate: Friday, September 25, 2026Venue: Club 135 by IndustriousAddress: 135 W 50th Street, New York, NY 10020Format: Invitation OnlyExpected Attendance: Approximately 200 participantsLanguage: EnglishHost: Office of the City of Yokohama Representative to the AmericasSponsors: ITO ENPartners: Greennex Global, ShibuLA Ventures, CleanLeap & Deep Tech Forum About the ForumThe global economy is undergoing a profound transformation driven by geopolitical uncertainty, the restructuring of global supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, & growing demand for energy & critical resources. Against this backdrop, the circular economy is emerging not only as an environmental agenda, but also as a strategic approach to strengthening economic competitiveness, resource security, industrial resilience, & sustainable growth. Held during Climate Week NYC 2026, the Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban Resilience will bring together city & regional government representatives, international organizations, corporations, investors, financial institutions, startups, & climate innovation leaders from Asia, North America, Europe, & beyond. Through business showcases, reverse pitches, keynote remarks, & cross-sector discussions, the Forum will connect urban challenges with innovation, investment, & international partnerships. It will also explore how cities can serve as platforms for collaboration among businesses, startups, investors, & global institutions. The Forum will serve as an important step toward Yokohama's major international initiatives in 2027, including GREENEXPO 2027, Asia-Pacific Circular Cities Forum (APCC-Forum), the Asia-Pacific Urban Forum, & broader international dialogue on circular & resilient urban development. View the Speaker ListMorning Programme: Business & Innovation ForumConnecting Innovation Ecosystems Across Asia, North America, & Europe 9:00-9:30 Registration & Networking Coffee9:30-9:40 Welcome Remarks9:40-10:30 Startup ShowcaseSelected startups will present innovative technologies & business models in the fields of the circular economy, climate technology, & urban sustainability. The session is designed to create opportunities for pilot projects, joint development, investment, strategic partnerships, & expansion into Japanese & broader Asian markets. Presenting Startups: TBD 10:30-11:20 Reverse PitchJapanese companies will present their business challenges, innovation priorities, & areas of interest to an audience of international startups. The session aims to identify potential partners & initiate discussions on joint development, pilot projects, & future business collaboration. Participating Companies: Nick Vega, Director on the Investments & Strategy team, Sumitomo Corporation Takeyori Nabeta, Business Development Manage at Chiyoda International Corporation / Venture Associate at DNX Ventures Junya Saka, Manager, Strategic Investment & Partnerships, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation Hirotaka Mori, Principal Researcher, Business Development & CVC, ENEOS Americas Additional companies: TBD 11:20-12:00 Innovation Leaders DialogueAI, the Circular Economy, & the Next Industrial Transformation Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries through major investment in semiconductors, data centers, digital infrastructure, & advanced industrial systems. At the same time, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition to a more sustainable & circular economy by improving efficiency across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI & the circular economy The potential of AI to improve resource efficiency & industrial decarbonization Partnerships needed to commercialize & scale next-generation technologies The roles of corporations, investors, & startups in the next industrial transformation Speakers: Durgesh Patel, Vice President, AI Center of Excellence, Hitachi Ray Hugel, CFA, Executive Director & Co-Head of Catalytic Capital & Private Credit, Closed Loop Partners Kazuhiko Nishioka, Co-Founder & CEO, Sun Metalon Kevin Ninomiya, CEO & Co-Founder, ShibuLA Ventures (Moderator) 12:00-1:30 Networking LunchAn opportunity for investors, startups, corporations, city leaders, & international organizations to connect across sectors, explore collaboration opportunities, & develop partnerships that can continue beyond the Forum. The networking lunch will also be open to participants attending the afternoon programme. Afternoon Programme: Policy & Leadership ForumAccelerating Circular Economy & Urban Resilience 1:30-1:40 Opening Remarks1:40-2:00 Keynote AddressThe Next Chapter of the Circular Economy: Competitiveness, Resilience, & Global Collaboration The circular economy is increasingly becoming a strategic framework for strengthening economic competitiveness, industrial resilience, resource security, & sustainable growth. The keynote will examine why accelerating the transition requires deeper collaboration among cities, businesses, investors, & international organizations, setting the stage for the Forum's discussions on innovation, partnerships, & global action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration Asia's rapid urbanization & growing policy ambition are making the region increasingly important to the global circular economy transition. Cities will play a central role in translating global goals into locally driven policies, partnerships, & practical action. This session will examine how Asian cities can work with global partners to accelerate circular solutions & create new opportunities for cooperation. Discussion themes include: Why Asia will be central to the next phase of the circular economy The role of cities in advancing circular solutions through policy, procurement, & partnerships Opportunities for collaboration between Asian cities & global partners Yokohama's role as a platform for international collaboration toward 2027 GREENEXPO 2027 & related international initiatives Speaker: Tomomi Yamashita, Director General for Global Initiatives, City of Yokohama Carlos Silva Filho, Member of United Nations Secretary-General's Advisory Board on Zero Waste 2:20-3:05 Session 2Investing in the Circular Economy: Innovation, Markets, & GrowthThe transition to a circular economy is creating new markets, attracting investment, & driving innovation across industries & cities worldwide. This session will explore how cities, businesses, investors, & innovation ecosystems can create market opportunities, attract capital & talent, & scale solutions capable of delivering both economic & environmental value. Discussion themes include: Emerging investment opportunities in the circular economy Building innovation ecosystems that attract capital & talent The role of cities in creating markets for circular solutions Public-private partnerships for scaling innovation Strengthening competitiveness through circular innovation Speakers: TBDModerator: TBD 3:05-3:50 Session 3Bridging Regions: Partnerships for Circular & Resilient Cities The circular transition cannot be delivered by cities, financial institutions, businesses, or international organizations acting independently. This session will explore how regional & global partnerships can connect urban priorities with technical expertise, investment, & implementation capacity. The discussion will focus on moving beyond the exchange of ideas toward concrete projects, financing mechanisms, & long-term collaboration. Discussion themes include: Connecting cities across Asia, North America, & other regions Mobilizing finance for circular & resilient urban projects Building pipelines of investable city projects Connecting cities with businesses, investors, & international institutions Scaling successful solutions across different markets Turning international dialogue into practical collaboration Continuing collaboration through international forums & Yokohama's initiatives in 2027 Speakers: Sandra Goldmark, Associate Dean for Engagement & Impact & Professor of Professional Practice, Columbia Climate School Local 2030 Coalition (Speaker TBA) Berat Senyerli, CEO of Bankable Zero Vijay Jagannathan, Senior Fellow at World Resources Institute (Moderator) 3:50-4:00 Closing RemarksWho Should AttendThe Forum is designed for: City & regional government representatives International organizations Corporations & business leaders Investors & financial institutions Startups & entrepreneurs Climate technology & circular economy experts Urban development & resilience professionals Innovation ecosystem leaders

events.name: Making The Case For Climate-Aligned Abundance & Urbanism
events.description: We welcome all guests to stay after the panel for a light reception. The fiscal & climate case for infill housing is increasingly hard to dispute - but data alone hasn't been enough to overcome the political & aesthetic resistance to density, even if it's for the better. This panel is about the messaging gap: how advocates, designers, & coalition-builders are translating cost curves & emissions data & examples of beautiful infill housing from around the world into narratives & images that make compact, mixed-use development the changes communities yearn for rather than something imposed on them. Panelists will share what's worked around the country - & what hasn't - in turning abundance into a story policymakers, developers, & the public actually want to be part of. Speakers: Rushad Nanavatty (Moderator),Managing Director, RMI  Brian Hanlon, CEO, Metropolitan Abundance Project + California YIMBY  Caroline Spears, Executive Director, Climate Cabinet Education  Heather Clark, CEO, Housing Multiplier Project  Justyn Huckleberry, Projects & Research Associate, WRI This session is hosted by World Resources Institute, Metropolitan Abundance Project, Gehl, Climate Cabinet, & the Parking Reform Network & is a part of the Urban Climate Solutions Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. This may include being added to mailing lists for future updates. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.

events.name: Climate Solns Showcase
events.description: Extreme heat & chronic flooding have become a new normal in New York City. On Governors Island, novel adaptation solutions that New Yorkers will depend on aren't only concepts; they're reality. events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? Reach out to Amy Newhall at an2933@columbia.edu.  _________________________________________________________________________________________ To obtain additional information about program offerings at Columbia University's School of Professional Studies, please contact an Admissions Counselor at inquire@sps.columbia.edu. If you require closed captioning, sign-language interpretation, or any other disability accommodations, please contact Disability Services, disability@columbia.edu, at least 10 days in advance. Services requested less than 10 days in advance cannot be guaranteed. Please visit Columbia University's Hub for Emergency Preparedness to stay up to date on the latest campus health & safety policies. This event is open to individuals irrespective of identity & sex.

events.name: AI & Sustainability Mgmt - Case Studies From The Field
events.description: This event is free entry with limited tickets available. The organizer will provide a calendar invite to guests up to capacity. If capacity is reached you will be notified. AI & Sustainability Management:Case Studies from the FieldAI is already playing a central role in many companies' sustainability strategy, management, & reporting efforts. Whether it is AI-based materiality, tools to assist in the calculation of greenhouse gas inventories, or AI-enabled sustainability reporting systems, this is an area of fast-moving innovation that has captured the imagination of sustainability practitioners. While we must take the environmental implications of AI usage seriously, we must also evaluate the potential that this technology represents - do the benefits outweigh the impacts? What We'll Explore: AI & Business Intelligence: How business intelligence data platforms are transforming data collection, analysis, & insight generation. AI-enabled sustainability - Is it worth the price?: What is the current state of the art knowledge in terms of the cost/benefit tradeoffs of AI in terms of environmental impacts? Building Qualitative & Quantitative Connections: How AI can help companies better understand the linkages between sustainability performance & financial performance. AI & Assurance: How AI-supported data processes & 3rd party verification connect. Is your organization ready for third party verification in the era of AI-based tools & processes? Speakers: Matt Gardner, Managing Partner at Sustainserv Julie Kae, VP of Sustainability at Qlik Technologies Julien Gervreau, Director at Sensiba LLP Who Should Attend:CSOs, CCOs, IROs, & sustainability professionals navigating the intersection of AI capabilities, reporting requirements, & stakeholder engagement in an increasingly complex sustainability landscape
