Is your organization ready for third party verification in the era of AI-based tools & processes? Speakers: Matt Gardner, Managing Partner at Sustainserv Julie Kae, VP of Sustainability at Qlik Technologies Julien Gervreau, Director at Sensiba LLP Who Should Attend:CSOs, CCOs, IROs, & sustainability professionals navigating the intersection of AI capabilities, reporting requirements, & stakeholder engagement in an increasingly complex sustainability landscape

Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. RSVP to join us in NYC & stay in the loop. Come curious. Leave caffeinated-and a few steps closer to shipping.   Location: NYC, shared after RSVP Time: 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Cost: Free

events.name: The Multi-Model Future: Specialized Models & Routing For Domain-Specific Tasks
events.description: Join AI engineering leaders from Brex, Baseten, Extend, & Vercel as they share what they've learned about choosing, routing, & running models efficiently at scale. Priority to RSVP will be for Engineers & Founders.  Topics We'll Cover: Open source models Model routing Token cost control Small task-specific models Our panelists: Eli Badgio, CTO & Co-Founder at Extend Christopher Wirick, Forward Deployed Engineer at Baseten Samarth (Sam) Chitgopekar, Software Engineer at Vercel TBD, Brex  What to Expect? One hour panel discussion  A crowd that includes engineers & founders  Drinks, bites & connections directly with the speakers, peers. Brex is the intelligent finance platform that empowers growing companies to spend smarter & move faster - in more than 200 markets. By combining the world's smartest corporate card with intuitive spend management software & banking, Brex enables founders & finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, & control spend effortlessly. Brex's AI-powered automation & agents eliminate manual expense & accounting tasks for customers. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies, from startups to enterprises, run their finances on Brex - including DoorDash, Anthropic, Zoom, Plaid, & SeatGeek. events.name: State Of Supply Chain Sustainability Report Launch
events.description: The 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report examines a paradox at the heart of corporate sustainability today: commitment is rising, even as the ability to deliver is becoming more difficult. The report explores how companies are responding to geopolitical disruption, governance gaps, fragmented sustainability data, rapid advances in Industrial & Agentic AI, & the broader challenge of embedding sustainability more deeply into supply chain decisions & operations. Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

events.name: NYFW Debrief: Fashion Networking Event
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. And by the time it's over, everyone needs a minute to actually talk about what happened. That's what this is. Once the tents come down & the last show wraps, we're getting the industry back in one room, no seating charts, no dress codes to stress over, no rushing between venues. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. Whether you were front row every day or watching it all unfold from your feed, come compare notes with people who get it. What to expect: Open conversation on the season's best (and most bewildering) moments Drinks & light bites (cash bar) Genuinely good networking (the kind that happens when everyone's a little more relaxed than they were all week) A room full of people worth exchanging numbers with Who it's for:Anyone in or around the fashion industry, designers, stylists, editors, marketers, PR, buyers, creatives, & the people who make fashion week actually happen behind the scenes. Dress code: however you want. You've earned a break from the outfit planning. Mark your calendar now Fashion Forward is a NYC-based community connecting fashion founders, designers, photographers, stylists, & creative leaders through curated experiences that favor depth, quality, & real connection over crowded rooms. By RSVP'ing, you agree to receive occasional marketing communications that can be shared with third parties & acknowledge that photography & video may be captured during the event for promotional purposes.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: From Risk To Oppty - How Capital Can Enable Climate Resilience
events.description: Climate & nature-related risk is accelerating faster than markets can price it, & insurers are often the first to feel it. The same dynamic appears elsewhere: investors hesitate to finance conservation & adaptation projects, while financial inclusion in emerging economies stalls. These share the same underlying reason, that the risk has outpaced the tools we have to price & fund it. Swissnex, in collaboration with the Consulate General of Switzerland in New York, Swiss Business Hub USA, Greater Zurich Area, & Global Infrastructure Basel, convenes senior professionals from banking, insurance, asset management, development finance, policy, research, & community organizations for a single morning that follows this market failure end to end. Together we will explore where it originates, to how capital rebuilds what has been lost, what actually gets built afterward, & what else still stands in the way. Switzerland is well positioned to convene this conversation. It sits at the center of global re/insurance, while its banks & insurers are increasingly operating within a regulatory framework that integrates climate & nature-related risk governance, alongside a democratically mandated net-zero target for 2050. This puts Switzerland in a position where voluntary commitments are increasingly being tested against financial & regulatory realities. Bringing together representatives from government, finance, insurance, & development institutions, this program explores how climate & nature-related risks can be better measured, priced, & financed. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Rethinking Energy Security - How Middle Powers Can Build A Pax Electricana
events.description: Almost 90% of LNG & 80% of oil transiting through the Strait of Hormuz is bound for Asia. When fossil fuels stall in chokepoints & politically volatile regions, the consequences reverberate almost instantly through global commodity markets.   Changing global material flows is integral to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors. events.name: Aligning Housing Abundance & Building Decarbonization
events.description: A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. This may include being added to mailing lists for future updates. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.

A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: Roots To Renewal - Green Careers Reentry Summit

It is about ensuring that the people who have historically been left out of economic opportunity have a meaningful role in shaping, building, & benefiting from what comes next.

events.name: Accommodating Growth In The Global South
events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. Once made, these decisions produce long-lasting impacts for climate, accessibility, & economies. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. Speakers: Robin King (Moderator), Director, Knowledge Capture & Collaboration, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella  Cynthia Goytia, Head of the Master of Science in Urban Economics Program, WRI  Solly Angel, Professor of City Planning, NYU Marron  Samhita Shiledar, Principal, RMI  Adriana Akers, Senior Project Manager, Gehl This session is hosted by Gehl, the NYU Marron Institute, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: Pilina Across The Pae'ina
events.description: Pilina(pee-LEE-nah) (n) is a Hawaiian word describing the relationships that connect people to one another, to place, & to the systems that sustain life.nPresented byCauseway ImpactandHawaii Green Growth,Pilina Across the Pae'inais a NYC Climate Week conversation exploring the future of place, reimagining climate finance through Hawaiian pilina, & highlighting how relationships shape resilient communities.nAcross theHawaiian Pae'ina(Hawaiian Archipelago) & the Pacific, island communities are responding to climate change through collaboration rather than isolation: bringing together indigenous leaders, conservationists, artists, philanthropists, politicians, youth advocates, & community members to affect sustainable policy. Their work offers practical models for resilience that extend far beyond Hawai'i & the Pacific islands, celebrating Hawaiian leadership in this important space.nWith speakers representing the Hawaiian 'ina (land), community,youthadvocacy,culture,leadership, andstewardship, we'll discuss:nLongstanding legacies of indigenous innovation & leadership in sustainable policy.nLegislative & community action like the Green Fee & the shared land ownership model.nLahaina's resilience & the strength of local connections & culture in the face of climate changenTrue to the spirit ofpilina, the conversation continues beyond the stage to ourpau hana(happy hour), the interactive portion of the event where we'll gather over light refreshments & engage in Hawaiian traditions.nJoin us duringClimate Week NYCatScandinavia Housefor an afternoon ofpilina(connection),kilo(observation), andkomo(participation) in Hawaii & Pacific resilience in action.

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten - #AIWeekNY
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Addressing Cost Of Climate Impact - Actions At Scale Of The City
events.description: How do cities bridge the gap between high-level climate vulnerability data & everyday financial execution? While municipalities globally are tracking climate risks, the challenge lies in transforming these insights into the routine machinery of city governance: capital planning, investment, & budgeting. Co-hosted by C40 Cities & Climate Solutions International to discuss their landmark report, Mainstreaming Climate Adaptation in City Financial Planning & Budgeting, this high-level panel brings together policy architects & municipal finance leaders. Moving beyond theory, the session will unpack how pioneering cities are using the report's foundational frameworks to institutionalize climate resilience across all levels of urban governance. What you'll experience: Inside the C40 Framework: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the report's core strategies for embedding climate adaptation guidelines into multi-year capital plans. Governance & Procurement Shifts: Learn how leading municipalities are breaking down departmental silos & modernizing procurement frameworks to automate resilient investment. Peer-to-Peer Networking: Connect with peer sustainability directors, municipal finance officers, & climate policy experts. Refreshments will be served. Featured Panelists & Moderator: Dr. Jan Whittington (CEO, Climate Solutions International; Professor of Urban Planning, UW) Claire Markgraf (Director, City Finance Programme, C40 Cities) - Moderator Marissa Aho (Principal/Practice Leader, Climate, Fehr & Peers, & Former Director of the Executive Climate Office for King County) Lia Cairone (Associate Director for the Environmental Sustainability & Resiliency Task Force, NYC Mayor's Office of Management & Budget) This event is hybrid in nature. Please reach out nikita.tatachar@climatesolutionsintl.com for any accessibility needs.

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? This Climate Week NYC event will take a clear-eyed look at the environmental case for autonomous vehicles & examine where the evidence supports the hype, & where it does not. A panel of top experts will discuss along with a Q&A session: Jeffrey Tumlin - former Exec. Director, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) David Zipper -- Contributing writer, Bloomberg City Lab; former Senior Fellow, MIT Mobility Initiative Rachel Weinberger -- Vice President, Transportation & Peter W. Herman Chair, Regional Planning Association Jeral Poskey - Founder, Swyft Cities; former project executive for transportation planning, Google Format: Panel Discussion followed by Q&A The discussion will explore the complicated relationship between automation, mobility, & sustainability. Rather than assuming new technology automatically leads to better outcomes, the discussion will focus on the many potential impacts: energy use, induced demand, land use, transit interactions, fleet models, & the difference between theoretical efficiency & actual environmental performance. Join us for a timely discussion on climate & the future of urban mobility.

events.name: PMAI Fight Right - Co-Founders Guide To Disagreement
events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Circular Innovation & Resilient Futures - Insights From The Arctic
events.description: Bringing together leaders from business, Indigenous communities, policymaking, finance, & academia, this session explores how Arctic innovation, from Indigenous knowledge to cutting-edge circular economy solutions, can deliver practical & scalable responses to climate, economic, & geopolitical challenges. The Arctic is experiencing some of the world's fastest environmental, economic, & geopolitical change. In response, Indigenous communities, businesses, researchers, policymakers, & investors are developing innovative approaches that strengthen resilience while supporting sustainable economic growth. Long before the term circular economy existed, Arctic Indigenous Peoples developed knowledge systems grounded in stewardship, resource efficiency, & long-term thinking. Today, these principles are complemented by advances in circular business models, clean technologies, sustainable finance, & policy innovation. Finland has emerged as a global leader in circular economy solutions, while Indigenous leadership across Spmi & the wider Arctic continues to demonstrate how traditional knowledge & community-driven approaches can shape resilient futures.

events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.description: Are you responsible for emissions you don't control? Join us for Summit in the Sky, a private panel & networking event held during Climate Week NYC 2026 at One World Trade Center. This invitation-only event brings together senior sustainability, procurement, & supply chain leaders from large corporates actively managing Scope 3 programs, to tackle the defining challenge of corporate decarbonization: being fully accountable for emissions that sit entirely outside your direct operations. Nearly 80% of sustainability leaders cite supplier data availability as their biggest barrier. events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.name: Sharing Heat - Industrial Energy Partnerships From Sweden & NY
events.description: Building Energy Exchange & the Swedish Energy Agency (SEA) are convening industry leaders to explore how industrial energy partnerships & innovative business models can transform waste heat into a valuable clean energy resource - & make thermal energy networks (TENs) financially viable investments.  Presentations will feature two pioneering projects. In Sweden, the energy provider Adven operates a 4th Generation District Heating & Cooling (4GDHC) network in the city of Nynshamn, which captures waste heat from the local Nynas refinery. In upstate New York, SUNY's flagship campus at the University at Buffalo is developing a TEN that will utilize waste heat from the Empire AI supercomputing center to decarbonize campus buildings.  A moderated discussion will examine the cross-sector collaborations, financing pathways, risk mitigation, & technical strategies behind these initiatives, exploring what each project can teach us about how to advance TENs in New York. Join us this Climate Week for this timely conversation & live Q&A, & network over coffee & small bites at the Exchange in downtown Manhattan!  Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeNiclas Carlsson, Head of International Market Development & Investment Promotion, Swedish Energy Agency Carter Strickland, Chief Sustainability Officer & Executive Director of Climate Action, State University of New York (SUNY) Presenters / PanelistsJonas Dyrke, Business Project Manager, AdvenJason Denue, Vice President of Energy & Principal, WENDEL CompaniesRyan McPherson, Chief Sustainability Officer, University of BuffaloDan Egan, Managing Director & Head of Americas Real Estate Sustainability, Blackstone - Moderator Program Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

events.name: From Risk To Oppty - How Capital Can Enable Climate Resilience
events.description: Climate & nature-related risk is accelerating faster than markets can price it, & insurers are often the first to feel it. The same dynamic appears elsewhere: investors hesitate to finance conservation & adaptation projects, while financial inclusion in emerging economies stalls. These share the same underlying reason, that the risk has outpaced the tools we have to price & fund it. Swissnex, in collaboration with the Consulate General of Switzerland in New York, Swiss Business Hub USA, Greater Zurich Area, & Global Infrastructure Basel, convenes senior professionals from banking, insurance, asset management, development finance, policy, research, & community organizations for a single morning that follows this market failure end to end. Together we will explore where it originates, to how capital rebuilds what has been lost, what actually gets built afterward, & what else still stands in the way. Switzerland is well positioned to convene this conversation. It sits at the center of global re/insurance, while its banks & insurers are increasingly operating within a regulatory framework that integrates climate & nature-related risk governance, alongside a democratically mandated net-zero target for 2050. This puts Switzerland in a position where voluntary commitments are increasingly being tested against financial & regulatory realities. Bringing together representatives from government, finance, insurance, & development institutions, this program explores how climate & nature-related risks can be better measured, priced, & financed. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.name: Industrial Decarbonization & Urban Resilience
events.description: Heat waves, domestic supply chains, data centers, & rising energy costs dominate headlines in 2026. While the challenges might seem distinct - many of the solutions are interdependent & already being deployed today. During NYC Climate Week, Suffolk Technologies, Morrison Foerster & Climate Salon are teaming up to discuss: How do we decarbonize our infrastructure while building for resiliency? We'll start with a panel to hear from experts working on solutions to address some of our biggest challenges, & then ask you for your ideas during roundtable discussions. Join us to tackle: Data Center Decarbonization Clean Manufacturing Gridtech Urban Resilience Financing Urban Pilots   Suffolk Technologies is a venture capital platform funding the next generation of companies solving built environment challenges. Suffolk Technologies invests in early & growth-stage startups transforming the built world across real estate & development, architecture, engineering & construction, property management, & smart cities. Leveraging Suffolk's expertise & broad network of industry leaders, Suffolk Technologies partners with visionary founders to accelerate industry-wide adoption of breakthrough innovations ranging from pre-product to growth stages. For more information about Suffolk Technologies' strategy & investments, visit SuffolkTech.com. Climate Salon is a 501c3 nonprofit organization focused on bringing stakeholders together to solve climate challenges. Through educational events, its network of support organizations, & charitable giving, Climate Salon accelerates community action to bring ideas to life. Morrison Foerster (MoFo) is a global law firm with 19 offices across the U.S., Europe, & Asia. Our comprehensive platform includes an award-winning Emerging Companies + Venture Capital (ECVC) practice that combines a deep understanding of market conditions with tailored legal strategies. We advise more than 1,700 entrepreneurs, founders, & venture investors, partnering with clients at every stage of the business lifecycle - from initial formation & financings, through late-stage financings & investments, mergers & acquisitions, & public offerings. In just the last five years, we have guided our clients through venture capital financings totaling over $110 billion & mergers & acquisitions with an aggregate transactional value exceeding $850 billion. Peter Fusco is a partner in the New York office & serves as co-head of the firm's Emerging Companies + Venture Capital Practice. He represents venture funds & tech companies throughout their lifecycle, from pre-incorporation planning to angel, seed, & growth rounds to exit transactions. Pete has been representing tech companies for more than two decades in the New York ecosystem & serves as outside general counsel to many startups, growth-stage companies, & venture funds. He also works closely with NYU/Tandon Future Lab's incubator ecosystem & its related programs. Pete looks forward to working with the Suffolk Technologies & Climate Salon communities to explore collaboration & provide practical legal guidance to support your businesses. If you'd like to connect, he can be reached directly at pfusco@mofo.com

events.name: Built World Resiliency - From Data Centers To Materials
events.description: This event (two panels & an accompanying happy hour with refreshments) spotlights high-growth emerging technology startups tackling critical infrastructure challenges in the Built Environment-from resilient power delivery for data centers to advanced materials & transparency platforms for infrastructure operations. We bring together founders with institutional real estate & infrastructure investors to connect frontier innovation with the capital & market access needed to scale durable, high-performance solutions across the global built world. The panels provide actionable insights to deliver reliable power for AI workloads, strengthen building-material supply chains, & improve procurement transparency through automated assessments-helping create a more resilient, resource-efficient built environment. The Built Environment is under pressure from every direction: surging energy demand, supply-chain volatility, tightening regulations, & aging infrastructure. The companies that will define the next era of real estate & infrastructure are building for resilience from day one. Built World Resiliency brings together startup founders & investors to explore how the next generation of infrastructure is being designed to perform under these new realities. Panel 1 - Powering AI: Building Resilient Compute Infrastructure (4:00 PM). AI is driving unprecedented demand for energy & physical infrastructure. This panel features two startups designing & engineering data centers & power systems that are faster to deploy, more efficient to operate, & less dependent on strained grid infrastructure-making resilience a competitive advantage, not a trade-off. Featuring: FLEXNODE's Chief Growth Officer Zak Kostura + ASTON POWER's co-founder Greg Robinson, moderated by Isela Bahena, Private Equity Infra at Nuveen   Panel 2 - Stronger Materials, Smarter Buildings (4:30 PM). The materials that go into every building are facing new scrutiny, from performance requirements & procurement mandates to environmental disclosure standards. This panel explores next-generation cement technology, AI-driven material intelligence, & automated lifecycle assessments that help project teams build with better data, better products, & greater confidence. Featuring: CURA's founder Erin Bobicki + PATHWAYS' founder Leise Sanderman + ACELABS' co-founder Vardhan Meta, moderated by Markus Gatterwe of Holcim (Ventures) The event opens with a networking session around 3:15/30 PM, followed by panels from 4:00-5:15 PM, & then a light happy hour. The lineup & content may change as we confirm additional speakers & institutional partners.

events.name: Circular Innovation & Resilient Futures - Insights From The Arctic
events.description: Bringing together leaders from business, Indigenous communities, policymaking, finance, & academia, this session explores how Arctic innovation, from Indigenous knowledge to cutting-edge circular economy solutions, can deliver practical & scalable responses to climate, economic, & geopolitical challenges. The Arctic is experiencing some of the world's fastest environmental, economic, & geopolitical change. In response, Indigenous communities, businesses, researchers, policymakers, & investors are developing innovative approaches that strengthen resilience while supporting sustainable economic growth. Long before the term circular economy existed, Arctic Indigenous Peoples developed knowledge systems grounded in stewardship, resource efficiency, & long-term thinking. Today, these principles are complemented by advances in circular business models, clean technologies, sustainable finance, & policy innovation. Finland has emerged as a global leader in circular economy solutions, while Indigenous leadership across Spmi & the wider Arctic continues to demonstrate how traditional knowledge & community-driven approaches can shape resilient futures.

In the context of geopolitical volatility, the case has never been stronger to leverage opportunities in regions with competitive advantages in clean energy & critical materials for deep decarbonization.  This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School.  Speakers: Shanta Barley, Director at Real Zero Hub, IIASASaul Griffith, Founder & Chief Scientist at Rewiring America & Rewiring AustraliaAmy Myers Jaffe, Director, Energy, Climate Justice & Sustainability Lab, & Research Professor at NYUGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: Beyond Mineral Supply Security - Partnerships & Community Rights
events.description: Critical minerals: who captures the value, who bears the risk? A panel on financing a just transition for producer nations. There is no climate transition without transition minerals & how they are governed will decide whether decarbonisation delivers development & prosperity for producer countries, or simply repeats extractive patterns under a green label. This panel co- convened with Oxfam examines the gap between the G7's Critical Minerals Action Plan, which frames minerals mainly as a supply security issue for consumer economies, & South Africa's 2025 G20 Critical Minerals Framework, which centres value retention, local industrialisation & community rights. With the UK holding the G20 presidency in 2027 & the G7 presidency in 2028, there is a genuine window to shift finance toward producer-country processing, regional value chains, & enforceable safeguards including Free, Prior & Informed Consent as a right, not a formality. Join us to explore what truly financed partnership with mineral-rich Global South nations could look like in practice.

events.name: When Data Goes Dark - Preparing For Climate Disasters In Era Of Science Disinvestment
events.description: Over the past year, climate science & environmental data & tools have faced steep disinvestment, but maintaining a strong scientific enterprise & the data it creates is critical to helping communities & businesses prepare for & respond to climate risks. When that data disappears, so does our ability to anticipate, prepare for, & respond to climate disasters before they strike. This panel starts by looking at what's been lost, & at the rescue efforts now underway to preserve high-fidelity climate data & disaster-cost datasets before they disappear for good. It then turns forward: what will it take to rebuild a more resilient, connected environmental data ecosystem - one built so that this kind of loss can't happen again? Join us for a conversation that moves from triage to reimagining, bringing together leaders in climate science, environmental data, global research, & emergency management to chart what comes next. Sponsored By:American Geophysical UnionClimate CentralThe New York Climate ExchangeOpen Environmental Data Project

events.name: State Of Supply Chain Sustainability Report Launch
events.description: The 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report examines a paradox at the heart of corporate sustainability today: commitment is rising, even as the ability to deliver is becoming more difficult. The report explores how companies are responding to geopolitical disruption, governance gaps, fragmented sustainability data, rapid advances in Industrial & Agentic AI, & the broader challenge of embedding sustainability more deeply into supply chain decisions & operations. Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

events.name: Accommodating Growth In The Global South
events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. Once made, these decisions produce long-lasting impacts for climate, accessibility, & economies. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. Speakers: Robin King (Moderator), Director, Knowledge Capture & Collaboration, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella  Cynthia Goytia, Head of the Master of Science in Urban Economics Program, WRI  Solly Angel, Professor of City Planning, NYU Marron  Samhita Shiledar, Principal, RMI  Adriana Akers, Senior Project Manager, Gehl This session is hosted by Gehl, the NYU Marron Institute, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. This may include being added to mailing lists for future updates. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.
