events.name: Family Offices & Investors Summit
events.description: 150 seats. One room. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). This year, we're raising the bar & want to double that number.  WHO'S BEEN IN THE ROOM: Invited Family Offices & Institutional Capital  KKR ($361B+ AUM, New York) - Global investment firm. Principal from KKR's Sustainability & Capital Formation team joining us.  Generation Investment Management ($44B+ AUM, San Francisco / London) - Al Gore's sustainable investment firm. Founding Partner Colin le Duc returning for the second consecutive year.  Rockefeller Foundation ($6B endowment, New York) - Director of Energy Technology & Innovation Shunondo Basu. Net-zero endowment commitment. Speaker at both 2025 summits, returning for 2026  Merit France / CMA CGM Saade Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  Energy Impact Partners ($4.5B AUM, New York) - Climate infrastructure VC backed by 80+ global utility & energy partners. Returning for 2026.  Schmidt Sciences (Multi-$B, Palo Alto) - Eric Schmidt's frontier science & technology initiative. Returning for 2026  Wittington Ventures ($500M venture platform / $21B Weston family, Canada) - The venture arm of one of North America's largest private family enterprises. Sending a new team member for the third consecutive event.  B Capital Group / EE Capital (Eduardo Saverin's $9B+ venture platform, Singapore) - One of Asia's most active frontier & climate tech investors, recently hired Temasek's Head of Sustainable Investing.  Merit France / CMA CGM Saad Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  TIME Ventures / Benioff Family ($300M+ committed to frontier tech & climate, San Francisco) - Salesforce founder Marc Benioff's personal fund backing fusion energy, reforestation, & ecopreneur ventures.  Ho Family Office / Banyan Group (100+ properties across 28 countries, Singapore) - Founder Ho Kwon Ping built a global hospitality empire from an abandoned tin mine. Now deploying family capital into resilience & adaptation across Asia.  PETRONAS Ventures ($800M+ CVC, Malaysia) - The energy giant's corporate venture arm, backing breakthrough energy startups from Kuala Lumpur to Silicon Valley.  Aglaia Family Office (Leading multi-family office, Singapore) - Independent MFO serving UHNW families from SEA.  BlackRock ($11.5T+ AUM, New York) - World's largest asset manager.  SK Discovery ($10B+ market cap, Seoul) - Korean industrial conglomerate's venture investment arm. Deploying across materials, energy, & chemicals innovation.  BASF Corporate Venture Capital ($87B revenue parent, Germany) - Venture arm of the world's largest chemical company.  Hennessy Capital Group ($1.8B+ deployed via SPAC, Houston) - Five completed climate & industrial technology SPACs.  SOSV HAX IndieBio ($1.5B AUM, San Francisco) - The #1 most active climate tech venture investor globally. GP returning for 2026 Invited Founders & Fund Managers  Nicholas Flanders - Co-Founder & CEO, Twelve (turning CO into jet fuel, backed by TPG Rise Climate)  Martijn Lopes Cardozo - Partner, Regeneration.VC (Leonardo DiCaprio-backed circular economy fund)  Brian Riordan - Co-Founder & COO, Avalanche Energy (compact fusion systems advancing next-generation clean energy)  Daria Saharova - General Partner, World Fund (350M European climate VC. One of Europe's largest dedicated climate funds. Joining SF 2026)  Peter Hirsch - Head of Sustainability & Partnerships, 2150 (300M+ urban sustainability deep tech VC, London/Copenhagen. Joining SF 2026)  Mira Inbar - Partner, ArcTern Ventures ($500M+ deployed into climate tech across 40+ companies. Joining SF 2026)  Jocelyn Matyas - Cisco Foundation (supporting climate innovation & early-stage impact ventures)  More speakers to be announced $110 BILLION in committed capital represented in this room. This is an 150-person event. Every seat is curated. No expo booths. No filler panels. Just the people writing checks & the founders building the future. OUR TRACK RECORD: WHO HAS BEEN IN THE ROOM: Since 2023, Family Offices & Investors summits & The Climate & Frontier Tech Coalition have convened 280+ verified family offices & LPs alumni across 8 cities - including New York, San Francisco, Paris, Singapore, & Abu Dhabi. New World Development market cap + private holdings) Corporate & Institutional Investors Who Have Attended: Temasek - ~$324B (US$324B net portfolio value as of March 2025; 52% in unlisted/private assets) GIC - ~$800-930B (estimated AUM; ~18% allocated to private equity + 13% to real estate) BlackRock - ~$675B in alternatives (total AUM $14T; top-5 global alternatives platform) Salesforce - ~$3B (Salesforce Ventures, one of the largest corporate VC arms) Circo - ~$1B (estimated private market exposure) Merrill Lynch - ~$3.4T+ (client assets via BofA Wealth Management; significant alts allocation) Bank of America - ~$5.7T (total assets; extensive private market & principal investment exposure) CP Group (Thailand) - ~$90B+ (Charoen Pokphand Group; Dhanin Chearavanont family conglomerate spanning agribusiness, telecom, retail) SCG (Siam Cement Group) - ~$15B (enterprise value; Crown Property Bureau) PTT Group (Thailand) - ~$50B+ (PTT Public Company market cap + subsidiaries; state-owned energy) NEOM - ~$500B (official project budget; backed by PIF, Saudi Arabia's $925B sovereign wealth fund) TotalEnergies - ~$160B (market cap; $2B+ annual venture/low-carbon investment) Shell - ~$200B (market cap; Shell Ventures active in energy transition & deep tech) Frontier & Venture Capital Firms Who Have Attended: LowerCarbon Capital - ~$2B+ (AUM across 4 funds; Chris Sacca-led climate VC) SOSV - ~$1.5B (AUM; most active deep tech pre-seed investor globally) DCVC - ~$3B+ (total AUM across multiple deep tech funds + DCVC Climate Select ~$400M) Breakthrough Energy Ventures - ~$3.5B+ (committed capital across 3 flagship funds; backed by Gates, Bezos, Bloomberg) Combined estimated private market exposure represented at Atlas Coaliton's events: $2.5T+ USD  Sponsors & Partners: Get full access to our alumni directory of 280+ verified past family offices guests - including family offices, institutional LPs, & hardware / frontier tech founders - through our WeTheAtlas Family Office & Investors Matching System. Search by investor type, AUM range, sector focus, & geography. Request warm introductions to any previous guest directly through the platform. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. With $22B committed across 1,200 members (70% investors, 30% founders), the coalition hosted events in 8+ cities, share a monthly newsletter, conduct media interviews, & connect active frontier & climate investors through deal flow. Learn more: https://www.atlascoalition.com/ By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with the organizers of Climate Week NYC.

All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Powering The AI Build-Out - India's Data Center Energy Demand Surge

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Aligning Housing Abundance & Building Decarbonization
events.description: A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. events.name: Future US Role In Global Conservation
events.description: What should the future U.S. role in global conservation look like, & whose experience & ideas should shape it? The biodiversity funding landscape changed dramatically in 2025 as the USG abruptly abandoned its international conservation commitments. The loss of approximately $500 million in annual U.S. international conservation funding, along with decades of government capacity & expertise, disrupted conservation efforts around the world. This moment demands more than restoring the former system. It creates an opportunity to examine it critically: what worked, what did not, whose perspectives carried weight, & what must change to build a more effective & durable approach. Hosted by Reimagining Global Conservation, this event will bring together international & locally rooted conservation practitioners, policy experts, funders, & other Climate Week participants. One Earth Partners will present findings from Beyond the Funding Gap, its global assessment of USAID's distinctive role in climate & environmental programming, the structural effects of its 2025 withdrawal, & priorities for future U.S. engagement. A diverse panel of practitioners will then offer locally-grounded perspectives on the future U.S. role, including concrete reforms, institutional changes, & practical proposals for a new global conservation playbook. The session will create space for participants to question familiar assumptions & contribute ideas grounded in their own experience. Biodiversity conservation is inseparable from resilience, livelihoods, stability, & security. Join us for a candid, nonpartisan conversation about how the United States can learn from the past & engage differently in the future.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Building For The Future - Data Centers, Water Stewardship & Decarbonization
events.description: Two of the hardest problems in corporate climate action right now are water & energy, & both are being tested in real time by companies making infrastructure decisions with long lifespans. This event brings together cross-sector practitioners to discuss what's working, what's stuck, & what needs to change to achieve meaningful, shared solutions at scale. Panel one - data centers & water: Water is an increasing source of tension as data center development accelerates. Data center developers are setting water positive commitments that include reducing water demand & increasing reuse, & also investing in water replenishment that goes beyond the fenceline to invest in watersheds. In this panel, we will bring together speakers representing hyperscalers, utilities, & communities to explore what is needed to effectively support communities & ecosystems while reducing data center risks. Panel two - portfolio decarbonization: Setting a corporate emissions target is straightforward; delivering it across a portfolio of facilities built over decades is not. Public & private sector panelists will discuss how large organizations sequence capital across sites with different ages, uses, & local grids - where electrification pencils out, where it doesn't yet, & what actually moves a portfolio rather than a single flagship building.

events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. Potential topics of discussion include: Seeding & sourcing innovation: How Massachusetts' & New York's university & research ecosystems can learn from each other to build a stronger, more connected pipeline from lab to startup Bridging the Second Valley of Death: How public dollars (through NYSERDA & MassCEC) & private capital across both states can help the most promising climate & energy companies scale from prototype to commercial pilot Keeping manufacturing in the Northeast: How Massachusetts & New York can work together, through shared infrastructure or incentives, to keep growing manufacturers here instead of losing them to other regions Lunch will be provided. Once our discussion wraps up, we invite you to stay for the Greentown Startup Showcase from 1:30 to 3:30 PM to see climate innovation in action. Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV! Agenda (times in ET) 12:30 PM - 12:40 PM: Welcome & mingling 12:40 PM - 12:50 PM: Welcome remarks / presentation from Greentown CEO Georgina Campbell Flatter 12:50 PM - 1:20 PM: VIP discussion on cross-border climate & energy collaboration 1:20 PM - 1:30 PM: Wrap up & establish next steps to increase collaboration between Massachusetts & New York 1:30 PM: Beginning of Startup Showcase event About Greentown As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, Greentown enables entrepreneurs to bring their technologies into the world through world-class incubation support, programs for collaborative innovation, & a global ecosystem of corporates, investors, researchers, governments, & philanthropists dedicated to scaling transformational technologies. Greentown Labs, the world's largest climatetech incubator network, provides entrepreneurs mission-critical access to labs, equipment, customers, capital, talent, community, & resources for business growth at its flagship incubators in Somerville, MA & Houston, TX. Please note: By registering for this event, you consent to your name, title, & company/organization being shared with other event attendees. events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Speakers & panels will be announced soon. Attendees will represent professionals leading sustainability efforts across sports, music, entertainment, media, merchandising, community impact, colleges & universities, alongside students & emerging professionals.

events.name: Addressing Cost Of Climate Impact - Actions At Scale Of The City
events.description: How do cities bridge the gap between high-level climate vulnerability data & everyday financial execution? While municipalities globally are tracking climate risks, the challenge lies in transforming these insights into the routine machinery of city governance: capital planning, investment, & budgeting. Co-hosted by C40 Cities & Climate Solutions International to discuss their landmark report, Mainstreaming Climate Adaptation in City Financial Planning & Budgeting, this high-level panel brings together policy architects & municipal finance leaders. Moving beyond theory, the session will unpack how pioneering cities are using the report's foundational frameworks to institutionalize climate resilience across all levels of urban governance. What you'll experience: Inside the C40 Framework: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the report's core strategies for embedding climate adaptation guidelines into multi-year capital plans. Governance & Procurement Shifts: Learn how leading municipalities are breaking down departmental silos & modernizing procurement frameworks to automate resilient investment. Peer-to-Peer Networking: Connect with peer sustainability directors, municipal finance officers, & climate policy experts. Refreshments will be served. Featured Panelists & Moderator: Dr. Jan Whittington (CEO, Climate Solutions International; Professor of Urban Planning, UW) Claire Markgraf (Director, City Finance Programme, C40 Cities) - Moderator Marissa Aho (Principal/Practice Leader, Climate, Fehr & Peers, & Former Director of the Executive Climate Office for King County) Lia Cairone (Associate Director for the Environmental Sustainability & Resiliency Task Force, NYC Mayor's Office of Management & Budget) This event is hybrid in nature. Please reach out nikita.tatachar@climatesolutionsintl.com for any accessibility needs.

events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.description: WHERE BUILDING TECH & MATERIALS COME TOGETHERThe annual Buildings + Materials Conference explores innovation & emerging technology in the development, design, materials, & systems of buildings. The event examines the current state & trajectory of building planning & operational solutions, strategies, & processes, providing insights & guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, & challenges. Connect. Inform. Advance.The premier network for advancing innovation & catalyzing collaboration throughout the built environment ecosystem. It Began As a Digital Community Connecting, Sharing, & LearningIn the fall of 2013, BuiltWorlds analysts began harnessing the power of digital media, crowd sourcing, & open innovation, sharing what they were learning & who they were meeting via social media & drawing in ever more passionate, open, experts who shared even more insights & data. The resulting network effect produced a global community of thousands of people actively providing data & contacts, curated by our analyst team, who then shared with back with the community in the form of actionable insights & deeper understanding. From the Community, A Powerful Research Network EmergedBuiltWorlds emerged as a free community, fueled by subscribers & supported by a small groups of sponsors. However, as the community grew, more members of the community wanted to access more of BuiltWorlds' research & collaborate more actively with others in the community.  Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Catalyzing Cities
events.description: Cities are increasingly expected to deliver climate resilience while navigating constrained budgets, aging infrastructure, & growing complexity. Yet many of the most impactful solutions already exist... the challenge is designing financing & partnership models that enable them to scale. This New York Climate Week, join Cool Climate Collective & Climate Vine, as we convene investors, city leaders, philanthropies & ecosystem partners for a discussion on how innovative financing structures & public-private collaboration can unlock catalytic outcomes for cities, particularly for New York. Drawing on emerging work in city outcomes & practical examples from around the world, we'll explore: New models for financing climate resilience beyond traditional procurement. How blended capital & partnership design can accelerate deployment. What is already working in practice & why. Lessons & systems insights informed by collaborators across the resilience ecosystem, including perspectives shared by our partners from UNDRR & Dark Matter Labs. The session is designed to be interactive, bringing together practitioners across sectors to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions, & identify opportunities for collaboration during Climate Week. Agenda 9:30 - 10:00 AM : Check-in & coffee networking 10:00 - 11:30 AM : Interactive discussion & programming 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM : Facilitated small-group discussions followed by open networking

events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? Reach out to Amy Newhall at an2933@columbia.edu.  _________________________________________________________________________________________ To obtain additional information about program offerings at Columbia University's School of Professional Studies, please contact an Admissions Counselor at inquire@sps.columbia.edu. If you require closed captioning, sign-language interpretation, or any other disability accommodations, please contact Disability Services, disability@columbia.edu, at least 10 days in advance. Services requested less than 10 days in advance cannot be guaranteed. Please visit Columbia University's Hub for Emergency Preparedness to stay up to date on the latest campus health & safety policies. This event is open to individuals irrespective of identity & sex.

events.name: 35% Moment - What Will It Take To Electrify Global Economy By 2035
events.description: Electricity meets barely a fifth of the world's final energy demand today. Yet electrification is the fastest lever governments have to cut emissions, insulate households from the next fossil fuel price shock, & maintain energy security. Getting there means moving vehicles, buildings, & industry onto electrons & modernizing & expanding the power grid faster than any economy has yet managed.  With over 100 companies, the EU, UN, & more, likely to commit to electrify 35% of final energy demand by 2035, this event will ask what it takes to electrify the economy within the next decade. The countries that pull it off first won't just hit a target, they'll write the playbook everyone else has to follow. This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School & Centre for Net Zero, a nonprofit research institute founded by Octopus Energy Group. Speakers:Devrim Celal, Chief Flexibility & Marketing Officer at Kraken TechnologiesDana Guernsey, CEO & Co-Founder at Voltus Robert Metcalfe, Chief Economist at Centre for Net Zero (part of the Octopus Energy Group) & Professor at Columbia SIPAGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: NYFW Debrief: Fashion Networking Event
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. And by the time it's over, everyone needs a minute to actually talk about what happened. That's what this is. Once the tents come down & the last show wraps, we're getting the industry back in one room, no seating charts, no dress codes to stress over, no rushing between venues. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. Whether you were front row every day or watching it all unfold from your feed, come compare notes with people who get it. What to expect: Open conversation on the season's best (and most bewildering) moments Drinks & light bites (cash bar) Genuinely good networking (the kind that happens when everyone's a little more relaxed than they were all week) A room full of people worth exchanging numbers with Who it's for:Anyone in or around the fashion industry, designers, stylists, editors, marketers, PR, buyers, creatives, & the people who make fashion week actually happen behind the scenes. Dress code: however you want. You've earned a break from the outfit planning. Mark your calendar now Fashion Forward is a NYC-based community connecting fashion founders, designers, photographers, stylists, & creative leaders through curated experiences that favor depth, quality, & real connection over crowded rooms. By RSVP'ing, you agree to receive occasional marketing communications that can be shared with third parties & acknowledge that photography & video may be captured during the event for promotional purposes.

events.name: South Asians In Climate Tech
events.description: South Asians are helping build, finance & scale many of the technologies shaping the global climate transition. Join the American South Asian Network during Climate Week NYC for a conversation with founders, investors & industry leaders working across clean energy, mobility, AI infrastructure, climate resilience & sustainable development. We will explore what it takes to move climate solutions from innovation to implementation, including access to capital, corporate adoption, infrastructure, policy & collaboration across the United States, India & global markets. The panel will be followed by networking with climate-tech founders, investors, operators, researchers & professionals from across the South Asian community & the wider climate ecosystem. Topics will include: Emerging climate technologies & business models Climate capital & the path from funding to scale Energy & infrastructure demands created by AI Corporate adoption & public-private partnerships Opportunities connecting the United States, India & global markets About the Hosts:American South Asian Network (ASAN) is the leading platform powering South Asian progress across the United States. We elevate, empower, & unite a rising generation of South Asian creators, entrepreneurs, executives, & change-makers through community, culture, & capital! Instagram | LinkedIn | WhatsApp community for South Asians

events.name: Trading For Food Security In Changing Climate
events.description: The Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) at MIT would like to invite you to a panel discussion titled Trading for Food Security in a Changing Climate". International food trade has become essential for global food security, but the same interconnected networks that move food also transmit shocks-climatic, economic, & geopolitical. A panel of relevant industry experts will examine the linkages between food trade & food security through the lens of healthy diets & introduce the Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, developed by MIT J-WAFS. The Index maps food-trade vulnerability across more than 180 countries. Join us for a moderated discussion on three questions: how to assess food security versus an inability to import; what balance of home-grown & imported food best serves healthy nutrition as diets shift; & where investment in productivity, infrastructure, & research are most needed as the climate changes. ModeratorGreg Sixt, Director, Food & Climate Systems Transformation (FACT) Alliance & Research Director for Food & Climate Systems, Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) Opening presentation: Introduction to the Jameel Index & J-WAFS work on food security, global change, & tradeKenneth Strzepek, Technical Lead, Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, MIT J-WAFS PanelistsProf. Sheryl Hendriks, Extraordinary Professor, University of Pretoria Mark Rosegrant, Research Fellow Emeritus, International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), Former Director of IFPRI's Environment & Production Technology Division Paola de Almeida, CEO, Natural Systems Capital & Jameel Index Advisory Committee Member

events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Food Solns Summit - Stories From Frontlines Of Climate & Farming
events.description: Climate Week NYC 2026's premier funder & field convening on food & agriculture. Please join us for a Climate Week NYC 2026 funder & field convening on food & agriculture as one of the most underleveraged pathways for climate, health, biodiversity, & community resilience. Too often, food & agriculture are treated as niche issues - separate from climate, public health, biodiversity, economic transition, rural resilience & democracy. But the food system sits at the center of all of them. This half-day convening will bring together farmers, fishers, frontline organizers, scientists, policymakers, journalists, funders & investors, & other leaders to explore what becomes possible when food systems are designed to regenerate rather than extract - rebuilding soil, advancing climate resilience & adaptation, protecting health, strengthening rural communities, restoring biodiversity, & renewing public trust. The event is receiving media sponsorship by Civil Eats & Consumer Reports, & is hosted collectively by Earthshare, Funders for Regenerative Agriculture, Global Alliance for the Future of Food, GRACE Communications Foundation, Ibirapitanga, Macdoch Foundation, & McKnight Foundation. A locally-sourced light breakfast will be served.

events.name: How Data Center Fights Renewing Local Power Across US
events.description: This is an in-person event happening as part of NYC Climate Week. To hear many in the tech industry tell it, data centers will bring wealth & prosperity not only to those who build them, but to the communities that ultimately live with & around them. However, drawing a longer historical arc is essential: AI is proposed as a new industrial moonshot in communities that have already seen the rise & fall of steel factories, coal plants, fracking infrastructure, & more. Today's companies are trying to sell communities on yet another industrial vision. On Sept. 22 at 5:30 p.m., join us in Midtown East, Manhattan, for a panel discussion featuring journalists, nonprofits, & community organizers who are uncovering the impact of data centers across the country & sharing that information with the public. Our panel discussion will feature Maia Woluchem, program director of Data & Society's Trustworthy Infrastructures program; Alejandra Martinez, The Texas Tribune environmental reporter & Pulitzer Center grantee; Brian Crawford, Texas resident with the nonprofit Protect the Paluxy Valley; & Ginny Marcille-Kerslake, Pennsylvania resident & Senior Organizer at Food & Water Watch. Kit R. Roane, award-winning senior producer at Retro Report, will be the moderator. This event is anchored by the launch of Data & Society's forthcoming report, The AI Factory: Data Centers, Power & Resistance in Late Industrial Pennsylvania, a landmark study emerging out of eighteen months of field research in the Keystone State, as well as Pulitzer Center-supported reporting on data center development by The Texas Tribune. Light refreshments will be served. Seating is limited, & R.S.V.P. is required. This panel discussion is co-organized by Data & Society, Retro Report, & The Pulitzer Center.

events.name: Net Zero Value Chains - Advancing Credible Scope 3 Decarbonization
events.description: The corporate climate landscape is moving toward greater rigor, with growing expectations for companies to substantiate climate action through credible data, accounting, & reporting. The GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard (LSRS) introduces a more robust framework for accounting & reporting land-based emissions & CO removals. However, implementation remains challenging, with companies navigating supplier data gaps, limited traceability, allocation challenges, & evolving assurance expectations. At the same time, organizations are exploring how market-based approaches can help accelerate credible Scope 3 action beyond their direct operations. Join corporate sustainability leaders, standard setters, climate experts, & solution providers to explore two key developments shaping the future of value chain decarbonization: Panel 1: Implementing the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard Hear from experts & early adopters on the practical challenges of implementing the LSRS, including data quality, traceability, allocation, reporting, & assurance. Learn what organizations are doing today-and what may be needed to support scalable implementation in the years ahead. Speakers:Matt Ramlow, Senior Research Associate, GHG P Martha Stevenson, Senior Director, Strategy & Research, Forests, WWF Noora Singh, Senior Director, Global Sustainability, PepsiCoChristina O'Keefe, Head of Sustainability, North America, Kerry Panel 2: The emerging role of Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) Explore how carbon credits, environmental certificates, & other market-based approaches could support Scope 3 decarbonization. Hear the latest perspectives on developments across the GHG Protocol, AMI Standard, & SBTi's Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2, alongside practical insights from companies already piloting these approaches. Speakers:Alex Kazaglis, Chief Strategy Officer, SBTiDavid Spitzley, Director, Climate & Nature | Global Sustainability, StarbucksJacob Isaacson, Associate Director of Climate Strategy, 3DegreesCynthia Cummis, Senior Vice President Value Chain Strategies, ClimeCo The event will conclude with networking drinks, providing an opportunity to continue the conversation & connect with peers from across the corporate climate ecosystem. Who should attend? Corporate sustainability & climate leaders Scope 3 & procurement professionals Standards & accounting experts NGOs & policy stakeholders Sustainability consultants & solution providers Register now to secure your place.

events.name: Making The Case For Climate-Aligned Abundance & Urbanism
events.description: We welcome all guests to stay after the panel for a light reception. The fiscal & climate case for infill housing is increasingly hard to dispute - but data alone hasn't been enough to overcome the political & aesthetic resistance to density, even if it's for the better. This panel is about the messaging gap: how advocates, designers, & coalition-builders are translating cost curves & emissions data & examples of beautiful infill housing from around the world into narratives & images that make compact, mixed-use development the changes communities yearn for rather than something imposed on them. Panelists will share what's worked around the country - & what hasn't - in turning abundance into a story policymakers, developers, & the public actually want to be part of. Speakers: Rushad Nanavatty (Moderator),Managing Director, RMI  Brian Hanlon, CEO, Metropolitan Abundance Project + California YIMBY  Caroline Spears, Executive Director, Climate Cabinet Education  Heather Clark, CEO, Housing Multiplier Project  Justyn Huckleberry, Projects & Research Associate, WRI This session is hosted by World Resources Institute, Metropolitan Abundance Project, Gehl, Climate Cabinet, & the Parking Reform Network & is a part of the Urban Climate Solutions Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. events.name: Convening The Next-Generation Materials Transition
events.description: The future of fashion depends on bringing next-generation materials to scale. While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. As one of the world's largest platforms for climate collaboration, it creates the ideal environment to build the relationships & shared understanding needed to move promising innovations beyond pilots & into practice. The Forum contributes to that momentum by connecting the people who can help shape the future of next-generation materials. Forum Partners Developed with & featuring voices from: Eco-Age - a purpose-led media & communications agency accelerating the fashion industry's transition to sustainability. Canopy - an award-winning environmental non-profit driving the shift to next-generation, forest-free fibres. Fashion for Good - the global platform for sustainable fashion innovation, connecting brands & innovators to scale breakthrough solutions. Material ConneXion - the world's leading materials insights company, connecting industries to the most innovative & sustainable materials available. Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) - New York's internationally renowned college for fashion, design, business & technology, fostering innovation, education & industry collaboration across the global fashion & textile sector. The Programme The Forum combines a keynote, structured workshops, & a networking reception. Through an invitation-based format & curated audience, participants will explore the opportunities & challenges shaping the next chapter of material innovation. The programme, speakers, & venue are currently being developed with our partners & will be announced in the coming weeks. Who Should Attend The Forum is designed for senior leaders in sustainability, sourcing, supply chain, & procurement across the fashion, apparel, & textile industry. It is built for the people inside the industry who are responsible for what gets made, how it is sourced, & what it is made from. Event Details 22 September 20263:30 PM - 7:30 PMFashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York City Pre-register now for priority access & programme updates. Registration is open but subject to review. We reserve the right to cancel registrations from organisations outside this scope. We look forward to seeing you there.

We have particularly deep experience in the broad range of issues that arise as environmental, social & governance (ESG) concerns & requirements become increasingly important. The firm brings together sophisticated, multidisciplinary & multinational teams to provide tailored & practical guidance across the evolving ESG & business integrity spectrum by counseling on trends & prudential issues, delivering concrete legal advice on evolving sustainability regulations & policies, & helping clients prepare for the legal, financial & reputational risks arising in this rapidly changing landscape. Learn more: https://www.debevoise.com/ About Trane Technologies:Trane Technologies is a global climate innovator. As one of U of T's most wide-ranging, comprehensive initiatives, the institute is unique in its aim to ensure students in every discipline across three campuses have an opportunity to gain the tools needed to take concrete steps toward implementing practical climate solutions. The institute is named in honour of Brian Lawson & Joannah Lawson in recognition of their transformative $60-million donation to help establish the institute.https://lci.utoronto.ca About Clever Carbon:At Clever Carbon, we teach people about carbon footprint in a hip & fun way! events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. events.description: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.
