events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Sharing Heat - Industrial Energy Partnerships From Sweden & NY
events.description: Building Energy Exchange & the Swedish Energy Agency (SEA) are convening industry leaders to explore how industrial energy partnerships & innovative business models can transform waste heat into a valuable clean energy resource - & make thermal energy networks (TENs) financially viable investments.  Presentations will feature two pioneering projects. In Sweden, the energy provider Adven operates a 4th Generation District Heating & Cooling (4GDHC) network in the city of Nynshamn, which captures waste heat from the local Nynas refinery. In upstate New York, SUNY's flagship campus at the University at Buffalo is developing a TEN that will utilize waste heat from the Empire AI supercomputing center to decarbonize campus buildings.  A moderated discussion will examine the cross-sector collaborations, financing pathways, risk mitigation, & technical strategies behind these initiatives, exploring what each project can teach us about how to advance TENs in New York. Join us this Climate Week for this timely conversation & live Q&A, & network over coffee & small bites at the Exchange in downtown Manhattan!  Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeNiclas Carlsson, Head of International Market Development & Investment Promotion, Swedish Energy Agency Carter Strickland, Chief Sustainability Officer & Executive Director of Climate Action, State University of New York (SUNY) Presenters / PanelistsJonas Dyrke, Business Project Manager, AdvenJason Denue, Vice President of Energy & Principal, WENDEL CompaniesRyan McPherson, Chief Sustainability Officer, University of BuffaloDan Egan, Managing Director & Head of Americas Real Estate Sustainability, Blackstone - Moderator Program Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

events.name: State Of Supply Chain Sustainability Report Launch
events.description: The 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report examines a paradox at the heart of corporate sustainability today: commitment is rising, even as the ability to deliver is becoming more difficult. The report explores how companies are responding to geopolitical disruption, governance gaps, fragmented sustainability data, rapid advances in Industrial & Agentic AI, & the broader challenge of embedding sustainability more deeply into supply chain decisions & operations. Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

events.name: Building For The Future - Data Centers, Water Stewardship & Decarbonization
events.description: Two of the hardest problems in corporate climate action right now are water & energy, & both are being tested in real time by companies making infrastructure decisions with long lifespans. This event brings together cross-sector practitioners to discuss what's working, what's stuck, & what needs to change to achieve meaningful, shared solutions at scale. Panel one - data centers & water: Water is an increasing source of tension as data center development accelerates. Data center developers are setting water positive commitments that include reducing water demand & increasing reuse, & also investing in water replenishment that goes beyond the fenceline to invest in watersheds. In this panel, we will bring together speakers representing hyperscalers, utilities, & communities to explore what is needed to effectively support communities & ecosystems while reducing data center risks. Panel two - portfolio decarbonization: Setting a corporate emissions target is straightforward; delivering it across a portfolio of facilities built over decades is not. Public & private sector panelists will discuss how large organizations sequence capital across sites with different ages, uses, & local grids - where electrification pencils out, where it doesn't yet, & what actually moves a portfolio rather than a single flagship building.

events.name: How Data Center Fights Renewing Local Power Across US
events.description: This is an in-person event happening as part of NYC Climate Week. To hear many in the tech industry tell it, data centers will bring wealth & prosperity not only to those who build them, but to the communities that ultimately live with & around them. However, drawing a longer historical arc is essential: AI is proposed as a new industrial moonshot in communities that have already seen the rise & fall of steel factories, coal plants, fracking infrastructure, & more. Today's companies are trying to sell communities on yet another industrial vision. On Sept. 22 at 5:30 p.m., join us in Midtown East, Manhattan, for a panel discussion featuring journalists, nonprofits, & community organizers who are uncovering the impact of data centers across the country & sharing that information with the public. Our panel discussion will feature Maia Woluchem, program director of Data & Society's Trustworthy Infrastructures program; Alejandra Martinez, The Texas Tribune environmental reporter & Pulitzer Center grantee; Brian Crawford, Texas resident with the nonprofit Protect the Paluxy Valley; & Ginny Marcille-Kerslake, Pennsylvania resident & Senior Organizer at Food & Water Watch. Kit R. Roane, award-winning senior producer at Retro Report, will be the moderator. This event is anchored by the launch of Data & Society's forthcoming report, The AI Factory: Data Centers, Power & Resistance in Late Industrial Pennsylvania, a landmark study emerging out of eighteen months of field research in the Keystone State, as well as Pulitzer Center-supported reporting on data center development by The Texas Tribune. Light refreshments will be served. Seating is limited, & R.S.V.P. is required. This panel discussion is co-organized by Data & Society, Retro Report, & The Pulitzer Center.

While the challenges might seem distinct - many of the solutions are interdependent & already being deployed today. During NYC Climate Week, Suffolk Technologies, Morrison Foerster & Climate Salon are teaming up to discuss: How do we decarbonize our infrastructure while building for resiliency? We'll start with a panel to hear from experts working on solutions to address some of our biggest challenges, & then ask you for your ideas during roundtable discussions. Join us to tackle: Data Center Decarbonization Clean Manufacturing Gridtech Urban Resilience Financing Urban Pilots   Suffolk Technologies is a venture capital platform funding the next generation of companies solving built environment challenges. Suffolk Technologies invests in early & growth-stage startups transforming the built world across real estate & development, architecture, engineering & construction, property management, & smart cities. Leveraging Suffolk's expertise & broad network of industry leaders, Suffolk Technologies partners with visionary founders to accelerate industry-wide adoption of breakthrough innovations ranging from pre-product to growth stages. For more information about Suffolk Technologies' strategy & investments, visit SuffolkTech.com. Climate Salon is a 501c3 nonprofit organization focused on bringing stakeholders together to solve climate challenges. Through educational events, its network of support organizations, & charitable giving, Climate Salon accelerates community action to bring ideas to life. Morrison Foerster (MoFo) is a global law firm with 19 offices across the U.S., Europe, & Asia. Our comprehensive platform includes an award-winning Emerging Companies + Venture Capital (ECVC) practice that combines a deep understanding of market conditions with tailored legal strategies. We advise more than 1,700 entrepreneurs, founders, & venture investors, partnering with clients at every stage of the business lifecycle - from initial formation & financings, through late-stage financings & investments, mergers & acquisitions, & public offerings. In just the last five years, we have guided our clients through venture capital financings totaling over $110 billion & mergers & acquisitions with an aggregate transactional value exceeding $850 billion. Peter Fusco is a partner in the New York office & serves as co-head of the firm's Emerging Companies + Venture Capital Practice. He represents venture funds & tech companies throughout their lifecycle, from pre-incorporation planning to angel, seed, & growth rounds to exit transactions. Pete has been representing tech companies for more than two decades in the New York ecosystem & serves as outside general counsel to many startups, growth-stage companies, & venture funds. He also works closely with NYU/Tandon Future Lab's incubator ecosystem & its related programs. Pete looks forward to working with the Suffolk Technologies & Climate Salon communities to explore collaboration & provide practical legal guidance to support your businesses. If you'd like to connect, he can be reached directly at pfusco@mofo.com

events.name: NY Tech Meetup - Climate Tech Edition
events.description: Join us for the September edition of the NY Tech Meetup, where we're partnering with Campus Deep Tech. This NY Tech Meetup includes a few special elements including an expert panel on resilience & the future of climate tech & one of the largest startup pitch competitions during Climate Week NYC. See the investors that will be in the room listed below! Each competing startup demoer is developing moonshot innovations originating in university research labs that will help address pressing resilience challenges across: Climate & Natural Disasters Energy, Water, Telecom, & AI Infrastructure Industrial Processes & Supply Chains Agriculture & Biodiversity Resilience technologies are solutions that mitigate risk by anticipating, absorbing, adapting to, & recovering from significant disruptions & growing friction due to climate & other external factors. Climate change has a cascading impact destabilizing natural & human systems. As risk & volatility continue to rise, new solutions will be needed to adapt. Campus Deep Tech helps deep tech startups working on impactful technologies connect with industry & investors through its cross-university network. This is an unmatched opportunity to present on stage during the biggest climate event of the year. events.name: Accommodating Growth In The Global South
events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. Once made, these decisions produce long-lasting impacts for climate, accessibility, & economies. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. Speakers: Robin King (Moderator), Director, Knowledge Capture & Collaboration, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella  Cynthia Goytia, Head of the Master of Science in Urban Economics Program, WRI  Solly Angel, Professor of City Planning, NYU Marron  Samhita Shiledar, Principal, RMI  Adriana Akers, Senior Project Manager, Gehl This session is hosted by Gehl, the NYU Marron Institute, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. This may include being added to mailing lists for future updates. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.

events.name: [Finland Pavilion At COP31] Ready To Scale - Are Markets Ready?
events.description: Low-climate-impact solutions are already here. Materials, fuels & technologies are ready to scale. But market dynamics are still forming. How can we move to create markets for low-climate-impact solutions, or risk losing the next competitiveness race? Join us for a lunch session & discover how available lower-climate-impact solutions can become the most attractive & profitable choice, & be the first to hear what the happiest country in the world has to offer at COP31. At New York Climate Week, Outokumpu & Neste are calling from the front lines of industrial decarbonization. Representing Finnish companies with global reach, they argue that proven lower-emission solutions are ready to scale, but governments need to step up to create favorable market conditions for these solutions & continue industrial investment. Program: Welcoming words (COP31)  - Tuuli Kaskinen, CEO, Climate Leadership Coalition Ambition statement - Kati ter Horst, CEO Outokumpu & Jukka Siukosaari, Senior Vice President, Public Affairs & Geopolitics Highlights from the Finland Pavilion program at COP31 Light Lunch will be available The event is hosted by the Partners of the Finland Pavilion at COP31 in Antalya, Trkiye. Through the Finland Pavilion, the companies aim to contribute to international dialogue on lowering industrial greenhouse emissions, accelerating energy transition, & the scaling of proven climate solutions. Clean energy | Industrial innovation | Clean technologies | Research | Carbon removal | Circular economy | Cities | Resilience Will we see you there? Save your spot by registering below. Hope to see you there!

events.name: The Shortlist - October Founder Showcase
events.description: The Shortlist NYC - October Founder Showcase (#10)The Shortlist is back for our monthly Founder Showcase & the room keeps getting better. This is a monthly curated, application-only evening connecting early-stage founders with exceptional operators across New York. No panels. No pitches to VCs. Just six founders building breakout companies, a room full of people who've built things themselves, & the kind of candid conversation you don't get at most events. Each founder will share what they're building, why it matters, & the specific roles they're actively hiring for right now - followed by a mixer. What to expect: Founders presenting at the seed through Series B stage. Operators, builders, & executives who've seen what good looks like. An intentionally small room designed for real connection. Who this is for: Exceptional operators - whether you're actively exploring your next role, casually curious, or simply want to stay close to what's being built in NYC right now. Founders will be announced in the days leading up to the event.  Attendance is intentionally limited. Apply to be considered. More information on The Shortlist can be found here. Founded by Andrew Yeung & Ivor Straford.

And how are global investors & insurers preparing for a changing climate? Hear fresh perspectives from senior leaders at Mubadala Investment Company, London Stock Exchange Group, Trane Technologies, ServiceNow, American Family Insurance, BrainBox AI & more-alongside renowned scientists, entrepreneurs & changemakers from Columbia Climate School, the University of Toronto, Rutgers University & the Clean Air Task Force. We'll explore everything from AI & decarbonization to living nature, carbon credits, climate risk, microplastics, geothermal energy & sustainable finance-all through lively, accessible conversations designed for curious minds. Whether you're completely new to climate or already working in the field, you'll leave with fresh ideas, practical insights & plenty to talk about. No climate experience necessary-just bring your curiosity! Meet our incredible speakers on the Carbon Newbie Summit website. Light breakfast & full lunch will be served  CO-HOSTSCNaughtDebevoise & PlimptonTrane TechnologiesUniversity of Toronto - Lawson Climate InstituteClever Carbon The Carbon Newbie Summit is an initiative of Clever Carbon.  LIVESTREAMING AVAILABLE - register for the livestream ticket to receive details Who should attend?From climate experts to professionals new to sustainability & climate, our Summit welcomes anyone curious & passionate about climate. By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with our co-hosts/sponsors. About CNaught:Trusted by buyers like Asana, Medium, & Tiger Global, CNaught makes it easy to drive real climate impact through high-quality carbon credit portfolios. We deliver access to sophisticated buying strategies, previously available only to the largest buyers, enabling companies of any size to take meaningful climate action. Learn more: https://www.cnaught.com/ About Debevoise & Plimpton:Debevoise & Plimpton LLP is a premier law firm with market-leading practices, a global perspective & strong New York roots. Our clients look to us to bring a distinctively high degree of quality, intensity & creativity to resolve legal challenges effectively & cost efficiently. We have particularly deep experience in the broad range of issues that arise as environmental, social & governance (ESG) concerns & requirements become increasingly important. The firm brings together sophisticated, multidisciplinary & multinational teams to provide tailored & practical guidance across the evolving ESG & business integrity spectrum by counseling on trends & prudential issues, delivering concrete legal advice on evolving sustainability regulations & policies, & helping clients prepare for the legal, financial & reputational risks arising in this rapidly changing landscape. Learn more: https://www.debevoise.com/ About Trane Technologies:Trane Technologies is a global climate innovator. Through our strategic brands Trane & Thermo King, & our portfolio of environmentally responsible products & services, we bring efficient & sustainable climate solutions to buildings, homes & transportation.https://tranetechnologies.com About University of Toronto - Lawson Climate Institute:Through a multidisciplinary approach, the Lawson Climate Institute is ramping up U of T's capacity to advance the technologies & policies needed for Canada to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. As one of U of T's most wide-ranging, comprehensive initiatives, the institute is unique in its aim to ensure students in every discipline across three campuses have an opportunity to gain the tools needed to take concrete steps toward implementing practical climate solutions. The institute is named in honour of Brian Lawson & Joannah Lawson in recognition of their transformative $60-million donation to help establish the institute.https://lci.utoronto.ca About Clever Carbon:At Clever Carbon, we teach people about carbon footprint in a hip & fun way! From content creation to carbon footprint workshops, we work with leading brands around the world to help raise carbon literacy because what gets measured gets changed! Learn more: https://clevercarbon.io/

events.name: Interior Ecologies
events.description: From simple greenhouses to botanic facilities, & from data centers to automated interiors, never before in history has architecture produced so many interiors for the non-human, challenging disciplinary notions on tectonics, light, comfort & entire regulatory frameworks. Once designed for & with the human, contemporary interiors have instead become exponentially complex materializations where the politics of our present moment are played out. Ultimately, who are they for? Interior Ecologies is a critical framework developed within the Master of Arts in Interior Architecture (MAIA) program at Geneva School of Art & Design (HEAD - Genve). It examines how interior architecture engages with climate change, resource circulation & multispecies coexistence alongside posthuman & more-than-human design perspectives. Rather than treating interiors as autonomous spaces, it calls on us to rethink them as complex ecologies in which human & nonhuman actors are entangled across broader planetary scales. This roundtable brings together voices from HEAD - Genve, MoMA, & Columbia GSAPP to reflect on how interior architecture can contribute to new ecological approaches to design, research, & professional practice. The event will also include a presentation of the scenographic installation developed by MAIA for Assembly, the Swiss presence at Climate Week NYC. Employing scaffolding & dismantlable systems as an embodiment of circular architecture, the installation demonstrates principles of reuse, adaptability, & reversibility, staking its claim as an active ecological agent within the space. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Aligning Housing Abundance & Building Decarbonization
events.description: A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. View all events in the track at https://www.urbanclimatesolution.org/. By registering for this event, you agree to share your contact information with the organizers of Urban Climate Solution & co-hosting partner organization(s) for this session. This may include being added to mailing lists for future updates. You also agree that photos, video, & materials captured during the session may be used to document & promote the event & the organizers' work.

events.name: Private Dinner for Investors & Series A+ Founders - The AI Founder Playbook
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For founders of fast-growing Series A+ startups, with a limited number of investor seats. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, and how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, and judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, and the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening:Dinner and conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, and investors. A handful of invited voices will anchor the discussion including heads of CVCs and later stage AI founders. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is expected to bring opinions. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, and what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition and hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view. ORGANIZED BY Elpis LabsWe work with the government sector and international trade agencies to help their startups find corporate partners in the U.S. The VerticalAn online publication, community platform, and event series focusing on international venture ecosystem. Trinovation Partners: The "Scale AI" of Venture Backed Startups We are an AI data operations partner for venture-backed teams building computer vision and AI products. We build and run dedicated annotation pods: named, trained teams assigned to your product, not an anonymous crowd. Covering image and video annotation, gold-set calibration, human-in-the-loop QA, and edge-case review. Pods launch in 1-2 weeks, scale with your deployments, and deliver quality you can audit: 500+ annotators deployed, 95%+ QA accuracy, and a 30% model accuracy lift for our clients. Independent and New York-based.

events.description: Join Leading Voices Shaping the Future of Climate & Conservation Technology SkyTruth is convening the field's top leaders & practitioners for a high-impact gathering focused on one overarching question: how can geospatial data accelerate our collective progress on the planet's most pressing environmental challenges? This isn't just a series of panels, but a working session designed to surface gaps, spark partnerships, & drive action. events.name: Built World Resiliency - From Data Centers To Materials
events.description: This event (two panels & an accompanying happy hour with refreshments) spotlights high-growth emerging technology startups tackling critical infrastructure challenges in the Built Environment-from resilient power delivery for data centers to advanced materials & transparency platforms for infrastructure operations. We bring together founders with institutional real estate & infrastructure investors to connect frontier innovation with the capital & market access needed to scale durable, high-performance solutions across the global built world. The panels provide actionable insights to deliver reliable power for AI workloads, strengthen building-material supply chains, & improve procurement transparency through automated assessments-helping create a more resilient, resource-efficient built environment. The Built Environment is under pressure from every direction: surging energy demand, supply-chain volatility, tightening regulations, & aging infrastructure. The companies that will define the next era of real estate & infrastructure are building for resilience from day one. Built World Resiliency brings together startup founders & investors to explore how the next generation of infrastructure is being designed to perform under these new realities. Panel 1 - Powering AI: Building Resilient Compute Infrastructure (4:00 PM). AI is driving unprecedented demand for energy & physical infrastructure. This panel features two startups designing & engineering data centers & power systems that are faster to deploy, more efficient to operate, & less dependent on strained grid infrastructure-making resilience a competitive advantage, not a trade-off. Featuring: FLEXNODE's Chief Growth Officer Zak Kostura + ASTON POWER's co-founder Greg Robinson, moderated by Isela Bahena, Private Equity Infra at Nuveen   Panel 2 - Stronger Materials, Smarter Buildings (4:30 PM). The materials that go into every building are facing new scrutiny, from performance requirements & procurement mandates to environmental disclosure standards. This panel explores next-generation cement technology, AI-driven material intelligence, & automated lifecycle assessments that help project teams build with better data, better products, & greater confidence. Featuring: CURA's founder Erin Bobicki + PATHWAYS' founder Leise Sanderman + ACELABS' co-founder Vardhan Meta, moderated by Markus Gatterwe of Holcim (Ventures) The event opens with a networking session around 3:15/30 PM, followed by panels from 4:00-5:15 PM, & then a light happy hour. The lineup & content may change as we confirm additional speakers & institutional partners.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Drone delivery gets regulatory approval - Now what? DoorDash just became only the eighth company ever to earn FAA air-carrier certification for drones, joining Amazon, Walmart, & Alphabet's Wing in a race that's now more about economics than regulation. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Backing Innovation - How States Investing In The Future
events.description: State venture funds are playing an increasingly important role in building regional innovation ecosystems. This panel brings together leaders from three of the Northeast's most active public VC programs - Connecticut Innovations, New York State's NY Ventures, & the New Jersey Economic Development Authority - for a candid discussion on how government capital is shaping the next generation of startups. Panelists will discuss how their funds source & evaluate deals, what differentiates public venture capital from traditional VC, & where they see the biggest opportunities for founders & investors across the region. Stick around afterwards for a happy hour with the founders & VCs. Meet the panelists: Danny Qiao is a Director on Connecticut Innovations' investment team, where he leads the team's consumer & international investment efforts. Prior to CI, he led consumer investing at Sweater Ventures, backing brands like IQBAR, Graza, Nomadica, OROS, & Havenly. He began his career at Accenture Strategy & later covered financial sponsors & financial institutions in investment banking at BNP Paribas. Danny holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management & a BS from Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations. Jennifer Tegan is the Managing Director of Empire State Development's New York Ventures, where she oversees over $320 million in investment programs aimed at fueling New York's startup ecosystem. Since joining in 2020, she has managed direct & indirect investment funds including the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund & the Emerging & Regional Manager Partner Fund (a fund of funds). An experienced investor & advocate, Jennifer previously spent 18 years as a partner at Cayuga Venture Fund. She has served on the board of the National Venture Capital Association & held leadership roles with Tompkins Financial Corporation & the Upstate Capital Association of New York. Jennifer holds an MBA from Cornell University, an MS from the University of Cincinnati, & a BA from Smith College. John Wisniewski is the Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives & Venture Products at New Jersey Economic Development Authority. His responsibilities include oversight of the state's investment into Strategic Innovation Centers, & venture investment programs. John started his career with ExxonMobil where he held various positions developing projects in the US & internationally.  He ran a private equity infrastructure fund based in the Middle East for Arcapita Bank, & then switched to venture capital working with Clean Energy Ventures Group. John has a BS in Chemical Engineering from Cooper Union, & an MBA from Rice University. Meet the hosts: Connecticut Innovations is Connecticut's venture capital arm, investing in early & growth-stage biotech, IT, & deep tech companies. NY Ventures is New York State's innovation venture capital fund, backing high-growth startups across the state. NJEDA's Venture Products team supports New Jersey's innovation ecosystem, including through the New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. Meet the sponsors: Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups & the accountants supporting them. With banking setup in minutes, cashback cards, & tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused, backed by support that goes to the end of the earth to help you win. Rho is a fintech company, not a bank. Checking & card services are provided by Webster Bank, N.A., member FDIC; savings account services are provided by American Deposit Management Co. & its partner banks. KPMG Private provides specialized advisory, audit, tax, & strategic consulting services tailored for emerging growth companies, startups, & private enterprises scaling up through various lifecycle stages. Whether you're launching a startup or accelerating your growth, the Emerging Growth team offers strategic insights & resources designed to support your business journey. #nyc #venturecapital #government

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: Trading For Food Security In Changing Climate
events.description: The Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) at MIT would like to invite you to a panel discussion titled Trading for Food Security in a Changing Climate". International food trade has become essential for global food security, but the same interconnected networks that move food also transmit shocks-climatic, economic, & geopolitical. A panel of relevant industry experts will examine the linkages between food trade & food security through the lens of healthy diets & introduce the Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, developed by MIT J-WAFS. The Index maps food-trade vulnerability across more than 180 countries. Join us for a moderated discussion on three questions: how to assess food security versus an inability to import; what balance of home-grown & imported food best serves healthy nutrition as diets shift; & where investment in productivity, infrastructure, & research are most needed as the climate changes. ModeratorGreg Sixt, Director, Food & Climate Systems Transformation (FACT) Alliance & Research Director for Food & Climate Systems, Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) Opening presentation: Introduction to the Jameel Index & J-WAFS work on food security, global change, & tradeKenneth Strzepek, Technical Lead, Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, MIT J-WAFS PanelistsProf. Sheryl Hendriks, Extraordinary Professor, University of Pretoria Mark Rosegrant, Research Fellow Emeritus, International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), Former Director of IFPRI's Environment & Production Technology Division Paola de Almeida, CEO, Natural Systems Capital & Jameel Index Advisory Committee Member

events.name: Family Offices & Investors Summit
events.description: 150 seats. One room. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). This year, we're raising the bar & want to double that number.  WHO'S BEEN IN THE ROOM: Invited Family Offices & Institutional Capital  KKR ($361B+ AUM, New York) - Global investment firm. Principal from KKR's Sustainability & Capital Formation team joining us.  Generation Investment Management ($44B+ AUM, San Francisco / London) - Al Gore's sustainable investment firm. Founding Partner Colin le Duc returning for the second consecutive year.  Rockefeller Foundation ($6B endowment, New York) - Director of Energy Technology & Innovation Shunondo Basu. Net-zero endowment commitment. Speaker at both 2025 summits, returning for 2026  Merit France / CMA CGM Saade Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  Energy Impact Partners ($4.5B AUM, New York) - Climate infrastructure VC backed by 80+ global utility & energy partners. Returning for 2026.  Schmidt Sciences (Multi-$B, Palo Alto) - Eric Schmidt's frontier science & technology initiative. Returning for 2026  Wittington Ventures ($500M venture platform / $21B Weston family, Canada) - The venture arm of one of North America's largest private family enterprises. events.description: Hi fellow founders  Angela & Hamza here from the AI Furnace. The AI Founders Supper Club is a private founders dinner club hosted by The AI Furnace (the largest community of AI startups in the world). Once a month, we host 15-20 early stage AI founders for a night of delicious food, discussions & connections with curated high quality founders in NYC. This is a referral based network, so feel free to apply here but the other way to get in is by being referred in by an existing founder member. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Meet dope founders building out of NYC Real conversations & place to vibe with other founders, solving similar problems ABOUT OUR HOSTS & SPONSORS The AI Furnace is NYC's largest & most active AI community. It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Stripe is a technology company that builds economic infrastructure for the internet. Businesses of every size - from new startups to public companies - use our software to accept payments & manage their businesses online.

events.name: Addressing Cost Of Climate Impact - Actions At Scale Of The City
events.description: How do cities bridge the gap between high-level climate vulnerability data & everyday financial execution? While municipalities globally are tracking climate risks, the challenge lies in transforming these insights into the routine machinery of city governance: capital planning, investment, & budgeting. Co-hosted by C40 Cities & Climate Solutions International to discuss their landmark report, Mainstreaming Climate Adaptation in City Financial Planning & Budgeting, this high-level panel brings together policy architects & municipal finance leaders. events.name: Beyond Mineral Supply Security - Partnerships & Community Rights
events.description: Critical minerals: who captures the value, who bears the risk? A panel on financing a just transition for producer nations. There is no climate transition without transition minerals & how they are governed will decide whether decarbonisation delivers development & prosperity for producer countries, or simply repeats extractive patterns under a green label. This panel co- convened with Oxfam examines the gap between the G7's Critical Minerals Action Plan, which frames minerals mainly as a supply security issue for consumer economies, & South Africa's 2025 G20 Critical Minerals Framework, which centres value retention, local industrialisation & community rights. With the UK holding the G20 presidency in 2027 & the G7 presidency in 2028, there is a genuine window to shift finance toward producer-country processing, regional value chains, & enforceable safeguards including Free, Prior & Informed Consent as a right, not a formality. Join us to explore what truly financed partnership with mineral-rich Global South nations could look like in practice.

events.name: Making The Case For Climate-Aligned Abundance & Urbanism
events.description: We welcome all guests to stay after the panel for a light reception. The fiscal & climate case for infill housing is increasingly hard to dispute - but data alone hasn't been enough to overcome the political & aesthetic resistance to density, even if it's for the better. This panel is about the messaging gap: how advocates, designers, & coalition-builders are translating cost curves & emissions data & examples of beautiful infill housing from around the world into narratives & images that make compact, mixed-use development the changes communities yearn for rather than something imposed on them. Panelists will share what's worked around the country - & what hasn't - in turning abundance into a story policymakers, developers, & the public actually want to be part of. Speakers: Rushad Nanavatty (Moderator),Managing Director, RMI  Brian Hanlon, CEO, Metropolitan Abundance Project + California YIMBY  Caroline Spears, Executive Director, Climate Cabinet Education  Heather Clark, CEO, Housing Multiplier Project  Justyn Huckleberry, Projects & Research Associate, WRI This session is hosted by World Resources Institute, Metropolitan Abundance Project, Gehl, Climate Cabinet, & the Parking Reform Network & is a part of the Urban Climate Solutions Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: Local Climate Imperative - Public-Private Partnerships In Action
events.description: Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion during Climate Week NYC 2026 As climate action increasingly takes shape at the local level, cities, businesses, & communities are finding new ways to work together to drive meaningful progress. Yet opportunities for public-sector climate leaders & corporate sustainability professionals to learn from one another remain surprisingly rare. Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion at BelCham Atelier, exploring the power of public-private partnerships to accelerate climate progress. Rather than a traditional panel, the program will feature a select group of speakers sharing practical examples of how collaboration across government, business, & community partners is driving meaningful change - from policy development & implementation to corporate strategy & investment. The remainder of the event will focus on networking & facilitated discussion, creating space for participants to share best practices, discuss common challenges, & identify new opportunities to work together. Join us for a morning of insightful conversation, meaningful connections, & practical ideas to help strengthen the partnerships driving climate action forward. About Agendi & Run on Climate Run on Climate & Agendi share a belief that accelerating climate progress requires stronger connections between the public & private sectors. While Run on Climate helps local governments advance ambitious climate policies & implementation, Agendi partners with companies to translate climate commitments into actionable business strategies. Bringing these communities together creates a unique opportunity to exchange perspectives, identify shared challenges, & explore new models for collaboration that can accelerate climate action at the local level.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. events.name: Roots To Renewal - Green Careers Reentry Summit
events.description: This event will bring together leaders across reentry, workforce development, government, philanthropy, & community to ask a critical question: How do we ensure that New York's transition to a green economy creates opportunity & economic mobility for communities too often excluded from emerging industries? Co-convened by Fordham University & The Institute for Justice & Opportunity (IJO) at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, the summit will explore how green career pathways can expand access to quality jobs & economic mobility for justice-impacted New Yorkers & their families, while ensuring their experiences & perspectives help inform how those pathways are built. The day moves from conversation to action, beginning with a candid City-State Fireside Chat & solutions-oriented discussions on reentry & workforce pathways, followed by an interactive Green Careers & Community Street Fair featuring workforce & service providers, the Bronx Green Jobs Center, a NYC Decarbonization Mural activation, community engagement, food, & live music. Because a just transition is not only about transforming our buildings, infrastructure, & communities. It is about ensuring that the people who have historically been left out of economic opportunity have a meaningful role in shaping, building, & benefiting from what comes next.

events.name: PMAI Fight Right - Co-Founders Guide To Disagreement
events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: The Scope 3 Paradox
events.description: Are you responsible for emissions you don't control? Join us for Summit in the Sky, a private panel & networking event held during Climate Week NYC 2026 at One World Trade Center. This invitation-only event brings together senior sustainability, procurement, & supply chain leaders from large corporates actively managing Scope 3 programs, to tackle the defining challenge of corporate decarbonization: being fully accountable for emissions that sit entirely outside your direct operations. Nearly 80% of sustainability leaders cite supplier data availability as their biggest barrier. events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise.
