events.name: Net Zero Value Chains - Advancing Credible Scope 3 Decarbonization
events.description: The corporate climate landscape is moving toward greater rigor, with growing expectations for companies to substantiate climate action through credible data, accounting, & reporting. The GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard (LSRS) introduces a more robust framework for accounting & reporting land-based emissions & CO removals. However, implementation remains challenging, with companies navigating supplier data gaps, limited traceability, allocation challenges, & evolving assurance expectations. At the same time, organizations are exploring how market-based approaches can help accelerate credible Scope 3 action beyond their direct operations. Join corporate sustainability leaders, standard setters, climate experts, & solution providers to explore two key developments shaping the future of value chain decarbonization: Panel 1: Implementing the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard Hear from experts & early adopters on the practical challenges of implementing the LSRS, including data quality, traceability, allocation, reporting, & assurance. Learn what organizations are doing today-and what may be needed to support scalable implementation in the years ahead. Speakers:Matt Ramlow, Senior Research Associate, GHG P Martha Stevenson, Senior Director, Strategy & Research, Forests, WWF Noora Singh, Senior Director, Global Sustainability, PepsiCoChristina O'Keefe, Head of Sustainability, North America, Kerry Panel 2: The emerging role of Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) Explore how carbon credits, environmental certificates, & other market-based approaches could support Scope 3 decarbonization. events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.description: Is the SaaS Pricing Model Dead?For twenty years, SaaS companies built their businesses around recurring subscriptions. AI is breaking that model. Seat licenses are turning into token pricing. Some customers want to pay for outcomes, not users. If you run a dev shop building AI products, or you're a funded founder trying to scale one, you're probably already feeling this. events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Crux Alliance
events.description: Crux Alliance is spotlighting the leaders driving smart climate policy in the world's highest-emitting countries at Climate Week NYC. Across our events, we'll bring together researchers & advocates to explore sustainable cities & transport, energy security, & electrification, highlighting the policies & communication strategies that unlock affordable clean energy & improve quality of life for millions. We look forward to connecting with you there. All events will be hosted on the 2nd floor of Lulla at the Motto by Hilton Chelsea, 113 West 24th Street. Tues., Sept. 228:00 - 9:30 AMWin-Win Policies: Unlocking Investment for a Sustainable FutureIn this session, organizations from the transport, appliances, & building operations sectors will discuss policies that discourage undesirable outcomes while helping to fund sustainable solutions in countries around the world.  Experts from ITDP, ICCT, CLASP, & GBPN will explore how these policy mechanisms were designed, implementation challenges, lessons learned, & their potential to support long-term urban sustainability goals. Participants will gain insights into how strategic policy interventions can be designed to help governments achieve multiple objectives simultaneously: reducing emissions, improving quality of life, & unlocking investment in sustainable development. SpeakersJacob Mason, Senior Global Program Director, Institute for Transportation & Development Policy Ana Mara Carreo, Senior Director of Climate, CLASP Tim Dallmann, Director of Global Program, International Council on Clean Transportation RSVP    crux alliance logo10:30 - 12:00 PMSuper Pollutants to Super Solutions: Targeting Diesel Black Carbon for Climate & Health BenefitsSuper pollutants like black carbon are compounding the effects of climate change & harming human health. But they are often overlooked in CO2-based climate policies. This event will explore how transportation & climate policies at all levels of government can better account for & address super pollutants rather than treating them as an afterthought.Speakers:Brooke Helmick, Director of Policy, New Jersey Environmental Justice Alliance Sean Maguire, Executive Director, Strategic Partnerships, Clean Air Fund Ray Minjares, Program Director, Heavy-Duty Vehicles, International Council on Clean Transportation Moderator: Claire Henley, Executive Director, Super Pollutant Action Alliance  RSVP  1:00 - 2:00 PMFrom Evidence to Impact: Communicating the Case for Smart PolicyRobust research on vehicle technology & transportation policy can't translate itself into policy-or into public understanding. This session brings together communications leaders to explore how to turn technical research into powerful messaging, tools, & products that policymakers, media, & the public can actually use. The conversation will discuss what makes evidence usable for regulators, how to package complex findings-like the economic, health, & environmental gains of stronger vehicle standards-into compelling, accessible formats, & how communications teams can bridge the gap between researchers & the decision-makers who shape transportation policy. SpeakersMichael Doerrer, Senior Director of Communications & Development, International Council on Clean Transportation Leah Qusba, CEO, GoodPower Elan Strait, Executive Director, Potential Energy Moderator: Sarah Spengeman, Communications Director, Crux Alliance RSVP  3:00 - 4:30 PMResisting the Easy Fix: The Limits of Coal as a National Response to Geopolitical ShiftsAs global fuel market disruptions & geopolitical tensions revive interest in domestic energy resources, this side event examines whether coal can realistically serve as a pillar of energy security & economic resilience. Drawing on experiences from major coal regions-Poland, Trkiye, China, the United States, & South Africa-experts will discuss how recent energy crises have reshaped national coal debates, the true costs of continued reliance, & the benefits of clean alternatives, supporting evidence-based dialogue ahead of COP31. SpeakersJoanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii, Poland Rabia Ferroukhi, Director, INETTT Secretariat Alkm Ba Gll, Director, SHURA Energy Transition Center, Trkiye Kevin Tu, Chief Advisor China, Agora Energiewende Tracy Ledger, Just Transition Programme Lead, Public Affairs Research Institute, South Africa Mary Anne Hitt, Managing Director of U.S. Initiatives, Climate Imperative Moderator: Steve Capanna, Director of Policy, Crux Alliance RSVP   4:30 - 6:30 PMMeet the "Wonks" Behind the Wins: A Networking Happy HourJoin Crux Alliance, ReNew2030, Global Grids Catalyst, & Growald Climate Fund for a Climate Week NYC happy hour celebrating the policy experts advancing climate policy where it has the greatest impact. The afternoon will include a short program spotlighting the work of these philanthropic initiatives & their partners, with plenty of time for building new connections. Come meet the wonks behind the wins: the people translating climate goals into policy that bends the curve, delivering cleaner air, lower costs, & better lives for millions. Brief remarks shared by:Rebecca Collyer, Executive Director, ReNew2030 Kartikeya Singh, Director, Collective Impact, Growald Climate Fund Joanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii RSVP    Wed., Sept. 238:00 - 9:30 AMFrom Gridlock to Grid-Ready: A Coordinated Path to 35-by-35The COP31 35-by-35 electrification pledge is an urgent call for governments to embrace an ambitious electrification plan. But that ambition will stall without fixing outdated grid planning & aging, insufficient grid infrastructure across major economies. Solutions exist-but building a clean, modern grid ready for all-electric buildings, industry, & transport requires coordination across sectors & stakeholders: developers, planners, & policymakers. This panel will discuss why we must tackle the grid challenge holistically & share how a coordinated approach is unlocking smarter policy, planning, operations, & deployment-and the affordability, reliability, & security benefits that follow. Panelists will share complementary approaches taking shape in the geographies that will make or break the electrification transition.

events.name: Future US Role In Global Conservation
events.description: What should the future U.S. role in global conservation look like, & whose experience & ideas should shape it? The biodiversity funding landscape changed dramatically in 2025 as the USG abruptly abandoned its international conservation commitments. The loss of approximately $500 million in annual U.S. international conservation funding, along with decades of government capacity & expertise, disrupted conservation efforts around the world. This moment demands more than restoring the former system. It creates an opportunity to examine it critically: what worked, what did not, whose perspectives carried weight, & what must change to build a more effective & durable approach. Hosted by Reimagining Global Conservation, this event will bring together international & locally rooted conservation practitioners, policy experts, funders, & other Climate Week participants. One Earth Partners will present findings from Beyond the Funding Gap, its global assessment of USAID's distinctive role in climate & environmental programming, the structural effects of its 2025 withdrawal, & priorities for future U.S. engagement. A diverse panel of practitioners will then offer locally-grounded perspectives on the future U.S. role, including concrete reforms, institutional changes, & practical proposals for a new global conservation playbook. The session will create space for participants to question familiar assumptions & contribute ideas grounded in their own experience. Biodiversity conservation is inseparable from resilience, livelihoods, stability, & security. Join us for a candid, nonpartisan conversation about how the United States can learn from the past & engage differently in the future.

events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: When Data Goes Dark - Preparing For Climate Disasters In Era Of Science Disinvestment
events.description: Over the past year, climate science & environmental data & tools have faced steep disinvestment, but maintaining a strong scientific enterprise & the data it creates is critical to helping communities & businesses prepare for & respond to climate risks. When that data disappears, so does our ability to anticipate, prepare for, & respond to climate disasters before they strike. This panel starts by looking at what's been lost, & at the rescue efforts now underway to preserve high-fidelity climate data & disaster-cost datasets before they disappear for good. It then turns forward: what will it take to rebuild a more resilient, connected environmental data ecosystem - one built so that this kind of loss can't happen again? Join us for a conversation that moves from triage to reimagining, bringing together leaders in climate science, environmental data, global research, & emergency management to chart what comes next. Sponsored By:American Geophysical UnionClimate CentralThe New York Climate ExchangeOpen Environmental Data Project

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: AI & Sustainability Mgmt - Case Studies From The Field
events.description: This event is free entry with limited tickets available. The organizer will provide a calendar invite to guests up to capacity. If capacity is reached you will be notified. AI & Sustainability Management:Case Studies from the FieldAI is already playing a central role in many companies' sustainability strategy, management, & reporting efforts. Whether it is AI-based materiality, tools to assist in the calculation of greenhouse gas inventories, or AI-enabled sustainability reporting systems, this is an area of fast-moving innovation that has captured the imagination of sustainability practitioners. While we must take the environmental implications of AI usage seriously, we must also evaluate the potential that this technology represents - do the benefits outweigh the impacts? What We'll Explore: AI & Business Intelligence: How business intelligence data platforms are transforming data collection, analysis, & insight generation. AI-enabled sustainability - Is it worth the price?: What is the current state of the art knowledge in terms of the cost/benefit tradeoffs of AI in terms of environmental impacts? Building Qualitative & Quantitative Connections: How AI can help companies better understand the linkages between sustainability performance & financial performance. AI & Assurance: How AI-supported data processes & 3rd party verification connect. Is your organization ready for third party verification in the era of AI-based tools & processes? Speakers: Matt Gardner, Managing Partner at Sustainserv Julie Kae, VP of Sustainability at Qlik Technologies Julien Gervreau, Director at Sensiba LLP Who Should Attend:CSOs, CCOs, IROs, & sustainability professionals navigating the intersection of AI capabilities, reporting requirements, & stakeholder engagement in an increasingly complex sustainability landscape

events.name: Making Circularity Pay Off
events.description: Learn to quantify the financial performance of circular products, & connect with industry experts over a European breakfast. We all believe in circularity, yet why is it taking off so slowly? One key reason is the lack of clear measurement of its financial value. To speed up adoption, we must be able to measure the economic impact of circular products. The Circular Value Index (CVI) does exactly this.   In this session, you will learn how to use the Index to quantify & communicate the financial performance of circular products. Experts from industry & academia will share concise insights & practical perspectives on applying circularity in business.   This year we also look ahead. The World Circular Economy Forum is where the global circular economy community sets its agenda, & we will share a special announcement about what comes next & how you can be part of it.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Drone delivery gets regulatory approval - Now what? DoorDash just became only the eighth company ever to earn FAA air-carrier certification for drones, joining Amazon, Walmart, & Alphabet's Wing in a race that's now more about economics than regulation. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of The Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: The New Blueprint - Climate Resiliency By Design
events.description: Discover how NYC is shaping the future of climate-resilient infrastructure & buildings through new policy, guidance, & real-world lessons. The New Blueprint: Climate Resiliency by Design As policymakers, planners & designers, we have learned a great deal over the last decade about the science & real-world impacts of our changing climate, as well as how to innovate & guide capital projects in New York City to become more resilient. We are now at a pivotal moment where this knowledge is being used to measure effectiveness & inform climate resilience requirements for the city's infrastructure & buildings. Representatives from the Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice, NYC Housing Preservation & Development, & Port Authority of NY & NJ will highlight key areas of focus within evolving climate resiliency design guidelines. This panel will provide valuable insights on updates to climate resiliency design requirements for capital infrastructure & building projects throughout New York City, while also showcasing lessons learned from ongoing & completed pilot projects. This panel presentation starts promptly at 10AM, attendees are encouraged to arrive early to grab coffee & a great seat! Following the presentation is a 30-minute networking reception with light refreshments & more coffee. *IN-PERSON EVENT CAPPED AT 50 PEOPLE*Please note, this is a hybrid event with two separate registration links for virtual & in-person. events.name: Extreme Heat & Vulnerable Populations Datathon

To celebrate, we're doubling down on our commitment to finding & scaling world-changing innovation with a million dollars in prize funding allocated to ten innovators & their solutions to this year's Global Challenges. events.description: Antenna House: The Value TransitionPresented by Sunrun | Powered by Antenna GroupSeptember 23, 2026 | LUME Studios, New York, NY The climate transition is broader than a moral issue. It's about value. The profitable path & the sustainable path are the same path. Solar is the cheapest form of energy. AI is driving demand at a scale only clean solutions can meet. The leaders finding faster, cheaper paths to power already stopped making the moral argument. They're moving because the business case is undeniable. The gap between proven & scaled has never been more urgent to close. No single company, sector, or technology closes it alone. This is the Age of Adoption. The question isn't what works. It's what gets understood, trusted, & scaled. That's the conversation at Antenna House 2026. Register below for the sessions you plan to attend: 10:40 AM - 11:25 AM: The State of Climate Storytelling: Media Panel with The Financial Times, Washington Post & Canary Media 11:30 AM - 12:35 PM: Where Sustainability Meets Storytelling 12:30 PM - 1:15 PM: The Race to Build the Next Generation City: A Conversation with Voltera CEO Frank Reig 1:40 PM - 2:20 PM: Trophy Assets Don't Need Saving. Everything Else Does. 2:30 PM - 3:10 PM: Shaping the Data Center Narrative 3:15 PM - 3:55 PM: AI Needs More Power. Who Builds It, What Gets Built, & Who Gets Paid? 4:00 PM - 4:40 PM: The Customer-First Path to Powering AI

The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. events.name: Convening The Next-Generation Materials Transition
events.description: The future of fashion depends on bringing next-generation materials to scale. While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. As one of the world's largest platforms for climate collaboration, it creates the ideal environment to build the relationships & shared understanding needed to move promising innovations beyond pilots & into practice. The Forum contributes to that momentum by connecting the people who can help shape the future of next-generation materials. Forum Partners Developed with & featuring voices from: Eco-Age - a purpose-led media & communications agency accelerating the fashion industry's transition to sustainability. Canopy - an award-winning environmental non-profit driving the shift to next-generation, forest-free fibres. Fashion for Good - the global platform for sustainable fashion innovation, connecting brands & innovators to scale breakthrough solutions. Material ConneXion - the world's leading materials insights company, connecting industries to the most innovative & sustainable materials available. Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) - New York's internationally renowned college for fashion, design, business & technology, fostering innovation, education & industry collaboration across the global fashion & textile sector. The Programme The Forum combines a keynote, structured workshops, & a networking reception. Through an invitation-based format & curated audience, participants will explore the opportunities & challenges shaping the next chapter of material innovation. The programme, speakers, & venue are currently being developed with our partners & will be announced in the coming weeks. Who Should Attend The Forum is designed for senior leaders in sustainability, sourcing, supply chain, & procurement across the fashion, apparel, & textile industry. It is built for the people inside the industry who are responsible for what gets made, how it is sourced, & what it is made from. Event Details 22 September 20263:30 PM - 7:30 PMFashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York City Pre-register now for priority access & programme updates. Registration is open but subject to review. We reserve the right to cancel registrations from organisations outside this scope. We look forward to seeing you there.

events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Aligning Housing Abundance & Building Decarbonization
events.description: A light lunch for all guests will be served after the panel. The housing affordability & climate crises are often addressed through separate - & sometimes competing - policy agendas. Housing advocates seek faster approvals, lower construction costs, & fewer barriers to infill development. Building decarbonization advocates seek to prevent decades of additional fossil-fuel dependence by advancing all-electric construction, stronger performance standards, & cleaner energy systems. But housing production & decarbonization do not have to be opposing goals. Well-designed infill housing can reduce transportation emissions, lower household energy costs, improve indoor air quality, & protect residents from extreme heat & wildfire smoke. Poorly designed or poorly sequenced requirements, however, can add cost, delay projects, strain electrical infrastructure, or disproportionately affect affordable & smaller-scale development. This session will examine where housing & decarbonization strategies reinforce one another, where genuine implementation tensions arise, & how policymakers, developers, advocates, utilities, & funders can resolve them. Panelists will explore practical approaches to codes, incentives, permitting, utility coordination, affordability protections, & policy sequencing that allow communities to build more housing without locking in long-term emissions or future retrofit costs. The session will conclude with a set of principles for advancing housing abundance, affordability, electrification, & climate resilience together. Speakers: Heather Clark (Moderator), CEO Housing Multiplier Project  Aimee Witteman, Chief Impact Officer, ULI  Matthew Lewis, Director of Communications, California YIMBY  Raghav Muralidharan, Manager, RMI  Paul Caine, Vice President, BB Holdings This session is hosted by the Urban Land Institute, the Housing-Climate Project, Gehl, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution Track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: The Scope 3 Paradox
events.description: Are you responsible for emissions you don't control? Join us for Summit in the Sky, a private panel & networking event held during Climate Week NYC 2026 at One World Trade Center. This invitation-only event brings together senior sustainability, procurement, & supply chain leaders from large corporates actively managing Scope 3 programs, to tackle the defining challenge of corporate decarbonization: being fully accountable for emissions that sit entirely outside your direct operations. Nearly 80% of sustainability leaders cite supplier data availability as their biggest barrier. Companies that actively engage suppliers are nine times more likely to hit their Scope 3 targets, yet only one in three currently do so. events.name: Making The Case For Climate-Aligned Abundance & Urbanism
events.description: We welcome all guests to stay after the panel for a light reception. The fiscal & climate case for infill housing is increasingly hard to dispute - but data alone hasn't been enough to overcome the political & aesthetic resistance to density, even if it's for the better. events.name: Fashioning Positive Impact - 20 Yrs Of Pioneering Circular Fashion
events.description: Fashioning Positive Impact: 20 Years of Circularity for Business Longevity. Hear from DEPLOY's Founder, Dr. Bernice Pan as she shares insights from two decades of circular, design-led thinking & how it can create lasting value for business, people & planet. EVENT OUTLINE For two decades, DEPLOY has tested what it means to build circularity into the foundations of a business - from product design & production to service, customer experience & long-term care. At this 'meet the founder' event, Dr. Bernice Pan will share reflections from 20 years of turning systems change theory into business practice, & consider how circular, design-led thinking can beautifully support business & planetary resilience, relevance & longevity. The session will bring together senior leaders from business, finance, sustainability & policy to explore what long-term value looks like in a resource-constrained world. About DEPLOY Founded in 2006, DEPLOY is one of the world's earliest ethical fashion pioneers & a strategic action plan to reform fashion. Its signature 360 Sustainability Compass puts care for makers, wearers & the planet at the heart of the business, embedding this approach across design, production, service, repair & long-term use. DEPLOY is the world's highest-scoring fashion B Corp, with a score of 176.8, & actively contributes towards 12 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. Its work has been recognised by the Great British Brands Award for Commitment to Planet, the Future Icon Award for Best Zero-Waste Brand & the Marie Claire Sustainability Award for Ethical Fashion Brand of the Year.

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: State Of Supply Chain Sustainability Report Launch
events.description: The 2026 State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report examines a paradox at the heart of corporate sustainability today: commitment is rising, even as the ability to deliver is becoming more difficult. The report explores how companies are responding to geopolitical disruption, governance gaps, fragmented sustainability data, rapid advances in Industrial & Agentic AI, & the broader challenge of embedding sustainability more deeply into supply chain decisions & operations. Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

Produced by the MIT Sustainable Supply Chain Lab at the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics & sponsored by C.H. Robinson Foundation, Breakthrough, & CO2 AI with Dassault Systmes, the report reveals where progress is real, where the constraints are tightening, & why greater efficiency & intelligence do not automatically translate into greater sustainability. Join us for a panel discussion in the Chelsea/Meatpacking District with the research team exploring four major themes from this year's findings: Two Gaps: How Geopolitics & Governance Are Testing Corporate Sustainability - how stronger corporate commitment is colliding with external disruption, while public sustainability ambition is outpacing the internal governance & accountability needed to deliver it. Where Sustainability Lives in the Supply Chain - where sustainability is actually embedded in supply chain decisions, where it remains weak, what benefits companies are realizing, & how measurement & collaboration are expanding across the value chain. AI & Sustainability - how organizations are using Industrial & Agentic AI, what AI is contributing to sustainability today, & why greater efficiency & autonomy do not necessarily translate into lower environmental impact. Freight Transportation & Warehousing - how two critical physical parts of the supply chain are progressing on decarbonization, where efficiency gains are reaching their limits, & how technology, economics, infrastructure, & regional differences are shaping what comes next. A confirmed ticket is required for entry. No walk-ins or unregistered guests will be accommodated.

events.name: Buildings & Materials Conference
events.description: WHERE BUILDING TECH & MATERIALS COME TOGETHERThe annual Buildings + Materials Conference explores innovation & emerging technology in the development, design, materials, & systems of buildings. The event examines the current state & trajectory of building planning & operational solutions, strategies, & processes, providing insights & guidance on implementation, use cases, opportunities, & challenges. Connect. Inform. Advance.The premier network for advancing innovation & catalyzing collaboration throughout the built environment ecosystem. It Began As a Digital Community Connecting, Sharing, & LearningIn the fall of 2013, BuiltWorlds analysts began harnessing the power of digital media, crowd sourcing, & open innovation, sharing what they were learning & who they were meeting via social media & drawing in ever more passionate, open, experts who shared even more insights & data. The resulting network effect produced a global community of thousands of people actively providing data & contacts, curated by our analyst team, who then shared with back with the community in the form of actionable insights & deeper understanding. From the Community, A Powerful Research Network EmergedBuiltWorlds emerged as a free community, fueled by subscribers & supported by a small groups of sponsors. However, as the community grew, more members of the community wanted to access more of BuiltWorlds' research & collaborate more actively with others in the community.  Striving to meet that need, the BuiltWorlds Member Network was formed, a research group within the larger BuiltWorlds Community, supporting the development of specific areas of research, collaborating in working forums, learning together in research tracks, & convening in person at conferences to go deeper into the research together, to compare notes in person, & to guide future research efforts. From The Network, Research Tracks Developed to Help Members Go Deeper into Key Areas of ChangeAs BuiltWorlds adds Member Companies to its research network, the number of research tracks offers & the depth of research & connection also continues to grow, as members learn & connect through a comprehensive & immersive mix of in person & digitally delivered content & programs.

events.name: Governing Wealth Transfer - Turning AI Tech Billions Into Climate Reparations

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

All attendees must submit an application & be approved to attend. If selected as a finalist we require one person from your team to record a demo on-site September 26th which will then be displayed at .local NYC. To be eligible to win, finalists must also be available on September 30th to attend MongoDB.local NYC & present their project.

events.name: Backing Innovation - How States Investing In The Future
events.description: State venture funds are playing an increasingly important role in building regional innovation ecosystems. This panel brings together leaders from three of the Northeast's most active public VC programs - Connecticut Innovations, New York State's NY Ventures, & the New Jersey Economic Development Authority - for a candid discussion on how government capital is shaping the next generation of startups. Panelists will discuss how their funds source & evaluate deals, what differentiates public venture capital from traditional VC, & where they see the biggest opportunities for founders & investors across the region. Stick around afterwards for a happy hour with the founders & VCs. Meet the panelists: Danny Qiao is a Director on Connecticut Innovations' investment team, where he leads the team's consumer & international investment efforts. Prior to CI, he led consumer investing at Sweater Ventures, backing brands like IQBAR, Graza, Nomadica, OROS, & Havenly. He began his career at Accenture Strategy & later covered financial sponsors & financial institutions in investment banking at BNP Paribas. Danny holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management & a BS from Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations. Jennifer Tegan is the Managing Director of Empire State Development's New York Ventures, where she oversees over $320 million in investment programs aimed at fueling New York's startup ecosystem. Since joining in 2020, she has managed direct & indirect investment funds including the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund & the Emerging & Regional Manager Partner Fund (a fund of funds). An experienced investor & advocate, Jennifer previously spent 18 years as a partner at Cayuga Venture Fund. She has served on the board of the National Venture Capital Association & held leadership roles with Tompkins Financial Corporation & the Upstate Capital Association of New York. Jennifer holds an MBA from Cornell University, an MS from the University of Cincinnati, & a BA from Smith College. John Wisniewski is the Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives & Venture Products at New Jersey Economic Development Authority. His responsibilities include oversight of the state's investment into Strategic Innovation Centers, & venture investment programs. John started his career with ExxonMobil where he held various positions developing projects in the US & internationally.  He ran a private equity infrastructure fund based in the Middle East for Arcapita Bank, & then switched to venture capital working with Clean Energy Ventures Group. John has a BS in Chemical Engineering from Cooper Union, & an MBA from Rice University. Meet the hosts: Connecticut Innovations is Connecticut's venture capital arm, investing in early & growth-stage biotech, IT, & deep tech companies. NY Ventures is New York State's innovation venture capital fund, backing high-growth startups across the state. NJEDA's Venture Products team supports New Jersey's innovation ecosystem, including through the New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. Meet the sponsors: Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups & the accountants supporting them. With banking setup in minutes, cashback cards, & tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused, backed by support that goes to the end of the earth to help you win. Rho is a fintech company, not a bank. Checking & card services are provided by Webster Bank, N.A., member FDIC; savings account services are provided by American Deposit Management Co. & its partner banks. KPMG Private provides specialized advisory, audit, tax, & strategic consulting services tailored for emerging growth companies, startups, & private enterprises scaling up through various lifecycle stages. Whether you're launching a startup or accelerating your growth, the Emerging Growth team offers strategic insights & resources designed to support your business journey. #nyc #venturecapital #government
