events.name: AI, Energy, Fight for Democracy & A Healthy, Affordable Future
events.description: Tishman AuditoriumClimate Week 2026 Keynote Event at The New School   We are excited to share that this vital conversation convenes a powerhouse lineup of community leaders, mayors, scientists, researchers, & journalists. Across three dynamic panel conversations, we'll examine the collision of technology, energy, & democracy; the rapid expansion of AI data centers; the legacy of nuclear weapons; the toll of these developments on Indigenous communities, communities of color, & rural areas; & the affordability crisis & what it will take for everyday people to build power & shape real solutions.    Together, these conversations connect today's most pressing challenges to a larger question: How do communities organize & build power within democratic structures when government & industry leave them behind?   AI's Hidden Toll   LaTricea AdamsPresident & CEO, Young, Gifted & Green, Memphis   Manish BapnaPresident & CEO, Natural Resources Defense Council, Washington, DC   Mayor Kate GallegoCity of Phoenix   Adam Mahoney (Moderator)National Climate & Environment Reporter, Capital B News, New Orleans   Nuclear Legacy: Mapping Local Impacts   Lilly AdamsCo-Creator, US Nuclear Impacts Map, Brooklyn, New York   Moeka De OroCo-Executive Director, Micronesia Climate Change Alliance, Guam/Guhan   Leona Morgan (Din)Indigenous Community Organizer & Anti-Nuclear Activist, Din No Nukes, Albuquerque, New Mexico   Sharon Weinberger (Moderator)Editor-in-Chief, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Washington, DC   Power in Our Hands: Solutions for an Affordable, Just Future   Dr. Ana Isabel BaptistaAssociate Professor of Environmental & Climate Justice at the Parsons School of Design & Director, Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, New York   Dr. Gretchen GoldmanPresident & CEO, Union of Concerned Scientists, Washington, DC   Bill McKibbenAuthor, Educator, Activist, & Founder, Third Act & 350.org, Vermont   Mayor Michelle WuCity of Boston Garrison Hayes (Moderator)Correspondent,  Mother Jones, Nashville This event is presented by the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, in collaboration with Climate Desk Live partners Mother Jones, Capital B News, & the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists. This event is free & open to the public. events.name: Crux Alliance
events.description: Crux Alliance is spotlighting the leaders driving smart climate policy in the world's highest-emitting countries at Climate Week NYC. Across our events, we'll bring together researchers & advocates to explore sustainable cities & transport, energy security, & electrification, highlighting the policies & communication strategies that unlock affordable clean energy & improve quality of life for millions. We look forward to connecting with you there. All events will be hosted on the 2nd floor of Lulla at the Motto by Hilton Chelsea, 113 West 24th Street. Tues., Sept. 228:00 - 9:30 AMWin-Win Policies: Unlocking Investment for a Sustainable FutureIn this session, organizations from the transport, appliances, & building operations sectors will discuss policies that discourage undesirable outcomes while helping to fund sustainable solutions in countries around the world.  Experts from ITDP, ICCT, CLASP, & GBPN will explore how these policy mechanisms were designed, implementation challenges, lessons learned, & their potential to support long-term urban sustainability goals. Participants will gain insights into how strategic policy interventions can be designed to help governments achieve multiple objectives simultaneously: reducing emissions, improving quality of life, & unlocking investment in sustainable development. SpeakersJacob Mason, Senior Global Program Director, Institute for Transportation & Development Policy Ana Mara Carreo, Senior Director of Climate, CLASP Tim Dallmann, Director of Global Program, International Council on Clean Transportation RSVP    crux alliance logo10:30 - 12:00 PMSuper Pollutants to Super Solutions: Targeting Diesel Black Carbon for Climate & Health BenefitsSuper pollutants like black carbon are compounding the effects of climate change & harming human health. But they are often overlooked in CO2-based climate policies. This event will explore how transportation & climate policies at all levels of government can better account for & address super pollutants rather than treating them as an afterthought.Speakers:Brooke Helmick, Director of Policy, New Jersey Environmental Justice Alliance Sean Maguire, Executive Director, Strategic Partnerships, Clean Air Fund Ray Minjares, Program Director, Heavy-Duty Vehicles, International Council on Clean Transportation Moderator: Claire Henley, Executive Director, Super Pollutant Action Alliance  RSVP  1:00 - 2:00 PMFrom Evidence to Impact: Communicating the Case for Smart PolicyRobust research on vehicle technology & transportation policy can't translate itself into policy-or into public understanding. This session brings together communications leaders to explore how to turn technical research into powerful messaging, tools, & products that policymakers, media, & the public can actually use. The conversation will discuss what makes evidence usable for regulators, how to package complex findings-like the economic, health, & environmental gains of stronger vehicle standards-into compelling, accessible formats, & how communications teams can bridge the gap between researchers & the decision-makers who shape transportation policy. SpeakersMichael Doerrer, Senior Director of Communications & Development, International Council on Clean Transportation Leah Qusba, CEO, GoodPower Elan Strait, Executive Director, Potential Energy Moderator: Sarah Spengeman, Communications Director, Crux Alliance RSVP  3:00 - 4:30 PMResisting the Easy Fix: The Limits of Coal as a National Response to Geopolitical ShiftsAs global fuel market disruptions & geopolitical tensions revive interest in domestic energy resources, this side event examines whether coal can realistically serve as a pillar of energy security & economic resilience. Drawing on experiences from major coal regions-Poland, Trkiye, China, the United States, & South Africa-experts will discuss how recent energy crises have reshaped national coal debates, the true costs of continued reliance, & the benefits of clean alternatives, supporting evidence-based dialogue ahead of COP31. SpeakersJoanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii, Poland Rabia Ferroukhi, Director, INETTT Secretariat Alkm Ba Gll, Director, SHURA Energy Transition Center, Trkiye Kevin Tu, Chief Advisor China, Agora Energiewende Tracy Ledger, Just Transition Programme Lead, Public Affairs Research Institute, South Africa Mary Anne Hitt, Managing Director of U.S. Initiatives, Climate Imperative Moderator: Steve Capanna, Director of Policy, Crux Alliance RSVP   4:30 - 6:30 PMMeet the "Wonks" Behind the Wins: A Networking Happy HourJoin Crux Alliance, ReNew2030, Global Grids Catalyst, & Growald Climate Fund for a Climate Week NYC happy hour celebrating the policy experts advancing climate policy where it has the greatest impact. The afternoon will include a short program spotlighting the work of these philanthropic initiatives & their partners, with plenty of time for building new connections. Come meet the wonks behind the wins: the people translating climate goals into policy that bends the curve, delivering cleaner air, lower costs, & better lives for millions. Brief remarks shared by:Rebecca Collyer, Executive Director, ReNew2030 Kartikeya Singh, Director, Collective Impact, Growald Climate Fund Joanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii RSVP    Wed., Sept. 238:00 - 9:30 AMFrom Gridlock to Grid-Ready: A Coordinated Path to 35-by-35The COP31 35-by-35 electrification pledge is an urgent call for governments to embrace an ambitious electrification plan. But that ambition will stall without fixing outdated grid planning & aging, insufficient grid infrastructure across major economies. Solutions exist-but building a clean, modern grid ready for all-electric buildings, industry, & transport requires coordination across sectors & stakeholders: developers, planners, & policymakers. This panel will discuss why we must tackle the grid challenge holistically & share how a coordinated approach is unlocking smarter policy, planning, operations, & deployment-and the affordability, reliability, & security benefits that follow. Panelists will share complementary approaches taking shape in the geographies that will make or break the electrification transition.

Drawing on experiences from major coal regions-Poland, Trkiye, China, the United States, & South Africa-experts will discuss how recent energy crises have reshaped national coal debates, the true costs of continued reliance, & the benefits of clean alternatives, supporting evidence-based dialogue ahead of COP31. SpeakersJoanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii, Poland Rabia Ferroukhi, Director, INETTT Secretariat Alkm Ba Gll, Director, SHURA Energy Transition Center, Trkiye Kevin Tu, Chief Advisor China, Agora Energiewende Tracy Ledger, Just Transition Programme Lead, Public Affairs Research Institute, South Africa Mary Anne Hitt, Managing Director of U.S. Initiatives, Climate Imperative Moderator: Steve Capanna, Director of Policy, Crux Alliance RSVP   4:30 - 6:30 PMMeet the "Wonks" Behind the Wins: A Networking Happy HourJoin Crux Alliance, ReNew2030, Global Grids Catalyst, & Growald Climate Fund for a Climate Week NYC happy hour celebrating the policy experts advancing climate policy where it has the greatest impact. The afternoon will include a short program spotlighting the work of these philanthropic initiatives & their partners, with plenty of time for building new connections. Come meet the wonks behind the wins: the people translating climate goals into policy that bends the curve, delivering cleaner air, lower costs, & better lives for millions. Brief remarks shared by:Rebecca Collyer, Executive Director, ReNew2030 Kartikeya Singh, Director, Collective Impact, Growald Climate Fund Joanna Makowiak Pandera, President, Forum Energii RSVP    Wed., Sept. 238:00 - 9:30 AMFrom Gridlock to Grid-Ready: A Coordinated Path to 35-by-35The COP31 35-by-35 electrification pledge is an urgent call for governments to embrace an ambitious electrification plan. But that ambition will stall without fixing outdated grid planning & aging, insufficient grid infrastructure across major economies. Solutions exist-but building a clean, modern grid ready for all-electric buildings, industry, & transport requires coordination across sectors & stakeholders: developers, planners, & policymakers. This panel will discuss why we must tackle the grid challenge holistically & share how a coordinated approach is unlocking smarter policy, planning, operations, & deployment-and the affordability, reliability, & security benefits that follow. Panelists will share complementary approaches taking shape in the geographies that will make or break the electrification transition.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Trading For Food Security In Changing Climate
events.description: The Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) at MIT would like to invite you to a panel discussion titled Trading for Food Security in a Changing Climate". International food trade has become essential for global food security, but the same interconnected networks that move food also transmit shocks-climatic, economic, & geopolitical. A panel of relevant industry experts will examine the linkages between food trade & food security through the lens of healthy diets & introduce the Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, developed by MIT J-WAFS. The Index maps food-trade vulnerability across more than 180 countries. Join us for a moderated discussion on three questions: how to assess food security versus an inability to import; what balance of home-grown & imported food best serves healthy nutrition as diets shift; & where investment in productivity, infrastructure, & research are most needed as the climate changes. ModeratorGreg Sixt, Director, Food & Climate Systems Transformation (FACT) Alliance & Research Director for Food & Climate Systems, Abdul Latif Jameel Water & Food Systems Lab (J-WAFS) Opening presentation: Introduction to the Jameel Index & J-WAFS work on food security, global change, & tradeKenneth Strzepek, Technical Lead, Jameel Index for Food Trade & Vulnerability, MIT J-WAFS PanelistsProf. Sheryl Hendriks, Extraordinary Professor, University of Pretoria Mark Rosegrant, Research Fellow Emeritus, International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), Former Director of IFPRI's Environment & Production Technology Division Paola de Almeida, CEO, Natural Systems Capital & Jameel Index Advisory Committee Member

events.name: Swiss Climatetech Showcase
events.description: Meet the next generation of Swiss climatetech founders as the Climate Collider 2026 cohort comes to Climate Week NYC. Eight Swiss startups - spanning carbon removal, geothermal drilling, sustainable agriculture, clean hydrogen, industrial efficiency, circular construction materials, advanced membranes, biomaterials, & textile recycling - will pitch their solutions to investors, researchers, & industry leaders shaping the future of climate innovation. Climate Collider is a startup camp powered by Innosuisse & managed by Swissnex, designed to strengthen transatlantic collaboration & connect Swiss startups with Boston & New York, two of the world's leading climatetech hubs. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: How Data Center Fights Renewing Local Power Across US
events.description: This is an in-person event happening as part of NYC Climate Week. To hear many in the tech industry tell it, data centers will bring wealth & prosperity not only to those who build them, but to the communities that ultimately live with & around them. However, drawing a longer historical arc is essential: AI is proposed as a new industrial moonshot in communities that have already seen the rise & fall of steel factories, coal plants, fracking infrastructure, & more. Today's companies are trying to sell communities on yet another industrial vision. On Sept. 22 at 5:30 p.m., join us in Midtown East, Manhattan, for a panel discussion featuring journalists, nonprofits, & community organizers who are uncovering the impact of data centers across the country & sharing that information with the public. Our panel discussion will feature Maia Woluchem, program director of Data & Society's Trustworthy Infrastructures program; Alejandra Martinez, The Texas Tribune environmental reporter & Pulitzer Center grantee; Brian Crawford, Texas resident with the nonprofit Protect the Paluxy Valley; & Ginny Marcille-Kerslake, Pennsylvania resident & Senior Organizer at Food & Water Watch. Kit R. Roane, award-winning senior producer at Retro Report, will be the moderator. This event is anchored by the launch of Data & Society's forthcoming report, The AI Factory: Data Centers, Power & Resistance in Late Industrial Pennsylvania, a landmark study emerging out of eighteen months of field research in the Keystone State, as well as Pulitzer Center-supported reporting on data center development by The Texas Tribune. Light refreshments will be served. Seating is limited, & R.S.V.P. is required. This panel discussion is co-organized by Data & Society, Retro Report, & The Pulitzer Center.

events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. events.name: Buildings & Grid - Clipping The Falcon Wing
events.description: Can buildings play a significant role in solving the crisis brewing in our power grids? Join Building Energy Exchange & the US Green Building Council (USGBC) for a moderated discussion with regulatory & industry experts exploring how building decarbonization can help address, rather than exacerbate, the current & future challenges facing our grid.   Our power grids face an array of converging & mounting challenges. After more than two decades of relatively flat consumption, the electrical grid is experiencing significant increases in demand driven by building & vehicle electrification, extreme weather events, & the rapid growth of data centers. At the same time, the transition to clean, renewable energy is creating new challenges in balancing supply & demand.   The costs to provide enough power for these increases are astronomical, & the lead-time to bring new generation online is a significant challenge. However, buildings can play a critical role in reducing the loads. By reducing overall energy use & managing peak demand, buildings can become active partners in supporting a more reliable, resilient, & decarbonized grid.  This session will explore the emerging grid issues & the various strategies-such as load shifting, peak load reduction, improved building envelopes, & geothermal-that buildings can deploy to reduce grid demand. Coffee & pastries will be served!   Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC  PresentationsZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  PanelistsRyan Dougherty, Executive Director, Geothermal Exchange OrganizationLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC - ModeratorJohn Rhodes, Chief Program Officer, NYS Department of Public ServiceZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

events.description: From Possibility to Practice: Advancing Climate Solutions in a Changing WorldFeaturing Eliza Barclay, The New York Times, & Joel Makower, TrellisThursday, September 24, 2026Climate Week NYC As part of Climate Week NYC, UC Berkeley's Master of Climate Solutions will convene a curated group of climate practitioners, alumni, & members of the broader Berkeley community for an invitation-only roundtable lunch. The gathering will open with remarks from Joel Makower of Trellis, a UC Berkeley alumnus & member of the Master of Climate Solutions Advisory Board. events.name: Food Solns Summit - Stories From Frontlines Of Climate & Farming
events.description: Climate Week NYC 2026's premier funder & field convening on food & agriculture. Please join us for a Climate Week NYC 2026 funder & field convening on food & agriculture as one of the most underleveraged pathways for climate, health, biodiversity, & community resilience. Too often, food & agriculture are treated as niche issues - separate from climate, public health, biodiversity, economic transition, rural resilience & democracy. events.name: Built Different - The Cities We Need
events.description: Climate change is already impacting our cities - decarbonization & climate resilience are now imperatives, not options. Technical innovation offers real tools to meet these challenges: buildings that are more efficient in their energy consumption & embodied carbon, & new ways of modeling & optimizing urban systems at scale. Whether through retrofitting what's already built or rethinking new construction, solutions are more available than ever. But availability is not the same as results. Getting these solutions integrated into the established, highly regulated planning processes requires political will, agility, & collaboration across disciplines. Swissnex & the ETH Alumni Association present a conversation across disciplinary silos on urban climate adaptation during Climate Week NYC, Showcasing cutting-edge technology developed by ETH spin-offs & discussing what it takes to apply the knowledge & tools available at scale. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Hidden Patterns - Visual Journey Of Networks
events.description: In this talk, Albert-Lszl Barabsi will chart the 25-year odyssey of BarabsiLab in crafting the visual lexicon of networks. The essence of complexity lies in connectivity. Whether we examine the vast expanse of the World Wide Web, the intricacies of a cell, or the marvel of the human brain, their complexity invariably stems from intricate interconnected networks. Connectivity is foundational to our biological makeup, our social fabric, & our communicative prowess. In this talk, Albert-Lszl Barabsi will chart the 25-year odyssey of BarabsiLab in crafting the visual lexicon of networks & connectivity, focusing on their recent monumental project for the 2024 Venice Architecture Biennale, which charts 50 years of architectural history. Dr. Barabsi is the Robert Gray Professor of Network Science at Northeastern University. He has exhibited at galleries all over the U.S & Europe & recently co-designed the opening experience for the Biennale Architettura di Venezia.

events.name: Are AI Datacenters A Threat To Our Clean Energy Future
events.description: NOTE: Registration is REQUIRED. Join Pratt Institute's Sustainable Environmental Systems program for our third annual just energy transition event during NYC Climate Week. Global & local experts will join in conversation across just energy challenges, solutions, & perspectives with a particular focus on the rapid expansion of energy-hungry datacenters powering artificial intelligence (AI).  Experts working on local & global energy issues will come together to discuss new policy dynamics, systemic & historic barriers in realizing a true Just Transition, & how these new datacenters could get us off track. This timely discussion will happen during the UN General Assembly & NYC Climate Week 2026, where key climate & energy transition issues will be at the center of next steps for the sustainable development goals & the broader theme of this year's Climate Week. Key themes of the conversation will include: decarbonization, climate finance, climate diplomacy, infrastructure, the path to net zero, water, tech & AI, incentives for transition, green economy, & the SDGs.   The panel will be feature local & global perspectives in a conversation moderated by a recent Pratt SES alumna, Jen Hung: Panelists:  Martha Molfetas | Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute; Senior Policy Consultant & Writer: Martha Molfetas is a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Environmental Economics. Martha is a senior climate & energy policy consultant, writer, & strategist with over 17-years of experience helping NGOs, think tanks, & businesses unpack climate, environmental justice, resource conflict, sustainable development, & global policy issues with organizations ranging from Dalberg Research to Transparency International, NRGI & Oil Change International to name a few. She was formerly a Senior Fellow working on just energy transition at New America. Her work has been published in: Current Affairs, The World Politics Review, The Global Policy Journal, Policy Mic, Common Dreams, & others. Summer Sandoval | Academic Coordinator, Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute & Community Investment & Implementation Director, USDN: Summer Sandoval is the Community Investment & Implementation Director at Urban Sustainability Directors Network (USDN), where she supports local governments & communities in navigating funding opportunities & realizing their projects to advance equitable climate action. Summer is also the Academic Coordinator & a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Urban Energy Management. Summer has worked at the intersection of climate, environmental, & energy justice in community-based organizations & city government.   Rami Dinnawi | Program Director, North Star Fund: Rami Dinnawi is a Lebanese/Palestinian grassroots activist based in New York City. Informed by generational knowledge of people's struggle for self-determination, Rami strives to ground his work within these historical legacies. He is currently serving as the NYC Program Director at North Star Fund. Prior to joining North Star Fund, Rami worked extensively in the New York environmental justice movement space, as the environmental justice campaign & policy manager at El Puente. Rami is currently serving on the Advisory Committee of the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School. With over a decade of organizing experience, Rami's commitment extends beyond borders, as he actively engages with activism & movements on a global scale. Pierre Canet | Global Head of Public Affairs & Policy, Client Earth: Pierre leads ClientEarth's Global Public Affairs & Policy team, overseeing the organisation's influence on decision-makers to achieve the systems change pursued in its strategy across the world. Before joining ClientEarth, Pierre was the Executive Director of Advocacy at WWF in France where he worked for a decade leading campaigns & programs on a diversity of environmental issues, from climate & energy to nature & plastics, collaborating at multiple levels throughout the WWF's global network. Prior to this, Pierre worked with the United Nations in New York on the preparation of the Rio+20 Summit & corporate climate engagement. He engaged significantly with activities around the Climate COP21 to influence the establishment of the Paris Agreement, & has substantial experience in building & developing high-impact activities from newly-established teams.

events.name: Net Zero Value Chains - Advancing Credible Scope 3 Decarbonization
events.description: The corporate climate landscape is moving toward greater rigor, with growing expectations for companies to substantiate climate action through credible data, accounting, & reporting. The GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard (LSRS) introduces a more robust framework for accounting & reporting land-based emissions & CO removals. However, implementation remains challenging, with companies navigating supplier data gaps, limited traceability, allocation challenges, & evolving assurance expectations. At the same time, organizations are exploring how market-based approaches can help accelerate credible Scope 3 action beyond their direct operations. Join corporate sustainability leaders, standard setters, climate experts, & solution providers to explore two key developments shaping the future of value chain decarbonization: Panel 1: Implementing the GHG Protocol Land Sector & Removals Standard Hear from experts & early adopters on the practical challenges of implementing the LSRS, including data quality, traceability, allocation, reporting, & assurance. Learn what organizations are doing today-and what may be needed to support scalable implementation in the years ahead. Speakers:Matt Ramlow, Senior Research Associate, GHG P Martha Stevenson, Senior Director, Strategy & Research, Forests, WWF Noora Singh, Senior Director, Global Sustainability, PepsiCoChristina O'Keefe, Head of Sustainability, North America, Kerry Panel 2: The emerging role of Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) Explore how carbon credits, environmental certificates, & other market-based approaches could support Scope 3 decarbonization. Hear the latest perspectives on developments across the GHG Protocol, AMI Standard, & SBTi's Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2, alongside practical insights from companies already piloting these approaches. Speakers:Alex Kazaglis, Chief Strategy Officer, SBTiDavid Spitzley, Director, Climate & Nature | Global Sustainability, StarbucksJacob Isaacson, Associate Director of Climate Strategy, 3DegreesCynthia Cummis, Senior Vice President Value Chain Strategies, ClimeCo The event will conclude with networking drinks, providing an opportunity to continue the conversation & connect with peers from across the corporate climate ecosystem. Who should attend? Corporate sustainability & climate leaders Scope 3 & procurement professionals Standards & accounting experts NGOs & policy stakeholders Sustainability consultants & solution providers Register now to secure your place.

events.name: From Risk To Oppty - How Capital Can Enable Climate Resilience
events.description: Climate & nature-related risk is accelerating faster than markets can price it, & insurers are often the first to feel it. The same dynamic appears elsewhere: investors hesitate to finance conservation & adaptation projects, while financial inclusion in emerging economies stalls. These share the same underlying reason, that the risk has outpaced the tools we have to price & fund it. Swissnex, in collaboration with the Consulate General of Switzerland in New York, Swiss Business Hub USA, Greater Zurich Area, & Global Infrastructure Basel, convenes senior professionals from banking, insurance, asset management, development finance, policy, research, & community organizations for a single morning that follows this market failure end to end. Together we will explore where it originates, to how capital rebuilds what has been lost, what actually gets built afterward, & what else still stands in the way. Switzerland is well positioned to convene this conversation. It sits at the center of global re/insurance, while its banks & insurers are increasingly operating within a regulatory framework that integrates climate & nature-related risk governance, alongside a democratically mandated net-zero target for 2050. This puts Switzerland in a position where voluntary commitments are increasingly being tested against financial & regulatory realities. Bringing together representatives from government, finance, insurance, & development institutions, this program explores how climate & nature-related risks can be better measured, priced, & financed. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Future Of The Grid - From Utility Infra To End Users
events.description: As electricity demand accelerates-driven by AI, electrification, & aging infrastructure-the future of the grid will be shaped by innovations at every level of the built environment. From utility-scale transmission & grid resilience to city permitting & home energy intelligence, the next generation of climate technology is transforming how we build, maintain, & power our communities. Join HearstLab for a morning exploring "The Future of the Grid" through a range of perspectives: Utility Scale: Strengthening critical grid infrastructure through AI-powered monitoring & predictive maintenance. City & Community: Modernizing permitting, planning, & local government to accelerate resilient development. Home & Building: Empowering property owners with intelligent tools to improve energy performance & navigate the transition to electrification. The program will feature live demos from HearstLab portfolio companies Bandora, Buzz Solutions, Symbium, Scope Zero, & VestedImpact & include discussions with leaders from government, utilities, & technology on the partnerships, policies, & innovations needed to build a more resilient, efficient, & intelligent energy future.

events.name: AI Needs More Power - Who Builds It, What Gets Built & Who Gets Paid
events.description: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. On-site resources are becoming critical & can potentially offer flexibility while reducing ratepayer impact. Moderated by Lisa Martine Jenkins of Latitude Media, energy leaders & investors from Aston Power, Commonwealth Station A, & Redwood Materials will debate where capital is moving, what actually needs to get built, & whether the AI boom will fundamentally reshape how, & from whom, large energy users get their power Moderator: Lisa Martine Jenkins | Editor | Latitude Media Panelists: Doug Chambers | Chief Development Officer | Aston Travis Metcalfe | Energy Strategist | Commonwealth Asset Management Group Kevin Berekemeyer | Co-Founder & CEO | Station A Claire McConnell | Vice President of Business Development | Redwood Materials Antenna Group is the public relations & strategic marketing agency of choice for climate, energy, mobility, real estate, & infrastructure leaders. events.name: Make It In Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest
events.description: Join us during NYC Climate Week for the Make It in Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest, where five early-stage climate technology startups will compete for up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support. Founders will be evaluated on innovation, feasibility, market potential, & potential impact. The winning startup will receive up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support to help accelerate its path to market. The prize includes: $5,000 in unrestricted prize funding from Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Up to an additional $5,000 in milestone-based commercialization support through National Grid's Clean Tech Incubation Program. Eligible expenses include prototype development & testing, patent & legal filing costs, market research, commercialization activities, & pilot implementation support. The Climate Tech Pitch Contest brings together founders, investors, industry leaders, & members of the innovation ecosystem to spotlight technologies addressing some of today's most pressing climate challenges. Finalists: PollenPal is using AI-powered sensors & computer vision to help beekeepers monitor hive health in real time, improve colony management, & address the growing challenge of honeybee colony loss. HiFIT is advancing offshore wind through innovative weld treatment technology that strengthens turbine structures, enabling longer service life, reduced steel consumption & maintenance costs, & lower embodied carbon. Novara Tech is developing mobile recycling technology that transforms hard-to-recycle composite waste from industries like wind energy & construction into reusable materials for urban infrastructure, reducing landfill waste & transportation costs. Kyber Energy is developing AI-powered energy management software that helps commercial & industrial businesses optimize electricity use, shift demand away from peak periods, & reduce both energy costs & grid emissions. AtmosOne AI is helping address growing demand on the electric grid by intelligently shifting flexible AI computing to off-peak periods, reducing grid strain & enabling more efficient use of existing energy infrastructure. Judges will be announced soon. This event is in partnership with the Malin & National Grid. The Malin is a beautifully designed workspace for ambitious founders, creatives, & industry leaders who value genuine community over transactional co-working, & they're across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration The discussion will focus on moving beyond the exchange of ideas toward concrete projects, financing mechanisms, & long-term collaboration. Discussion themes include: Connecting cities across Asia, North America, & other regions Mobilizing finance for circular & resilient urban projects Building pipelines of investable city projects Connecting cities with businesses, investors, & international institutions Scaling successful solutions across different markets Turning international dialogue into practical collaboration Continuing collaboration through international forums & Yokohama's initiatives in 2027 Speakers: Sandra Goldmark, Associate Dean for Engagement & Impact & Professor of Professional Practice, Columbia Climate School Local 2030 Coalition (Speaker TBA) Berat Senyerli, CEO of Bankable Zero Vijay Jagannathan, Senior Fellow at World Resources Institute (Moderator) 3:50-4:00 Closing RemarksWho Should AttendThe Forum is designed for: City & regional government representatives International organizations Corporations & business leaders Investors & financial institutions Startups & entrepreneurs Climate technology & circular economy experts Urban development & resilience professionals Innovation ecosystem leaders

events.name: Mind The Gap - Aligning Insurance, Policy & Nature For Climate Resilience
events.description: Climate change & nature loss are reshaping insurance markets & widening the protection gap. More frequent & severe floods, storms, wildfires, & droughts are driving losses higher, while degraded ecosystems are reducing the natural protections communities rely on, from flood absorption to heat mitigation. Together, these trends are pushing climate-related insured losses up by an unsustainable 5% to 7% annually in real terms. This session will focus on practical solutions to close the growing insurance gap by aligning policy, regulation, finance, insurance practice, & investment in nature.

events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.name: PMAI Fight Right - Co-Founders Guide To Disagreement
events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. events.name: Beyond Mineral Supply Security - Partnerships & Community Rights
events.description: Critical minerals: who captures the value, who bears the risk? A panel on financing a just transition for producer nations. There is no climate transition without transition minerals & how they are governed will decide whether decarbonisation delivers development & prosperity for producer countries, or simply repeats extractive patterns under a green label. This panel co- convened with Oxfam examines the gap between the G7's Critical Minerals Action Plan, which frames minerals mainly as a supply security issue for consumer economies, & South Africa's 2025 G20 Critical Minerals Framework, which centres value retention, local industrialisation & community rights. With the UK holding the G20 presidency in 2027 & the G7 presidency in 2028, there is a genuine window to shift finance toward producer-country processing, regional value chains, & enforceable safeguards including Free, Prior & Informed Consent as a right, not a formality. Join us to explore what truly financed partnership with mineral-rich Global South nations could look like in practice.

events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. events.name: Implementing Circularity In Interior Design
events.description: Connecting the Dots Our interior spaces remains trapped in a persistent & costly system of frequent renovation, demolition, & disposal, resulting in an unsustainable churn of materials. While circular design offers a path forward, the challenge isn't just designing for circularity; it's creating the network of relationships needed to make it work, connecting the many stakeholders responsible for shaping, operating, & renewing interior spaces. Our panel of stakeholders across the value chain will examine what is needed to really implement the circularity loop - to keep materials in circulation, reduce waste, lower costs, create jobs, & transform the interiors industry from a linear model of consumption to a truly circular one. Join us for a lively & provocative discussion. Moderators: David Bergman, Architect, Educator, Founder / Director, CCID  Speakers: Yarden Harari, Associate Principal, ArcadisRobin Reigi, Owner, Robin ReigiDoug Pilgrim, Business Development / Sustainability Manager, Davies OfficeMichael Orbank, Sustainability Manager, STO

events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. events.name: Powering The AI Build-Out - India's Data Center Energy Demand Surge
events.description: CleanMax invites you to a moderated panel bringing together hyperscalers, independent power producers & other market participants to examine how India's rapidly scaling data-centre sector will meet its power demand-and what role renewable energy, storage & firm-power structures need to play in getting there. What the panel will explore  The scale & geography of India's data-centre power demand-and what a realistic, bankable renewable-energy pipeline could look like through 2030.  Whether renewables & storage can deliver 24/7, high-reliability power at a viable cost, & where grid, transmission, land & infrastructure constraints could limit new capacity.  How hyperscalers & power producers are structuring supply-from physical & group-captive arrangements to VPPAs & CFDs-and which models are becoming genuinely bankable.  The broader policy & regulatory clarity needed to accelerate investment & give developers, buyers & financiers confidence in long-term delivery.  How data-centre growth can earn community acceptance & support sustainable development through transparent engagement & meaningful local benefits around land, water, infrastructure & livelihoods. Warm regards, CleanMax Team

events.name: Invisible Crisis - Innovating For Age Of Extreme Heat
events.description: Campus Deep Tech, Anywhere Ventures, The Hazelwood Network, & Tailwind Futures are bringing together a curated group of startups, investors, industry leaders, & academics during Climate Week NYC to explore the mounting challenges posed by extreme heat globally & novel technologies being developed to help people & industries adapt. Industry leaders & investors will present 'reverse pitches' where they will identify specific challenges & opportunity areas where they would like to see innovators focus next. Startups & leading academics will share the cutting-edge technologies they are developing & their commercial potential. Why Attend: Discover breakthrough technologies Engage directly with scientists working at the frontier of extreme heat resilience & cooling technologies Identify investment & partnership opportunities Become part of the region's growing deep tech ecosystem Run of Show: Reverse pitch presentations from industry leaders & investors Startup & researcher presentations from across Columbia, Princeton, Yale, & other leading universities Networking reception (drinks & light bites included) Extreme Heat X Technology Challenges: People & communities: Heat stress & disease, productivity, access to AC, essential services, wildfires Agriculture: Disrupted photosynthesis & pollination slashing crop yields Energy systems: Power-plant cooling constraints, declining solar output, transmission derating, transformer failures, & peak-demand blackouts Cooling & electronics: Overloaded / overheated HVAC, data-center cooling systems, telecom, electronics Transportation & supply chains: Buckling roads & rails, stressed bridges, aviation disruptions, vehicle breakdowns, cold-chain failures Water & wastewater: Pipe leakage, water-supply interruptions, failures of pumps & treatment systems Industrial operations: Machinery overheating, shortened equipment life, material expansion, product defects Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV!

events.name: From Framework To Front Line - Advancing Housing Resilience & Affordability
events.description: RPA & Enterprise explore using policy & partnerships to protect affordable homes, accelerate recovery & strengthen communities. Climate-driven disasters are placing growing pressure on an already constrained housing supply, threatening existing homes, increasing costs for residents & housing providers, & making it more difficult for communities to meet urgent affordability needs. As municipalities grapple with the need to build more resilient communities able to withstand extreme weather events, the critical question is how policymakers, planners, & housing experts can translate ambitious blueprints into effective, local action. This panel will bring together Regional Plan Association (RPA) & Enterprise Community Partners to examine the policies, planning decisions, & implementation strategies needed to protect existing housing & accelerate recovery. Drawing from national standards & regional planning frameworks, panelists will examine the challenges communities & housing providers face, & highlight the resources & partnerships needed to address the intersecting climate & housing crisis. Enterprise Community Partners will draw on insights from its Climate Resilience Academies to highlight the challenges affordable housing owners, operators, & developers face in preparing their portfolios for climate risks while safeguarding residents. Through its work with more than 150 participants across U.S. regions, Enterprise has seen that housing providers increasingly understand the urgency of resilience but often lack the staff capacity, funding, technical expertise, & region-specific guidance needed to act. Enterprise will discuss opportunities to close these gaps to further help housing providers move from awareness to implementation.Regional Plan Association will draw from its Averting Crisis report & subsequent work with communities in the New York metropolitan region to examine how housing growth & climate resilience can be advanced together. RPA will share real-time lessons being learned about effective ways to move from high-altitude planning to on-the-ground implementation, highlighting its work with local governments, community organizations, & neighborhood stakeholders in seven communities across Queens, Westchester, & Long Island. The work will result in local actions that affect zoning changes, land-use reform, investments & complementary policies to align housing growth with climate risk & capacity. These organizations will offer expertise on climate readiness & disaster response, connecting federal & local policy to on-the-ground implementation to make communities more resilient amid the growing housing affordability crisis.

events.name: The New Sustainability
events.description: Are you looking for an inspirational way to launch your 2026 UNGA & New York Climate Week? Join us on Sunday evening for our annual reception & be a part of the conversation.   This reception brings together Nordic & North American changemakers, global sustainability leaders for an evening of ideas, inspiration, & informal exchange. The event is hosted by UN Global Compact Finland & Miltton, one of the Nordics top consultancies.  It is also supported by the UN Global Compact Country Networks of Sweden, Denmark, Iceland, & Canada. Expect: Short, sharp perspectives from leaders shaping the new sustainability-and navigating what it means for business, impact, & global competitiveness. Think bold ideas, fresh perspectives, meaningful matchmaking, & conversations that challenge the status quo. Whether you're driving change, exploring new partnerships, or simply curious about where sustainability is heading next, this is your room-and a great way to kick off the UN General Assembly & New York Climate Week.  Our speakers:   Georg Kell - Georg Kell is a globally respected thought leader in sustainability & responsible business, best known as the founding Executive Director of the UN Global Compact. A pioneer in putting sustainability at the heart of corporate strategy, he has spent decades connecting business, government, & society to drive positive global change. Today, he continues to shape conversations around responsible leadership, sustainable investing, & the future of business. Eeva Taimisto, Miltton - Eeva will be premiering the results from: The Evolving Language of Sustainability & Climate: How Chief Sustainability Officer's narratives are shifting. A study on how sustainability language & narratives are evolving among the world's largest companies, analysing communications from the Forbes Global 2000. The findings reveal some fascinating shifts in priorities, vocabulary, & strategic framing. Comments & discussions on the perspectives behind the results. Speakers TBC. And maybe even more to come...  Hope to see you there!

events.name: Decarbonizing Everyday Life
events.description: Fossil fuels are all around us, & not just when it comes to transport & electricity. In your closet, your kitchen, your medicine cabinet, even your walls, petroleum products are hiding in plain sight. Our daily lives are built on embodied carbon in the most literal sense. And unlike metal, glass, or plant-based materials, they return cleanly to neither industry nor the earth. They degrade, but never disappear. Decarbonization is about more than renewable energy. It means remaking the stuff of our everyday lives, & with it the supply chains, design decisions, & consumer habits that put that stuff in our hands. This conversation brings together materials innovators, designers, & industry experts working on sustainable alternatives, from new recycling technologies to bio-based alternatives for petroleum-derived textiles, packing materials, & cosmetics. Together they will explore the innovations that could help us move past plastic, & how we can get those sustainable materials out of the lab & into our homes. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Economics Of AI - Is SaaS Pricing Model Dead?
events.description: Is the SaaS Pricing Model Dead?For twenty years, SaaS companies built their businesses around recurring subscriptions. AI is breaking that model. Seat licenses are turning into token pricing. Some customers want to pay for outcomes, not users. And inference costs are quietly becoming one of the biggest line items on the P&L. If you run a dev shop building AI products, or you're a funded founder trying to scale one, you're probably already feeling this. Even if you haven't figured out what to do about it yet. Join York Effect for a live panel with a Head of Product & a CFO, digging into pricing, unit economics, & what happens when the cost of delivering software starts moving faster than your pricing model can keep up. Who should attend: Software development firms & AI product builders. Series A+ founders scaling SaaS. Also relevant for product leaders, CFOs, finance execs, & investors watching this space. Who's behind this: Tova Feldheim & Caroline Jerome are co-founders of York Effect. York Effect Sprints are decision-making frameworks built to reveal what will actually scale in a Series A+ business... & what won't. Their KPI Reality Check, a complimentary 30-minute assessment, gives founders clarity on where they truly stand. events.name: Nordic Investor Night - LP Reception
events.description: We're back for round two! Last year during New York Climate Week, we gathered a roomful of international investors & Nordic LPs & GPs for the first time to talk about the opportunities up north & added a little flavour to the evening by bringing in delicacies from the Nordics. This year we're doing it again! And here's the pitch: the Nordics have become a hotbed for the climate economy. events.name: Demo Day
events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC!Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC.Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance. Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people.RSVP here: https://nyc.aitinkerers.org/p/september-demo-day-ft-posthog-verWhat is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If youre deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community.Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions. Read more in the FAQSome slots still available, submit your demo!  Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? This is your moment to share with like-minded AI tinkerers!A demo is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!) FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy!Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI TinkerersPlease note that capacity is limited, so well prioritize those who are able to present a demo.Demo vibes Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:00 Networking & pizzas9:00 Doors CloseMore informationIf you are new to AI Tinkerers, please read the AI Tinkerers FAQ & join our Discord channel: https://discord.gg/8WsqnC6Hk3SponsorsPostHogPostHog is an all-in-one product OS designed for engineers, offering product analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, & surveys in a single platform. It enables teams to understand user behavior, deploy features, & analyze data without patching together multiple tools. Founded in Y Combinator (W20), it supports both cloud-hosted & open-source self-hosting.Veris AI (Venue Host)Veris AI accelerates agent development & deployment with a simulation sandbox platform that delivers robust, compliant AI systems at speed. Veris sandbox is pre-loaded with test scenarios, simulated tools, & personas. Using the sandbox, you can run thousands of simulated interactions across routine workflows, challenging edge cases, & adversarial scenarios. Veris AI creates root-cause analysis reports, regression testing gates, & prompt or RL optimization loops to improve the agent using these interactions before the agent touches the first real system or customer.CopilotKitCopilotKit is an open-source framework for building AI copilots & agent-native experiences directly into your app. It gives you React components & hooks for in-app chat, generative UI, & shared state between your frontend & agents, & it works with agent frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, & Mastra through the AG-UI protocol. Ship agents that live inside the product instead of beside it.TavilyTavily is a search engine built for AI agents. Its API returns real-time, source-cited web results & page extracts optimized for LLM context, so agents & RAG pipelines can ground answers in current information with a single call. Tavily powers research agents, assistants, & data pipelines for teams that need reliable web access without scraping infrastructure.Start building now!Were bringing a builder-first lineup of demos & giving the community a space to share work in progress, trade notes, & meet other serious practitioners.

events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.
