From investment & catalog value to technology, new revenue opportunities & an increasingly complex global rights marketplace, the discussion will explore how a leading music publisher deploys resources, drives growth, & maximizes the long-term value of songs. events.name: AI Adoption Open Mic & Happy Hour - Volume 3
events.description: New York still doesn't need another boring AI panel. So, we're bringing back the AI Adoption Open Mic & Happy Hour for round three. After two packed nights bringing New York's AI community together, PAIR's Open Mic returns for another evening of drinks, new connections & refreshingly honest conversations about how AI is actually being used at work. The format is simple: anyone can take the mic & has 100 seconds to share something they've built, tested or learned with AI, & the difference it made. Previous speakers have included people from Google, Adobe & some of New York's most ambitious companies, with pitches covering new agents, practical workflows, unexpected experiments & lessons learned the hard way. The strongest pitch of the night will win a $500 cash prize & a three-year PAIR licence worth more than $800. P.S. events.name: Up/Link - SpaceTech Business Summit
events.description: If you fund space companies, build them, or buy from them - this is your room. Join 200 qualified leaders for two days of business-focused programming & at least four curated 1:1 meetings, matched to your priorities & booked before you arrive. Two days where the space economy does business.The space economy is moving from breakthrough technologies & individual missions toward durable commercial markets. But those markets don't emerge on their own. They require capital to finance them, capabilities to build them, & customers ready to buy. Up/Link brings those pieces together in New York - the founders building commercial space companies, the investors funding them, & the enterprise & government buyers writing the contracts. The question running through the program is simple: What has to get funded, built, & bought for the next generation of space markets to take hold? Up/Link answers it two ways at once - mainstage insight, & a structured program of curated 1:1 meetings. Insight on the stage. Deals in the room - one matched meeting at a time.

events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: Sharing Heat - Industrial Energy Partnerships From Sweden & NY
events.description: Building Energy Exchange & the Swedish Energy Agency (SEA) are convening industry leaders to explore how industrial energy partnerships & innovative business models can transform waste heat into a valuable clean energy resource - & make thermal energy networks (TENs) financially viable investments.  Presentations will feature two pioneering projects. In Sweden, the energy provider Adven operates a 4th Generation District Heating & Cooling (4GDHC) network in the city of Nynshamn, which captures waste heat from the local Nynas refinery. In upstate New York, SUNY's flagship campus at the University at Buffalo is developing a TEN that will utilize waste heat from the Empire AI supercomputing center to decarbonize campus buildings.  A moderated discussion will examine the cross-sector collaborations, financing pathways, risk mitigation, & technical strategies behind these initiatives, exploring what each project can teach us about how to advance TENs in New York. Join us this Climate Week for this timely conversation & live Q&A, & network over coffee & small bites at the Exchange in downtown Manhattan!  Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeNiclas Carlsson, Head of International Market Development & Investment Promotion, Swedish Energy Agency Carter Strickland, Chief Sustainability Officer & Executive Director of Climate Action, State University of New York (SUNY) Presenters / PanelistsJonas Dyrke, Business Project Manager, AdvenJason Denue, Vice President of Energy & Principal, WENDEL CompaniesRyan McPherson, Chief Sustainability Officer, University of BuffaloDan Egan, Managing Director & Head of Americas Real Estate Sustainability, Blackstone - Moderator Program Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

events.name: Interior Ecologies
events.description: From simple greenhouses to botanic facilities, & from data centers to automated interiors, never before in history has architecture produced so many interiors for the non-human, challenging disciplinary notions on tectonics, light, comfort & entire regulatory frameworks. Once designed for & with the human, contemporary interiors have instead become exponentially complex materializations where the politics of our present moment are played out. Ultimately, who are they for? Interior Ecologies is a critical framework developed within the Master of Arts in Interior Architecture (MAIA) program at Geneva School of Art & Design (HEAD - Genve). It examines how interior architecture engages with climate change, resource circulation & multispecies coexistence alongside posthuman & more-than-human design perspectives. Rather than treating interiors as autonomous spaces, it calls on us to rethink them as complex ecologies in which human & nonhuman actors are entangled across broader planetary scales. This roundtable brings together voices from HEAD - Genve, MoMA, & Columbia GSAPP to reflect on how interior architecture can contribute to new ecological approaches to design, research, & professional practice. The event will also include a presentation of the scenographic installation developed by MAIA for Assembly, the Swiss presence at Climate Week NYC. Employing scaffolding & dismantlable systems as an embodiment of circular architecture, the installation demonstrates principles of reuse, adaptability, & reversibility, staking its claim as an active ecological agent within the space. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: Future US Role In Global Conservation
events.description: What should the future U.S. role in global conservation look like, & whose experience & ideas should shape it? The biodiversity funding landscape changed dramatically in 2025 as the USG abruptly abandoned its international conservation commitments. The loss of approximately $500 million in annual U.S. international conservation funding, along with decades of government capacity & expertise, disrupted conservation efforts around the world. This moment demands more than restoring the former system. It creates an opportunity to examine it critically: what worked, what did not, whose perspectives carried weight, & what must change to build a more effective & durable approach. Hosted by Reimagining Global Conservation, this event will bring together international & locally rooted conservation practitioners, policy experts, funders, & other Climate Week participants. One Earth Partners will present findings from Beyond the Funding Gap, its global assessment of USAID's distinctive role in climate & environmental programming, the structural effects of its 2025 withdrawal, & priorities for future U.S. engagement. A diverse panel of practitioners will then offer locally-grounded perspectives on the future U.S. role, including concrete reforms, institutional changes, & practical proposals for a new global conservation playbook. The session will create space for participants to question familiar assumptions & contribute ideas grounded in their own experience. Biodiversity conservation is inseparable from resilience, livelihoods, stability, & security. Join us for a candid, nonpartisan conversation about how the United States can learn from the past & engage differently in the future.

events.name: Circular Innovation & Resilient Futures - Insights From The Arctic
events.description: Bringing together leaders from business, Indigenous communities, policymaking, finance, & academia, this session explores how Arctic innovation, from Indigenous knowledge to cutting-edge circular economy solutions, can deliver practical & scalable responses to climate, economic, & geopolitical challenges. The Arctic is experiencing some of the world's fastest environmental, economic, & geopolitical change. In response, Indigenous communities, businesses, researchers, policymakers, & investors are developing innovative approaches that strengthen resilience while supporting sustainable economic growth. Long before the term circular economy existed, Arctic Indigenous Peoples developed knowledge systems grounded in stewardship, resource efficiency, & long-term thinking. Today, these principles are complemented by advances in circular business models, clean technologies, sustainable finance, & policy innovation. Finland has emerged as a global leader in circular economy solutions, while Indigenous leadership across Spmi & the wider Arctic continues to demonstrate how traditional knowledge & community-driven approaches can shape resilient futures.

events.name: Catalyzing Cities
events.description: Cities are increasingly expected to deliver climate resilience while navigating constrained budgets, aging infrastructure, & growing complexity. Yet many of the most impactful solutions already exist... the challenge is designing financing & partnership models that enable them to scale. This New York Climate Week, join Cool Climate Collective & Climate Vine, as we convene investors, city leaders, philanthropies & ecosystem partners for a discussion on how innovative financing structures & public-private collaboration can unlock catalytic outcomes for cities, particularly for New York. Drawing on emerging work in city outcomes & practical examples from around the world, we'll explore: New models for financing climate resilience beyond traditional procurement. How blended capital & partnership design can accelerate deployment. What is already working in practice & why. Lessons & systems insights informed by collaborators across the resilience ecosystem, including perspectives shared by our partners from UNDRR & Dark Matter Labs. The session is designed to be interactive, bringing together practitioners across sectors to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions, & identify opportunities for collaboration during Climate Week. Agenda 9:30 - 10:00 AM : Check-in & coffee networking 10:00 - 11:30 AM : Interactive discussion & programming 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM : Facilitated small-group discussions followed by open networking

events.name: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionGenerative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.  The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers & builders can go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, & to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made.  What to ExpectA full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, & system admins who know these problems cold End-of-day demos to judges, investors, & real TA leaders The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers  PrizesWinners walk away with build-tool & platform credits, expert consulting sessions, & investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders & buyers.  JudgesTiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral & hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships. Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator & builder in the HR-tech ecosystem. Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside. Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel. Shiv Jethi - Engineer at SpaceX. Olivia Iarmak - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality & operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Prince Rumi - Excelsior Edge Ventures, Partner | AI Researcher Rami Abouemira, formerly People Ops at Square & VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR & Founders Foundry. Ishaan Das (TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation & product design for several recruiting firms & recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg. More judges to be announced - investors & TA buyers joining the panel.  Who Should AttendEngineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML Founders & aspiring founders who like shipping fast Recent grads, master's students, & NYC college builders TA ops & recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build.  Credit SponsorsSolari is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, & desktops from one API, & automate at scale. Block Convey is an AI reliability & observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval & decisions, identify where it fails, & improve it.  HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Integral Recruiting (IRD): Enterprise talent-acquisition & iCIMS/ATS specialists, & stewards of the ~350-member SAI community of TA operators & system admins. Greg Mendez: NYU. Bringing the university's builder & HR-analytics community into the room. TechSHRM is NYU Tandon's, award-winning student chapter of the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM). Established in 1987, we bridge data science, technology, & organizational strategy through people analytics - leveraging data to optimize workforce decision-making, recruitment, & employee performance.

events.name: Fusion Research Symposium - Optimizing Symmetry In Fusion Plasmas
events.description: Join us for the Fusion Research Symposium: Optimizing Symmetry in Fusion Plasmas, part of Climate Week at Columbia Engineering. Discover the research & innovation advancing the future of fusion energy at this dynamic symposium hosted by the Fusion Research Center together with the Max Planck Society Institute for Plasma Physics. Bringing together leading voices from academia, government, research institutions, & industry, the program will explore cutting-edge advances in fusion energy & plasma science, the role of international collaboration, & the opportunities for engagement in this exciting area. Through keynote remarks, panel discussions, hear from experts at the forefront of the field. Through student flash talks & posters, discover the breadth of research underway at the Fusion Research Center & beyond. The symposium will conclude with a reception & laboratory tours, offering an opportunity to connect with researchers & experience the Center's work firsthand. Featured Speakers: David Spergel, President, Simons Foundation Angela Olinto, Provost, Columbia University Najat Mokhtar, Deputy Director General, International Atomic Energy Agency Thomas Klinger, Director, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Greifswald Tim Happel, Director, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Garching Ellen Smeele, Chief of Staff, Proxima Fusion Thomas Pedersen, Chief Technical Officer, Type One Energy David Gates, Chief Technical Officer, Thea Energy Phil Snyder, VP of Plasma Physics, Commonwealth Fusion Systems Dr. Josefine Proll, Group leader, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics Discover the research. Meet today's leaders & the next generation of talent. Explore the future of fusion. This event is part of Climate Week at Columbia Engineering. Media interested in attending or covering the event must RSVP to engmediarelations@columbia.edu Campus Access:In accordance with the University's current visitor guidelines, all non-Columbia guests will receive a QR code within a few hours of the event date. The code will be sent to you via email from CU Guest Access & must be presented for campus entry, along with a government-issued ID.  Accessibility:Columbia University makes every effort to accommodate individuals with disabilities. If you require disability accommodations to attend an event at Columbia University, please contact the Office of Disability Services at 212.854.2388 or access@columbia.edu. Photography/Videography:Columbia Engineering reserves the right to capture & use images (including video, photo, audio) of participants at this event in its current or future marketing materials. These materials include but are not limited to: social media, digital and/or print posters, email & web-based materials. By attending & participating in this event, you are consenting to having your image captured for these purposes. If you have concerns about your likeness being used, please reach out to engineeringcommunications@columbia.edu & we will accommodate your request.

events.name: Grids In Transition
events.description: The US power sector is entering a complex new phase driven by rapidly expanding electricity demand. While generation capacity is growing, the critical challenge is delivering clean, reliable, & affordable power to homes, businesses, & industry. This transformation is uniquely defined by surging electrification, the rise of AI & large data centers, the growth of distributed energy resources, & expanding heavy industry loads-creating unprecedented stress on the power grid.  America's goals for energy security, economic growth, & industrial competitiveness rely as much on grid modernization as they do on expanding generation. Grid capacity now often dictates where new generation projects & data centers are located, & how quickly electrification can scale across transportation, buildings, & manufacturing. If the grids are not strengthened faster, progress will slow down, costs will rise, congestion & reliability problems will increase, & economic opportunities could be lost.  Originally built for a different era, the US transmission & distribution networks are now operating near their limits, facing challenges including integration of renewables, bidirectional power flows, rising peak demand, declining system inertia, & increasing climate & cybersecurity risks. Grids must evolve from passive infrastructure into an intelligent, dynamic system that manages flexibility, resilience, & reliability in real time.  Meeting this moment requires urgent expansion & modernization of the power grids-a priority reinforced by the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power initiative to accelerate critical grid infrastructure. With record investments underway, electricity grids must transform to support growing demand, manage emerging risks, & integrate varied generation resources more effectively.  However, grid transformation is complex, requiring close coordination among federal & state regulators, regional transmission organizations, utilities, technology providers, investors, & communities. No single policy, market mechanism, or technology can deliver this transition alone.  In this context, Global Transmission is organizing a conference on Grids in Transition - US on September 24, 2026, in New York City. This conference will place grids at the center of the conversation about the future of the US electricity industry, bringing together policymakers, regulators, system operators, utilities, technology leaders, & investors to examine how the grid must evolve to support the nation's rapidly changing power system.  Building on the success of our past grid & electrification events, this conference will provide a timely opportunity to discuss the challenges, trade-offs, & solutions needed for developing the electricity networks of the future. This event will offer vital insights & collaboration opportunities on the transformative role of grids in the American energy landscape.

events.name: Who Gets To Fund The Future?
events.description: A funder dialogue on how philanthropy can resource grassroots movements, solidarity funding infrastructure & climate justice in a time of rising far-right power. Far-right forces are organizing across borders, attacking land, food systems, rights, democracy & climate justice. Grassroots movements have been building alternatives long before this moment of crisis. This morning gathering will bring together movement leaders, movement-aligned funding networks, popular finance initiatives & funders for a participatory conversation on how resources can move with greater trust, proximity & solidarity. The event will include short provocations, space for questions & discussion, & time for connection. Together, we will explore what kinds of funding infrastructure help movements build power, what gets in the way, & how philanthropy can respond with more courage & usefulness in this moment. Speakers will include:Loren Cardeli, Executive Director, A Growing Culture Luis Carlos Costa, Executive Director, FINAPOP Juliana Tinoco, Co-Founder, Global South House Mamadou Goita, Executive Director, Institute for Research & Promotion of Alternatives in Development, Mali.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Building For The Future - Data Centers, Water Stewardship & Decarbonization
events.description: Two of the hardest problems in corporate climate action right now are water & energy, & both are being tested in real time by companies making infrastructure decisions with long lifespans. This event brings together cross-sector practitioners to discuss what's working, what's stuck, & what needs to change to achieve meaningful, shared solutions at scale. Panel one - data centers & water: Water is an increasing source of tension as data center development accelerates. Data center developers are setting water positive commitments that include reducing water demand & increasing reuse, & also investing in water replenishment that goes beyond the fenceline to invest in watersheds. In this panel, we will bring together speakers representing hyperscalers, utilities, & communities to explore what is needed to effectively support communities & ecosystems while reducing data center risks. Panel two - portfolio decarbonization: Setting a corporate emissions target is straightforward; delivering it across a portfolio of facilities built over decades is not. Public & private sector panelists will discuss how large organizations sequence capital across sites with different ages, uses, & local grids - where electrification pencils out, where it doesn't yet, & what actually moves a portfolio rather than a single flagship building.

events.name: When Data Goes Dark - Preparing For Climate Disasters In Era Of Science Disinvestment
events.description: Over the past year, climate science & environmental data & tools have faced steep disinvestment, but maintaining a strong scientific enterprise & the data it creates is critical to helping communities & businesses prepare for & respond to climate risks. When that data disappears, so does our ability to anticipate, prepare for, & respond to climate disasters before they strike. This panel starts by looking at what's been lost, & at the rescue efforts now underway to preserve high-fidelity climate data & disaster-cost datasets before they disappear for good. It then turns forward: what will it take to rebuild a more resilient, connected environmental data ecosystem - one built so that this kind of loss can't happen again? Join us for a conversation that moves from triage to reimagining, bringing together leaders in climate science, environmental data, global research, & emergency management to chart what comes next. Sponsored By:American Geophysical UnionClimate CentralThe New York Climate ExchangeOpen Environmental Data Project

events.name: 35% Moment - What Will It Take To Electrify Global Economy By 2035
events.description: Electricity meets barely a fifth of the world's final energy demand today. Yet electrification is the fastest lever governments have to cut emissions, insulate households from the next fossil fuel price shock, & maintain energy security. Getting there means moving vehicles, buildings, & industry onto electrons & modernizing & expanding the power grid faster than any economy has yet managed.  With over 100 companies, the EU, UN, & more, likely to commit to electrify 35% of final energy demand by 2035, this event will ask what it takes to electrify the economy within the next decade. The countries that pull it off first won't just hit a target, they'll write the playbook everyone else has to follow. This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School & Centre for Net Zero, a nonprofit research institute founded by Octopus Energy Group. Speakers:Devrim Celal, Chief Flexibility & Marketing Officer at Kraken TechnologiesDana Guernsey, CEO & Co-Founder at Voltus Robert Metcalfe, Chief Economist at Centre for Net Zero (part of the Octopus Energy Group) & Professor at Columbia SIPAGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: Rethink Waste, Reduce Emissions & Unlock Value
events.description: The Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House invite you to a reception & conversation on global circularity. Resource scarcity, shifting global supply chains, & climate change are reshaping the landscape for businesses, governments, & communities. We need solutions that create economic value for businesses & individuals while advancing climate goals. One place to look for these solutions is in our waste. The Circularity Gap Report estimates that roughly 25.4 trillion in economic value is lost globally each year through linear take-make-waste practices. This Value Gap represents 31% of global GDP, meaning that for every 3 of economic value created worldwide, about 1 is lost. Increasing circularity, which simply means keeping materials in use for as long as possible, could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 39%. Circularity is not only good for the bottom line & the environment, but can also improve quality of life through more durable products, greater affordability, & connected communities. If the benefits are so clear, what will it take to scale circularity? How do we align businesses, governments, & communities around a shared path forward? To kick off Climate Week NYC, Scandinavia House is pleased to partner with Columbia Climate School for a conversation on the promise of a circular economy. Join leaders from the public & private sectors as they explore practical solutions & emerging innovations, lessons learned from Nordic leadership, & the challenges that remain. The program will conclude with a special announcement from Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, followed by a reception to connect & continue the conversation. Alexis Abramson - Opening RemarksDean & Professor, Columbia Climate School Sandra Goldmark - ModeratorProfessor of Professional Practice in the Faculty of Climate, Columbia Climate School Anu MntySenior Lead, International Programs, Sitra John MuirHead of USA, 3stepIT Miia RantanenConsul General of Finland in New York Presented By: Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House Please note, this program is a private event. If you would like to share this invitation, or if you have general questions, please contact development@climate.columbia.edu. Registration is required.

We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). Chris Sacca-led climate VC) SOSV - ~$1.5B (AUM; most active deep tech pre-seed investor globally) DCVC - ~$3B+ (total AUM across multiple deep tech funds + DCVC Climate Select ~$400M) Breakthrough Energy Ventures - ~$3.5B+ (committed capital across 3 flagship funds; backed by Gates, Bezos, Bloomberg) Combined estimated private market exposure represented at Atlas Coaliton's events: $2.5T+ USD  Sponsors & Partners: Get full access to our alumni directory of 280+ verified past family offices guests - including family offices, institutional LPs, & hardware / frontier tech founders - through our WeTheAtlas Family Office & Investors Matching System. Search by investor type, AUM range, sector focus, & geography. Request warm introductions to any previous guest directly through the platform. Reach out to us at : team@wetheatlas.com WHAT HAPPENED AFTER OUR LAST SUMMITS This is not a talking shop. Capital moves in this room. $15M Raised - Twelve (SAF Carbon Transformation). An introduction made through our summit network connected Twelve - the company turning CO into jet fuel & chemicals for Mercedes-Benz, P&G, & British Airways - with the CMA CGM Saad family office. Result: $15M raised to scale the technology that's replacing fossil fuels with air & water. $37M+ in Funds LPs Investments Value Facilitated in 2025. Across our summits & coalition network, Atlas team facilitated more than $37M in transaction value between LPs & GPs of frontier & climate tech funds in a single year. 500+ Investor-Innovators Connections Made. Our events don't end when the panels do. Through structured 1:1 matching, post-event introductions, & the WeTheAtlas platform, our summits have generated over 500 qualified LP-GPs connections since 2024. Every number on this page is real. We don't count badge scans. We count capital deployed. THE FORMAT: BUILT FOR DEALS, NOT PANELS This is not a 3,000-person conference with a lanyard & a prayer. Here's exactly how the day works: 150 attendees. That's it. We cap attendance & curate every seat. Ratio target: 50% LPs & family offices, 30% GPs & fund managers, 20% frontier tech founders. Everyone in the room is either writing checks or building companies worth funding. Structured 1:1 Investor-Founder Matching. Every sponsors is matched with up to 10 relevant connections before the event through our WeTheAtlas matching system. You'll arrive knowing exactly who to meet, what time & which table number - no cold intros, no wasted conversations. 3 Deep-Dive Panels (Not TED Talks) Moderated discussions with founders & investors who are in the trenches - not keynotes from people selling you a vision. Topics this year:  Energy Abundance: Nuclear Power, SAF & the New Economics of the Energy Renaissance  From Bits to Atoms: Physical AI, Robotics & the Climate Resilient Infrastructure Revolution  LP & GP Perspectives: Deploying Capital in Vital, Frontier Tech, Resilience & the Rise of Secondaries  Old Money, New Frontiers: Foundations, Endowments & Corporates Are Funding Existential Resilience  The 2026 Portfolio: How Family Offices Are Navigating War, Tariffs, Reshoring & the New World Order About WeTheAtlas WeTheAtlas is the capital mobilization platform for frontier & climate tech. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. With $22B committed across 1,200 members (70% investors, 30% founders), the coalition hosted events in 8+ cities, share a monthly newsletter, conduct media interviews, & connect active frontier & climate investors through deal flow. Learn more: https://www.atlascoalition.com/ By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with the organizers of Climate Week NYC.

events.name: Building Better Trading Strategies w/ AI
events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: AI Tinkerers Demo Day w/ PostHog
events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC! Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQ Some slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? This is your moment to share with like-minded AI tinkerers! A demo is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!)  FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo. Demo vibes  Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:00 Networking & pizzas9:00 Doors CloseMore informationIf you are new to AI Tinkerers, please read the AI Tinkerers FAQ & join our Discord channel: https://discord.gg/8WsqnC6Hk3 SponsorsPostHogPostHog is an all-in-one product OS designed for engineers, offering product analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, & surveys in a single platform. It enables teams to understand user behavior, deploy features, & analyze data without patching together multiple tools. Founded in Y Combinator (W20), it supports both cloud-hosted & open-source self-hosting. Veris AI (Venue Host)Veris AI accelerates agent development & deployment with a simulation sandbox platform that delivers robust, compliant AI systems at speed. Veris sandbox is pre-loaded with test scenarios, simulated tools, & personas. Using the sandbox, you can run thousands of simulated interactions across routine workflows, challenging edge cases, & adversarial scenarios. Veris AI creates root-cause analysis reports, regression testing gates, & prompt or RL optimization loops to improve the agent using these interactions before the agent touches the first real system or customer. Start building now!We're bringing a builder-first lineup of demos & giving the community a space to share work in progress, trade notes, & meet other serious practitioners.

events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? Reach out to Amy Newhall at an2933@columbia.edu.  _________________________________________________________________________________________ To obtain additional information about program offerings at Columbia University's School of Professional Studies, please contact an Admissions Counselor at inquire@sps.columbia.edu. If you require closed captioning, sign-language interpretation, or any other disability accommodations, please contact Disability Services, disability@columbia.edu, at least 10 days in advance. Services requested less than 10 days in advance cannot be guaranteed. Please visit Columbia University's Hub for Emergency Preparedness to stay up to date on the latest campus health & safety policies. This event is open to individuals irrespective of identity & sex.

events.name: Traceability & Nature-Positive Supply Chains
events.description: World Wildlife Fund & the Tapestry Foundation are hosting a day of discussion & interaction focused on traceability & accountability in supply chains during Climate Week NYC, & you're invited! From Vision to Action: Traceability, Circularity, & Policy for Climate-Resilient, Nature-Positive Supply Chains will foster a high-level dialogue on how traceability, circularity, & policy can serve as strategic enablers for cross-sector resilient & transparent supply chains. Featured topics: Global Traceability Framework for Beef & Leather: Interoperable traceability for nature-positive supply chains - Supported by WWF, Tapestry, Institute of Food Technologists, Textile Exchange, & Better Food Future Policy Momentum for Climate-Resilient Supply Chains: Long-term stability & resilience for the Amazon & other important biomes - Supported by WWF & the Inter-American Development Bank, featuring government representatives. Material Flows, Intelligence, Traceability & Data for a Circular Textiles System - Supported by WWF, Accelerating Circularity, & BSR Join us for an engaging discussion about traceability, material flow, & policy as an enabler of transformation. Breakfast will be served beginning at 8:15 am. Lunch will be served. More details, including the full agenda & guest speakers, will be shared soon.

events.name: Nexus Meetup
events.description: A casual, pay-your-own-way networking event designed for professionals to connect, share ideas, & build lasting relationships across the broader business & technology ecosystem. Meet fellow professionals, expand your network, & enjoy a relaxed evening together. Food & beverages are available for individual purchase. Who Attends: Founders & startups PR & Agency teams Venture Capitalists Consultants Finance professionals Content & social media marketers Marketing technology professionals Attendance is limited to help keep conversations meaningful, so please apply for a spot. We look forward to meeting you! About Our Meet Ups: Our Meet Ups are relaxed, industry-agnostic gatherings built for professionals who want to unplug from the standard corporate routine & connect on a human level. Whether you are looking to exchange fresh perspectives, brainstorm new concepts, or simply meet peers navigating similar spaces, this environment is designed for open-ended conversation & organic relationship-building. What It Is: An open, welcoming community space to meet new connections. An opportunity to exchange industry perspectives & uncover unexpected collaborations. A low-pressure, welcoming atmosphere with no formal agenda or mandatory pitches. What It Isn't: RTM Nexus Meet Up is not a curated buyer/seller event & is not structured around guaranteed access to a specific target audience, vertical, company type, or decision-maker profile (ICP). Looking for something more targeted? If you need to connect with a specific niche-such as retail, fashion, beauty, CPG, or enterprise brand leaders-check out our "Retail Leaders Receptions" & "Nexus Mixers" instead. Those events are intentionally curated & sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

events.name: Propel Demo Night - Founder Showcase
events.description: Demo Day is for the cohort. Demo Night is for everyone else.nWho we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms.nTen companies, five minutes each, in front of an investor room. You do not need to be in a programme. You need a product & five minutes.nDemo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run. 26,666 people on the guest list, 35+ investors in the room. This is the recurring open version of that night.nEvery attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation.nThe nightn6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waitingn7:00 Ten companies, five minutes eachn8:15 Room favourite, voted liven8:30 Open floor with the investors in the roomn9:00 ClosenTicketsnGeneral admission, free.nPresent Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room & professional video of your pitch.nTitle Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per night. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.nFree for Propel Private Network members.nDinner is highly encouraged, the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late.nWhat Propel actually does for youn1  Innovation in Public  our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply heren2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now  someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membershipn3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlistn4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-foundersn5  Providers already in the room. This is not theoretical. Moshe Cohen, CPA of Cohen & Co runs tax strategy, bookkeeping & fractional CFO work for Propel founders & takes bookings through us. Thirty minute paid session, 120 dollars  Book Moshe. Stephen Michael Consulting, a 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises entering the startup ecosystem, 150 dollars  Book a strategy call. If you provide a service & want a table at the next one, that is what the provider ticket is.nOn camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly.nNewsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380.nAbout The WilsonnThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio.nThe Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair WagenWhat Propel does, & what it has producednNine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run.nFounders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive.nFounders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplacenWork with Stephen directly. A 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises trying to get into the startup ecosystem. Book a strategy call, browse the marketplace50nHiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find onenProduct Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it.nCapital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next onenMasterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendarnThe GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohortnThe Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work.nCommunity Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. Happy hour runs from 2 to 4 on Saturday, October 10th, out on the water with the harbor & the skyline as the backdrop.nWhat to Expect:nA cross-section of people working on cities & public systems: public servants, technologists, founders, funders, consultants, & nonprofit operatorsnGenuine conversations across different corners of civic & urban tech: different roles, different focus areas, all in one placenNo sales pitches, no panels, just good companynFun prizes via our always-popular raffle nOptional activities before the happy hour so you can make a full island day of itnMake a Full Day of It:nThe main extra is a volunteer session with the Billion Oyster Project. They're restoring NY Harbor with oyster reefs, a natural fit for a group that spends its weekdays working on cities & public systems.nYou can also join Jer Thorp for Bird Data Portraits from 1 to 2. Jer is a data artist & bird enthusiast, & he'll help you make a data portrait of your favorite local bird using data from eBird. All materials will be provided, & you'll wrap up right as the happy hour begins.nPick Your Ticket:nHappy Hour Only: The main event, 2 to 4 on the water. Ferry over whenever works for you.nHappy Hour + Volunteer: The volunteer session, then straight into the happy hour. Starts with a 9:15am ferry & wraps at 2:30.
