events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. For more information, please visit the Queens AI website.

events.name: Built World Resiliency - From Data Centers To Materials
events.description: This event (two panels & an accompanying happy hour with refreshments) spotlights high-growth emerging technology startups tackling critical infrastructure challenges in the Built Environment-from resilient power delivery for data centers to advanced materials & transparency platforms for infrastructure operations. We bring together founders with institutional real estate & infrastructure investors to connect frontier innovation with the capital & market access needed to scale durable, high-performance solutions across the global built world. The panels provide actionable insights to deliver reliable power for AI workloads, strengthen building-material supply chains, & improve procurement transparency through automated assessments-helping create a more resilient, resource-efficient built environment. The Built Environment is under pressure from every direction: surging energy demand, supply-chain volatility, tightening regulations, & aging infrastructure. The companies that will define the next era of real estate & infrastructure are building for resilience from day one. Built World Resiliency brings together startup founders & investors to explore how the next generation of infrastructure is being designed to perform under these new realities. Panel 1 - Powering AI: Building Resilient Compute Infrastructure (4:00 PM). events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Local Climate Imperative - Public-Private Partnerships In Action
events.description: Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion during Climate Week NYC 2026 As climate action increasingly takes shape at the local level, cities, businesses, & communities are finding new ways to work together to drive meaningful progress. Yet opportunities for public-sector climate leaders & corporate sustainability professionals to learn from one another remain surprisingly rare. Agendi & Run on Climate invite you to an intimate breakfast discussion at BelCham Atelier, exploring the power of public-private partnerships to accelerate climate progress. Rather than a traditional panel, the program will feature a select group of speakers sharing practical examples of how collaboration across government, business, & community partners is driving meaningful change - from policy development & implementation to corporate strategy & investment. The remainder of the event will focus on networking & facilitated discussion, creating space for participants to share best practices, discuss common challenges, & identify new opportunities to work together. Join us for a morning of insightful conversation, meaningful connections, & practical ideas to help strengthen the partnerships driving climate action forward. About Agendi & Run on Climate Run on Climate & Agendi share a belief that accelerating climate progress requires stronger connections between the public & private sectors. While Run on Climate helps local governments advance ambitious climate policies & implementation, Agendi partners with companies to translate climate commitments into actionable business strategies. Bringing these communities together creates a unique opportunity to exchange perspectives, identify shared challenges, & explore new models for collaboration that can accelerate climate action at the local level.

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Climate-Smart Food Systems - Geospatial Innovation, Cloud, AI
events.description: Climate volatility is reshaping global agriculture & food systems & the need for scalable, data-driven solutions has never been more urgent. Join Taylor Geospatial & AWS for a candid conversation on the future of climate resilience in food systems, & the role geospatial technologies, AI, cloud infrastructure, & cross-sector collaboration play in building that future. From modeling how crops will fare under tomorrow's climates, to mapping how food moves from field to global market & communities who need it most, to efficient nitrogen management, our speakers are shaping & building the next generation of tools on AWS cloud & AI. This session will spotlight how open data, cloud computing, AI & strategic partnership are accelerating innovation & foregrounds real experiences with what it takes to scale these solutions from proof-of-concept to global impact. Why attendSee innovation in action: hear directly from teams building new models for agrifood supply chains & agricultural resilience Understand the power of collaboration: learn how partnerships between technologists, researchers, & funders are enabling applied innovation at scale Connect & engage: join a network of technical experts & leaders accelerating food system resilience through open science & advanced technology Who should attendTechnical professionals, program & project managers, & startup teams working at the intersection of geospatial technology, cloud/AI infrastructure, & sustainable agriculture. We also encourage program leads & decision-makers from international NGOs, philanthropic & commercial organizations exploring technology for social & environmental impact at scale. AgendaWelcome & introductory remarks from AWS & Taylor Geospatial Panel discussion Moderated Q&A Lunch reception Panel SpeakersKat Esser - Principal, Global Impact Accelerators, AWS Skilling & Social Impact Rachel Opitz - Program Manager, Geospatial Innovation for Food Security, Taylor Geospatial Ben Strong - Earth Genome Matt Houser - NICCEE / University of Maryland / The Nature Conservancy Sarah Garvey - NICCEE / University of Maryland Praveen Pankajakshan - UrbanKissan

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? This Climate Week NYC event will take a clear-eyed look at the environmental case for autonomous vehicles & examine where the evidence supports the hype, & where it does not. A panel of top experts will discuss along with a Q&A session: Jeffrey Tumlin - former Exec. Director, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) David Zipper -- Contributing writer, Bloomberg City Lab; former Senior Fellow, MIT Mobility Initiative Rachel Weinberger -- Vice President, Transportation & Peter W. Herman Chair, Regional Planning Association Jeral Poskey - Founder, Swyft Cities; former project executive for transportation planning, Google Format: Panel Discussion followed by Q&A The discussion will explore the complicated relationship between automation, mobility, & sustainability. Rather than assuming new technology automatically leads to better outcomes, the discussion will focus on the many potential impacts: energy use, induced demand, land use, transit interactions, fleet models, & the difference between theoretical efficiency & actual environmental performance. Join us for a timely discussion on climate & the future of urban mobility.

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. In the context of geopolitical volatility, the case has never been stronger to leverage opportunities in regions with competitive advantages in clean energy & critical materials for deep decarbonization.  This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School.  Speakers: Shanta Barley, Director at Real Zero Hub, IIASASaul Griffith, Founder & Chief Scientist at Rewiring America & Rewiring AustraliaAmy Myers Jaffe, Director, Energy, Climate Justice & Sustainability Lab, & Research Professor at NYUGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: Addressing Cost Of Climate Impact - Actions At Scale Of The City
events.description: How do cities bridge the gap between high-level climate vulnerability data & everyday financial execution? While municipalities globally are tracking climate risks, the challenge lies in transforming these insights into the routine machinery of city governance: capital planning, investment, & budgeting. Co-hosted by C40 Cities & Climate Solutions International to discuss their landmark report, Mainstreaming Climate Adaptation in City Financial Planning & Budgeting, this high-level panel brings together policy architects & municipal finance leaders. Moving beyond theory, the session will unpack how pioneering cities are using the report's foundational frameworks to institutionalize climate resilience across all levels of urban governance. What you'll experience: Inside the C40 Framework: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the report's core strategies for embedding climate adaptation guidelines into multi-year capital plans. Governance & Procurement Shifts: Learn how leading municipalities are breaking down departmental silos & modernizing procurement frameworks to automate resilient investment. Peer-to-Peer Networking: Connect with peer sustainability directors, municipal finance officers, & climate policy experts. Refreshments will be served. Featured Panelists & Moderator: Dr. Jan Whittington (CEO, Climate Solutions International; Professor of Urban Planning, UW) Claire Markgraf (Director, City Finance Programme, C40 Cities) - Moderator Marissa Aho (Principal/Practice Leader, Climate, Fehr & Peers, & Former Director of the Executive Climate Office for King County) Lia Cairone (Associate Director for the Environmental Sustainability & Resiliency Task Force, NYC Mayor's Office of Management & Budget) This event is hybrid in nature. Please reach out nikita.tatachar@climatesolutionsintl.com for any accessibility needs.

events.name: Grids In Transition
events.description: The US power sector is entering a complex new phase driven by rapidly expanding electricity demand. While generation capacity is growing, the critical challenge is delivering clean, reliable, & affordable power to homes, businesses, & industry. This transformation is uniquely defined by surging electrification, the rise of AI & large data centers, the growth of distributed energy resources, & expanding heavy industry loads-creating unprecedented stress on the power grid.  America's goals for energy security, economic growth, & industrial competitiveness rely as much on grid modernization as they do on expanding generation. Grid capacity now often dictates where new generation projects & data centers are located, & how quickly electrification can scale across transportation, buildings, & manufacturing. If the grids are not strengthened faster, progress will slow down, costs will rise, congestion & reliability problems will increase, & economic opportunities could be lost.  Originally built for a different era, the US transmission & distribution networks are now operating near their limits, facing challenges including integration of renewables, bidirectional power flows, rising peak demand, declining system inertia, & increasing climate & cybersecurity risks. Grids must evolve from passive infrastructure into an intelligent, dynamic system that manages flexibility, resilience, & reliability in real time.  Meeting this moment requires urgent expansion & modernization of the power grids-a priority reinforced by the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power initiative to accelerate critical grid infrastructure. With record investments underway, electricity grids must transform to support growing demand, manage emerging risks, & integrate varied generation resources more effectively.  However, grid transformation is complex, requiring close coordination among federal & state regulators, regional transmission organizations, utilities, technology providers, investors, & communities. No single policy, market mechanism, or technology can deliver this transition alone.  In this context, Global Transmission is organizing a conference on Grids in Transition - US on September 24, 2026, in New York City. This conference will place grids at the center of the conversation about the future of the US electricity industry, bringing together policymakers, regulators, system operators, utilities, technology leaders, & investors to examine how the grid must evolve to support the nation's rapidly changing power system.  Building on the success of our past grid & electrification events, this conference will provide a timely opportunity to discuss the challenges, trade-offs, & solutions needed for developing the electricity networks of the future. This event will offer vital insights & collaboration opportunities on the transformative role of grids in the American energy landscape.

events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. In order to use this service, you MUST be a ticket-holder, & you MUST register your child(ren) before September 11th by acquiring a Childcare Ticket. Each child you register requires a ticket registration. There are limited spots available, so please sign up sooner rather than later! If you have any questions, please email us at citycamp+childcare@beta.nyc. Accessibility & Accommodations We want CityCamp to be usable by everyone who wants to take part. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request. Service animals are always welcome. The conference is delivered in English & uses technical terms. If you need ASL interpretation, or have any other accessibility question or request, email us at citycamp@beta.nyc by Friday, September 4. Requests after that date are welcome, & we will do what we can, but we cannot promise to fill them. Code of Conduct BetaNYC is committed to hosting safe & open spaces for all. By participating in this space, you are committing yourself to BetaNYC's Code of Conduct & Anti-Harassment Policy. Health Policy If you're not feeling well, PLEASE stay home. We strive to create a safe environment for everyone. (Please see our refund policy for questions.) We encourage everyone to wear a high-quality mask at all times (except when eating & drinking). We will have ample KF-94 masks in various sizes for you to wear. Masks keep our staff, volunteers, & attendees safe. Masking helps prevent the spread of viruses - this is science, based on data! Refund Policy Contact us to request a refund. We will try to honor all of your refund requests at citycamp+refund@beta.nyc. Please note that some ticketing fees are nonrefundable.

events.name: Private Dinner for Investors & Series A+ Founders - The AI Founder Playbook
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For founders of fast-growing Series A+ startups, with a limited number of investor seats. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, and how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, and judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, and the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening:Dinner and conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, and investors. A handful of invited voices will anchor the discussion including heads of CVCs and later stage AI founders. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is expected to bring opinions. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, and what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition and hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view. ORGANIZED BY Elpis LabsWe work with the government sector and international trade agencies to help their startups find corporate partners in the U.S. The VerticalAn online publication, community platform, and event series focusing on international venture ecosystem. Trinovation Partners: The "Scale AI" of Venture Backed Startups We are an AI data operations partner for venture-backed teams building computer vision and AI products. We build and run dedicated annotation pods: named, trained teams assigned to your product, not an anonymous crowd. Covering image and video annotation, gold-set calibration, human-in-the-loop QA, and edge-case review. Pods launch in 1-2 weeks, scale with your deployments, and deliver quality you can audit: 500+ annotators deployed, 95%+ QA accuracy, and a 30% model accuracy lift for our clients. Independent and New York-based.

events.name: Industrial Decarbonization & Urban Resilience
events.description: Heat waves, domestic supply chains, data centers, & rising energy costs dominate headlines in 2026. While the challenges might seem distinct - many of the solutions are interdependent & already being deployed today. During NYC Climate Week, Suffolk Technologies, Morrison Foerster & Climate Salon are teaming up to discuss: How do we decarbonize our infrastructure while building for resiliency? We'll start with a panel to hear from experts working on solutions to address some of our biggest challenges, & then ask you for your ideas during roundtable discussions. Join us to tackle: Data Center Decarbonization Clean Manufacturing Gridtech Urban Resilience Financing Urban Pilots   Suffolk Technologies is a venture capital platform funding the next generation of companies solving built environment challenges. Suffolk Technologies invests in early & growth-stage startups transforming the built world across real estate & development, architecture, engineering & construction, property management, & smart cities. Leveraging Suffolk's expertise & broad network of industry leaders, Suffolk Technologies partners with visionary founders to accelerate industry-wide adoption of breakthrough innovations ranging from pre-product to growth stages. For more information about Suffolk Technologies' strategy & investments, visit SuffolkTech.com. Climate Salon is a 501c3 nonprofit organization focused on bringing stakeholders together to solve climate challenges. Through educational events, its network of support organizations, & charitable giving, Climate Salon accelerates community action to bring ideas to life. Morrison Foerster (MoFo) is a global law firm with 19 offices across the U.S., Europe, & Asia. Our comprehensive platform includes an award-winning Emerging Companies + Venture Capital (ECVC) practice that combines a deep understanding of market conditions with tailored legal strategies. We advise more than 1,700 entrepreneurs, founders, & venture investors, partnering with clients at every stage of the business lifecycle - from initial formation & financings, through late-stage financings & investments, mergers & acquisitions, & public offerings. In just the last five years, we have guided our clients through venture capital financings totaling over $110 billion & mergers & acquisitions with an aggregate transactional value exceeding $850 billion. Peter Fusco is a partner in the New York office & serves as co-head of the firm's Emerging Companies + Venture Capital Practice. He represents venture funds & tech companies throughout their lifecycle, from pre-incorporation planning to angel, seed, & growth rounds to exit transactions. Pete has been representing tech companies for more than two decades in the New York ecosystem & serves as outside general counsel to many startups, growth-stage companies, & venture funds. He also works closely with NYU/Tandon Future Lab's incubator ecosystem & its related programs. Pete looks forward to working with the Suffolk Technologies & Climate Salon communities to explore collaboration & provide practical legal guidance to support your businesses. If you'd like to connect, he can be reached directly at pfusco@mofo.com

events.description: Note: we are postponing & redesigning this event for September. This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - revenue cycle, coding, & operations insiders-  **Researchers** - with data, insights, & unmet needs to solve-  **Tech co-founders** - developers & AI builders seeking high-impact problems (apply for discounted tickets)-  **Early founders** - ideas at any stage, ready to validate fast MedStartr Challenge Winners are 22 more likely to succeed. --- There are many more ticket Types available on MedStartr.ai/launchathon: | Type | Price | Details ||------|-------|---------|| General Admission | $50| Open enrollment || Two Pack | $80| Everything is better with friends || VIP | $100 | Dedicated mentor time + Health Impact Forum ticket || Early Bird | $0-25 | Apply to attend - going fast || Tech Co-Founder | $50 | Apply - discounted for technical builders || Mentor | Free | Apply via MedStartr.ai || Volunteer | Free | Help us run the event || Demo Table | $1,000 | Table for laptop, monitor + 1 rollup banner | Register & buy tickets here or for more options [visit the MedStartr.ai Healthcare Innovation platform with more details!](http://medstartr.ai/launchathon) Confirmed Sponsors Arya Health  Stack.ai  Health Impact Forum Interested in sponsoring?Five tiers from $2,500 Community to $50,000 Title. About MedStartr 17 years building the global healthcare innovation community. 9,000+ innovations reviewed. 250,000+ credentialed stakeholders. 1,200+ events in 41 cities. The team behind over 120 contests & crowdchallenges for over 200 sponsors since 2010. We also run the investment funds & accelerators, also named MedStartr where we invest in & accelerate the teams that win challenges like this one. Check out the new [MedStartr.ai](http://medstartr.ai) alpha Just Launched 7/14/2026! About ClawCamp ClawCamp is a global community advancing mastery of AI agents - from first personal agent to advanced multi-agent workflows. 1,400+ events  120+ cities  100,000+ attendees trained. The AI training backbone of the Launchathon build weekend. Visit them at clawcamp.us Khan Siddiqui, MDDr. Khan Siddiqui is a physician-entrepreneur, technologist, & radiologist at the forefront of the medical AI revolution. As CEO & Co-Founder of HOPPR, he leads the development of advanced multimodal foundation models designed to democratize AI training & accelerate medical imaging development for healthcare systems worldwide.He previously served as Chief Medical Officer & Chief Strategy Officer of Hyperfine, where he helped take the company public & deploy Swoop - the world's first FDA-cleared, portable bedside MRI system. In 2012 he founded higi, a consumer health network of thousands of biometric screening kiosks across North American pharmacies, culminating in a multi-billion-dollar acquisition. Earlier, as a principal program manager & AI architect at Microsoft, he designed the deep-learning image infrastructure used to train the Xbox Kinect. A recognized pioneer in imaging informatics, Dr. Siddiqui received the 2025 Imaging Informatics Innovator Award from the Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine (SIIM) & holds dozens of patents across medical image processing, machine learning, & healthcare analytics.

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: Hidden Patterns - Visual Journey Of Networks
events.description: In this talk, Albert-Lszl Barabsi will chart the 25-year odyssey of BarabsiLab in crafting the visual lexicon of networks. The essence of complexity lies in connectivity. Whether we examine the vast expanse of the World Wide Web, the intricacies of a cell, or the marvel of the human brain, their complexity invariably stems from intricate interconnected networks. Connectivity is foundational to our biological makeup, our social fabric, & our communicative prowess. In this talk, Albert-Lszl Barabsi will chart the 25-year odyssey of BarabsiLab in crafting the visual lexicon of networks & connectivity, focusing on their recent monumental project for the 2024 Venice Architecture Biennale, which charts 50 years of architectural history. Dr. Barabsi is the Robert Gray Professor of Network Science at Northeastern University. He has exhibited at galleries all over the U.S & Europe & recently co-designed the opening experience for the Biennale Architettura di Venezia.

events.name: Fashioning Positive Impact - 20 Yrs Of Pioneering Circular Fashion
events.description: Fashioning Positive Impact: 20 Years of Circularity for Business Longevity. Hear from DEPLOY's Founder, Dr. Bernice Pan as she shares insights from two decades of circular, design-led thinking & how it can create lasting value for business, people & planet. EVENT OUTLINE For two decades, DEPLOY has tested what it means to build circularity into the foundations of a business - from product design & production to service, customer experience & long-term care. At this 'meet the founder' event, Dr. Bernice Pan will share reflections from 20 years of turning systems change theory into business practice, & consider how circular, design-led thinking can beautifully support business & planetary resilience, relevance & longevity. The session will bring together senior leaders from business, finance, sustainability & policy to explore what long-term value looks like in a resource-constrained world. About DEPLOY Founded in 2006, DEPLOY is one of the world's earliest ethical fashion pioneers & a strategic action plan to reform fashion. Its signature 360 Sustainability Compass puts care for makers, wearers & the planet at the heart of the business, embedding this approach across design, production, service, repair & long-term use. DEPLOY is the world's highest-scoring fashion B Corp, with a score of 176.8, & actively contributes towards 12 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. Its work has been recognised by the Great British Brands Award for Commitment to Planet, the Future Icon Award for Best Zero-Waste Brand & the Marie Claire Sustainability Award for Ethical Fashion Brand of the Year.

events.name: AI Needs More Power - Who Builds It, What Gets Built & Who Gets Paid
events.description: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. On-site resources are becoming critical & can potentially offer flexibility while reducing ratepayer impact. Moderated by Lisa Martine Jenkins of Latitude Media, energy leaders & investors from Aston Power, Commonwealth Station A, & Redwood Materials will debate where capital is moving, what actually needs to get built, & whether the AI boom will fundamentally reshape how, & from whom, large energy users get their power Moderator: Lisa Martine Jenkins | Editor | Latitude Media Panelists: Doug Chambers | Chief Development Officer | Aston Travis Metcalfe | Energy Strategist | Commonwealth Asset Management Group Kevin Berekemeyer | Co-Founder & CEO | Station A Claire McConnell | Vice President of Business Development | Redwood Materials Antenna Group is the public relations & strategic marketing agency of choice for climate, energy, mobility, real estate, & infrastructure leaders. If you're a startup, investor, or global corporation that's looking to tell your climate story, demonstrate your impact, or accelerate your growth, Antenna Group's team of industry insiders is ready to help. Learn more at antennagroup.com.

events.name: Brunch & Learn
events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Drone delivery gets regulatory approval - Now what? DoorDash just became only the eighth company ever to earn FAA air-carrier certification for drones, joining Amazon, Walmart, & Alphabet's Wing in a race that's now more about economics than regulation. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionGenerative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.  The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Event DescriptionGenerative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.  The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. We connect family offices, institutional LPs, & regional conglomerates with the founders building the future of energy, AI infrastructure, robotics, & industrial decarbonization. The platform integrates four engines:  Summits - 150-person curated events in New York & San Francisco bringing LPs face-to-face with frontier tech founders  The Adaptive Economy Newsletter - Weekly intelligence reaching 15,000+ frontier & resilience investors & founders worldwide  LP-GP Matching - Proprietary family offices / LPs & investor-founder matching system powering warm introductions year-round  SPVs & Co-Investment - Direct co-investment vehicles alongside vetted fund managers & family offices In 2025: $37M+ in investments facilitated. 280+ family offices alumni. 1,200+ coalition members representing $500B in committed capital. Learn more: wethetatlas.com About The Atlas Coalition The Atlas Coalition is a community focused on funding vital innovations for our society & our only planet. events.name: Implementing Circularity In Interior Design
events.description: Connecting the Dots Our interior spaces remains trapped in a persistent & costly system of frequent renovation, demolition, & disposal, resulting in an unsustainable churn of materials. While circular design offers a path forward, the challenge isn't just designing for circularity; it's creating the network of relationships needed to make it work, connecting the many stakeholders responsible for shaping, operating, & renewing interior spaces. Our panel of stakeholders across the value chain will examine what is needed to really implement the circularity loop - to keep materials in circulation, reduce waste, lower costs, create jobs, & transform the interiors industry from a linear model of consumption to a truly circular one. Join us for a lively & provocative discussion. Moderators: David Bergman, Architect, Educator, Founder / Director, CCID  Speakers: Yarden Harari, Associate Principal, ArcadisRobin Reigi, Owner, Robin ReigiDoug Pilgrim, Business Development / Sustainability Manager, Davies OfficeMichael Orbank, Sustainability Manager, STO

events.name: Global Forum On Circular Economy & Urban Resilience
events.description: Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban ResilienceDate: Friday, September 25, 2026Venue: Club 135 by IndustriousAddress: 135 W 50th Street, New York, NY 10020Format: Invitation OnlyExpected Attendance: Approximately 200 participantsLanguage: EnglishHost: Office of the City of Yokohama Representative to the AmericasSponsors: ITO ENPartners: Greennex Global, ShibuLA Ventures, CleanLeap & Deep Tech Forum About the ForumThe global economy is undergoing a profound transformation driven by geopolitical uncertainty, the restructuring of global supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, & growing demand for energy & critical resources. Against this backdrop, the circular economy is emerging not only as an environmental agenda, but also as a strategic approach to strengthening economic competitiveness, resource security, industrial resilience, & sustainable growth. Held during Climate Week NYC 2026, the Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban Resilience will bring together city & regional government representatives, international organizations, corporations, investors, financial institutions, startups, & climate innovation leaders from Asia, North America, Europe, & beyond. Through business showcases, reverse pitches, keynote remarks, & cross-sector discussions, the Forum will connect urban challenges with innovation, investment, & international partnerships. It will also explore how cities can serve as platforms for collaboration among businesses, startups, investors, & global institutions. The Forum will serve as an important step toward Yokohama's major international initiatives in 2027, including GREENEXPO 2027, Asia-Pacific Circular Cities Forum (APCC-Forum), the Asia-Pacific Urban Forum, & broader international dialogue on circular & resilient urban development. View the Speaker ListMorning Programme: Business & Innovation ForumConnecting Innovation Ecosystems Across Asia, North America, & Europe 9:00-9:30 Registration & Networking Coffee9:30-9:40 Welcome Remarks9:40-10:30 Startup ShowcaseSelected startups will present innovative technologies & business models in the fields of the circular economy, climate technology, & urban sustainability. The session is designed to create opportunities for pilot projects, joint development, investment, strategic partnerships, & expansion into Japanese & broader Asian markets. Presenting Startups: TBD 10:30-11:20 Reverse PitchJapanese companies will present their business challenges, innovation priorities, & areas of interest to an audience of international startups. The session aims to identify potential partners & initiate discussions on joint development, pilot projects, & future business collaboration. Participating Companies: Nick Vega, Director on the Investments & Strategy team, Sumitomo Corporation Takeyori Nabeta, Business Development Manage at Chiyoda International Corporation / Venture Associate at DNX Ventures Junya Saka, Manager, Strategic Investment & Partnerships, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation Hirotaka Mori, Principal Researcher, Business Development & CVC, ENEOS Americas Additional companies: TBD 11:20-12:00 Innovation Leaders DialogueAI, the Circular Economy, & the Next Industrial Transformation Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries through major investment in semiconductors, data centers, digital infrastructure, & advanced industrial systems. At the same time, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition to a more sustainable & circular economy by improving efficiency across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI & the circular economy The potential of AI to improve resource efficiency & industrial decarbonization Partnerships needed to commercialize & scale next-generation technologies The roles of corporations, investors, & startups in the next industrial transformation Speakers: Durgesh Patel, Vice President, AI Center of Excellence, Hitachi Ray Hugel, CFA, Executive Director & Co-Head of Catalytic Capital & Private Credit, Closed Loop Partners Kazuhiko Nishioka, Co-Founder & CEO, Sun Metalon Kevin Ninomiya, CEO & Co-Founder, ShibuLA Ventures (Moderator) 12:00-1:30 Networking LunchAn opportunity for investors, startups, corporations, city leaders, & international organizations to connect across sectors, explore collaboration opportunities, & develop partnerships that can continue beyond the Forum. The networking lunch will also be open to participants attending the afternoon programme. Afternoon Programme: Policy & Leadership ForumAccelerating Circular Economy & Urban Resilience 1:30-1:40 Opening Remarks1:40-2:00 Keynote AddressThe Next Chapter of the Circular Economy: Competitiveness, Resilience, & Global Collaboration The circular economy is increasingly becoming a strategic framework for strengthening economic competitiveness, industrial resilience, resource security, & sustainable growth. The keynote will examine why accelerating the transition requires deeper collaboration among cities, businesses, investors, & international organizations, setting the stage for the Forum's discussions on innovation, partnerships, & global action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration Asia's rapid urbanization & growing policy ambition are making the region increasingly important to the global circular economy transition. Cities will play a central role in translating global goals events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. Happy hour runs from 2 to 4 on Saturday, October 10th, out on the water with the harbor & the skyline as the backdrop.nWhat to Expect:nA cross-section of people working on cities & public systems: public servants, technologists, founders, funders, consultants, & nonprofit operatorsnGenuine conversations across different corners of civic & urban tech: different roles, different focus areas, all in one placenNo sales pitches, no panels, just good companynFun prizes via our always-popular raffle nOptional activities before the happy hour so you can make a full island day of itnMake a Full Day of It:nThe main extra is a volunteer session with the Billion Oyster Project. They're restoring NY Harbor with oyster reefs, a natural fit for a group that spends its weekdays working on cities & public systems.nYou can also join Jer Thorp for Bird Data Portraits from 1 to 2. Jer is a data artist & bird enthusiast, & he'll help you make a data portrait of your favorite local bird using data from eBird. All materials will be provided, & you'll wrap up right as the happy hour begins.nPick Your Ticket:nHappy Hour Only: The main event, 2 to 4 on the water. Ferry over whenever works for you.nHappy Hour + Volunteer: The volunteer session, then straight into the happy hour. Starts with a 9:15am ferry & wraps at 2:30. Spots are limited, & we'll follow up with details.nHappy Hour + Workshop: Bird Data Portraits with Jer Thorp from 1 to 2, then straight into the happy hour. Materials provided, spots are limited.nWho Should Come:nIf you work in civic & urban tech, or anywhere adjacent, you belong here. Whether you've been to every happy hour or never made it to one, a Saturday afternoon on the island is a pretty great place to start. Expect good company & the kind of conversations that only happen when we get out from behind our screens.nGetting There:nGovernors Island is a short ferry ride from Lower Manhattan or Brooklyn. Suggested ferry times & a map to the exact spot on the island will be shared upon RSVP approval.nnFine print: By attending this event, you agree to abide by our code of conduct.

events.name: Business Dads
events.description: What is Business Dads?Business Dads is a curated community for fathers with young children (under 5) who are building ambitious careers in the middle of beautiful chaos. Our lives are loud. Sleep is optional. Childcare is expensive-especially in NYC. Most days feel like a sprint that starts before sunrise & ends well after bedtime. And yet. We're founders, executives, investors, operators, & sales leaders who are deeply committed to building meaningful businesses & being present dads. That shared reality, short on sleep, short on time, but long on ambition, is what makes Business Dads special. This is a room for men who want to grow professionally, support one another practically, & model what purposeful work looks like for the little humans watching us every day (even when they're screaming at 3am).
