events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Are AI Datacenters A Threat To Our Clean Energy Future
events.description: NOTE: Registration is REQUIRED. Join Pratt Institute's Sustainable Environmental Systems program for our third annual just energy transition event during NYC Climate Week. Global & local experts will join in conversation across just energy challenges, solutions, & perspectives with a particular focus on the rapid expansion of energy-hungry datacenters powering artificial intelligence (AI).  Experts working on local & global energy issues will come together to discuss new policy dynamics, systemic & historic barriers in realizing a true Just Transition, & how these new datacenters could get us off track. This timely discussion will happen during the UN General Assembly & NYC Climate Week 2026, where key climate & energy transition issues will be at the center of next steps for the sustainable development goals & the broader theme of this year's Climate Week. Key themes of the conversation will include: decarbonization, climate finance, climate diplomacy, infrastructure, the path to net zero, water, tech & AI, incentives for transition, green economy, & the SDGs.   The panel will be feature local & global perspectives in a conversation moderated by a recent Pratt SES alumna, Jen Hung: Panelists:  Martha Molfetas | Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute; Senior Policy Consultant & Writer: Martha Molfetas is a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Environmental Economics. Martha is a senior climate & energy policy consultant, writer, & strategist with over 17-years of experience helping NGOs, think tanks, & businesses unpack climate, environmental justice, resource conflict, sustainable development, & global policy issues with organizations ranging from Dalberg Research to Transparency International, NRGI & Oil Change International to name a few. She was formerly a Senior Fellow working on just energy transition at New America. Her work has been published in: Current Affairs, The World Politics Review, The Global Policy Journal, Policy Mic, Common Dreams, & others. Summer Sandoval | Academic Coordinator, Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute & Community Investment & Implementation Director, USDN: Summer Sandoval is the Community Investment & Implementation Director at Urban Sustainability Directors Network (USDN), where she supports local governments & communities in navigating funding opportunities & realizing their projects to advance equitable climate action. Summer is also the Academic Coordinator & a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Urban Energy Management. Summer has worked at the intersection of climate, environmental, & energy justice in community-based organizations & city government.   Rami Dinnawi | Program Director, North Star Fund: Rami Dinnawi is a Lebanese/Palestinian grassroots activist based in New York City. Informed by generational knowledge of people's struggle for self-determination, Rami strives to ground his work within these historical legacies. He is currently serving as the NYC Program Director at North Star Fund. Prior to joining North Star Fund, Rami worked extensively in the New York environmental justice movement space, as the environmental justice campaign & policy manager at El Puente. Rami is currently serving on the Advisory Committee of the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School. With over a decade of organizing experience, Rami's commitment extends beyond borders, as he actively engages with activism & movements on a global scale. Pierre Canet | Global Head of Public Affairs & Policy, Client Earth: Pierre leads ClientEarth's Global Public Affairs & Policy team, overseeing the organisation's influence on decision-makers to achieve the systems change pursued in its strategy across the world. Before joining ClientEarth, Pierre was the Executive Director of Advocacy at WWF in France where he worked for a decade leading campaigns & programs on a diversity of environmental issues, from climate & energy to nature & plastics, collaborating at multiple levels throughout the WWF's global network. Prior to this, Pierre worked with the United Nations in New York on the preparation of the Rio+20 Summit & corporate climate engagement. He engaged significantly with activities around the Climate COP21 to influence the establishment of the Paris Agreement, & has substantial experience in building & developing high-impact activities from newly-established teams.

events.name: Race To Recover America's Critical Minerals - When Startups & Industry Team Up
events.description: The US imports the vast majority of the critical minerals that power its defense, aerospace, & semiconductor industries - but a meaningful share of what it needs may already be sitting in waste piles at the industrial sites that exist today. Join KOMPAS VC, SOSV, & At One Ventures for a breakfast conversation on what it actually takes to turn that waste into supply - & why the answer increasingly runs through a corporate partnership between a deep-tech innovator & an industrial incumbent, scaling proven technology beyond the pilot stage, not one company going it alone. We'll hear directly from Helios & Atalco, a live example of how corporate partnerships move promising technology from pilot to commercial scale, on infrastructure that already exists. Expect a short, focused fireside chat, brief perspectives from our venture partners, & plenty of time to connect over breakfast with others working at the intersection of hard tech, industrial partnerships, & the circular economy

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). ExOIS is a not-for-profit, non-commercial consortium housed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, dedicated to advancing responsible research on ocean iron fertilization as a method of marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR). Learn more: https://oceaniron.org/ Registration approvals will begin in late August.

events.name: Make It In Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest
events.description: Join us during NYC Climate Week for the Make It in Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest, where five early-stage climate technology startups will compete for up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support. Founders will be evaluated on innovation, feasibility, market potential, & potential impact. The winning startup will receive up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support to help accelerate its path to market. The prize includes: $5,000 in unrestricted prize funding from Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Up to an additional $5,000 in milestone-based commercialization support through National Grid's Clean Tech Incubation Program. Eligible expenses include prototype development & testing, patent & legal filing costs, market research, commercialization activities, & pilot implementation support. The Climate Tech Pitch Contest brings together founders, investors, industry leaders, & members of the innovation ecosystem to spotlight technologies addressing some of today's most pressing climate challenges. Finalists: PollenPal is using AI-powered sensors & computer vision to help beekeepers monitor hive health in real time, improve colony management, & address the growing challenge of honeybee colony loss. HiFIT is advancing offshore wind through innovative weld treatment technology that strengthens turbine structures, enabling longer service life, reduced steel consumption & maintenance costs, & lower embodied carbon. Novara Tech is developing mobile recycling technology that transforms hard-to-recycle composite waste from industries like wind energy & construction into reusable materials for urban infrastructure, reducing landfill waste & transportation costs. Kyber Energy is developing AI-powered energy management software that helps commercial & industrial businesses optimize electricity use, shift demand away from peak periods, & reduce both energy costs & grid emissions. AtmosOne AI is helping address growing demand on the electric grid by intelligently shifting flexible AI computing to off-peak periods, reducing grid strain & enabling more efficient use of existing energy infrastructure. Judges will be announced soon. This event is in partnership with the Malin & National Grid. The Malin is a beautifully designed workspace for ambitious founders, creatives, & industry leaders who value genuine community over transactional co-working, & they're offering our network 25% off day passes & meeting rooms at their Brooklyn Heights location, using code DBP25 through the end of 2026, redeemable here. About Make It in Brooklyn Make It in Brooklyn is Downtown Brooklyn Partnership's innovation platform supporting startups through pitch competitions, ecosystem-building initiatives, & direct entrepreneurial support programs. Through year-round programming, Make It in Brooklyn connects founders with capital, mentors, customers, & the resources needed to grow & scale their businesses.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.name: Backing Innovation - How States Investing In The Future
events.description: State venture funds are playing an increasingly important role in building regional innovation ecosystems. This panel brings together leaders from three of the Northeast's most active public VC programs - Connecticut Innovations, New York State's NY Ventures, & the New Jersey Economic Development Authority - for a candid discussion on how government capital is shaping the next generation of startups. Panelists will discuss how their funds source & evaluate deals, what differentiates public venture capital from traditional VC, & where they see the biggest opportunities for founders & investors across the region. Stick around afterwards for a happy hour with the founders & VCs. Meet the panelists: Danny Qiao is a Director on Connecticut Innovations' investment team, where he leads the team's consumer & international investment efforts. Prior to CI, he led consumer investing at Sweater Ventures, backing brands like IQBAR, Graza, Nomadica, OROS, & Havenly. He began his career at Accenture Strategy & later covered financial sponsors & financial institutions in investment banking at BNP Paribas. Danny holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management & a BS from Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations. Jennifer Tegan is the Managing Director of Empire State Development's New York Ventures, where she oversees over $320 million in investment programs aimed at fueling New York's startup ecosystem. Since joining in 2020, she has managed direct & indirect investment funds including the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund & the Emerging & Regional Manager Partner Fund (a fund of funds). An experienced investor & advocate, Jennifer previously spent 18 years as a partner at Cayuga Venture Fund. She has served on the board of the National Venture Capital Association & held leadership roles with Tompkins Financial Corporation & the Upstate Capital Association of New York. Jennifer holds an MBA from Cornell University, an MS from the University of Cincinnati, & a BA from Smith College. John Wisniewski is the Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives & Venture Products at New Jersey Economic Development Authority. His responsibilities include oversight of the state's investment into Strategic Innovation Centers, & venture investment programs. John started his career with ExxonMobil where he held various positions developing projects in the US & internationally.  He ran a private equity infrastructure fund based in the Middle East for Arcapita Bank, & then switched to venture capital working with Clean Energy Ventures Group. John has a BS in Chemical Engineering from Cooper Union, & an MBA from Rice University. Meet the hosts: Connecticut Innovations is Connecticut's venture capital arm, investing in early & growth-stage biotech, IT, & deep tech companies. NY Ventures is New York State's innovation venture capital fund, backing high-growth startups across the state. NJEDA's Venture Products team supports New Jersey's innovation ecosystem, including through the New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. Meet the sponsors: Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups & the accountants supporting them. With banking setup in minutes, cashback cards, & tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused, backed by support that goes to the end of the earth to help you win. Rho is a fintech company, not a bank. Checking & card services are provided by Webster Bank, N.A., member FDIC; savings account services are provided by American Deposit Management Co. & its partner banks. KPMG Private provides specialized advisory, audit, tax, & strategic consulting services tailored for emerging growth companies, startups, & private enterprises scaling up through various lifecycle stages. Whether you're launching a startup or accelerating your growth, the Emerging Growth team offers strategic insights & resources designed to support your business journey. #nyc #venturecapital #government

'reverse pitches' where they will identify specific challenges & opportunity areas where they would like to see innovators focus next. Startups & leading academics will share the cutting-edge technologies they are developing & their commercial potential. Why Attend: Discover breakthrough technologies Engage directly with scientists working at the frontier of extreme heat resilience & cooling technologies Identify investment & partnership opportunities Become part of the region's growing deep tech ecosystem Run of Show: Reverse pitch presentations from industry leaders & investors Startup & researcher presentations from across Columbia, Princeton, Yale, & other leading universities Networking reception (drinks & light bites included) Extreme Heat X Technology Challenges: People & communities: Heat stress & disease, productivity, access to AC, essential services, wildfires Agriculture: Disrupted photosynthesis & pollination slashing crop yields Energy systems: Power-plant cooling constraints, declining solar output, transmission derating, transformer failures, & peak-demand blackouts Cooling & electronics: Overloaded / overheated HVAC, data-center cooling systems, telecom, electronics Transportation & supply chains: Buckling roads & rails, stressed bridges, aviation disruptions, vehicle breakdowns, cold-chain failures Water & wastewater: Pipe leakage, water-supply interruptions, failures of pumps & treatment systems Industrial operations: Machinery overheating, shortened equipment life, material expansion, product defects Big thanks to our venue sponsor, SOSV!

events.name: 35% Moment - What Will It Take To Electrify Global Economy By 2035
events.description: Electricity meets barely a fifth of the world's final energy demand today. Yet electrification is the fastest lever governments have to cut emissions, insulate households from the next fossil fuel price shock, & maintain energy security. Getting there means moving vehicles, buildings, & industry onto electrons & modernizing & expanding the power grid faster than any economy has yet managed.  With over 100 companies, the EU, UN, & more, likely to commit to electrify 35% of final energy demand by 2035, this event will ask what it takes to electrify the economy within the next decade. The countries that pull it off first won't just hit a target, they'll write the playbook everyone else has to follow. This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School & Centre for Net Zero, a nonprofit research institute founded by Octopus Energy Group. Speakers:Devrim Celal, Chief Flexibility & Marketing Officer at Kraken TechnologiesDana Guernsey, CEO & Co-Founder at Voltus Robert Metcalfe, Chief Economist at Centre for Net Zero (part of the Octopus Energy Group) & Professor at Columbia SIPAGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: Buildings & Grid - Clipping The Falcon Wing
events.description: Can buildings play a significant role in solving the crisis brewing in our power grids? Join Building Energy Exchange & the US Green Building Council (USGBC) for a moderated discussion with regulatory & industry experts exploring how building decarbonization can help address, rather than exacerbate, the current & future challenges facing our grid.   Our power grids face an array of converging & mounting challenges. After more than two decades of relatively flat consumption, the electrical grid is experiencing significant increases in demand driven by building & vehicle electrification, extreme weather events, & the rapid growth of data centers. At the same time, the transition to clean, renewable energy is creating new challenges in balancing supply & demand.   The costs to provide enough power for these increases are astronomical, & the lead-time to bring new generation online is a significant challenge. However, buildings can play a critical role in reducing the loads. By reducing overall energy use & managing peak demand, buildings can become active partners in supporting a more reliable, resilient, & decarbonized grid.  This session will explore the emerging grid issues & the various strategies-such as load shifting, peak load reduction, improved building envelopes, & geothermal-that buildings can deploy to reduce grid demand. Coffee & pastries will be served!   Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC  PresentationsZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  PanelistsRyan Dougherty, Executive Director, Geothermal Exchange OrganizationLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC - ModeratorJohn Rhodes, Chief Program Officer, NYS Department of Public ServiceZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: AI Tinkerers Demo Day w/ PostHog
events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC! Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. events.name: Building Better Trading Strategies w/ AI
events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? This Climate Week NYC event will take a clear-eyed look at the environmental case for autonomous vehicles & examine where the evidence supports the hype, & where it does not. A panel of top experts will discuss along with a Q&A session: Jeffrey Tumlin - former Exec. Director, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) David Zipper -- Contributing writer, Bloomberg City Lab; former Senior Fellow, MIT Mobility Initiative Rachel Weinberger -- Vice President, Transportation & Peter W. Herman Chair, Regional Planning Association Jeral Poskey - Founder, Swyft Cities; former project executive for transportation planning, Google Format: Panel Discussion followed by Q&A The discussion will explore the complicated relationship between automation, mobility, & sustainability. Rather than assuming new technology automatically leads to better outcomes, the discussion will focus on the many potential impacts: energy use, induced demand, land use, transit interactions, fleet models, & the difference between theoretical efficiency & actual environmental performance. Join us for a timely discussion on climate & the future of urban mobility.

events.name: Governing Wealth Transfer - Turning AI Tech Billions Into Climate Reparations
events.description: Interrogate, reimagine, & practice new models for resource governance. Date & Time: September 24th, 4:00 PM - 6:00 PM Location: The New School - Additional Event Details will be sent out in a follow up email.  Implementing effective climate solutions requires a fundamental shift in how resources are distributed. Data centers & the rise of technology not only impact the ecological & social health of our communities, the massive influx of AI & tech wealth is reshaping philanthropy. It is clear that while financial resources exist, the global systems at hand lack the accountable & moral capacity to implement justly. In this dialogue across speakers with different perspectives, we will explore how to direct this next wave of capital including a look into our solution for moving tech billions toward climate reparations.  This is a critical moment for frontline communities to intervene & pivot tech wealth toward the resources we all need to live, rest, & thrive in the places we love. We invite you to learn how Taproot Earth is building a durable alternative of climate finance, rooted in self-determination & collective decision-making, where communities determine how these funds protect, repair, & steward our water, energy, & land. Refreshments to follow. Registration is required & will close Monday 9/21.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: Rethink Waste, Reduce Emissions & Unlock Value
events.description: The Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House invite you to a reception & conversation on global circularity. Resource scarcity, shifting global supply chains, & climate change are reshaping the landscape for businesses, governments, & communities. We need solutions that create economic value for businesses & individuals while advancing climate goals. One place to look for these solutions is in our waste. The Circularity Gap Report estimates that roughly 25.4 trillion in economic value is lost globally each year through linear take-make-waste practices. This Value Gap represents 31% of global GDP, meaning that for every 3 of economic value created worldwide, about 1 is lost. Increasing circularity, which simply means keeping materials in use for as long as possible, could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 39%. Circularity is not only good for the bottom line & the environment, but can also improve quality of life through more durable products, greater affordability, & connected communities. If the benefits are so clear, what will it take to scale circularity? How do we align businesses, governments, & communities around a shared path forward? To kick off Climate Week NYC, Scandinavia House is pleased to partner with Columbia Climate School for a conversation on the promise of a circular economy. Join leaders from the public & private sectors as they explore practical solutions & emerging innovations, lessons learned from Nordic leadership, & the challenges that remain. The program will conclude with a special announcement from Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, followed by a reception to connect & continue the conversation. Alexis Abramson - Opening RemarksDean & Professor, Columbia Climate School Sandra Goldmark - ModeratorProfessor of Professional Practice in the Faculty of Climate, Columbia Climate School Anu MntySenior Lead, International Programs, Sitra John MuirHead of USA, 3stepIT Miia RantanenConsul General of Finland in New York Presented By: Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House Please note, this program is a private event. If you would like to share this invitation, or if you have general questions, please contact development@climate.columbia.edu. Registration is required.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Decarbonizing Everyday Life
events.description: Fossil fuels are all around us, & not just when it comes to transport & electricity. In your closet, your kitchen, your medicine cabinet, even your walls, petroleum products are hiding in plain sight. Our daily lives are built on embodied carbon in the most literal sense. And unlike metal, glass, or plant-based materials, they return cleanly to neither industry nor the earth. They degrade, but never disappear. Decarbonization is about more than renewable energy. It means remaking the stuff of our everyday lives, & with it the supply chains, design decisions, & consumer habits that put that stuff in our hands. This conversation brings together materials innovators, designers, & industry experts working on sustainable alternatives, from new recycling technologies to bio-based alternatives for petroleum-derived textiles, packing materials, & cosmetics. Together they will explore the innovations that could help us move past plastic, & how we can get those sustainable materials out of the lab & into our homes. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.description: From Possibility to Practice: Advancing Climate Solutions in a Changing WorldFeaturing Eliza Barclay, The New York Times, & Joel Makower, TrellisThursday, September 24, 2026Climate Week NYC As part of Climate Week NYC, UC Berkeley's Master of Climate Solutions will convene a curated group of climate practitioners, alumni, & members of the broader Berkeley community for an invitation-only roundtable lunch. The gathering will open with remarks from Joel Makower of Trellis, a UC Berkeley alumnus & member of the Master of Climate Solutions Advisory Board. Joel will then join fellow UC Berkeley alumna Eliza Barclay of The New York Times for a candid conversation about what they are seeing from the front lines of climate journalism, business, science, health, & the environment. Together, Barclay & Makower will explore how the climate story is changing, where meaningful progress is taking hold, where momentum remains constrained, & which developments deserve greater attention. Their exchange will then open into a facilitated roundtable conversation. Participants will bring their own experiences & perspectives to a shared discussion about what it takes to move climate solutions from possibility to practice within complex & rapidly changing real-world systems. The program will conclude with reflections from Kat Hunt, drawing on her experience addressing the MCS graduating class & her perspective on the next generation of climate leadership. Designed as a working conversation rather than a traditional panel, the lunch will create space for candid exchange, practical insight, & meaningful connections among leaders working across sectors & disciplines. Attendance is limited to 25 guests & is by invitation. Advance registration is required. Additional details will be shared with confirmed participants.

events.name: From Framework To Front Line - Advancing Housing Resilience & Affordability
events.description: RPA & Enterprise explore using policy & partnerships to protect affordable homes, accelerate recovery & strengthen communities. Climate-driven disasters are placing growing pressure on an already constrained housing supply, threatening existing homes, increasing costs for residents & housing providers, & making it more difficult for communities to meet urgent affordability needs. As municipalities grapple with the need to build more resilient communities able to withstand extreme weather events, the critical question is how policymakers, planners, & housing experts can translate ambitious blueprints into effective, local action. This panel will bring together Regional Plan Association (RPA) & Enterprise Community Partners to examine the policies, planning decisions, & implementation strategies needed to protect existing housing & accelerate recovery. Drawing from national standards & regional planning frameworks, panelists will examine the challenges communities & housing providers face, & highlight the resources & partnerships needed to address the intersecting climate & housing crisis. Enterprise Community Partners will draw on insights from its Climate Resilience Academies to highlight the challenges affordable housing owners, operators, & developers face in preparing their portfolios for climate risks while safeguarding residents. Through its work with more than 150 participants across U.S. regions, Enterprise has seen that housing providers increasingly understand the urgency of resilience but often lack the staff capacity, funding, technical expertise, & region-specific guidance needed to act. Enterprise will discuss opportunities to close these gaps to further help housing providers move from awareness to implementation.Regional Plan Association will draw from its Averting Crisis report & subsequent work with communities in the New York metropolitan region to examine how housing growth & climate resilience can be advanced together. RPA will share real-time lessons being learned about effective ways to move from high-altitude planning to on-the-ground implementation, highlighting its work with local governments, community organizations, & neighborhood stakeholders in seven communities across Queens, Westchester, & Long Island. The work will result in local actions that affect zoning changes, land-use reform, investments & complementary policies to align housing growth with climate risk & capacity. These organizations will offer expertise on climate readiness & disaster response, connecting federal & local policy to on-the-ground implementation to make communities more resilient amid the growing housing affordability crisis.

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Powering The AI Build-Out - India's Data Center Energy Demand Surge
events.description: CleanMax invites you to a moderated panel bringing together hyperscalers, independent power producers & other market participants to examine how India's rapidly scaling data-centre sector will meet its power demand-and what role renewable energy, storage & firm-power structures need to play in getting there. What the panel will explore  The scale & geography of India's data-centre power demand-and what a realistic, bankable renewable-energy pipeline could look like through 2030.  Whether renewables & storage can deliver 24/7, high-reliability power at a viable cost, & where grid, transmission, land & infrastructure constraints could limit new capacity.  How hyperscalers & power producers are structuring supply-from physical & group-captive arrangements to VPPAs & CFDs-and which models are becoming genuinely bankable.  The broader policy & regulatory clarity needed to accelerate investment & give developers, buyers & financiers confidence in long-term delivery.  How data-centre growth can earn community acceptance & support sustainable development through transparent engagement & meaningful local benefits around land, water, infrastructure & livelihoods. Warm regards, CleanMax Team

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.name: Convening The Next-Generation Materials Transition
events.description: The future of fashion depends on bringing next-generation materials to scale. While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. As one of the world's largest platforms for climate collaboration, it creates the ideal environment to build the relationships & shared understanding needed to move promising innovations beyond pilots & into practice. The Forum contributes to that momentum by connecting the people who can help shape the future of next-generation materials. Forum Partners Developed with & featuring voices from: Eco-Age - a purpose-led media & communications agency accelerating the fashion industry's transition to sustainability. Canopy - an award-winning environmental non-profit driving the shift to next-generation, forest-free fibres. Fashion for Good - the global platform for sustainable fashion innovation, connecting brands & innovators to scale breakthrough solutions. Material ConneXion - the world's leading materials insights company, connecting industries to the most innovative & sustainable materials available. Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) - New York's internationally renowned college for fashion, design, business & technology, fostering innovation, education & industry collaboration across the global fashion & textile sector. The Programme The Forum combines a keynote, structured workshops, & a networking reception. Through an invitation-based format & curated audience, participants will explore the opportunities & challenges shaping the next chapter of material innovation. The programme, speakers, & venue are currently being developed with our partners & will be announced in the coming weeks. Who Should Attend The Forum is designed for senior leaders in sustainability, sourcing, supply chain, & procurement across the fashion, apparel, & textile industry. It is built for the people inside the industry who are responsible for what gets made, how it is sourced, & what it is made from. Event Details 22 September 20263:30 PM - 7:30 PMFashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York City Pre-register now for priority access & programme updates. Registration is open but subject to review. We reserve the right to cancel registrations from organisations outside this scope. We look forward to seeing you there.

events.name: PMAI Fight Right - Co-Founders Guide To Disagreement
events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

The firm represents emerging companies, venture investors & limited partners across all stages of investment, in seed financings, growth rounds, mergers & acquisitions & exit transactions. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? events.description: From simple greenhouses to botanic facilities, & from data centers to automated interiors, never before in history has architecture produced so many interiors for the non-human, challenging disciplinary notions on tectonics, light, comfort & entire regulatory frameworks. Once designed for & with the human, contemporary interiors have instead become exponentially complex materializations where the politics of our present moment are played out. Ultimately, who are they for? Interior Ecologies is a critical framework developed within the Master of Arts in Interior Architecture (MAIA) program at Geneva School of Art & Design (HEAD - Genve). It examines how interior architecture engages with climate change, resource circulation & multispecies coexistence alongside posthuman & more-than-human design perspectives. Rather than treating interiors as autonomous spaces, it calls on us to rethink them as complex ecologies in which human & nonhuman actors are entangled across broader planetary scales. This roundtable brings together voices from HEAD - Genve, MoMA, & Columbia GSAPP to reflect on how interior architecture can contribute to new ecological approaches to design, research, & professional practice. The event will also include a presentation of the scenographic installation developed by MAIA for Assembly, the Swiss presence at Climate Week NYC. Employing scaffolding & dismantlable systems as an embodiment of circular architecture, the installation demonstrates principles of reuse, adaptability, & reversibility, staking its claim as an active ecological agent within the space. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Accommodating Growth In The Global South
events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. Once made, these decisions produce long-lasting impacts for climate, accessibility, & economies. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. Speakers: Robin King (Moderator), Director, Knowledge Capture & Collaboration, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella  Cynthia Goytia, Head of the Master of Science in Urban Economics Program, WRI  Solly Angel, Professor of City Planning, NYU Marron  Samhita Shiledar, Principal, RMI  Adriana Akers, Senior Project Manager, Gehl This session is hosted by Gehl, the NYU Marron Institute, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: Catalyzing Cities
events.description: Cities are increasingly expected to deliver climate resilience while navigating constrained budgets, aging infrastructure, & growing complexity. Yet many of the most impactful solutions already exist... the challenge is designing financing & partnership models that enable them to scale. This New York Climate Week, join Cool Climate Collective & Climate Vine, as we convene investors, city leaders, philanthropies & ecosystem partners for a discussion on how innovative financing structures & public-private collaboration can unlock catalytic outcomes for cities, particularly for New York. Drawing on emerging work in city outcomes & practical examples from around the world, we'll explore: New models for financing climate resilience beyond traditional procurement. How blended capital & partnership design can accelerate deployment. What is already working in practice & why. Lessons & systems insights informed by collaborators across the resilience ecosystem, including perspectives shared by our partners from UNDRR & Dark Matter Labs. The session is designed to be interactive, bringing together practitioners across sectors to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions, & identify opportunities for collaboration during Climate Week. Agenda 9:30 - 10:00 AM : Check-in & coffee networking 10:00 - 11:30 AM : Interactive discussion & programming 11:30 AM - 12:30 PM : Facilitated small-group discussions followed by open networking

events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. For more information, please visit the Queens AI website.
