events.name: Carbon Newbie Summit
events.description: The Carbon Newbie Summit is back for its 6th edition!  What can whales teach us about economics? How is AI transforming the way buildings use energy? And how are global investors & insurers preparing for a changing climate? Hear fresh perspectives from senior leaders at Mubadala Investment Company, London Stock Exchange Group, Trane Technologies, ServiceNow, American Family Insurance, BrainBox AI & more-alongside renowned scientists, entrepreneurs & changemakers from Columbia Climate School, the University of Toronto, Rutgers University & the Clean Air Task Force. We'll explore everything from AI & decarbonization to living nature, carbon credits, climate risk, microplastics, geothermal energy & sustainable finance-all through lively, accessible conversations designed for curious minds. Whether you're completely new to climate or already working in the field, you'll leave with fresh ideas, practical insights & plenty to talk about. No climate experience necessary-just bring your curiosity! Meet our incredible speakers on the Carbon Newbie Summit website. Light breakfast & full lunch will be served  CO-HOSTSCNaughtDebevoise & PlimptonTrane TechnologiesUniversity of Toronto - Lawson Climate InstituteClever Carbon The Carbon Newbie Summit is an initiative of Clever Carbon.  LIVESTREAMING AVAILABLE - register for the livestream ticket to receive details Who should attend?From climate experts to professionals new to sustainability & climate, our Summit welcomes anyone curious & passionate about climate. By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with our co-hosts/sponsors. About CNaught:Trusted by buyers like Asana, Medium, & Tiger Global, CNaught makes it easy to drive real climate impact through high-quality carbon credit portfolios. We deliver access to sophisticated buying strategies, previously available only to the largest buyers, enabling companies of any size to take meaningful climate action. Learn more: https://www.cnaught.com/ About Debevoise & Plimpton:Debevoise & Plimpton LLP is a premier law firm with market-leading practices, a global perspective & strong New York roots. Our clients look to us to bring a distinctively high degree of quality, intensity & creativity to resolve legal challenges effectively & cost efficiently. We have particularly deep experience in the broad range of issues that arise as environmental, social & governance (ESG) concerns & requirements become increasingly important. The firm brings together sophisticated, multidisciplinary & multinational teams to provide tailored & practical guidance across the evolving ESG & business integrity spectrum by counseling on trends & prudential issues, delivering concrete legal advice on evolving sustainability regulations & policies, & helping clients prepare for the legal, financial & reputational risks arising in this rapidly changing landscape. Learn more: https://www.debevoise.com/ About Trane Technologies:Trane Technologies is a global climate innovator. Through our strategic brands Trane & Thermo King, & our portfolio of environmentally responsible products & services, we bring efficient & sustainable climate solutions to buildings, homes & transportation.https://tranetechnologies.com About University of Toronto - Lawson Climate Institute:Through a multidisciplinary approach, the Lawson Climate Institute is ramping up U of T's capacity to advance the technologies & policies needed for Canada to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. As one of U of T's most wide-ranging, comprehensive initiatives, the institute is unique in its aim to ensure students in every discipline across three campuses have an opportunity to gain the tools needed to take concrete steps toward implementing practical climate solutions. The institute is named in honour of Brian Lawson & Joannah Lawson in recognition of their transformative $60-million donation to help establish the institute.https://lci.utoronto.ca About Clever Carbon:At Clever Carbon, we teach people about carbon footprint in a hip & fun way! From content creation to carbon footprint workshops, we work with leading brands around the world to help raise carbon literacy because what gets measured gets changed! Learn more: https://clevercarbon.io/

It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Stripe is a technology company that builds economic infrastructure for the internet. Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people.RSVP here: https://nyc.aitinkerers.org/p/september-demo-day-ft-posthog-verWhat is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If youre deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community.Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions. Read more in the FAQSome slots still available, submit your demo!  Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? This is your moment to share with like-minded AI tinkerers!A demo is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!) FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy!Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI TinkerersPlease note that capacity is limited, so well prioritize those who are able to present a demo.Demo vibes Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:00 Networking & pizzas9:00 Doors CloseMore informationIf you are new to AI Tinkerers, please read the AI Tinkerers FAQ & join our Discord channel: https://discord.gg/8WsqnC6Hk3SponsorsPostHogPostHog is an all-in-one product OS designed for engineers, offering product analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, & surveys in a single platform. Veris sandbox is pre-loaded with test scenarios, simulated tools, & personas. Using the sandbox, you can run thousands of simulated interactions across routine workflows, challenging edge cases, & adversarial scenarios. Veris AI creates root-cause analysis reports, regression testing gates, & prompt or RL optimization loops to improve the agent using these interactions before the agent touches the first real system or customer.CopilotKitCopilotKit is an open-source framework for building AI copilots & agent-native experiences directly into your app. It gives you React components & hooks for in-app chat, generative UI, & shared state between your frontend & agents, & it works with agent frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, & Mastra through the AG-UI protocol. Ship agents that live inside the product instead of beside it.TavilyTavily is a search engine built for AI agents. Its API returns real-time, source-cited web results & page extracts optimized for LLM context, so agents & RAG pipelines can ground answers in current information with a single call. Tavily powers research agents, assistants, & data pipelines for teams that need reliable web access without scraping infrastructure.Start building now!Were bringing a builder-first lineup of demos & giving the community a space to share work in progress, trade notes, & meet other serious practitioners.

events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. Over Greentown's 15-year history, the organization has supported 700+ startups that have gone on to raise $15B+ & create 16,000+ jobs. Greentown has hubs in Somerville & Houston, so while most of our members are based in Massachusetts or Texas, our membership is growing beyond these two states, & we intend to double down on that growth. New York's climate & energy ecosystem, with some of the country's most ambitious climate policy, deepest capital markets, & strongest research institutions, is a critical part of where we see Greentown's impact growing next, & this event is one step toward building deeper roots here. Please join the Greentown leadership team to discuss how we can collectively shape the future of climate & energy innovation in New York & Massachusetts - we want to hear from you! You'll be joined by climate & energy leaders from the investment community, large corporates, government, foundations, academia, & the startup community itself, from the Northeast & beyond. Space is limited to keep the conversation intimate, so we hope you'll RSVP soon. Potential topics of discussion include: Seeding & sourcing innovation: How Massachusetts' & New York's university & research ecosystems can learn from each other to build a stronger, more connected pipeline from lab to startup Bridging the Second Valley of Death: How public dollars (through NYSERDA & MassCEC) & private capital across both states can help the most promising climate & energy companies scale from prototype to commercial pilot Keeping manufacturing in the Northeast: How Massachusetts & New York can work together, through shared infrastructure or incentives, to keep growing manufacturers here instead of losing them to other regions Lunch will be provided. events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: AI, Energy, Fight for Democracy & A Healthy, Affordable Future
events.description: Tishman AuditoriumClimate Week 2026 Keynote Event at The New School   We are excited to share that this vital conversation convenes a powerhouse lineup of community leaders, mayors, scientists, researchers, & journalists. Across three dynamic panel conversations, we'll examine the collision of technology, energy, & democracy; the rapid expansion of AI data centers; the legacy of nuclear weapons; the toll of these developments on Indigenous communities, communities of color, & rural areas; & the affordability crisis & what it will take for everyday people to build power & shape real solutions.    Together, these conversations connect today's most pressing challenges to a larger question: How do communities organize & build power within democratic structures when government & industry leave them behind?   AI's Hidden Toll   LaTricea AdamsPresident & CEO, Young, Gifted & Green, Memphis   Manish BapnaPresident & CEO, Natural Resources Defense Council, Washington, DC   Mayor Kate GallegoCity of Phoenix   Adam Mahoney (Moderator)National Climate & Environment Reporter, Capital B News, New Orleans   Nuclear Legacy: Mapping Local Impacts   Lilly AdamsCo-Creator, US Nuclear Impacts Map, Brooklyn, New York   Moeka De OroCo-Executive Director, Micronesia Climate Change Alliance, Guam/Guhan   Leona Morgan (Din)Indigenous Community Organizer & Anti-Nuclear Activist, Din No Nukes, Albuquerque, New Mexico   Sharon Weinberger (Moderator)Editor-in-Chief, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Washington, DC   Power in Our Hands: Solutions for an Affordable, Just Future   Dr. Ana Isabel BaptistaAssociate Professor of Environmental & Climate Justice at the Parsons School of Design & Director, Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, New York   Dr. Gretchen GoldmanPresident & CEO, Union of Concerned Scientists, Washington, DC   Bill McKibbenAuthor, Educator, Activist, & Founder, Third Act & 350.org, Vermont   Mayor Michelle WuCity of Boston Garrison Hayes (Moderator)Correspondent,  Mother Jones, Nashville This event is presented by the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, in collaboration with Climate Desk Live partners Mother Jones, Capital B News, & the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists. This event is free & open to the public. events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.

events.name: Visualizing Climate Worlds - Data, AI & Immersive Futures
events.description: Thanks to a proliferation of climate data, processed & interpreted with AI tools & new visualization methods, we can recognize new patterns in our relationship with our cities & our planet, predict extreme events or future hazards, & inform the hard work of climate adaptation & mitigation. Visualizing Climate Worlds brings together three projects that turn data into new ways of seeing - & living in - a changing planet. The Better Planet Laboratory at CU Boulder uses satellite data, sensors, & AI to monitor global food & environmental systems, transforming planetary-scale information into early-warning & decision tools for a more resilient, equitable future. MIT's Urban Metabolism Environmental Research & Action Lab (UMERA) applies Material Flow Analysis & machine learning to 11,000+ cities worldwide, surfacing productive & sometimes unexpected climate sister-city networks & modeling how they converge on unique sustainability paths to 2050. And BEAM Studio's TIDELANDS 2100 draws on NOAA flood models & the oral histories of Rhode Island's coastal residents to build immersive VR worlds of adaptation in place. Together they move from planetary monitoring to urban comparison to lived experience, asking: once we can model & see a changing planet, how do we choose to live in it? More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Interior Ecologies
events.description: From simple greenhouses to botanic facilities, & from data centers to automated interiors, never before in history has architecture produced so many interiors for the non-human, challenging disciplinary notions on tectonics, light, comfort & entire regulatory frameworks. Once designed for & with the human, contemporary interiors have instead become exponentially complex materializations where the politics of our present moment are played out. Ultimately, who are they for? Interior Ecologies is a critical framework developed within the Master of Arts in Interior Architecture (MAIA) program at Geneva School of Art & Design (HEAD - Genve). It examines how interior architecture engages with climate change, resource circulation & multispecies coexistence alongside posthuman & more-than-human design perspectives. Rather than treating interiors as autonomous spaces, it calls on us to rethink them as complex ecologies in which human & nonhuman actors are entangled across broader planetary scales. This roundtable brings together voices from HEAD - Genve, MoMA, & Columbia GSAPP to reflect on how interior architecture can contribute to new ecological approaches to design, research, & professional practice. The event will also include a presentation of the scenographic installation developed by MAIA for Assembly, the Swiss presence at Climate Week NYC. Employing scaffolding & dismantlable systems as an embodiment of circular architecture, the installation demonstrates principles of reuse, adaptability, & reversibility, staking its claim as an active ecological agent within the space. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.

events.name: Industrial Decarbonization & Urban Resilience
events.description: Heat waves, domestic supply chains, data centers, & rising energy costs dominate headlines in 2026. While the challenges might seem distinct - many of the solutions are interdependent & already being deployed today. During NYC Climate Week, Suffolk Technologies, Morrison Foerster & Climate Salon are teaming up to discuss: How do we decarbonize our infrastructure while building for resiliency? We'll start with a panel to hear from experts working on solutions to address some of our biggest challenges, & then ask you for your ideas during roundtable discussions. Join us to tackle: Data Center Decarbonization Clean Manufacturing Gridtech Urban Resilience Financing Urban Pilots   Suffolk Technologies is a venture capital platform funding the next generation of companies solving built environment challenges. Suffolk Technologies invests in early & growth-stage startups transforming the built world across real estate & development, architecture, engineering & construction, property management, & smart cities. Leveraging Suffolk's expertise & broad network of industry leaders, Suffolk Technologies partners with visionary founders to accelerate industry-wide adoption of breakthrough innovations ranging from pre-product to growth stages. For more information about Suffolk Technologies' strategy & investments, visit SuffolkTech.com. Climate Salon is a 501c3 nonprofit organization focused on bringing stakeholders together to solve climate challenges. Through educational events, its network of support organizations, & charitable giving, Climate Salon accelerates community action to bring ideas to life. Morrison Foerster (MoFo) is a global law firm with 19 offices across the U.S., Europe, & Asia. Our comprehensive platform includes an award-winning Emerging Companies + Venture Capital (ECVC) practice that combines a deep understanding of market conditions with tailored legal strategies. We advise more than 1,700 entrepreneurs, founders, & venture investors, partnering with clients at every stage of the business lifecycle - from initial formation & financings, through late-stage financings & investments, mergers & acquisitions, & public offerings. In just the last five years, we have guided our clients through venture capital financings totaling over $110 billion & mergers & acquisitions with an aggregate transactional value exceeding $850 billion. Peter Fusco is a partner in the New York office & serves as co-head of the firm's Emerging Companies + Venture Capital Practice. He represents venture funds & tech companies throughout their lifecycle, from pre-incorporation planning to angel, seed, & growth rounds to exit transactions. Pete has been representing tech companies for more than two decades in the New York ecosystem & serves as outside general counsel to many startups, growth-stage companies, & venture funds. He also works closely with NYU/Tandon Future Lab's incubator ecosystem & its related programs. Pete looks forward to working with the Suffolk Technologies & Climate Salon communities to explore collaboration & provide practical legal guidance to support your businesses. If you'd like to connect, he can be reached directly at pfusco@mofo.com

events.name: Building Better Trading Strategies w/ AI
events.description: Everyone is talking about using AI to build trading strategies. Few people are talking about how to determine whether those strategies actually work.  There's no question that AI is transforming quantitative finance. What once required a team of quantitative analysts & developers can now be accelerated with AI, but identifying strategies that survive real market conditions still requires expertise, rigorous testing, & disciplined research.  Join the team behind AI Velocity Trading for a behind-the-scenes look at how we use AI to research, test, & validate systematic options strategies.  We'll walk through our complete workflow, from idea generation & statistical validation to backtesting, paper trading, & ongoing performance analysis to show how our research has become a growing library of professionally tested strategies available through AI Velocity Trading.  Rather than spending months building infrastructure or testing ideas from scratch, users can explore, paper trade, & implement quantitatively researched strategies with a single click, all while understanding the methodology behind each one.  Whether you're an engineer, founder, investor, or trader, you'll get an inside look at how AI is changing quantitative research & how AI Velocity Trading combines AI, data, & quantitative expertise to turn research into deployable trading strategies. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Grids In Transition
events.description: The US power sector is entering a complex new phase driven by rapidly expanding electricity demand. While generation capacity is growing, the critical challenge is delivering clean, reliable, & affordable power to homes, businesses, & industry. This transformation is uniquely defined by surging electrification, the rise of AI & large data centers, the growth of distributed energy resources, & expanding heavy industry loads-creating unprecedented stress on the power grid.  America's goals for energy security, economic growth, & industrial competitiveness rely as much on grid modernization as they do on expanding generation. Grid capacity now often dictates where new generation projects & data centers are located, & how quickly electrification can scale across transportation, buildings, & manufacturing. If the grids are not strengthened faster, progress will slow down, costs will rise, congestion & reliability problems will increase, & economic opportunities could be lost.  Originally built for a different era, the US transmission & distribution networks are now operating near their limits, facing challenges including integration of renewables, bidirectional power flows, rising peak demand, declining system inertia, & increasing climate & cybersecurity risks. Grids must evolve from passive infrastructure into an intelligent, dynamic system that manages flexibility, resilience, & reliability in real time.  Meeting this moment requires urgent expansion & modernization of the power grids-a priority reinforced by the U.S. Department of Energy's Speed to Power initiative to accelerate critical grid infrastructure. With record investments underway, electricity grids must transform to support growing demand, manage emerging risks, & integrate varied generation resources more effectively.  However, grid transformation is complex, requiring close coordination among federal & state regulators, regional transmission organizations, utilities, technology providers, investors, & communities. No single policy, market mechanism, or technology can deliver this transition alone.  In this context, Global Transmission is organizing a conference on Grids in Transition - US on September 24, 2026, in New York City. This conference will place grids at the center of the conversation about the future of the US electricity industry, bringing together policymakers, regulators, system operators, utilities, technology leaders, & investors to examine how the grid must evolve to support the nation's rapidly changing power system.  Building on the success of our past grid & electrification events, this conference will provide a timely opportunity to discuss the challenges, trade-offs, & solutions needed for developing the electricity networks of the future. This event will offer vital insights & collaboration opportunities on the transformative role of grids in the American energy landscape.

events.name: Scaling Global Climate Solns Thru Culture & Heritage
events.description: Climate Week NYC: Learn how the UNFCCC Plan to Accelerate Solutions is advancing heritage-informed decarbonization.  Heritage-informed decarbonization applies the wisdom, places, & practices of the past to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in the present & future. It safeguards & generates cultural value-the shared practices & identities that connect people to each other. Heritage-informed decarbonization solutions include the use of traditional, repairable, low-carbon materials; materials salvage & reuse; heating, cooling, & ventilation strategies; climate-responsive design features; occupant behaviors; urban planning practices; cultural practices & relationships; & the recovery, restoration, & transmission of knowledge. Through its Action Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has recognized the Plan to Accelerate Heritage-Informed Building Decarbonization as a framework to scale these proven solutions through policy. This gathering at Climate Week NYC brings together community leaders, policymakers, heritage & built environment practitioners to learn more about the role of culture & cultural heritage in global climate action. Convened by the Climate Heritage Network, Cornell Atkinson Center for Sustainability, Gensler Family AAP NYC Center, ICOMOS, ICLEI, World Monuments Fund, & Architecture 2030, panelists will focus on what steps are needed to strengthen policymakers' capacity to integrate heritage solutions into climate change mitigation policies in the building & construction sector by 2030. Participants will learn about synergies with policy efforts prioritizing whole-life carbon reductions, energy efficiency, & materials circularity, & the coalition's immediate goals for COP 31 & beyond. FEATURED SPEAKERS:   Billie Faircloth, FAIA, LEED BD+C, Cornell Atkinson Center Scholar & Associate Professor, Cofounder of Built Buildings Lab Billie Faircloth, FAIA, is a design leader who has transformed practice-based research & earned a national & international reputation for demonstrating its value, methods, & outcomes. As partner & research director at the Philadelphia-based architectural practice KieranTimberlake from 2008-24, Faircloth led the firm's Research Group, a transdisciplinary team recognized for applying research, design, & problem-solving processes from fields as diverse as environmental management, industrial ecology, chemical physics, materials science, & sculpture. Her central message: inquiry is a newfound form of professional agency & a driver for practice transformation. Andrew Potts, Preserving Legacies Director of Policy & Partnerships Andrew Potts is the Director of Policy & Partnerships for the National Geographic Society-funded Preserving Legacies project. His work includes supporting Heritage Adapts! A campaign that aims to help thousands of heritage sites & cultural practices implement locally led climate adaptation actions by 2030 in alignment with the UN Global Goal on Adaptation's cultural heritage target. Potts also serves as Heritage & Climate Action Adviser to Europa Nostra & is a member of the ICOMOS Climate Action Working Group. In his native United States, Potts served on the Expert Advisory Committee for the US Advisory Council on Historic Preservation during the administration of former President Joseph R. Biden. A policy & finance for development (FfD) lawyer, he has focused on cultural & climate change policy since 2015. Lori Ferriss, Built Buildings Lab Co-founder & Executive Director Lori Ferriss, AIA, PE, LEED AP BD+C, is Co-founder & Executive Director of Built Buildings Lab & an internationally recognized expert on leveraging existing & historic buildings for equitable climate change mitigation & adaptation. An award-winning architect & structural engineer, her work aims to elevate the environmental, cultural, & economic value of preservation & reuse to advance the systems of policy & practice that shape the built environment. She is a past Chair of the AIA Committee on the Environment (COTE) & APT's Technical Committee on Sustainable Preservation (APT TC-SP), & she serves on the Climate Heritage Network Steering Committee. Meredith Wiggins, World Monuments Fund Senior Director of Climate Adaptation Dr. Meredith Wiggins works at the intersection of climate action, cultural heritage, & sustainable development. As Senior Director of Climate Adaptation at World Monuments Fund (WMF), she guides climate strategy across WMF's global portfolio, assessing environmental risks & opportunities while advancing practical approaches to adaptation for heritage places & landscapes. An archaeologist by training, Dr. Wiggins brings deep expertise in heritage protection, policy, planning, & international development to her work. She currently oversees WMF's Climate Heritage Initiative & leads Cultivating Resilience,' a global program focused on risk assessment & adaptation for biocultural landscapes. Ege Yildirim, ICOMOS Trkiye Climate Co-coordinator Dr. A. Ege Yildirim is an urban planner specializing in heritage conservation, with over 25 years of experience related to cultural heritage policy & governance, UNESCO World Heritage, & sustainable development. She was a Fulbright Scholar at Pratt Institute (New York), Senior Fellow for Archaeological Site Management at Koc University (Istanbul), & a Salzburg Global Seminar fellow. Her previous positions include heritage planner at the Abu Dhabi Authority for Culture & Heritage, site manager for the Historic Guild Town of Mudurnu, & ICOMOS Focal Point for the SDGs. She founded Terra Mudurnu, a social venture for heritage-based sustainable development. Ege is currently supporting ICOMOS Trkiye, Europa Nostra, Heritage Adapts!, & the Climate Heritage Network for the Culture at COP31 platform.  * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * This event is free & open to the public. Registration is required (one registration per attendee). Check-in is located in the lobby of the Tata Innovation Center; please bring your ID. For updates, please follow us on Eventbrite, Instagram @CornellAAP @CornellAAPNYC. If you would like to be notified about our upcoming events, please complete this form.

events.name: Fashioning Positive Impact - 20 Yrs Of Pioneering Circular Fashion
events.description: Fashioning Positive Impact: 20 Years of Circularity for Business Longevity. Hear from DEPLOY's Founder, Dr. Bernice Pan as she shares insights from two decades of circular, design-led thinking & how it can create lasting value for business, people & planet. EVENT OUTLINE For two decades, DEPLOY has tested what it means to build circularity into the foundations of a business - from product design & production to service, customer experience & long-term care. At this 'meet the founder' event, Dr. Bernice Pan will share reflections from 20 years of turning systems change theory into business practice, & consider how circular, design-led thinking can beautifully support business & planetary resilience, relevance & longevity. The session will bring together senior leaders from business, finance, sustainability & policy to explore what long-term value looks like in a resource-constrained world. About DEPLOY Founded in 2006, DEPLOY is one of the world's earliest ethical fashion pioneers & a strategic action plan to reform fashion. Its signature 360 Sustainability Compass puts care for makers, wearers & the planet at the heart of the business, embedding this approach across design, production, service, repair & long-term use. DEPLOY is the world's highest-scoring fashion B Corp, with a score of 176.8, & actively contributes towards 12 of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. Its work has been recognised by the Great British Brands Award for Commitment to Planet, the Future Icon Award for Best Zero-Waste Brand & the Marie Claire Sustainability Award for Ethical Fashion Brand of the Year.

events.name: AI, Energy, Fight for Democracy & A Healthy, Affordable Future
events.description: Tishman AuditoriumClimate Week 2026 Keynote Event at The New School   We are excited to share that this vital conversation convenes a powerhouse lineup of community leaders, mayors, scientists, researchers, & journalists. Across three dynamic panel conversations, we'll examine the collision of technology, energy, & democracy; the rapid expansion of AI data centers; the legacy of nuclear weapons; the toll of these developments on Indigenous communities, communities of color, & rural areas; & the affordability crisis & what it will take for everyday people to build power & shape real solutions.    Together, these conversations connect today's most pressing challenges to a larger question: How do communities organize & build power within democratic structures when government & industry leave them behind?   AI's Hidden Toll   LaTricea AdamsPresident & CEO, Young, Gifted & Green, Memphis   Manish BapnaPresident & CEO, Natural Resources Defense Council, Washington, DC   Mayor Kate GallegoCity of Phoenix   Adam Mahoney (Moderator)National Climate & Environment Reporter, Capital B News, New Orleans   Nuclear Legacy: Mapping Local Impacts   Lilly AdamsCo-Creator, US Nuclear Impacts Map, Brooklyn, New York   Moeka De OroCo-Executive Director, Micronesia Climate Change Alliance, Guam/Guhan   Leona Morgan (Din)Indigenous Community Organizer & Anti-Nuclear Activist, Din No Nukes, Albuquerque, New Mexico   Sharon Weinberger (Moderator)Editor-in-Chief, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Washington, DC   Power in Our Hands: Solutions for an Affordable, Just Future   Dr. Ana Isabel BaptistaAssociate Professor of Environmental & Climate Justice at the Parsons School of Design & Director, Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, New York   Dr. Gretchen GoldmanPresident & CEO, Union of Concerned Scientists, Washington, DC   Bill McKibbenAuthor, Educator, Activist, & Founder, Third Act & 350.org, Vermont   Mayor Michelle WuCity of Boston Garrison Hayes (Moderator)Correspondent,  Mother Jones, Nashville This event is presented by the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School, in collaboration with Climate Desk Live partners Mother Jones, Capital B News, & the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists. This event is free & open to the public. events.description: Distribution is Your Moat: A series on Distribution & Marketing for Startups August 6 9:30 am: Innovation Is Your Moat ft. Alex Chung Presented by Surface AI "As the cost of code goes to zero, distribution is your only moat." While marketing, distribution, & go-to-market are established fields with many tried & true methods, each startup's playbook will be as unique as its company. To help companies understand, define, & grow their distribution, Ari Spool of Surface AI brings together a selection of startup marketing leaders for a breakfast panel to strategize. Refreshments by Donut Pub. Alex Chung is Head of Growth at System, a telehealth company built around clinician-prescribed peptide therapies. Alex has worked on both sides of the growth equation. Before System, she led growth at a consumer AI startup. Before that, she invested as a venture capitalist. That mix shapes how she evaluates markets, builds trust in unfamiliar categories, & turns early attention into real revenue. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago & an MBA from Chicago Booth. This conversation gets into the core challenge of her work: how to take a product that customers don't fully understand, build credibility around it, find the right audience, & convert interest into lasting growth. The principles apply well beyond telehealth. Outside of work, Alex is training for her third marathon, in Tokyo. Surface AI is an autonomous landing-page optimization engine. We connect to your existing site with one line of code - a quick setup through your CMS. From there Surface automatically generates & tests new headlines, CTAs, layouts, & images in brand voice, shifting traffic toward what's winning & continuously optimizing over time. All attendees will receive a free 14-day trial of Surface!

events.name: Plug and Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNY
events.description: Plug and Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each.Most hackathons give you hours  sometimes days  to solve one problem.Rapid Fire is different.In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 24 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, and communicate your thinking under pressure.Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop and submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge.No long build cycle. No endless polishing. Youll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, and make tradeoffs in real time.How It WorksParticipants will form teams of 24 people.Over the course of the event, teams will face 34 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time.For each round:A new problem is announcedTeams have approximately 45 minutes to respondTeams submit their solution before the deadlineJudges score the submissionsThe next challenge beginsScores accumulate across the rounds, and the team with the strongest overall performance wins.The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making.What Are We Looking For?You do not need to build a fully finished product.Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution.What matters is your ability to:Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works.Who Should Join?This event is designed for a mix of:Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, and anyone interested in building with AI.You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets  technical, product, design, operations, and strategy.Come with teammates or meet people at the event.Why Rapid Fire?Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan.They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, and decisive execution.Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, and as a team.Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster.Schedule5:00  5:30 Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30  5:45 Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45  6:30 First Problem6:30  7:15 Second Problem7:15  8:00 Third Problem8:00 - 8:30 Judging Session8:30  9:00 Winners Announcement & Group PhotosSponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a  About Plug and PlayPlug and Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, and government agencies. We also run startup acceleration programs and have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, and Rappi. events.name: A Civic Tech'ish Happy Hour - Island Edition
events.description: We're taking Civic Tech'ish to Governors Island. events.name: Taste Of Climate Week
events.description: Visiting NYC for Climate Week? Here's where to eat. Taste of Climate Week: NYC is a city-wide dining initiative connecting Climate Week attendees & New Yorkers with Midtown restaurants serving planet-friendly specials all week long... because what's on your plate is one of the most powerful climate actions you can take! Throughout Climate Week NYC (September 20-27), participating restaurants across Midtown Manhattan will be featuring special menu items & discounts. And thanks to our partners at Beyond Meat, you can look forward to plant-based options at several locally owned spots, so you can skip the big chains & eat some of New York's best food! The week kicks off with a launch event on Monday, September 21 from 7-9pm at Le Botaniste in Penn Plaza. Join us for an evening of plant-based bites, drinks, & conversation with leaders who are working to make the food system better, healthier, & more affordable - we'll feature a live panel & plenty of time to connect with the community doing this work. Sign up below to stay in the loop. We'll keep you updated on participating restaurants, panel speakers, & everything you need to know to eat well & eat WITH IMPACT during Climate Week NYC.

events.name: Climate Cafe with CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Pilina Across The Pae'ina
events.description: Pilina(pee-LEE-nah) (n) is a Hawaiian word describing the relationships that connect people to one another, to place, & to the systems that sustain life.nPresented byCauseway ImpactandHawaii Green Growth,Pilina Across the Pae'inais a NYC Climate Week conversation exploring the future of place, reimagining climate finance through Hawaiian pilina, & highlighting how relationships shape resilient communities.nAcross theHawaiian Pae'ina(Hawaiian Archipelago) & the Pacific, island communities are responding to climate change through collaboration rather than isolation: bringing together indigenous leaders, conservationists, artists, philanthropists, politicians, youth advocates, & community members to affect sustainable policy. Their work offers practical models for resilience that extend far beyond Hawai'i & the Pacific islands, celebrating Hawaiian leadership in this important space.nWith speakers representing the Hawaiian 'ina (land), community,youthadvocacy,culture,leadership, andstewardship, we'll discuss:nLongstanding legacies of indigenous innovation & leadership in sustainable policy.nLegislative & community action like the Green Fee & the shared land ownership model.nLahaina's resilience & the strength of local connections & culture in the face of climate changenTrue to the spirit ofpilina, the conversation continues beyond the stage to ourpau hana(happy hour), the interactive portion of the event where we'll gather over light refreshments & engage in Hawaiian traditions.nJoin us duringClimate Week NYCatScandinavia Housefor an afternoon ofpilina(connection),kilo(observation), andkomo(participation) in Hawaii & Pacific resilience in action.

events.description: When Co-Founders Disagree: Preventing & Navigating Founder DisputesYour co-founder may be one of the most important relationships you have as a founder, & one of the hardest to navigate when things go wrong. Pioneering Minds AI is pleased to host this interactive workshop with Christopher Edwards (Partner, Reitler) on how founders can prevent, manage, & resolve co-founder disputes before they become company-threatening problems. Rather than a traditional legal presentation, this session will center around real-world situations, practical frameworks, & candid discussion about the disagreements founders actually encounter while building a company. What We'll Cover Why co-founder relationships break down, from misaligned expectations & uneven contributions to disagreements over strategy, fundraising, compensation, & control What founders should agree on early, roles, responsibilities, equity, decision-making authority, vesting, & expectations around commitment How to build a disagreement mechanism before you actually need one What happens when founders reach a deadlock, & how governance & legal documents can help Founder departures & breakups, what happens to equity, IP, board seats, & control when someone leaves Real-world lessons from founder disputes & situations that could have been handled differently How to have difficult conversations without turning a business disagreement into a personal conflict Interactive Workshop We want the conversation to be candid & useful. Attendees will have the opportunity to discuss scenarios, ask questions, & work through how they might handle difficult co-founder situations themselves. Who Should Attend This workshop is designed for: Founders currently building with one or more co-founders Early-stage teams thinking about equity, roles, & governance Founders considering bringing on a co-founder Anyone who has experienced, or wants to avoid, a difficult founder breakup The best time to figure out how you'll handle a co-founder dispute is before you have one. Agenda: 6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:15 p.m. - Session begins7:05 p.m. - Q&A7:45 p.m. - End of session About Reitler:Reitler is a top-ranked venture capital law firm with offices in New York, Los Angeles, & Princeton. Reitler is consistently ranked as a Top 10 venture capital law firm by Pitchbook & has been recognized by Chambers as a global leader in its Startups & Emerging Companies category. With thousands of venture financings completed since our founding, we bring deep experience & practical insight to help our clients achieve their goals efficiently. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. events.name: Carbon Newbie Summit
events.description: The Carbon Newbie Summit is back for its 6th edition!  What can whales teach us about economics? How is AI transforming the way buildings use energy? And how are global investors & insurers preparing for a changing climate? Hear fresh perspectives from senior leaders at Mubadala Investment Company, London Stock Exchange Group, Trane Technologies, ServiceNow, American Family Insurance, BrainBox AI & more-alongside renowned scientists, entrepreneurs & changemakers from Columbia Climate School, the University of Toronto, Rutgers University & the Clean Air Task Force. We'll explore everything from AI & decarbonization to living nature, carbon credits, climate risk, microplastics, geothermal energy & sustainable finance-all through lively, accessible conversations designed for curious minds. Whether you're completely new to climate or already working in the field, you'll leave with fresh ideas, practical insights & plenty to talk about. No climate experience necessary-just bring your curiosity! Meet our incredible speakers on the Carbon Newbie Summit website. Light breakfast & full lunch will be served  CO-HOSTSCNaughtDebevoise & PlimptonTrane TechnologiesUniversity of Toronto - Lawson Climate InstituteClever Carbon The Carbon Newbie Summit is an initiative of Clever Carbon.  LIVESTREAMING AVAILABLE - register for the livestream ticket to receive details Who should attend?From climate experts to professionals new to sustainability & climate, our Summit welcomes anyone curious & passionate about climate. By registering for this event, you agree to share your registration information with our co-hosts/sponsors. About CNaught:Trusted by buyers like Asana, Medium, & Tiger Global, CNaught makes it easy to drive real climate impact through high-quality carbon credit portfolios. We deliver access to sophisticated buying strategies, previously available only to the largest buyers, enabling companies of any size to take meaningful climate action. Learn more: https://www.cnaught.com/ About Debevoise & Plimpton:Debevoise & Plimpton LLP is a premier law firm with market-leading practices, a global perspective & strong New York roots. Our clients look to us to bring a distinctively high degree of quality, intensity & creativity to resolve legal challenges effectively & cost efficiently. We have particularly deep experience in the broad range of issues that arise as environmental, social & governance (ESG) concerns & requirements become increasingly important. The firm brings together sophisticated, multidisciplinary & multinational teams to provide tailored & practical guidance across the evolving ESG & business integrity spectrum by counseling on trends & prudential issues, delivering concrete legal advice on evolving sustainability regulations & policies, & helping clients prepare for the legal, financial & reputational risks arising in this rapidly changing landscape. Learn more: https://www.debevoise.com/ About Trane Technologies:Trane Technologies is a global climate innovator. Through our strategic brands Trane & Thermo King, & our portfolio of environmentally responsible products & services, we bring efficient & sustainable climate solutions to buildings, homes & transportation.https://tranetechnologies.com About University of Toronto - Lawson Climate Institute:Through a multidisciplinary approach, the Lawson Climate Institute is ramping up U of T's capacity to advance the technologies & policies needed for Canada to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. As one of U of T's most wide-ranging, comprehensive initiatives, the institute is unique in its aim to ensure students in every discipline across three campuses have an opportunity to gain the tools needed to take concrete steps toward implementing practical climate solutions. The institute is named in honour of Brian Lawson & Joannah Lawson in recognition of their transformative $60-million donation to help establish the institute.https://lci.utoronto.ca About Clever Carbon:At Clever Carbon, we teach people about carbon footprint in a hip & fun way! From content creation to carbon footprint workshops, we work with leading brands around the world to help raise carbon literacy because what gets measured gets changed! Learn more: https://clevercarbon.io/

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

Global demand & national security priorities are converging, making this area critical to the next decade of industrial & economic growth. As part of Climate Week NYC, meet 20+ deep tech companies driving that transformation - all graduates of HAX, SOSV's hard-tech program & the world's most active pre-seed investor for deep tech founders. events.name: Navigating Enterprise Transformation - Data, People & Strategy In Action
events.description: Join us on September 24 in-person or online via Zoom! In an era of rapid technological acceleration, executing a true enterprise transformation is an existential imperative that goes far beyond deploying sophisticated AI tools. It requires shifting from an engineering-led culture to a customer-first growth engine, breaking deep-seated organizational silos, & aligning technology directly to strategic outcomes. Join Michael Raj, Vice President of Strategic Modeling & Analytics at Verizon, for a deep dive into the digital transformation underway across Verizon's enterprise as part of Columbia University's Information & Knowledge Strategy (IKNS) Seminar Series. This in-person event at Columbia University's Faculty House will be followed by a networking reception. Livestream also available. Sitting at the center of Verizon's Transformation Command Center (TCC), the Strategic Modeling & Analytics team acts as the cross-functional connective tissue-equipping cross-functional Tiger Teams & business units with the evidence-based analytics, ground-truth modeling, & decision frameworks required to turn strategic intent into measurable value. Drawing from active execution across multiple strategic transformation pillars, Michael Raj, Vice President at Verizon, will walk through how Verizon is building a Single Source of Truth (SSOT), scaling an AI-First workflow architecture, & accelerating execution cycles across the enterprise. The presentation will explicitly tie these transformation initiatives back to the three core pillars of the IKNS curriculum: Data & Analytics: Moving beyond theoretical hype to ground-truth analytical models that drive tangible P&L impact-from machine-learning models predicting voluntary churn & lifetime value (LTV) to AI-driven automated work intelligence for CapEx/OpEx allocation & propensity modeling for network risk. People & Networks: Driving holistic change management & cultural transformation to overcome internal inertia & build broad-based buy-in across the enterprise. Integration & Strategy: Architecting an intelligent, customer-first infrastructure that replaces siloed departmental metrics with unified business scorecards. Michael will share how the TCC bridges Network, Supply Chain, Finance, & Customer Experience to establish clear ROI, optimize capital allocation, & align executive leadership across the enterprise value chain. Can't make it at this particular time? Register anyway, & we will send you the recording. Questions? Reach out to Amy Newhall at an2933@columbia.edu.  _________________________________________________________________________________________ To obtain additional information about program offerings at Columbia University's School of Professional Studies, please contact an Admissions Counselor at inquire@sps.columbia.edu. If you require closed captioning, sign-language interpretation, or any other disability accommodations, please contact Disability Services, disability@columbia.edu, at least 10 days in advance. Services requested less than 10 days in advance cannot be guaranteed. Please visit Columbia University's Hub for Emergency Preparedness to stay up to date on the latest campus health & safety policies. This event is open to individuals irrespective of identity & sex.

events.name: Advancing Climate Solns In A Changing World
events.description: From Possibility to Practice: Advancing Climate Solutions in a Changing WorldFeaturing Eliza Barclay, The New York Times, & Joel Makower, TrellisThursday, September 24, 2026Climate Week NYC As part of Climate Week NYC, UC Berkeley's Master of Climate Solutions will convene a curated group of climate practitioners, alumni, & members of the broader Berkeley community for an invitation-only roundtable lunch. The gathering will open with remarks from Joel Makower of Trellis, a UC Berkeley alumnus & member of the Master of Climate Solutions Advisory Board. Joel will then join fellow UC Berkeley alumna Eliza Barclay of The New York Times for a candid conversation about what they are seeing from the front lines of climate journalism, business, science, health, & the environment. Together, Barclay & Makower will explore how the climate story is changing, where meaningful progress is taking hold, where momentum remains constrained, & which developments deserve greater attention. Their exchange will then open into a facilitated roundtable conversation. Participants will bring their own experiences & perspectives to a shared discussion about what it takes to move climate solutions from possibility to practice within complex & rapidly changing real-world systems. The program will conclude with reflections from Kat Hunt, drawing on her experience addressing the MCS graduating class & her perspective on the next generation of climate leadership. Designed as a working conversation rather than a traditional panel, the lunch will create space for candid exchange, practical insight, & meaningful connections among leaders working across sectors & disciplines. Attendance is limited to 25 guests & is by invitation. Advance registration is required. Additional details will be shared with confirmed participants.

events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. This series was initiated by the late Michael Sorkin, distinguished professor of architecture & director of the Urban Design Program at the Spitzer School, & curated by him for eleven years.   AccessibilityFor live captioning, ASL interpretation, or access requests, please contact ssadean@ccny.cuny.edu.    Statement of Conduct The City College of New York, founded on a vision of access to excellence, educates thousands of students each year & encourages civic & robust debate, respectful dissent, & thoughtful inquiry. Consistent with this commitment, City College supports academic freedom & convenes conversations representing multiple perspectives throughout the year. The views expressed at events are those of the individual speaker(s) & do not necessarily reflect the opinion of the college. All participants are expected to treat others with respect & consideration, uphold personal & professional integrity, & comply with all applicable College policies & venue rules.  Image CreditsThomas Baltes (portrait); WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities (all others)

events.name: AI Tinkerers Demo Day w/ PostHog
events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC! Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQ Some slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? This is your moment to share with like-minded AI tinkerers! A demo is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!)  FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo. Demo vibes  Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:00 Networking & pizzas9:00 Doors CloseMore informationIf you are new to AI Tinkerers, please read the AI Tinkerers FAQ & join our Discord channel: https://discord.gg/8WsqnC6Hk3 SponsorsPostHogPostHog is an all-in-one product OS designed for engineers, offering product analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, & surveys in a single platform. It enables teams to understand user behavior, deploy features, & analyze data without patching together multiple tools. Founded in Y Combinator (W20), it supports both cloud-hosted & open-source self-hosting. Veris AI (Venue Host)Veris AI accelerates agent development & deployment with a simulation sandbox platform that delivers robust, compliant AI systems at speed. Veris sandbox is pre-loaded with test scenarios, simulated tools, & personas. Using the sandbox, you can run thousands of simulated interactions across routine workflows, challenging edge cases, & adversarial scenarios. Veris AI creates root-cause analysis reports, regression testing gates, & prompt or RL optimization loops to improve the agent using these interactions before the agent touches the first real system or customer. Start building now!We're bringing a builder-first lineup of demos & giving the community a space to share work in progress, trade notes, & meet other serious practitioners.

Veris AI creates root-cause analysis reports, regression testing gates, & prompt or RL optimization loops to improve the agent using these interactions before the agent touches the first real system or customer. Start building now!We're bringing a builder-first lineup of demos & giving the community a space to share work in progress, trade notes, & meet other serious practitioners.

events.name: Decarbonizing Everyday Life
events.description: Fossil fuels are all around us, & not just when it comes to transport & electricity. In your closet, your kitchen, your medicine cabinet, even your walls, petroleum products are hiding in plain sight. Our daily lives are built on embodied carbon in the most literal sense. And unlike metal, glass, or plant-based materials, they return cleanly to neither industry nor the earth. They degrade, but never disappear. Decarbonization is about more than renewable energy. It means remaking the stuff of our everyday lives, & with it the supply chains, design decisions, & consumer habits that put that stuff in our hands. This conversation brings together materials innovators, designers, & industry experts working on sustainable alternatives, from new recycling technologies to bio-based alternatives for petroleum-derived textiles, packing materials, & cosmetics. Together they will explore the innovations that could help us move past plastic, & how we can get those sustainable materials out of the lab & into our homes. More information, speakers, & event program This event is part of Assembly, the main Swiss stage at Climate Week NYC 2026. As world leaders gather in Midtown Manhattan, Swissnex assembles Swiss & global voices - from private sector innovators & researchers to artists & policymakers - in the East Village for three days of communal climate thinking & action. Assembly speaks to deliberation & democracy - the idea that communities must collectively define their futures - as well as the ongoing, creative, improvisational process of constructing those futures from the pieces of our present.
