events.name: Rethink Waste, Reduce Emissions & Unlock Value
events.description: The Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House invite you to a reception & conversation on global circularity. Resource scarcity, shifting global supply chains, & climate change are reshaping the landscape for businesses, governments, & communities. We need solutions that create economic value for businesses & individuals while advancing climate goals. One place to look for these solutions is in our waste. The Circularity Gap Report estimates that roughly 25.4 trillion in economic value is lost globally each year through linear take-make-waste practices. This Value Gap represents 31% of global GDP, meaning that for every 3 of economic value created worldwide, about 1 is lost. Increasing circularity, which simply means keeping materials in use for as long as possible, could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 39%. Circularity is not only good for the bottom line & the environment, but can also improve quality of life through more durable products, greater affordability, & connected communities. If the benefits are so clear, what will it take to scale circularity? How do we align businesses, governments, & communities around a shared path forward? To kick off Climate Week NYC, Scandinavia House is pleased to partner with Columbia Climate School for a conversation on the promise of a circular economy. Join leaders from the public & private sectors as they explore practical solutions & emerging innovations, lessons learned from Nordic leadership, & the challenges that remain. The program will conclude with a special announcement from Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund, followed by a reception to connect & continue the conversation. Alexis Abramson - Opening RemarksDean & Professor, Columbia Climate School Sandra Goldmark - ModeratorProfessor of Professional Practice in the Faculty of Climate, Columbia Climate School Anu MntySenior Lead, International Programs, Sitra John MuirHead of USA, 3stepIT Miia RantanenConsul General of Finland in New York Presented By: Columbia Climate School & Scandinavia House Please note, this program is a private event. If you would like to share this invitation, or if you have general questions, please contact development@climate.columbia.edu. Registration is required.

events.name: City Camp
events.description: Join us for the return of CityCamp NYC!What is CityCamp?A CityCamp is an unstructured conference in which the agenda is created by attendees on the day of the event. Using "Open Space Technology," we foster purpose-driven discussions around policy, programs, tech, tools, data, & our communities. Our "unconference" convenes city officials, technologists, community organizations, analysts, academia, & beyond; together, we re-imagine how collaboration & tools can help grow & sustain a healthy future for our neighborhoods. At CityCamp NYC, you are not an attendee; you are a participant. An unconference focuses on intersectional dialogue & collaboration. No demos or memos. No product pitches or corporate agendas. You, the participant, set the agenda. Together, we design & organize each session. All participants play active roles in respectful dialogue, conversations, workshops, & discussions. Our goal is simple: open exchange geared toward action. You come to share & learn. NYC technology, data, design, & policy - for us, by us! Tickets & Opportunities:Are you a student or looking for a scholarship or volunteer opportunity? Volunteer:We need volunteers to support the unconference. You spend one part of the day helping out & the other as an attendee. Learn more & apply before Monday, August 24, at 11:59 PM at this site. Scholarships:A select number of scholarship tickets are available & will prioritize traditionally underserved & underrepresented communities. Learn more & apply before Wednesday, September 17, at 12:00 PM; apply here. Do you work for a Government agency/department?If you work for a government agency/department & want to purchase a general admission ticket by check or purchase order (PO), government ticket opportunities close on Wednesday, September 17, by 5:00 PM. Please email us at citycamp@beta.nyc. Sponsors, want to support the conference?We're looking for mission-aligned sponsors to help cover conference costs, including meals, coffee, childcare, & ASL interpretation. Learn more about our opportunities to support by filling out this form. Press & Media: Interested in covering the event?Media credentials are available to reporters, editors working as reporters, producers, video camera operators, & still photographers who present valid press identification. If you want to attend to cover a session or the event, email us your valid press identification to citycamp@beta.nyc. We will follow up. General Event Information:What is included in my ticket? All tickets include access to a full day of conference sessions, lunch, snacks, & coffee. We offer free, professional on-site childcare. Space is limited. Please register if you are interested. Childcare We have contracted on-site childcare for children under the age of 18. In order to use this service, you MUST be a ticket-holder, & you MUST register your child(ren) before September 11th by acquiring a Childcare Ticket. Each child you register requires a ticket registration. There are limited spots available, so please sign up sooner rather than later! If you have any questions, please email us at citycamp+childcare@beta.nyc. Accessibility & Accommodations We want CityCamp to be usable by everyone who wants to take part. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request. Service animals are always welcome. The conference is delivered in English & uses technical terms. If you need ASL interpretation, or have any other accessibility question or request, email us at citycamp@beta.nyc by Friday, September 4. Requests after that date are welcome, & we will do what we can, but we cannot promise to fill them. Code of Conduct BetaNYC is committed to hosting safe & open spaces for all. By participating in this space, you are committing yourself to BetaNYC's Code of Conduct & Anti-Harassment Policy. Health Policy If you're not feeling well, PLEASE stay home. We strive to create a safe environment for everyone. (Please see our refund policy for questions.) We encourage everyone to wear a high-quality mask at all times (except when eating & drinking). We will have ample KF-94 masks in various sizes for you to wear. Masks keep our staff, volunteers, & attendees safe. Masking helps prevent the spread of viruses - this is science, based on data! Refund Policy Contact us to request a refund. We will try to honor all of your refund requests at citycamp+refund@beta.nyc. Please note that some ticketing fees are nonrefundable.

events.name: Will Autonomous Vehicles Improve The Environment
events.description: As cities rethink transportation in the face of climate change, autonomous vehicles are often presented as a promising part of the solution. But do they actually reduce emissions, congestion, & resource use, or do they risk making these problems worse? This Climate Week NYC event will take a clear-eyed look at the environmental case for autonomous vehicles & examine where the evidence supports the hype, & where it does not. A panel of top experts will discuss along with a Q&A session: Jeffrey Tumlin - former Exec. Director, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA) David Zipper -- Contributing writer, Bloomberg City Lab; former Senior Fellow, MIT Mobility Initiative Rachel Weinberger -- Vice President, Transportation & Peter W. Herman Chair, Regional Planning Association Jeral Poskey - Founder, Swyft Cities; former project executive for transportation planning, Google Format: Panel Discussion followed by Q&A The discussion will explore the complicated relationship between automation, mobility, & sustainability. Rather than assuming new technology automatically leads to better outcomes, the discussion will focus on the many potential impacts: energy use, induced demand, land use, transit interactions, fleet models, & the difference between theoretical efficiency & actual environmental performance. Join us for a timely discussion on climate & the future of urban mobility.

events.name: Buildings & Grid - Clipping The Falcon Wing
events.description: Can buildings play a significant role in solving the crisis brewing in our power grids? Join Building Energy Exchange & the US Green Building Council (USGBC) for a moderated discussion with regulatory & industry experts exploring how building decarbonization can help address, rather than exacerbate, the current & future challenges facing our grid.   Our power grids face an array of converging & mounting challenges. After more than two decades of relatively flat consumption, the electrical grid is experiencing significant increases in demand driven by building & vehicle electrification, extreme weather events, & the rapid growth of data centers. At the same time, the transition to clean, renewable energy is creating new challenges in balancing supply & demand.   The costs to provide enough power for these increases are astronomical, & the lead-time to bring new generation online is a significant challenge. However, buildings can play a critical role in reducing the loads. By reducing overall energy use & managing peak demand, buildings can become active partners in supporting a more reliable, resilient, & decarbonized grid.  This session will explore the emerging grid issues & the various strategies-such as load shifting, peak load reduction, improved building envelopes, & geothermal-that buildings can deploy to reduce grid demand. Coffee & pastries will be served!   Opening RemarksRichard Yancey, CEO, Building Energy ExchangeLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC  PresentationsZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  PanelistsRyan Dougherty, Executive Director, Geothermal Exchange OrganizationLaurie Kerr, Principal Climate Advisor, USGBC - ModeratorJohn Rhodes, Chief Program Officer, NYS Department of Public ServiceZack Semke, Co-Founder & Director, Passive House Accelerator  Schedule 9:00 am - Doors open  9:15 am - Welcome & Presentations  10 am - Panel Discussion & Q+A  10:55 am - Closing Remarks  11:00 am - Networking

events.name: Implementing Circularity In Interior Design
events.description: Connecting the Dots Our interior spaces remains trapped in a persistent & costly system of frequent renovation, demolition, & disposal, resulting in an unsustainable churn of materials. While circular design offers a path forward, the challenge isn't just designing for circularity; it's creating the network of relationships needed to make it work, connecting the many stakeholders responsible for shaping, operating, & renewing interior spaces. Our panel of stakeholders across the value chain will examine what is needed to really implement the circularity loop - to keep materials in circulation, reduce waste, lower costs, create jobs, & transform the interiors industry from a linear model of consumption to a truly circular one. events.name: Are AI Datacenters A Threat To Our Clean Energy Future
events.description: NOTE: Registration is REQUIRED. Join Pratt Institute's Sustainable Environmental Systems program for our third annual just energy transition event during NYC Climate Week. Global & local experts will join in conversation across just energy challenges, solutions, & perspectives with a particular focus on the rapid expansion of energy-hungry datacenters powering artificial intelligence (AI).  Experts working on local & global energy issues will come together to discuss new policy dynamics, systemic & historic barriers in realizing a true Just Transition, & how these new datacenters could get us off track. This timely discussion will happen during the UN General Assembly & NYC Climate Week 2026, where key climate & energy transition issues will be at the center of next steps for the sustainable development goals & the broader theme of this year's Climate Week. Key themes of the conversation will include: decarbonization, climate finance, climate diplomacy, infrastructure, the path to net zero, water, tech & AI, incentives for transition, green economy, & the SDGs.   The panel will be feature local & global perspectives in a conversation moderated by a recent Pratt SES alumna, Jen Hung: Panelists:  Martha Molfetas | Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute; Senior Policy Consultant & Writer: Martha Molfetas is a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Environmental Economics. Martha is a senior climate & energy policy consultant, writer, & strategist with over 17-years of experience helping NGOs, think tanks, & businesses unpack climate, environmental justice, resource conflict, sustainable development, & global policy issues with organizations ranging from Dalberg Research to Transparency International, NRGI & Oil Change International to name a few. She was formerly a Senior Fellow working on just energy transition at New America. Her work has been published in: Current Affairs, The World Politics Review, The Global Policy Journal, Policy Mic, Common Dreams, & others. Summer Sandoval | Academic Coordinator, Visiting Assistant Professor, Pratt Institute & Community Investment & Implementation Director, USDN: Summer Sandoval is the Community Investment & Implementation Director at Urban Sustainability Directors Network (USDN), where she supports local governments & communities in navigating funding opportunities & realizing their projects to advance equitable climate action. Summer is also the Academic Coordinator & a Visiting Assistant Professor at Pratt Institute's Graduate Center for Planning & the Environment, where she teaches Urban Energy Management. Summer has worked at the intersection of climate, environmental, & energy justice in community-based organizations & city government.   Rami Dinnawi | Program Director, North Star Fund: Rami Dinnawi is a Lebanese/Palestinian grassroots activist based in New York City. Informed by generational knowledge of people's struggle for self-determination, Rami strives to ground his work within these historical legacies. He is currently serving as the NYC Program Director at North Star Fund. Prior to joining North Star Fund, Rami worked extensively in the New York environmental justice movement space, as the environmental justice campaign & policy manager at El Puente. Rami is currently serving on the Advisory Committee of the Tishman Environment & Design Center at The New School. With over a decade of organizing experience, Rami's commitment extends beyond borders, as he actively engages with activism & movements on a global scale. Pierre Canet | Global Head of Public Affairs & Policy, Client Earth: Pierre leads ClientEarth's Global Public Affairs & Policy team, overseeing the organisation's influence on decision-makers to achieve the systems change pursued in its strategy across the world. Before joining ClientEarth, Pierre was the Executive Director of Advocacy at WWF in France where he worked for a decade leading campaigns & programs on a diversity of environmental issues, from climate & energy to nature & plastics, collaborating at multiple levels throughout the WWF's global network. Prior to this, Pierre worked with the United Nations in New York on the preparation of the Rio+20 Summit & corporate climate engagement. He engaged significantly with activities around the Climate COP21 to influence the establishment of the Paris Agreement, & has substantial experience in building & developing high-impact activities from newly-established teams.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: From Lab To Scale - Building Northeast's Climate Innovation Pipeline
events.description: Greentown is home to 300+ climate, energy, & industrial startups innovating for a better world. To support those startups, we have 130,000 square feet of innovation space, including nearly 50,000 square feet of prototyping lab space, as well as networks of 60+ corporate partners, 300+ active investors, & countless subject matter experts. events.name: From Framework To Front Line - Advancing Housing Resilience & Affordability
events.description: RPA & Enterprise explore using policy & partnerships to protect affordable homes, accelerate recovery & strengthen communities. Climate-driven disasters are placing growing pressure on an already constrained housing supply, threatening existing homes, increasing costs for residents & housing providers, & making it more difficult for communities to meet urgent affordability needs. As municipalities grapple with the need to build more resilient communities able to withstand extreme weather events, the critical question is how policymakers, planners, & housing experts can translate ambitious blueprints into effective, local action. This panel will bring together Regional Plan Association (RPA) & Enterprise Community Partners to examine the policies, planning decisions, & implementation strategies needed to protect existing housing & accelerate recovery. Drawing from national standards & regional planning frameworks, panelists will examine the challenges communities & housing providers face, & highlight the resources & partnerships needed to address the intersecting climate & housing crisis. Enterprise Community Partners will draw on insights from its Climate Resilience Academies to highlight the challenges affordable housing owners, operators, & developers face in preparing their portfolios for climate risks while safeguarding residents. Through its work with more than 150 participants across U.S. regions, Enterprise has seen that housing providers increasingly understand the urgency of resilience but often lack the staff capacity, funding, technical expertise, & region-specific guidance needed to act. Enterprise will discuss opportunities to close these gaps to further help housing providers move from awareness to implementation.Regional Plan Association will draw from its Averting Crisis report & subsequent work with communities in the New York metropolitan region to examine how housing growth & climate resilience can be advanced together. RPA will share real-time lessons being learned about effective ways to move from high-altitude planning to on-the-ground implementation, highlighting its work with local governments, community organizations, & neighborhood stakeholders in seven communities across Queens, Westchester, & Long Island. The work will result in local actions that affect zoning changes, land-use reform, investments & complementary policies to align housing growth with climate risk & capacity. These organizations will offer expertise on climate readiness & disaster response, connecting federal & local policy to on-the-ground implementation to make communities more resilient amid the growing housing affordability crisis.

events.name: Accommodating Growth In The Global South
events.description: All guests are welcome to arrive early for a light lunch & networking beginning around noon. Most of the world's urban growth over the next few decades will happen in cities that don't yet exist at scale - concentrated in the Global South, where population growth is fastest & infrastructure is least locked in. Whether that growth compounds sprawl-driven emissions or avoids them depends on choices being made right now about housing & land use policy, as well as transportation infrastructure investments. Once made, these decisions produce long-lasting impacts for climate, accessibility, & economies. This panel will draw from the experience of urban planning, land use, & transportation experts actively working on efforts in the global south. Speakers: Robin King (Moderator), Director, Knowledge Capture & Collaboration, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella  Cynthia Goytia, Head of the Master of Science in Urban Economics Program, WRI  Solly Angel, Professor of City Planning, NYU Marron  Samhita Shiledar, Principal, RMI  Adriana Akers, Senior Project Manager, Gehl This session is hosted by Gehl, the NYU Marron Institute, the Parking Reform Network, & WRI & is a part of The Urban Climate Solution track at NYC Climate Week 2026. events.name: Race To Recover America's Critical Minerals - When Startups & Industry Team Up
events.description: The US imports the vast majority of the critical minerals that power its defense, aerospace, & semiconductor industries - but a meaningful share of what it needs may already be sitting in waste piles at the industrial sites that exist today. Join KOMPAS VC, SOSV, & At One Ventures for a breakfast conversation on what it actually takes to turn that waste into supply - & why the answer increasingly runs through a corporate partnership between a deep-tech innovator & an industrial incumbent, scaling proven technology beyond the pilot stage, not one company going it alone. We'll hear directly from Helios & Atalco, a live example of how corporate partnerships move promising technology from pilot to commercial scale, on infrastructure that already exists. Expect a short, focused fireside chat, brief perspectives from our venture partners, & plenty of time to connect over breakfast with others working at the intersection of hard tech, industrial partnerships, & the circular economy

Through student flash talks & posters, discover the breadth of research underway at the Fusion Research Center & beyond. The symposium will conclude with a reception & laboratory tours, offering an opportunity to connect with researchers & experience the Center's work firsthand. Featured Speakers: David Spergel, President, Simons Foundation Angela Olinto, Provost, Columbia University Najat Mokhtar, Deputy Director General, International Atomic Energy Agency Thomas Klinger, Director, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Greifswald Tim Happel, Director, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Garching Ellen Smeele, Chief of Staff, Proxima Fusion Thomas Pedersen, Chief Technical Officer, Type One Energy David Gates, Chief Technical Officer, Thea Energy Phil Snyder, VP of Plasma Physics, Commonwealth Fusion Systems Dr. Josefine Proll, Group leader, Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics Discover the research. events.description: Note: we are postponing & redesigning this event for September. This was a new event type & let's just say, it wasn't as popular as we thought it would be so, in true crowd-validator style, we are going back to the drawing board. Please contact us if you have constructive feedback. Thanks & Stay tuned!Alex Fair Original write up - subject to change. Presented by MedStartr in Partnership with ClawCamp You bring the vision. We'll help you launch a company - in a weekend. Healthcare is broken in a hundred ways we all see daily. You've felt it as a patient. diagnosed it as a clinician. doded around it as a builder, & hated it as a person who came into healthcare to help people. The things you see that could be better are hard to fix, & it bothers you that they seem incorrigible. But then you got an idea of something that could help, if you could just build it & get it in the hands of people like you to help patients get better care & the system & caregivers to give better care. We know, we have met thousands of you & ARE you too. That's why we have run this group for almost 18 years & done so many events. But now, with the help of AI & the new MedStartr.ai platform, we can help even more. So we created what we are calling a "Launchathon" to help with all that & this is the first one! The NYC HealthTech Launchathon is your chance to do something about it. No startup experience required. No coding background needed. Just bring your problem, your perspective, & your curiosity - & we'll bring the AI tools, expert faculty, mentors, investors, & community to help you build something real. The Program: 3 Phases, 8 Weeks  Phase I  HealthTech ClawCamp  August 1-2 **Day 1 - August 1 | Stack AI HQ, One World Trade Center**Learn. Ideate. Validate with Experts on hand & Build or add to your team from other folks like yourself. Meet amazing people. Pitch problems. Learn from expert AI faculty, upskill. Present or Find a problem worth solving - & the team to solve it with. No startup idea or coding required, but bring your passion to build solutions to the problems in healthcare. Day 2 - August 2 | Arya Health HQ, NYC**Build Something Real. Build prototypes. Validate ideas. Design workflows. Interview users. Use AI, code, & creativity. Leave Day 2 with something real - a working prototype posted to MedStartr.ai Qualifies you for Phase II (Also Awards of tokens & other great stuff from Day 2 Winners)  Phase II  MedStartr Crowd Challenge  August 2 - October 6 Your Build goes live on MedStartr.ai where 250,000+ credentialed healthcare stakeholders - patients, clinicians, investors, partners - can review, comment, follow, pilot, & share. More eyes. More feedback. More signal on what actually matters. Teams keep building & iterating based on what the crowd says.  Phase III  Launchathon Finals  October 6Health Impact Forum  Microsoft  Times Square, NYC The top crowd-validated teams take the stage at one of NYC's biggest healthcare innovation gatherings. Compete for **over $1 million** in investment, accelerator spots, pilots, partnerships, software credits, & everything a startup needs to succeed. Keynote SpeakersDay 1: Khan Siddiqui, MDCEO & Co-Founder, HOPPR  2025 SIIM Imaging Informatics Innovator"From Hacking to Scale" Brian Yarnell3x Exited HealthTech Founder Day 2: Grace Cordovano, PhDBoard Certified Patient Advocate  CancerX*"Designing for the Patient Experience"* 15 other MedStartr Mentors & 7 AI expert trainers to help you validate, plan & build your ideas out better & faster## Who Should Attend? This is for **everyone who touches healthcare** - not just developers: -  **Clinicians** - physicians, nurses, NPs, PAs who see broken workflows daily-  **Patients & caregivers** - living the gaps in care & navigation firsthand-  **Admins & billers** - revenue cycle, coding, & operations insiders-  **Researchers** - with data, insights, & unmet needs to solve-  **Tech co-founders** - developers & AI builders seeking high-impact problems (apply for discounted tickets)-  **Early founders** - ideas at any stage, ready to validate fast MedStartr Challenge Winners are 22 more likely to succeed. --- There are many more ticket Types available on MedStartr.ai/launchathon: | Type | Price | Details ||------|-------|---------|| General Admission | $50| Open enrollment || Two Pack | $80| Everything is better with friends || VIP | $100 | Dedicated mentor time + Health Impact Forum ticket || Early Bird | $0-25 | Apply to attend - going fast || Tech Co-Founder | $50 | Apply - discounted for technical builders || Mentor | Free | Apply via MedStartr.ai || Volunteer | Free | Help us run the event || Demo Table | $1,000 | Table for laptop, monitor + 1 rollup banner | Register & buy tickets here or for more options [visit the MedStartr.ai Healthcare Innovation platform with more details!](http://medstartr.ai/launchathon) Confirmed Sponsors Arya Health  Stack.ai  Health Impact Forum Interested in sponsoring?Five tiers from $2,500 Community to $50,000 Title. About MedStartr 17 years building the global healthcare innovation community. 9,000+ innovations reviewed. 250,000+ credentialed stakeholders. 1,200+ events in 41 cities. The team behind over 120 contests & crowdchallenges for over 200 sponsors since 2010. We also run the investment funds & accelerators, also named MedStartr where we invest in & accelerate the teams that win challenges like this one. Check out the new [MedStartr.ai](http://medstartr.ai) alpha Just Launched 7/14/2026! About ClawCamp ClawCamp is a global community advancing mastery of AI agents - from first personal agent to advanced multi-agent workflows. 1,400+ events  120+ cities  100,000+ attendees trained. The AI training backbone of the Launchathon build weekend. Visit them at clawcamp.us Khan Siddiqui, MDDr. Khan Siddiqui is a physician-entrepreneur, technologist, & radiologist at the forefront of the medical AI revolution. As CEO & Co-Founder of HOPPR, he leads the development of advanced multimodal foundation models designed to democratize AI training & accelerate medical imaging development for healthcare systems worldwide.He previously served as Chief Medical Officer & Chief Strategy Officer of Hyperfine, where he helped take the company public & deploy Swoop - the world's first FDA-cleared, portable bedside MRI system. In 2012 he founded higi, a consumer health network of thousands of biometric screening kiosks across North American pharmacies, culminating in a multi-billion-dollar acquisition. Earlier, as a principal program manager & AI architect at Microsoft, he designed the deep-learning image infrastructure used to train the Xbox Kinect. A recognized pioneer in imaging informatics, Dr. Siddiqui received the 2025 Imaging Informatics Innovator Award from the Society for Imaging Informatics in Medicine (SIIM) & holds dozens of patents across medical image processing, machine learning, & healthcare analytics.

events.description: How AI Can Help Investors Navigate Interconnected Risks Through Systems-Aware InvestingA Climate Week Brunch-and-Learn with US SIF, hosted by Calamos Investments, featuring The Investment Integration Project (TIIP) Join US SIF during Climate Week NYC 2026 for an exclusive brunch-and-learn featuring leaders from The Investment Integration Project (TIIP), one of the world's leading organizations advancing the practice of systems-level investing. Today's investors face risks that extend far beyond the financial performance of individual companies. Climate instability, biodiversity loss, economic exclusion, geopolitical uncertainty, public health challenges, & other interconnected forces increasingly shape long-term market outcomes. Understanding these systems-level risks is becoming essential for investors seeking resilient portfolios & durable long-term returns. During this interactive discussion, TIIP will introduce SAIL (Systems Aware Investing Launchpad), its AI-enhanced platform designed to help investors understand, analyze, & implement systems-aware investment strategies. Attendees will learn how artificial intelligence can support investors in identifying systemic risks, evaluating opportunities, & integrating systems thinking into investment policies, stewardship, asset allocation, & portfolio management. Whether you're a financial advisor, institutional investor, asset manager, consultant, or sustainability professional, this session will provide practical insights into one of the most rapidly evolving areas of sustainable investing. You'll also hear from US SIF about resources developed specifically for financial advisors, including upcoming educational initiatives. This session is approved for 1.0 hour of CFP Continuing Education (CE) credit. To receive credit, please provide your CFP Board ID during registration.

events.name: Builders & Brews
events.description: Builders & Brews: Hack Edition Builders & Brew is getting a hackathon twist! Nebius is bringing together builders from around the world along with Nvidia & Tavily for a global online hackathon focused on experimenting with open-source AI & turning new ideas into working projects! As part of the hackathon, Nebius & Tavily are bringing a special series of Builders & Brew: Hack Edition to local builder communities around the world & we're excited to bring the experience to NYC with our local partner LangChain. Expect the coffee, workshops, & laid-back community you know, plus hands-on support, mentorship, team formation, & focused building time. Explore an idea, meet potential teammates, or make progress on your hackathon project. And there's something extra for the builders: each city in the series will have its own local winner. Come build with us & put your project in the running to represent your city! Not participating in the hackathon? You're still welcome. Come learn, experiment, meet other builders, or work on something of your own. No pressure & no pitches,just agents, coffee, building, & good company. About the Global AI HackathonThe hackathon invites AI builders, ML engineers, founders, & developers to create practical AI systems using NVIDIA open-source models & Nebius infrastructure. The complete brief- including challenges, timeline, rules, prizes, & submission details-will be announced in late August. Until then, join us to explore ideas, get familiar with the tools, & start building. What's happeningNebius provides scalable AI cloud infrastructure that helps teams build, deploy, & scale AI applications efficiently. Tavily is the real-time search engine for AI agents & RAG workflows, offering fast, secure APIs for web search & content extraction. What to expect Welcome & an introduction to the upcoming hackathon  Nebius, Tavily & LangChain platform onboarding & technical setup  Team formation & project ideation  Technical workshops  Mentoring & troubleshooting  Several hours of focused building  Informal progress demos  Clear next steps for continuing your project  Opportunities to share product feedback directly with the teams What you'll get Free coffee & non-caffeinated drinks  Tavily credits  Nebius Token Factory credits  Time & space to brainstorm, start building, or improve an existing project  A chance to meet potential teammates  Access to technical experts for guidance & support  A head start on the upcoming hackathon and some very cool merch Who should comeAI builders & ML engineers Developers curious about agents & open-source AI Hackathon participants looking for ideas or teammates Founders building practical AI products Anyone interested in experimenting with Nebius, NVIDIA models, or Tavily Coffee & music lovers All experience levels are welcome. You don't need a team, a finished idea, or previous hackathon experience. How it worksMeet other builders, join the workshops, brainstorm ideas, & spend a few focused hours building. You won't be required to submit a project, but the experience is designed to help you make meaningful progress toward building-and, if you choose, submitting-something for the hackathon. Full details are coming soon. RSVP to join us in NYC & stay in the loop. Come curious. Leave caffeinated-and a few steps closer to shipping.   Location: NYC, shared after RSVP Time: 9:00 AM-5:00 PM Cost: Free

events.name: Convening The Next-Generation Materials Transition
events.description: The future of fashion depends on bringing next-generation materials to scale. While innovation continues to accelerate, turning breakthrough solutions into industry-wide adoption requires collaboration across the entire value chain. This Climate Week NYC, Eco-Age is convening the organisations, brands, & initiatives helping to shape that future. The Forum creates a platform where leaders can share knowledge, build partnerships, & explore practical pathways to adoption, connecting the people who each play a vital role in scaling next-generation materials. While global brands play an important role in leading the transition, commercial scale will ultimately depend on adoption across the wider fashion market, emerging brands to suppliers, material innovators, manufacturers, investors, NGOs, & solution providers. The Forum is designed to move that conversation forward & focus on commercial adoption, supply chain readiness, investment, sourcing, & the partnerships that can accelerate progress across the industry. Climate Week NYC is where global leaders come together to turn ambition into action. As one of the world's largest platforms for climate collaboration, it creates the ideal environment to build the relationships & shared understanding needed to move promising innovations beyond pilots & into practice. The Forum contributes to that momentum by connecting the people who can help shape the future of next-generation materials. Forum Partners Developed with & featuring voices from: Eco-Age - a purpose-led media & communications agency accelerating the fashion industry's transition to sustainability. Canopy - an award-winning environmental non-profit driving the shift to next-generation, forest-free fibres. Fashion for Good - the global platform for sustainable fashion innovation, connecting brands & innovators to scale breakthrough solutions. Material ConneXion - the world's leading materials insights company, connecting industries to the most innovative & sustainable materials available. Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) - New York's internationally renowned college for fashion, design, business & technology, fostering innovation, education & industry collaboration across the global fashion & textile sector. The Programme The Forum combines a keynote, structured workshops, & a networking reception. Through an invitation-based format & curated audience, participants will explore the opportunities & challenges shaping the next chapter of material innovation. The programme, speakers, & venue are currently being developed with our partners & will be announced in the coming weeks. Who Should Attend The Forum is designed for senior leaders in sustainability, sourcing, supply chain, & procurement across the fashion, apparel, & textile industry. It is built for the people inside the industry who are responsible for what gets made, how it is sourced, & what it is made from. Event Details 22 September 20263:30 PM - 7:30 PMFashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York City Pre-register now for priority access & programme updates. Registration is open but subject to review. We reserve the right to cancel registrations from organisations outside this scope. We look forward to seeing you there.

events.name: Scaling In Europe - Climate Tech & The Slovakia Advantage
events.description: Join us during New York Climate Week for a discussion on climate technology, clean energy, sustainable infrastructure, & the technologies shaping the next generation of industry.As the transition to a cleaner economy accelerates, Europe is becoming an increasingly important market for climate technology, energy innovation, & sustainable infrastructure. Slovakia offers a compelling platform for this transition, combining a strong nuclear energy base, advanced industry, & a growing technology & innovation ecosystem. The program will highlight Slovak companies scaling internationally, the growing energy demands of AI & data centers, & the role of next-generation nuclear technology in Europe's clean energy future. PROGRAM8:30 AM | Breakfast & NetworkingCoffee & light breakfast 9:00 AM | IntroductionVladimir LackoviSpecial Representative to the U.S. for Trade & Investment, SARIOZuzana SerinovPolicy Manager, AmCham Slovakia 9:15 AM | Keynote - Building Sustainable AI Infrastructure: The Energy & Technology Challenge Faith TaylorSVP Global Sustainability & Citizenship Officer, Kyndryl AI is rapidly increasing demand for data centers, computing power, energy, & resilient digital infrastructure. Faith Taylor will explore how businesses can build more sustainable AI infrastructure & manage the growing intersection of technology, energy, & climate. She will also highlight Kyndryl's growing technology & business services presence in Slovakia, where the company supports organizations with AI, cloud, data, infrastructure modernization, & digital transformation. 9:30 AM | Success Story - Smart Waste, Slovak Roots: Scaling Sensoneo's Technology in the U.S. Roman GdovjakVP of Business Development (USA, Canada), Sensoneo Sensoneo is a Slovak smart waste management company helping cities, manufacturers, facilities, & waste collectors make waste collection & recycling more efficient through smart sensors, data, & route optimization. With projects across the United States, Sensoneo demonstrates how Slovak climate technology can scale internationally while helping organizations reduce costs, improve resource efficiency, & deliver measurable environmental impact. 9:45 AM | The Next Generation of Nuclear Energy Miroslav ariskVP of Strategy & Chief Representative, newcleo Americas newcleo is developing advanced nuclear technology based on lead-cooled fast reactors, with the ambition to provide safer, sustainable, & long-term energy solutions for Europe. The presentation will explore how next-generation nuclear technology could contribute to Europe's energy security & industrial decarbonization. 10:00 AM | Networking Reception Continue the conversation over refreshments & connect with participating companies, investors, policymakers, & partners. Faith Taylor is Senior Vice President of Global Citizenship & Sustainability at Kyndryl, the world's largest IT infrastructure company in over 60 countries & $15B in sales, where she leads ESG strategy across environmental stewardship, social impact, & governance. Under her leadership, Kyndryl set a Science Based Targets-validated Net Zero goal for 2040, cut GHG emissions 18% in under four years, & earned an EcoVadis Gold Medal, placing it in the top 5% of companies assessed. Kyndryl has also been named to Forbes' Top 200 Net Zero Leaders & TIME's list of the World's Most Sustainable Companies. Previously, Faith led ESG at Tesla & built Wyndham Worldwide's sustainability program from scratch, earning it recognition as the hospitality industry's Dow Jones Sustainability World Leader for 7 years in a row. She co-led the World Travel & Tourism Council's Sustainability group, publishing the industry's first ESG reporting framework. Faith serves on CMC Energy Services' Board of Directors & was named a Top 20 ESG Woman Leader in 2025 by Sustainability Magazine. She holds a degree from Stanford & an MBA from Wharton.   The event is organized by the Slovak Investment & Trade Development Agency (SARIO) & AmCham Slovakia, with the support of the Consulate General of the Slovak Republic in New York.

events.description: New York's decision to temporarily halt permitting for new hyperscale data centers is the latest sign of a much bigger collision: AI needs enormous amounts of power, but who will build it, what needs to be deployed, who will finance it, & who will ultimately pay for it? From Texas & Virginia to Europe, the race to power AI is driving demand for new generation, transmission, storage & other infrastructure, & creating a potentially massive new opportunity for investors, developers & energy companies. events.description: Are you responsible for emissions you don't control? Join us for Summit in the Sky, a private panel & networking event held during Climate Week NYC 2026 at One World Trade Center. This invitation-only event brings together senior sustainability, procurement, & supply chain leaders from large corporates actively managing Scope 3 programs, to tackle the defining challenge of corporate decarbonization: being fully accountable for emissions that sit entirely outside your direct operations. Nearly 80% of sustainability leaders cite supplier data availability as their biggest barrier. events.name: Powering The AI Build-Out - India's Data Center Energy Demand Surge
events.description: CleanMax invites you to a moderated panel bringing together hyperscalers, independent power producers & other market participants to examine how India's rapidly scaling data-centre sector will meet its power demand-and what role renewable energy, storage & firm-power structures need to play in getting there. What the panel will explore  The scale & geography of India's data-centre power demand-and what a realistic, bankable renewable-energy pipeline could look like through 2030.  Whether renewables & storage can deliver 24/7, high-reliability power at a viable cost, & where grid, transmission, land & infrastructure constraints could limit new capacity.  How hyperscalers & power producers are structuring supply-from physical & group-captive arrangements to VPPAs & CFDs-and which models are becoming genuinely bankable.  The broader policy & regulatory clarity needed to accelerate investment & give developers, buyers & financiers confidence in long-term delivery.  How data-centre growth can earn community acceptance & support sustainable development through transparent engagement & meaningful local benefits around land, water, infrastructure & livelihoods. Warm regards, CleanMax Team

events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.description: Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban ResilienceDate: Friday, September 25, 2026Venue: Club 135 by IndustriousAddress: 135 W 50th Street, New York, NY 10020Format: Invitation OnlyExpected Attendance: Approximately 200 participantsLanguage: EnglishHost: Office of the City of Yokohama Representative to the AmericasSponsors: ITO ENPartners: Greennex Global, ShibuLA Ventures, CleanLeap & Deep Tech Forum About the ForumThe global economy is undergoing a profound transformation driven by geopolitical uncertainty, the restructuring of global supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, & growing demand for energy & critical resources. Against this backdrop, the circular economy is emerging not only as an environmental agenda, but also as a strategic approach to strengthening economic competitiveness, resource security, industrial resilience, & sustainable growth. Held during Climate Week NYC 2026, the Global Forum on Circular Economy & Urban Resilience will bring together city & regional government representatives, international organizations, corporations, investors, financial institutions, startups, & climate innovation leaders from Asia, North America, Europe, & beyond. Through business showcases, reverse pitches, keynote remarks, & cross-sector discussions, the Forum will connect urban challenges with innovation, investment, & international partnerships. It will also explore how cities can serve as platforms for collaboration among businesses, startups, investors, & global institutions. The Forum will serve as an important step toward Yokohama's major international initiatives in 2027, including GREENEXPO 2027, Asia-Pacific Circular Cities Forum (APCC-Forum), the Asia-Pacific Urban Forum, & broader international dialogue on circular & resilient urban development. View the Speaker ListMorning Programme: Business & Innovation ForumConnecting Innovation Ecosystems Across Asia, North America, & Europe 9:00-9:30 Registration & Networking Coffee9:30-9:40 Welcome Remarks9:40-10:30 Startup ShowcaseSelected startups will present innovative technologies & business models in the fields of the circular economy, climate technology, & urban sustainability. The session is designed to create opportunities for pilot projects, joint development, investment, strategic partnerships, & expansion into Japanese & broader Asian markets. Presenting Startups: TBD 10:30-11:20 Reverse PitchJapanese companies will present their business challenges, innovation priorities, & areas of interest to an audience of international startups. The session aims to identify potential partners & initiate discussions on joint development, pilot projects, & future business collaboration. Participating Companies: Nick Vega, Director on the Investments & Strategy team, Sumitomo Corporation Takeyori Nabeta, Business Development Manage at Chiyoda International Corporation / Venture Associate at DNX Ventures Junya Saka, Manager, Strategic Investment & Partnerships, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation Hirotaka Mori, Principal Researcher, Business Development & CVC, ENEOS Americas Additional companies: TBD 11:20-12:00 Innovation Leaders DialogueAI, the Circular Economy, & the Next Industrial Transformation Artificial intelligence is reshaping industries through major investment in semiconductors, data centers, digital infrastructure, & advanced industrial systems. At the same time, AI has the potential to accelerate the transition to a more sustainable & circular economy by improving efficiency across manufacturing, energy, logistics, resource management, & recycling. This session will explore: How AI is reshaping industrial competitiveness Emerging opportunities at the intersection of AI & the circular economy The potential of AI to improve resource efficiency & industrial decarbonization Partnerships needed to commercialize & scale next-generation technologies The roles of corporations, investors, & startups in the next industrial transformation Speakers: Durgesh Patel, Vice President, AI Center of Excellence, Hitachi Ray Hugel, CFA, Executive Director & Co-Head of Catalytic Capital & Private Credit, Closed Loop Partners Kazuhiko Nishioka, Co-Founder & CEO, Sun Metalon Kevin Ninomiya, CEO & Co-Founder, ShibuLA Ventures (Moderator) 12:00-1:30 Networking LunchAn opportunity for investors, startups, corporations, city leaders, & international organizations to connect across sectors, explore collaboration opportunities, & develop partnerships that can continue beyond the Forum. The networking lunch will also be open to participants attending the afternoon programme. Afternoon Programme: Policy & Leadership ForumAccelerating Circular Economy & Urban Resilience 1:30-1:40 Opening Remarks1:40-2:00 Keynote AddressThe Next Chapter of the Circular Economy: Competitiveness, Resilience, & Global Collaboration The circular economy is increasingly becoming a strategic framework for strengthening economic competitiveness, industrial resilience, resource security, & sustainable growth. The keynote will examine why accelerating the transition requires deeper collaboration among cities, businesses, investors, & international organizations, setting the stage for the Forum's discussions on innovation, partnerships, & global action. Keynote Speaker:Jibran Ahmed, Lead, Economic Development, Urban Transformation, World Economic Forum 2:00-2:20 Session 1Asia's Circular Future: New Opportunities for Global Collaboration Asia's rapid urbanization & growing policy ambition are making the region increasingly important to the global circular economy transition. Cities will play a central role in translating global goals into locally driven policies, partnerships, & practical action. This session will examine how Asian cities can work with global partners to accelerate circular solutions & create new opportunities for cooperation. Discussion themes include: Why Asia will be central to the next phase of the circular economy The role of cities in advancing circular solutions through policy, procurement, & partnerships Opportunities for collaboration between Asian cities & global partners Yokohama's role as a platform for international collaboration toward 2027 GREENEXPO 2027 & related international initiatives Speaker: Tomomi Yamashita, Director General for Global Initiatives, City of Yokohama Carlos Silva Filho, Member of United Nations Secretary-General's Advisory Board on Zero Waste 2:20-3:05 Session 2Investing in the Circular Economy: Innovation, Markets, & GrowthThe transition to a circular economy is creating new markets, attracting investment, & driving innovation across industries & cities worldwide. This session will explore how cities, businesses, investors, & innovation ecosystems can create market opportunities, attract capital & talent, & scale solutions capable of delivering both economic & environmental value. Discussion themes include: Emerging investment opportunities in the circular economy Building innovation ecosystems that attract capital & talent The role of cities in creating markets for circular solutions Public-private partnerships for scaling innovation Strengthening competitiveness through circular innovation Speakers: TBDModerator: TBD 3:05-3:50 Session 3Bridging Regions: Partnerships for Circular & Resilient Cities The circular transition cannot be delivered by cities, financial institutions, businesses, or international organizations acting independently. This session will explore how regional & global partnerships can connect urban priorities with technical expertise, investment, & implementation capacity. The discussion will focus on moving beyond the exchange of ideas toward concrete projects, financing mechanisms, & long-term collaboration. Discussion themes include: Connecting cities across Asia, North America, & other regions Mobilizing finance for circular & resilient urban projects Building pipelines of investable city projects Connecting cities with businesses, investors, & international institutions Scaling successful solutions across different markets Turning international dialogue into practical collaboration Continuing collaboration through international forums & Yokohama's initiatives in 2027 Speakers: Sandra Goldmark, Associate Dean for Engagement & Impact & Professor of Professional Practice, Columbia Climate School Local 2030 Coalition (Speaker TBA) Berat Senyerli, CEO of Bankable Zero Vijay Jagannathan, Senior Fellow at World Resources Institute (Moderator) 3:50-4:00 Closing RemarksWho Should AttendThe Forum is designed for: City & regional government representatives International organizations Corporations & business leaders Investors & financial institutions Startups & entrepreneurs Climate technology & circular economy experts Urban development & resilience professionals Innovation ecosystem leaders

events.name: NYFW Debrief: Fashion Networking Event
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. Just a proper debrief: what collections landed, what trends are actually going to stick past the week, which shows everyone's still talking about, & which ones nobody will remember by October. This one's for the designers, stylists, editors, buyers, PR people, models, photographers, & everyone else who spent the past week running on adrenaline & iced coffee. Whether you were front row every day or watching it all unfold from your feed, come compare notes with people who get it. What to expect: Open conversation on the season's best (and most bewildering) moments Drinks & light bites (cash bar) Genuinely good networking (the kind that happens when everyone's a little more relaxed than they were all week) A room full of people worth exchanging numbers with Who it's for:Anyone in or around the fashion industry, designers, stylists, editors, marketers, PR, buyers, creatives, & the people who make fashion week actually happen behind the scenes. Dress code: however you want. events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

We're decoding whether drone delivery can actually scale profitably or whether the real bottleneck was never the FAA to begin with. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionGenerative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.  The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers & builders can go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, & to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made.  What to ExpectA full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, & system admins who know these problems cold End-of-day demos to judges, investors, & real TA leaders The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers  PrizesWinners walk away with build-tool & platform credits, expert consulting sessions, & investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders & buyers.  JudgesTiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral & hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships. Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator & builder in the HR-tech ecosystem. Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside. Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel. Shiv Jethi - Engineer at SpaceX. Olivia Iarmak - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality & operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Prince Rumi - Excelsior Edge Ventures, Partner | AI Researcher Rami Abouemira, formerly People Ops at Square & VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR & Founders Foundry. Ishaan Das (TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation & product design for several recruiting firms & recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg. More judges to be announced - investors & TA buyers joining the panel.  Who Should AttendEngineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML Founders & aspiring founders who like shipping fast Recent grads, master's students, & NYC college builders TA ops & recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build.  Credit SponsorsSolari is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, & desktops from one API, & automate at scale. Block Convey is an AI reliability & observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval & decisions, identify where it fails, & improve it.  HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Integral Recruiting (IRD): Enterprise talent-acquisition & iCIMS/ATS specialists, & stewards of the ~350-member SAI community of TA operators & system admins. Greg Mendez: NYU. Bringing the university's builder & HR-analytics community into the room. TechSHRM is NYU Tandon's, award-winning student chapter of the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM). Established in 1987, we bridge data science, technology, & organizational strategy through people analytics - leveraging data to optimize workforce decision-making, recruitment, & employee performance.

events.name: Family Offices & Investors Summit
events.description: 150 seats. One room. For the family offices & investors shaping the next decade of climate & frontier tech. *************************************** A NOTE ON THIS YEAR'S FORMAT After 6 summits & conversations with some of the most respected allocators in our network, we rebuilt this event from the ground up. The feedback was clear: fewer people, sharper curation, more structured conversations, less noise. We listened. This year, we are introducing a phased entry system designed to protect the quality of every interaction in the room. Phase 1 (2:00 PM): Family offices & institutional LPs enter first. For one full hour, the room belongs exclusively to verified allocators. No pitches. No founders. No fund managers. Just the people who write the largest checks, meeting each other on their own terms. Phase 2 (3:00 PM): Fund managers & GPs join. They enter a room where 45+ family offices are already warmed up & engaged. Thematic breakout rooms open by vertical: Energy Abundance, Grid Optimization, Climate Resilience, Built Environment. No random panels. Every room has a thesis. Phase 3 (4:00 PM): Founders enter. They walk into a room of 90+ allocators & fund managers who have been having substantive capital conversations for two hours. The conversations are flowing. The context is set. 150 seats. Three phases. Every phase designed so the right people meet at the right moment. We are not getting bigger. We are getting better. This is the most curated, most intentional event we have ever produced. If you have been in our rooms before, you will notice the difference. If this is your first time, you are walking into something we spent three years learning how to build. For this 7th edition of our summit, we are coming back with a professional event production team, snacks & wine, jazz band & a investors speed dating platform designed to break the ice & maximize your fundraising during Climate Week NYC! The Family Offices & Investors Summit @ Climate Week NYC is not another conference - it's a curated, closed-door gathering where LPs, GPs, & climate founders sit at the same table & do business. Last year, our events facilitated over $37M in investments & transactions (+the ones we have not made aware of). This year, we're raising the bar & want to double that number.  WHO'S BEEN IN THE ROOM: Invited Family Offices & Institutional Capital  KKR ($361B+ AUM, New York) - Global investment firm. Principal from KKR's Sustainability & Capital Formation team joining us.  Generation Investment Management ($44B+ AUM, San Francisco / London) - Al Gore's sustainable investment firm. Founding Partner Colin le Duc returning for the second consecutive year.  Rockefeller Foundation ($6B endowment, New York) - Director of Energy Technology & Innovation Shunondo Basu. Net-zero endowment commitment. Speaker at both 2025 summits, returning for 2026  Merit France / CMA CGM Saade Family (~$18B family fortune, France) - The world's 3rd largest shipping company. Committed $18B to fleet decarbonization & launched a $1.5B Pulse Fund dedicated to frontier & clean energy innovation.  Energy Impact Partners ($4.5B AUM, New York) - Climate infrastructure VC backed by 80+ global utility & energy partners. Returning for 2026.  Schmidt Sciences (Multi-$B, Palo Alto) - Eric Schmidt's frontier science & technology initiative. events.name: Retrofits For Resilience - From Policy To Implementation
events.description: For Climate Week 2026, the Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering presents Retrofits for Resilience: From Policy to Implementation in partnership with NYU Corporate Engagement & the Center for the Sustainable Built Environment at NYU Schack. Featured Speakers: Bomee Jung, Cadence OneFive Will DiMaggio, Building Efficiency & Decarbonization at NYC Mayor's Office of Climate & Environmental Justice Moderator: Suhail Y Tayeb, NYU Schack Institute of Real Estate more to be announced! Retrofits are often framed primarily as a climate mitigation tool, a way to cut emissions from the buildings we already have. At the neighborhood level, they often can also serve an equally urgent purpose: strengthening residential climate resilience against flooding, extreme heat, & degraded air quality, often for the communities that can least afford to wait for these improvements. However, as extreme weather increases in frequency & severity, cities are grappling with issues like high upfront costs, labor shortages, disruption to tenants, deferred maintenance, & aging infrastructure that limit the speed & scale of retrofit programs. The good news is that emerging technologies, financing approaches, & public-private partnerships are creating new pathways to accelerate retrofit implementation. Using New York City as a jumping off point, we'll examine the following questions: How can innovative technologies help address affordability, capacity, & workforce constraints for residential retrofits? And how can cities adopt, de-risk, & scale these solutions? What is the potential for retrofit programs to also support climate resilience & improved quality of life, in addition to energy efficiency & emissions reductions? What new approaches are needed, from measuring ROI to assessing risk, to support resilience planning in retrofit programs? And what role can innovation play in these changes?

events.name: Reforest The Future
events.description: Reforestation is ready for a reckoningThe scale of reforestation the planet needs & the pace at which it's happening are nowhere close. We know this. So how do we accelerate the pace & scale of reforestation? The Reforest the Future summit is a half-day event that brings together practitioners, funders, community leaders, & indigenous voices to actively tackle that question together. The summit focuses on 3 key levers that move restoration forward: Track I: Who Pays for a Forest?FINANCE TRACKInvestment models, blended finance, & how capital structures can move restoration from a concept to funded & delivering on the ground. Track II:  How Do We Build Forests That Last?TOOLS, TECH & TRAININGSeed systems, project deployment, monitoring technology, & the training pipelines needed to build real capacity across the organizations & communities driving restoration forward. Track III:  Who Are Forests For?COMMUNITIES TRACKCentering Indigenous & local communities, & the practices that make restoration equitable, locally rooted, & enduring. The summit opens with breakfast & a keynote, moves into the 3 tracks, & ends with a closing luncheon. Along the way, expect diverse perspectives, hard-won lessons, working through the challenges, & figuring out what comes next. Sessions details & speakers to be announced soon. For more details, please visit: https://terraformation.com/new-york-climate-week-2026 About Terraformation (host):Terraformation is building the enabling layer for the global reforestation movement. Our hybrid for-profit/nonprofit model enables us to advance the innovation, capacity building, & narrative leadership the movement needs to scale while developing high-integrity, landscape-scale native forest projects. We treat forests as infrastructure for human well-being - protecting water, food, culture, livelihoods, & climate - & we center our work around the Indigenous people, communities, & practitioners who bring forests back to life.
