events.name: From Crisis To Proximity - A New Social Contract For Cities
events.description: Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. By rethinking how we organize time, space, & everyday access, proximity provides a powerful framework for transforming urban life. Concepts such as the x-minute city & high-quality social life demonstrate how human-scale ecosystems can reduce carbon emissions, ease daily stress, strengthen communities, & create new forms of economic value. In this vision, proximity is neither a trend nor a lifestyle choice, but a structural response to the crises shaping urban futures - one that can make cities more humane, inclusive, & resilient. As a new urban era emerges, proximity becomes the cornerstone of a renewed pact between citizens, institutions, & territories, enabling people not only to live in cities but to flourish in them.  Carlos Moreno, a French-Colombian scholar based in Paris since age 20, is Professor at IAE Paris-Sorbonne & Scientific Director of the ETI Chair. A multidisciplinary researcher, he is internationally recognized for innovative ideas to improve urban life. Creator of the 15-Minute City, he received the 2022 UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour. He is a member of the French Academy of Technologies, the International Academy of Architecture, the American Academy of Housing & Communities, & Sigma Xi. Widely awarded & influential, his writings appear in 14 languages, & he is regarded as one of the world's leading contemporary urban thinkers.  Lewis Mumford Lecture SeriesEach spring, the Spitzer School of Architecture & its Urban Design Program present the Lewis Mumford Lecture & seminar. Named for writer, architecture critic, & urbanist Lewis Mumford, who attended City College, the series invites the world's most distinguished urbanists to speak freely & publicly about the future of cities & the social purposes of architecture. Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today's urban crises - climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, & social fragmentation - lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being & quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection & decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity - the capacity for people to remain connected - has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion. This lecture argues that we must go further & establish a new social contract for cities, grounded in proximity as a civic, ecological, & economic principle. events.name: Governing Wealth Transfer - Turning AI Tech Billions Into Climate Reparations
events.description: Interrogate, reimagine, & practice new models for resource governance. Date & Time: September 24th, 4:00 PM - 6:00 PM Location: The New School - Additional Event Details will be sent out in a follow up email.  Implementing effective climate solutions requires a fundamental shift in how resources are distributed. Data centers & the rise of technology not only impact the ecological & social health of our communities, the massive influx of AI & tech wealth is reshaping philanthropy. It is clear that while financial resources exist, the global systems at hand lack the accountable & moral capacity to implement justly. In this dialogue across speakers with different perspectives, we will explore how to direct this next wave of capital including a look into our solution for moving tech billions toward climate reparations.  This is a critical moment for frontline communities to intervene & pivot tech wealth toward the resources we all need to live, rest, & thrive in the places we love. We invite you to learn how Taproot Earth is building a durable alternative of climate finance, rooted in self-determination & collective decision-making, where communities determine how these funds protect, repair, & steward our water, energy, & land. Refreshments to follow. Registration is required & will close Monday 9/21.

events.name: Make It In Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest
events.description: Join us during NYC Climate Week for the Make It in Brooklyn Climate Tech Pitch Contest, where five early-stage climate technology startups will compete for up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support. Founders will be evaluated on innovation, feasibility, market potential, & potential impact. The winning startup will receive up to $10,000 in funding & commercialization support to help accelerate its path to market. The prize includes: $5,000 in unrestricted prize funding from Downtown Brooklyn Partnership. Up to an additional $5,000 in milestone-based commercialization support through National Grid's Clean Tech Incubation Program. Eligible expenses include prototype development & testing, patent & legal filing costs, market research, commercialization activities, & pilot implementation support. The Climate Tech Pitch Contest brings together founders, investors, industry leaders, & members of the innovation ecosystem to spotlight technologies addressing some of today's most pressing climate challenges. Finalists: PollenPal is using AI-powered sensors & computer vision to help beekeepers monitor hive health in real time, improve colony management, & address the growing challenge of honeybee colony loss. HiFIT is advancing offshore wind through innovative weld treatment technology that strengthens turbine structures, enabling longer service life, reduced steel consumption & maintenance costs, & lower embodied carbon. Novara Tech is developing mobile recycling technology that transforms hard-to-recycle composite waste from industries like wind energy & construction into reusable materials for urban infrastructure, reducing landfill waste & transportation costs. Kyber Energy is developing AI-powered energy management software that helps commercial & industrial businesses optimize electricity use, shift demand away from peak periods, & reduce both energy costs & grid emissions. AtmosOne AI is helping address growing demand on the electric grid by intelligently shifting flexible AI computing to off-peak periods, reducing grid strain & enabling more efficient use of existing energy infrastructure. Judges will be announced soon. This event is in partnership with the Malin & National Grid. The Malin is a beautifully designed workspace for ambitious founders, creatives, & industry leaders who value genuine community over transactional co-working, & they're offering our network 25% off day passes & meeting rooms at their Brooklyn Heights location, using code DBP25 through the end of 2026, redeemable here. About Make It in Brooklyn Make It in Brooklyn is Downtown Brooklyn Partnership's innovation platform supporting startups through pitch competitions, ecosystem-building initiatives, & direct entrepreneurial support programs. Through year-round programming, Make It in Brooklyn connects founders with capital, mentors, customers, & the resources needed to grow & scale their businesses.

events.name: Bending The Climate Curve
events.description: Addressing climate change by bending the climate curve will require both reducing emissions, & atmospheric carbon dioxide removal strategies that integrate the ocean's central role in Earth's climate system. As interest grows in the ocean's capacity to store carbon, so does the need for knowledge-based approaches that are guided by strong ethical & governance frameworks. This event will explore the state of emerging methods to enhance the ocean's natural carbon sink, in particular phytoplankton-based approaches. Our panel of experts will discuss how diverse approaches can inform responsible innovation & implementation, as well as the guardrails needed to guide field trials & future action while safeguarding our shared ocean. Moderator Alexandra Talty (Climate & ocean journalist, former Pulitzer Center Ocean Reporting fellow & co-founder of Ocean CDR Watch) Panelists Ken Buesseler (Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions, Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution) Danielle Ringer (Community Leaders & mCDR (CLaM), Ringer Consulting, Kodiak, Alaska) Fatima Candace Vahlsing (Ocean Conservancy) Event Schedule 8:30am-9:30am - Light Breakfast & Networking 9:30am-11am - Main Program (Opening Remarks, Panel Discussion, Audience Q&A) 11am-12pm - Networking This event is hosted by Exploring Ocean Iron Solutions (ExOIS). events.name: 35% Moment - What Will It Take To Electrify Global Economy By 2035
events.description: Electricity meets barely a fifth of the world's final energy demand today. Yet electrification is the fastest lever governments have to cut emissions, insulate households from the next fossil fuel price shock, & maintain energy security. Getting there means moving vehicles, buildings, & industry onto electrons & modernizing & expanding the power grid faster than any economy has yet managed.  With over 100 companies, the EU, UN, & more, likely to commit to electrify 35% of final energy demand by 2035, this event will ask what it takes to electrify the economy within the next decade. The countries that pull it off first won't just hit a target, they'll write the playbook everyone else has to follow. This special event will be co-presented by the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School & Centre for Net Zero, a nonprofit research institute founded by Octopus Energy Group. Speakers:Devrim Celal, Chief Flexibility & Marketing Officer at Kraken TechnologiesDana Guernsey, CEO & Co-Founder at Voltus Robert Metcalfe, Chief Economist at Centre for Net Zero (part of the Octopus Energy Group) & Professor at Columbia SIPAGernot Wagner (moderator), Climate Economist & Faculty Director of the Climate Knowledge Initiative at Columbia Business School

events.name: Backing Innovation - How States Investing In The Future
events.description: State venture funds are playing an increasingly important role in building regional innovation ecosystems. This panel brings together leaders from three of the Northeast's most active public VC programs - Connecticut Innovations, New York State's NY Ventures, & the New Jersey Economic Development Authority - for a candid discussion on how government capital is shaping the next generation of startups. Panelists will discuss how their funds source & evaluate deals, what differentiates public venture capital from traditional VC, & where they see the biggest opportunities for founders & investors across the region. Stick around afterwards for a happy hour with the founders & VCs. Meet the panelists: Danny Qiao is a Director on Connecticut Innovations' investment team, where he leads the team's consumer & international investment efforts. Prior to CI, he led consumer investing at Sweater Ventures, backing brands like IQBAR, Graza, Nomadica, OROS, & Havenly. He began his career at Accenture Strategy & later covered financial sponsors & financial institutions in investment banking at BNP Paribas. Danny holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management & a BS from Cornell University's School of Industrial & Labor Relations. Jennifer Tegan is the Managing Director of Empire State Development's New York Ventures, where she oversees over $320 million in investment programs aimed at fueling New York's startup ecosystem. Since joining in 2020, she has managed direct & indirect investment funds including the NYS Innovation Venture Capital Fund & the Emerging & Regional Manager Partner Fund (a fund of funds). An experienced investor & advocate, Jennifer previously spent 18 years as a partner at Cayuga Venture Fund. She has served on the board of the National Venture Capital Association & held leadership roles with Tompkins Financial Corporation & the Upstate Capital Association of New York. Jennifer holds an MBA from Cornell University, an MS from the University of Cincinnati, & a BA from Smith College. John Wisniewski is the Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives & Venture Products at New Jersey Economic Development Authority. His responsibilities include oversight of the state's investment into Strategic Innovation Centers, & venture investment programs. John started his career with ExxonMobil where he held various positions developing projects in the US & internationally.  He ran a private equity infrastructure fund based in the Middle East for Arcapita Bank, & then switched to venture capital working with Clean Energy Ventures Group. John has a BS in Chemical Engineering from Cooper Union, & an MBA from Rice University. Meet the hosts: Connecticut Innovations is Connecticut's venture capital arm, investing in early & growth-stage biotech, IT, & deep tech companies. NY Ventures is New York State's innovation venture capital fund, backing high-growth startups across the state. NJEDA's Venture Products team supports New Jersey's innovation ecosystem, including through the New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. Meet the sponsors: Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups & the accountants supporting them. Whether you're launching a startup or accelerating your growth, the Emerging Growth team offers strategic insights & resources designed to support your business journey. #nyc #venturecapital #government

events.name: Why You Think the Way You Do About Money
events.description:
Why You Think the Way You Do About Money: A live panel on the psychology behind every financial decision you've ever made

​Here's a question nobody asks at a normal finance event:

​Why does your best friend save obsessively while you can't walk past a sale, even though you make the same salary?

​Why do you know exactly what you "should" do with your money and still not do it?

​Why did you inherit your dad's spending anxiety instead of his frugality?

​That's the whole point of this panel. Rebecca Pino (financial advisor) and Suzanne Kirkendall (behavioral scientist) are turning the mic on each other — and on you.

​No slide decks, no "5 tips to save more" energy. Just two people who study money and behavior for a living, asking each other the questions they actually want answered, then opening the floor so the audience can grill them both together.

events.name: Derek Parfit's Birthday!
events.description:
Derek Parfit was perhaps the greatest moral philosopher of the 20th century, in how he shaped the discipline and raised important new questions. 

He gave us the Repugnant Conclusion and the Hitchhiker's Dilemma, and put a plug for giving 10% into On What Matters, his masterpiece. Had he lived long enough to finish another volume, he had plans to discuss existential risk and dive deeper into questions of how we ought to act.

How to celebrate Parfit's life and work? You could discuss population ethics, philosophize about something else, or consider, as a group, ways to make your lives slightly more rational. (Or just eat cake and sing Happy Birthday and engage in idle, friendly conversation; Parfit surely wouldn't object.)

events.description:
This is a social event hosted for jhana meditators and those who are curious about jhana meditation. During the meeting we will meditate but there will be no instruction; you're welcome to meditate however you like or to sit quietly for an hour.

Please bring food and drinks to share. Paper cups, plates, bowls, utensils, and napkins will be provided.
Meditation cushions will not be provided.  Please bring whatever you need to make yourself comfortable.  We will be meeting in The Lounge.
DIRECTIONS
There are two grey doors at the address. Enter the one on the RIGHT (to the right of Savino's Quality Pasta) and proceed straight up the stairs to the second floor.

events.name: NYCResistor Ham Radio Club
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/nycresistor-ham-radio-club-tickets-1633091413379

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.
Come make some noise in the weird and wonderful medium of radio!This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.
Please note that refunds must be requested 24 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

events.name: -1 to Anduril with Trae Stephens
events.description:
South Park Commons is delighted to host Trae Stephens as part of our -1 to Now series.
Event Details
3:00pm: Doors Open + Mingling
3:30-4:30pm: Fireside Chat

Trae is a General Partner at Founders Fund. He is also Co-founder and Executive Chairman of Anduril Industries, a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems.
Previously, Trae was an early employee at Palantir Technologies, where he led teams focused on growth in the intelligence/defense space as well as international expansion, helping large organizations solve their hardest data analysis problems. He was also an integral part of the product team, leading the design and strategy for new product offerings. While at Palantir, Trae also served as an adjunct faculty member at Georgetown University.
Prior to Palantir, Trae worked as a computational linguist building enterprise solutions to Arabic/Persian name matching and data enrichment within the United States Intelligence community. He began his career working in the office of then Congressman Rob Portman and in the Political Affairs Office at the Embassy of Afghanistan in Washington, D.C. immediately following the installation of Hamid Karzai’s transitional government. Trae graduated from the School of Foreign Service at Georgetown University.

About South Park Commons (SPC)
SPC is a technical community and venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, and technologists figure out what to work on next—what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible.
SPC events are open to members, alumni, and special guests of the community. The best way to join events at SPC is to apply for SPC membership.
*Please note doors close at event start time and we are unable to accommodate pending, waitlist, or late arrivals.

events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/learn-to-use-a-laser-cutter-to-cut-and-etch-your-own-designs-tickets-2001386748641

Harness the power of an Epilog 60 Watt Laser! In this class you'll learn everything you need.Harness the power of an Epilog 60 Watt Laser! In this class you'll learn everything you need to know to make the ideas in your head become a reality with a laser.
In this three hour class, you will learn:
How to set up a file for cutting on the laser cutter in Inkscape or Adobe Illustrator.Laser cutter safety including materials testing.Laser cutter operation including configuration, cuts and raster etching in common materials like wood, acrylic, cardboard and others.At the end of class, you will go home with:
One laser cut project, either the class default or a simple one of your own design (see below for details)Resistor Laser Certification, enabling you to use our laser on Craft Nights.Please bring the following to class:
A laptop with either Inkscape (free: download here: https://inkscape.org/release/inkscape-1.2.1/) or Adobe Illustrator installed.
A USB jump drive
The following items are optional if you'd like to try cutting a simple custom design. If your file ends up being too complicated, we may have you do the class default project first, just to learn the laser in the time allotted - but we'll definitely help you with your more complex cut at a free Craft Night in future!
An SVG vector file of a simple shape you'd like to cut for your first cut.A piece of 1/8 inch or thinner wood, acrylic or cardboard you'd like to cut. If you can't bring your own material, small pieces will be made available, or larger pieces for purchase on site.Please be on time for the start of class! If you're late you will miss your slot.
This class will be taught by NYC Resistor member Woody. As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.
Please note that refunds must be requested 72 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.

events.name: Synthesizer Night @ NYC Resistor
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/synthesizer-night-nyc-resistor-tickets-2002480300484

Gathering musicians, enthusiasts, and curious minds to connect, collaborate, and share their passion for synthesis. BYO synth encouraged!Join us at NYC Resistor, a makerspace in Brooklyn for an electrifying Synthesizer Night! Get ready to unleash your creativity, explore sonic landscapes, and connect with fellow synth enthusiasts in an evening dedicated to the mesmerizing world of synthesizers. This is a pay-what-you-wish event (recommended donation $8).
Synthesizer Night at NYC Resistor is a celebration of all things synthesizer. Whether you're a seasoned musician, an avid collector, or simply fascinated by the possibilities of electronic sound, this event offers a unique opportunity to gather with like-minded individuals and revel in the captivating soundscape of synthesizers.
At Synthesizer Night, participants are encouraged to bring their own synthesizers, from vintage analog gems to cutting-edge modular wonders. It's a chance to showcase your personal setup, experiment with new equipment, and dive into the rich sonic tapestry that synthesizers offer.
For those looking to enhance the collaborative experience, consider arriving early to connect your synthesizer to a MIDI/CV clock. This allows for synchronized timing among all instruments, creating a seamless musical fusion during impromptu jam sessions.
In addition to the collaborative jam sessions, the event provides a unique opportunity for a show and tell/play with anything that attendees bring. Share your favorite gear, experiment with different setups, and engage in hands-on exploration of various synthesizers and electronic music equipment.
The event unfolds in a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere, providing a platform for musicians, enthusiasts, and curious minds to connect, collaborate, and share their passion for synthesis. Whether you're a beginner seeking guidance or an expert eager to inspire others, Synthesizer Night is the perfect setting to engage in conversations, exchange knowledge, and foster a vibrant community. 
Throughout the evening, you'll have the opportunity to engage in impromptu jam sessions, where the collective energy of multiple synthesizers intertwines to create awe-inspiring sounds. Experience the joy of collaborating with fellow musicians, experiment with different genres and styles, and let the unique characteristics of each instrument shape your sonic explorations.
Additionally, for those who wish to showcase their skills and perform, there will be dedicated performance slots. Take center stage, captivate the audience, and let your creativity soar as you demonstrate the full potential of your synthesizer setup. To sign up for a performance slot, email classes@nycresistor.com or join our Discord and post to #synth.
Whether you're an ardent synth enthusiast, an aspiring musician, or simply curious about the captivating world of synthesizers, Synthesizer Night at NYC Resistor is an event that will inspire, educate, and leave you in awe of the boundless possibilities that electronic sound offers. Don't miss this opportunity to immerse yourself in an evening of music, collaboration, and innovation. Mark your calendars, pack up your favorite synths, and join us at NYC Resistor for a night you won't soon forget. We can't wait to see you there!
This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.

In this wire wrapping workshop, we will unlock our creative potential by crafting unique objects from aluminum wire and stones.You'll learn four simple weaving techniques that build into complex, stimulating details, and how to embed stones and beads securely into your designs. Once you've mastered the techniques, you'll put them to use creating either a wand or a bracelet. Participants can also personalize their piece with their choice of stones and beads.
Quartz points, assorted gemstone beads, and aluminum wire will be provided. Feel free to bring your own stones and beads.
Who is this class for:
Anyone that likes working with their hands and small repetitive details.
Your Instructor:I am an artist that approaches many mediums and loves working with her hands. My visual language stems from my proclivity for organic details and fluid dynamics. Wire wrapping has been an important medium in my exploration in tandem with stones and crystals. I enjoy creating small 'magical' objects with different combinations of stones, wire wrapping techniques, metals, anything to create pieces that feel alive and otherworldly but also intuitive and instinctually familiar.

events.name: PCB Artwork: Make your own business card
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/pcb-artwork-make-your-own-business-card-tickets-2002916205287

Printed circuit boards aren't just for electronics. Their layered structure make them a surprisingly expressive artistic medium.Printed circuit boards aren't just for electronics. Their layered structure, copper traces, soldermask colors, and silkscreen printing make them a surprisingly expressive artistic medium.
In this workshop, you'll use PCBs to design your own business card (or any other kind of card), ready to fabricate in real fiberglass and copper.
You'll edit and manipulate vector art in **Inkscape**, convert your artwork into a **KiCAD** footprint, and place it on a board ready to be fabricated. Along the way, you'll learn how PCB fabricators interpret computer graphics: how vector paths become physical primitives, how colors map to fabrication layers, and how artwork gets distributed across copper, soldermask, and silkscreen to create the final board.
No electronics background required — this workshop is about graphic design and fabrication, not circuit theory or soldering. If you have a computer, you can make a graphic PCB! If you already know how to design a PCB, this can help you level up their visual appeal. Background in working with SVG is helpful but not required.
To bring:
LaptopThis workshop is lead by Alex Tait.
There are 2 spots reserved for people who cannot access the class at the full price, so please make use of one of these half-off need-based tickets if that is your situation. Checkout Code: 4-ACCESSTIX

events.name: Simple Data Networks for Multidisciplinary Artists
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/simple-data-networks-for-multidisciplinary-artists-tickets-2002982579815

Learn to create projects involving multiple separate components that communicate together to provide unique interactive experiences!If you're a multidisciplinary artist who likes to explore combinations of multiple different backgrounds, mediums or genres, or if you're a curious experimentalist who loves to mix and match various skillsets or software tools, you may not always find one single solution or application that accomplishes everything your project needs. You often just have to create the solution yourself!Consider these examples:- Using a physical sensor (distance, light, pressure, etc.) as an input to a computer program- Using a machine learning model (hand pose, body pose, face detection, etc.) to interface with an interactive kinetic or LED-based sculpture- Creating a handheld or wearable wireless controller for your generative synthesized musical instrument, allowing you to move around freely instead of being stuck to your computer on stage, or better yet, repurposing an existing smartphone to function as one- Enabling audience participation during a performance through the smartphones they already own- Solving any creative problem where no out-of-the-box solution already exists!For these tasks above and many many more, you may just have to break down your idea into separate components, handle each component separately using whichever tool that's best for the job, and then allow those components to work together to solve the larger task. No compromise needed!To accomplish this, we will go over OSC, the most widely supported real-time communication protocol that exists. OSC is the common language that your favorite hardware/software tool most likely speaks, and which allows multiple otherwise-incompatible programs to easily communicate with each other. We will introduce some basic networking concepts and dive right into how to send/receive OSC messages between devices. We'll work in pairs to mix-and-match different software tools together and see what kinds of interactions we can create. Time permitting, we'll have some time for creative brainstorming and ideation at the end. 

What kinds of projects and experiences would you want to create with this technology? Who is the class for? This 95% code-free workshop is intended to complement your existing interests and skills.Creative multimedia tools that support OSC include:- TouchDesigner- Max/MSP- Ableton (with M4L)- Processing / OpenFrameworks / p5.js- Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi- Unity/Unreal- Any iOS/Android mobile device- Just raw code baby (Python, Node.js, C++, etc.)- Many othersIf you already use or are interested in any of the items listed above, or are just curious to explore the potential of networking together multiple programs/devices, this beginner-friendly, 95% code-free (code starter examples provided) workshop is a great starting point.Bring a laptop and your smartphone!
Instructor bio:
Yonatan Rozin is a multidisciplinary interactive technologist, prototyper, educator and classically-trained percussionist based in New York City. His freelance and personal practice frequently explores novel combinations of multimedia software and hardware platforms in the creation of unfamiliar installations, performances and experiences. As a freelance interactive art consultant, software engineer at the Harvestworks Digital Media Arts Center and avid collaborator, he has created bespoke interactive solutions for numerous independent artists across a variety of mediums and backgrounds.
This is a masks optional workshop.

This weekend, ML researchers, wet-lab biologists, bioinformaticians, and founders are hacking at SPC on multimodal patient datasets.
On Sunday, they show their work. Teams will demo what they found: new biological insights, new algorithmic approaches, new ways to visualize messy human data. Maybe even a bespoke therapeutic for a specific case.
Judged by the SPC team and guest experts.
Schedule 
4:30PM — Science Fair Style Demos
5:30PM — Finalist Demos + Prizes
About South Park Commons (SPC)
SPC is a technical community and venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, and technologists figure out what to work on next—what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible.
SPC events are open to members, alumni, and special guests of the community. The best way to join events at SPC is to apply for SPC membership.

events.name: Classics-plus-Bible reading group returns(!!!) with Session 2.1: Creation and corruption
events.description:
Welcome back! / Start here!

At long last, we will resume our discussion group where we pair Bible passages with classic literature and philosophy. No beliefs required!
We will be kicking off Season Two at the very beginning with Genesis chapters 1-4, alongside a variety of other texts about new beginnings and falls from grace.
Our sessions will run for about 2 hours, with a break in the middle. These events are free of tuition, but you must own a physical Bible, and you will be required to purchase or borrow some more books as we go along.
Exact readings for this session
Forthcoming. Please check back here closer to the time.
The non-biblical texts will add up to a substantial amount of prep. They will be available online.
About Season Two
This new season overall is called “Dangers, toils, and snares”. We’ll be covering a variety of stories about temptation and suffering, with heavy doses of Genesis and Job, and with perspectives from the likes of Borges, Oscar Wilde, Kierkegaard, Kafka, Simone Weil, Dostoevsky, Boethius, Nietzsche, Flannery O’Connor, and more. As a capstone, we will conclude with multiple sessions on Melville’s Moby-Dick.
This theme will last us through the Spring/Summer 2027, with sessions roughly every other Wednesday.
Unlike in Season One, which served mainly as an introduction to the Bible itself, Season Two will lean more heavily on the “classics” half of our quest. The reading load will be heavier and more modern.

Come join us for an introductory through-hole solderSoldering is one of the most important skills you'll need for working with electronics. Come join us for an introductory through-hole soldering workshop. Soldering enables you to create sturdy connections between electrical components. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to use a soldering iron safely and effectively, and get plenty of practice with both soldering and de-soldering techniques. We'll be soldering up some Game of Life kits - LED tiles that generate nifty animations. events.description:
South Park Commons is excited to host Tanay Kothari, co-founder & CEO of Wispr (and SPC alum) for a fireside chat.
Event Details
3:00pm: Doors Open
3:30-4:30pm: Fireside Chat
Tanay Kothari is the co-founder and CEO of Wispr, the AI-powered voice productivity tool. A four-time founder, he launched FeatherX, an AI personalization startup for online stores, while still in college. After it was acquired by Cerebra Technologies, he joined the company to lead engineering and product. Earlier, he built Convert, a music discovery platform that grew to more than 2.5 million organic monthly active users.

Tanay holds a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and a master’s degree in Artificial Intelligence from Stanford, where he taught the university’s Deep Learning course alongside Prof. Andrew Ng and published research at the Stanford AI Lab. He also served as President of the Stanford Venture Capital Club for three years. In 2023, he was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

About South Park Commons (SPC)
SPC is a technical community and venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, and technologists figure out what to work on next—what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible.
SPC events are open to members, alumni, and special guests of the community. The best way to join events at SPC is to apply for SPC membership.

At Skild, Abhinav focuses on building a general-purpose brain for robots with a long-term goal of building general purpose intelligence. Abhinav is known for pioneering contributions to AI, including scaling visual and robot learning, self-supervised learning, and lifelong learning systems.

events.description:
We're delighted to host Sriram Krishnan at South Park Commons.
Sriram Krishnan most recently served as Senior White House Policy Advisor on Artificial Intelligence, where he was an architect of the U.S. AI Action Plan.

Prior to his White House role, Sriram was a General Partner at Andreessen Horowitz, where he led the firm's international expansion and invested across AI, infrastructure, and consumer technology. He has also held senior product leadership roles at Microsoft, Meta, and Twitter, including early work building Windows Azure and scaling Meta's mobile advertising platform.
Agenda:
11:30am: Doors Open
12:00pm—1:00pm: Fireside Chat & Q&A
About South Park Commons (SPC)
SPC is a technical community and venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, and technologists figure out what to work on next—what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible.
SPC events are open to members, alumni, and special guests of the community. The best way to join events at SPC is to apply for SPC membership.
*Please note doors close at event start time and we are unable to accommodate pending, waitlist, or late arrivals.

events.name: AI Agents Build Day with Genspark
events.description: ​Turn your curiosity about AI into something you can actually use.​Join AI After 5 for a hands-on Genspark AI agent session where we’ll explore what’s possible, build together, and share what we create. Bring an idea, a recurring task, or a problem you’d love AI to help solve.​Agenda​We’ll start with a live Genspark walkthrough, then build a project from scratch so you can see the full process: framing the ask, giving the agent context, reviewing its output, and refining the result.​You’ll leave with​A project you’ve started building around a real need.​A clearer understanding of how to turn an idea into instructions an AI agent can act on.​Practical experience reviewing and improving AI-generated work.​5,000 creditsto experiment and build.​Hosted by​Christopher Martinez— Founder and ecosystem operator at the intersection of AI and healthcare, with a technical foundation as a data and cloud engineer. Founder of Ziora Copilot.​MinaMina Abdulla— Founder ofGenee, an AI-powered coaching platform andAI After 5, a community for women learning and building with AI. Before becoming a founder, she spent 8+ years at Google, most recently leading AI education and upskilling initiatives.​Sam Chien— Former post-training engineer on xAI’s Grok Enterprise team, where he built RL training environments for long-horizon enterprise tasks. Founder of an RL-environment-as-a-service platform backed by Google AI Fund, Betaworks, Hickory Fall Ventures, and NVIDIA Inception.​Sharon Rao, MD— Physician-entrepreneur, exited EdTech founder, ex-COO to the largest MedEd brand (3M+ audience, 300K+ platform subscribers) and NYC Health × Tech community host. She represents healthcare and life sciences at the table.
